Round 252.decision_summary: Parser CommonMark conformance — recognize indented fenced code blocks (§98) and require whitespace after ATX hash sequence (§62)
changes_bullets: crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs: fenced-code-block detection now allows 0–3 leading spaces (CommonMark §98). Previously `line.starts_with("```")` required the fence at column 0, so indented fences (common inside list items) were ignored and their body lines were re-interpreted as ATX headings.

crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs::parse_heading: require space, tab, or end-of-line after the `#{1,6}` sequence and reject lines with 4+ leading spaces (CommonMark §62). Previously `#1 prose` and `    # x` were lifted to headings, creating spurious numbered H1 sections from inline `#N` prose references.

crates/mnemosyne-validator/src/parser.rs tests: 5 regression tests added — `atx_heading_requires_space_after_hashes`, `atx_heading_rejects_four_plus_leading_spaces`, `parse_markdown_indented_fence_is_recognized`, `parse_markdown_round_trips_indented_fence_with_hash_lines`, `parse_markdown_inline_hash_number_in_prose_is_not_heading`.

crates/mnemosyne-cli/src/main.rs::cmd_validate: when round-trip fails, dump the section_id and cross_ref BTreeSet diff (a-only / b-only, capped at 15 / 20 entries) so authors can locate which typed-fact tuples drifted between parse → emit → re-parse. Diagnostic only fires on failure path — happy-path output unchanged.
verification_bullets: cargo test --release -p mnemosyne-validator: 28 parser tests pass (23 pre-existing + 5 new regression tests).

watching-zenoh adoption regression: round-trip mandatory 10/13 → 13/13 with parser fix alone, no source-markdown edits required. T1 orphan total 87 → 75 across changelog-config alignment + parser fix.
mnemosyne self-application validate-workspace unaffected: docs=1/1, T1 orphan=0, round-trip=1/1, style violation counts unchanged from pre-fix baseline.
carry_forward_bullets: list-item-nested fences (CommonMark §49) — where the fence indent matches the enclosing list item's content-indent column rather than 0–3 spaces — remain unhandled; the parser still treats them as plain prose. Full coverage requires list-item state tracking, which is a larger refactor than this conformance round. Acceptable carry: no current Mnemosyne self-doc or known external workspace depends on this case.
diagnostic dump in cmd_validate could later evolve into a structured `--diff-format=json` flag for tooling consumers; current eprintln-only form is sufficient for human authoring loops.

PluginRegistry storage type changed from Box<dyn Validator> to Box<dyn ErasedValidator> — coercion from Box<V: Validator> is automatic via the blanket impl so register_validator(Box::new(my_validator)) keeps its call syntax; registry.validator(key) now returns &dyn ErasedValidator

mnemosyne_core::ValidationFinding struct removed entirely — the stringly-typed kind: Option<String> + extras: BTreeMap<String, Value> shape is no longer the trait return value; typed Self::Finding replaces it; pre-release no-compat policy applies (no external API to preserve)

CodeRefViolation + Citation + ViolationKind gained Serialize derive — default externally-tagged enum form is the auto-derived shape on the ErasedValidator boundary; cli renders a separately-defined flat shape via to_cli_json

It was the Lock 1 measurement spike that proved the typed-fact data shape is portable across rust/kotlin/python/cpp/protobuf; that measurement is closed and recorded in the changelog. The code has had zero consumers — production or cross-crate test — since, and its design_doc_schema_fixture diverged from the real fact model after Round 330 dropped appended_at. Round 337 — decide the incremental-proje.decision_summary: Decide convergence C's incremental-projection architecture jointly with D, resolving the two questions R336 surfaced, derived from the cost-no-object textbook + Phase-0 AI-efficiency mandate. (1) CQRS split: the cli/ops write side appends to the git-native log (SSOT) and stays RocksDB-free (R328); the read side owns the RocksDB index + Salsa cascade and projects, meeting at the core::Transport seam. (2) Salsa memoization is in-process, so C is a warm read-side projection service, not a new authoring-CLI edge; the host binary is bound when the first warm consumer exists (MCP the natural first home per Phase 0; a standalone server daemon deferred per YAGNI invariant #3), and the cli keeps its one-shot full-rebuild path for human/CI use. (3) Engine = fine_grained.rs; the coarse runtime.rs design (monolithic snapshot_payload, non-incremental by construction) is retired at C's implementation (no-legacy-carry). (4) Layer-1 design_doc content feeds the projection engine as Salsa inputs — the engine is a Layer-3-producing read model, not the Layer-0 core, so invariant #4 holds; validation needs only the Layer-0 skeleton. (5) Sequencing (no half-finished): validation projection first (Layer-0 walking skeleton proving the warm-host + RocksDB-free split), then the render projection (the chosen target) superseding the full-rebuild auto_regenerate. Design only — no code; D is co-designed with C, not sequential.

Round 340 — convergence D incremental re.decision_summary: Replace ProjectionService::reload's wholesale rebuild with reconcile_branch_index, which reuses the live BranchIndex handle and every unchanged per-record handle and mutates only the fields that changed — so a re-sync re-executes only the changed entities' sub-queries (size-independent invalidation) and the warm Salsa memo cache survives. This delivers the incremental advantage the fine-grained engine exists for on the validate_projection(refresh=true) path R339 wired; build_branch_index stays the wholesale path for initial construction. Section and ChangelogEntry reconcile field-by-field by stable key (entity_id / round_number); CrossRef and FrozenList reconcile at set granularity since relation rows have no stable identity; the BranchIndex lists reset only on membership change, so a field-only edit does not invalidate the aggregator's list dependency.
changes_bullets: mnemosyne-cascade: add reconcile_branch_index — re-sync an existing BranchIndex to a new fact snapshot by applying the minimal Salsa-input delta. Section and ChangelogEntry reconcile field-by-field keyed by entity_id / round_number (a matching key reuses the record handle and sets only the fields that changed; a new key allocates; a dropped key falls out of the list); CrossRef and FrozenList reconcile at set granularity since relation rows carry no stable identity (identical projected tuples keep the old handles, otherwise the list is reallocated).

The BranchIndex Vec and map fields are reset only when membership changes, so a field-only edit leaves them bit-identical (the same mutated handles) and the aggregator's dependency on the list is not invalidated — only the changed record's sub-query re-runs.

mnemosyne-projection: ProjectionService::reload now re-syncs via reconcile_branch_index instead of project_branch (the build_branch_index wholesale path), reusing the warm BranchIndex handle so unchanged entities keep their memoized sub-queries across a re-sync; build still uses the wholesale path for initial construction.

Effect: the validate_projection(refresh=true) path R339 wired is now actually incremental — a single-section edit re-executes only that section's sub-query rather than the whole branch, the defining property the fine-grained Salsa engine exists for, now exercised on a live path.

Round 346 — sever the cascade→facts re-e.decision_summary: Make the CQRS RocksDB-free invariant (R328/R337/R338, ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4-5) true structurally, not just behaviorally. The mcp binary still linked librocksdb-sys via the sole chain mnemosyne-store(rocksdb) → facts → cascade → projection → mcp. Root cause: cascade imported the 5 canonical fact structs from mnemosyne-facts, but R328 MOVED those structs to mnemosyne-core (facts only re-exported them) and cascade uses none of facts's RocksDB-coupled API — so cascade→facts was pure pre-R328 re-export residue. Fix: cascade depends on mnemosyne-core (not facts) and imports the structs from there; the now-dead public struct re-export is removed from facts (facts publicly exports only its own codec/persist binding, matching its crate doc); facts persist.rs imports the structs from core directly. Severs the sole chain — cascade/projection/mcp are now RocksDB-free at link time, store confined to the facts/index/server write subgraph. server/store/facts/index stay orphaned-but-kept (convergence substrate, invariant #1) — unchanged.

And convergence B was labeled 'Active keystone — write the missing projection,' though the projection, the composite-key persist, and ChangelogEntry's scalar-shape settlement all landed (R329/R330/R332); only routing live queries through the durable index remains, and that is scale-gated YAGNI — the warm in-memory projection serves dogfood scale, and the composite-key index is reserved for the corpus size a flat JSON scan cannot serve (§4 / invariant #3). This round corrects the §5 opening paragraph, the ChangelogEntry convergence-table row, the 'other consequences today' block, and the convergence-B sequence bullet to describe the actual landed state. ARCHITECTURE.md is a forward-looking human-facing artifact (not a frozen atomic-store entry); its header rule 'code is the debt, update the doc' applies in reverse here — the code advanced past the doc, so the doc is corrected to match. Documentation correctness only; no code change.

Round 351.decision_summary: Fix two latent UTF-8 mid-codepoint panic defects in the validate-code-refs citation extractors (mnemosyne-validate/code_refs.rs), surfaced by an independent robustness review. Both used a hardcoded +1 byte advance at an offset that can sit on a multibyte char boundary: (1) extract_citations's word-boundary-reject branch did start = i + 1 — with a non-ASCII entry_id_prefix, i is at a multibyte boundary and the next line[start..] slice panics; (2) is_external_section_cite computed the last whitespace-delimited token via rfind(char::is_whitespace).map(|i| i + 1) in two places — char::is_whitespace matches multibyte Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+2028), so +1 lands mid-codepoint and the token slice panics. Both are the SAME bug class already fixed in the sibling extract_inventory_citations_with_tail (Round 279 Bug #1, char_indices-driven) but never propagated to these two functions. Fix (1) advances by the matched char's len_utf8; fix (2) routes both whitespace-split sites through one new last_whitespace_token_start helper that advances by len_utf8 — a single helper so the fix cannot be half-applied to one site and missed at the other, the very omission this round closes. Reachable only via non-default config (non-ASCII entry_id_prefix / configured external_section prefixes), so no default-path crash, but a general-purpose validator must not panic on adversarial source content. Code-only; no atomic store or GENERATED.md change; R279 audit anchor verified present.

Both had zero callers in production and tests — the strict variants delegate to get_mut directly, not to the bare accessors. Round 369 — strip_section_marker canonic.decision_summary: strip_section_marker canonical in mnemosyne-core — DRY 5 verbatim §-marker normalize sites (two private helpers + 3 inline copies), the R353/R357/R358 canonical-converter class
changes_bullets: Added `mnemosyne-core::strip_section_marker(&str) -> &str` — the canonical normalizer that strips a section id's optional leading `§` reference marker (`§43` -> `43`, bare ids pass through). The marker-strip operation and its `'§'` literal now live in one L0 place instead of being re-derived per call site.

Three crates had independently re-derived the identical idiom `s.strip_prefix('§').unwrap_or(s)`: `mnemosyne-mcp::strip_section` (23 callers) and `mnemosyne-cli::strip_section_prefix` (22 callers) were verbatim private helpers, plus inline copies in ops/query.rs, cli/main.rs arg-parse, and parser/lib.rs split_section_number. Two crates writing the same private helper is the canonical-converter DRY class of Round 353 / Round 357 / Round 358.
Deleted mcp's `strip_section` wrapper as pure redundancy — every one of its 23 callers was a `.to_string()` closure with no fn-pointer use — and routed them to the imported canonical via rename.

Kept cli's `strip_section_prefix` as a thin owned-`String` adapter that delegates to the canonical: it has genuine ergonomics an `&str`-returning fn lacks (its result is stored in arg structs and it is used as a `.map(strip_section_prefix)` fn pointer in four places). The strip logic is single-sourced; only the owned-return adaptation is local.
The 3 inline normalize sites (ops query, cli main arg-parse, parser split_section_number) now call the canonical directly.

Deliberately left untouched the 3 conditional-parse sites that branch on marker presence — parser:338 (`strip_prefix('§')?`), parser:577 (`if let Some` + `'§'.len_utf8()` byte advance), query:331 (`if let Some`): those test or extract conditioned on the marker, a different operation than normalize, and a `&str -> &str` helper cannot express the presence test. Also left the ~30 `format!("§{}")` display/error sites: prepending the sigil in human-facing strings is not the strip operation, and routing them through a const would harm readability for no behavior benefit.
verification_bullets: 5 new core unit tests for strip_section_marker: leading marker stripped, bare id passthrough, empty string, marker-only -> empty, doubled marker strips only the first.
696 workspace tests pass / 0 fail / 47 ignored (+5 vs the prior 691, all in core).
clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean.

Behavior byte-identical: the canonical body is the exact idiom it replaced, so GENERATED.md is unchanged and validate-workspace round-trip 1/1 + verify-generated stay green (T3 reject 0, GENERATED.md=sync).
carry_forward_bullets: `AtomicSection.normative_excerpt` is write-only today (CLI + MCP setter, zero read consumers) — deferred RFC-002 spec-citation substrate. A persisted schema field with a frozen-once-set invariant; NOT autonomously deletable (data-loss + frozen-ledger risk). Surfaced by the SSOT audit; flagged for user decision, not removed.

`mnemosyne-index` and `mnemosyne-server` remain built-but-unwired into the live cli/mcp path (convergence B index-materialization / D write-side txn service). Intentional convergence substrate per ARCHITECTURE.md §3; YAGNI re-justification candidates only if those stages stay deferred — never delete.

Extracted normative_excerpt validation into build_normative_excerpt, now shared by the post-create setter AND the inline-at-create path; manifest entries anchor the excerpt frozen-at-create (RFC-002 FR-1). Added a field-invariant parity test that feeds the same edge inputs through both write paths and asserts identical accept/reject verdicts.

import_sections runs a 3-way classification per entry: absent->create / byte-identical->no-op (idempotent re-run) / divergent->reject the WHOLE manifest. Atomicity is free via run_atomic_mutate: any reject returns Err before the single save, so the freshly-loaded store is discarded and the disk is untouched; an all-no-op manifest writes nothing (written_bytes 0). Manifest order = parents before children (a child resolves a parent inserted earlier in the same batch).

Round 375 — strip § sigil in import-sect.decision_summary: Fix import_sections leaking the § citation sigil into store keys (a §-form manifest rendered §§ double-sigil, silently): strip § in the shared build_candidate_section so add_section and import_sections normalize section_id + parent_section identically for every caller.
changes_bullets: build_candidate_section (the one shared section-create core) now strips a leading `§` citation sigil from section_id AND parent_section via mnemosyne_core::strip_section_marker (trim-strip-trim). add_section and import_sections both route through it, so a citation-form manifest entry (`"§scxml-1"`) stores the bare key `scxml-1` regardless of caller — symmetric with the CLI/MCP add_section paths that already stripped. Also fixes parent_section lookup for §-form manifests (now matches the bare stored keys).

The bug (SCE-found, R373 regression): import_sections' CLI handler did not strip §, unlike cmd_add_section, so a §-form manifest stored `§scxml-1` and generate-docs rendered `### §§scxml-1` (double sigil). validate-workspace round-trips fine (store internally self-consistent) so it was SILENT corruption. Fixing in the shared core (not just the CLI handler) closes the footgun for every caller — direct primitive, CLI, and any future MCP import tool.
Chose strip (lenient, accept §-or-bare) over reject-at-parse, to match add_section's established normalization behavior.

The add_section behavior change (now strips via the core) broke no existing test — full atomic suite 116 pass.

Round 377 — commit↔ledger gate multi-wor.decision_summary: commit↔ledger drift gate (R293/R301) assumed a single-workspace repo: it scanned repo-global commit subjects for (R<n>) labels and diffed against one workspace ledger, so in a multi-workspace mono-repo a sibling workspace round label false-flagged every workspace (SCE adoption report). Two-part fix, same class as R376 citation-namespace. D1: path-scope the git-log scan to the workspace subtree (git log -- .) so a sibling-only label no longer bleeds in. D2: [commit_ledger].severity (default reject, preserving the R301 dogfood hard-reject) lets a consumer workspace whose (R<n>) labels are not Mnemosyne changelog rounds downgrade to warn/info — the drift line still prints, the exit code is not gated. Round-namespace relabeling deferred YAGNI: the gate is a Mnemosyne self-development invariant that does not apply to a pure consumer ledger.

Round 383 — set-membership symbol bindin.decision_summary: RFC-002 FR-3 symbol enforcement under-represented the store. The validator indexed Implementation.symbol as section->file->symbol via an iterator .collect() into BTreeMap, so when a section recorded more than one symbol in the same file (which add_section_implementation explicitly allows — set semantics, only exact (file,symbol) dups rejected) the collect kept only the last, and a legitimate cite inside any earlier symbol falsely surfaced as SymbolMismatch. R383 makes the index set-valued (section->file->{symbols}); a cite is bound at symbol granularity iff its resolved enclosing symbol is a MEMBER of the registered set. Backward compatible (a set of one reproduces the prior single-symbol check). This is a correctness fix aligning the validator index with the store invariant, not a new capability.

Round 384 — Path B curation tooling (pro.decision_summary: Path B (code->section binding) adoption needs a curation path: an external consumer with thousands of existing citations cannot hand-author every section->file->symbol implementation entry. R384 adds propose-implementations, a read-only tool that scans the cited code, resolves each citations enclosing symbol via the language SymbolResolver, and emits the proposed implementation sets (plus ready-to-run add-section-implementation commands) for maintainer ratification — the review doubles as an audit of where each section is cited. Paired with it, the cpp resolver gains documented-symbol semantics: a section citation in source is conventionally a doc comment ABOVE the declaration it documents, but tree-sitters smallest-enclosing-node would bind it to the outer namespace/class; documented_symbol detects a comment that (with no intervening blank line) immediately precedes a declaration and binds to that declaration instead, falling through to enclosing scope for file-header/taxonomy comments. Both additive and read-only; no severity or scan behaviour changes.

Round 386 — complete [workspace] root: o.decision_summary: The [workspace] root override was only half-wired: repo_root() returned the RESOLVED root, then ops called discover_config(resolved_root), which walks UP and misses a subdir-located mnemosyne.toml — so a ledger rooted in a subdirectory (the SCE 3-workspace layout) silently fell back to the default sidecar, loading an empty store (section_missing 58). R386 completes it: ops take an anchor (the toml dir) and resolve the declared [workspace] root themselves via workspace_root_from; workspace-relative sidecar/output/doc/code paths join the declared root, while an explicit --sidecar/--output override short-circuits discovery and joins the anchor. Round 391 — North Star clarified: spec i.decision_summary: Clarifies the ARCHITECTURE North Star (section 1) so its model is not re-derived. A specification is one instance of a narrative (spec subset narrative), not a coordinate second pillar: spec-compliance is the tractable beachhead, a game-engine narrative manager is the encompassing target, and the North Star does not change as the medium widens. Facts are multi-axis: the actual/historical fact and each agent's understood fact are distinct facts on distinct axes, both true; frames are never cross-validated for agreement, and an actor's behaviour derives from its own frame. branch is therefore the epistemic-frame mechanism (coexisting perspectival truths, never merged), which is the deep reason the bitemporal/branch foundation is load-bearing, not speculative. Validation is frame-scoped: strict within a frame, cross-frame disagreement is data not a violation. Adds section 1.1 and tweaks the North Star blockquote to mark the subset relation. Doc-only; ARCHITECTURE is hand-maintained (not round-trip).

Round 403 — normative_excerpt becomes EP.decision_summary: Flip normative_excerpt.text from a frozen hand-authored value to a derived cache projected from the committed EPUB. The hand-authoring set_section_normative_excerpt (atomic fn + CLI verb + MCP tool) is deleted per no-legacy-carry, leaving import_epub_excerpts and import_sections-inline as the two write paths, both routing through one build_normative_excerpt validator pinned by a field-invariant parity test.

Round 405 — EPUB-file provenance: SpecSo.decision_summary: Close the EPUB-as-content-SSOT loop with the EPUB-file provenance anchor. SpecSource gains epub_path + epub_sha256 pinning the committed content-SSOT EPUB. validate-content-drift, when those are set, re-hashes the committed EPUB file offline and compares to the pin — a mismatch (the EPUB was swapped/updated) or a missing file is gated under [content_drift].severity alongside the per-excerpt cache scan. This is the more fundamental gate: if the EPUB file drifted, every excerpt is suspect even when each still matches its own now-stale hash. Round 406 — seal-excerpt-hashes: seal co.decision_summary: SCE's RFC reply showed that EPUB-as-content-SSOT is one model, not the only one: a consumer whose excerpt text is authored by its own extractor (SCE's direct-body scope is finer than the EPUB div granularity — 0/196 byte-identical, projecting EPUB text would collapse 196 precise excerpts into 167 heading-polluted overlapping blobs) treats its own text as SSOT, with the EPUB file pin as source provenance only. R403 deleted the hand-authoring setter assuming EPUB is the sole text source, leaving no way to fill text_sha256 from already-stored text (report-excerpt-hash-backfill reports only; import-epub-excerpts is EPUB-sourced). seal_excerpt_hashes fills the gap: for each excerpt with an empty text_sha256, set text_sha256 = sha256(text), sealing the authored text as its own revalidation baseline — never overwriting text and never re-sealing a populated hash (a wrong populated hash stays drift for validate-content-drift). This unblocks SCE's 196 excerpts without regression and generalizes the model: excerpt text may be EPUB-projected or consumer-authored, unified by the integrity hash and the EPUB-file provenance pin.

Never overwrites text or a populated hash; idempotent (a second run seals 0).

Round 407 — medium-forge heading-scope e.decision_summary: SCE adopted the full EPUB-as-content-SSOT model (committed EPUB = authoritative excerpt text), un-holding ask 2. medium-forge must extract at HEADING granularity, not container subtree: W3C SCXML section ids are finer than div1..div4 (Appendix D has ~15 h4 function sections under one div1), so container.text_content() collapsed 29 distinct ids onto one blob (0/196 byte-identical). New --text-scope {container,heading}: heading mode emits each section's direct body (heading to next heading, descendants excluded) with the heading text excluded (the body-only canonical rule — the heading already lives in AtomicSection.title), porting SCE's proven heading-to-next-heading extractor for cutover diff fidelity. Container-only sections emit the locator only (no text), so import-epub-excerpts skips them while import-epub-anchors keeps the pointer. An anchor-collapse guard signals distinct ids that resolve to identical text via needs_review + confidence 0.0 rather than emitting a duplicate sha. EPUB rendering is unchanged; no Rust or schema change (import-epub-excerpts already overwrites text+text_sha256 unconditionally). Resolves the gating dependency for SCE's full EPUB-SSOT cutover.

Round 409 — parent_doc canonical post-R4.decision_summary: SCE asked the canonical value of AtomicSection.parent_doc after R400 removed the render path. Investigation: parent_doc is a mandatory non-empty L0 SectionSkeleton field (medium-neutral; surfaced in query / facts / schema / cascade index; mutable via set_section_parent_doc) and is NOT validated against any file post-R400 (the file-path interpretation died with the markdown-doc parser and render). CANONICAL: parent_doc is a free-form LOGICAL owning-document / namespace label, not a filesystem path and not provenance (provenance lives in normative_excerpt.anchor_url + [workspace.spec_source]). Of SCE's three options: option 2 (clear/null) is structurally impossible (mandatory non-empty); option 1 (keep docs/GENERATED.md) is a harmless-but-stale render-era leftover, not canonical; option 3 (a meaningful logical doc id) is correct, with the caveat that the target is a grouping label, never a source URL. Re-binding is cosmetic (no functional consumer breaks) and safe (set_section_parent_doc is a dedicated mutable setter, not frozen-ledger). Aligned the dogfood's sections to the logical label mnemosyne-design so adopters can follow the canonical without diverging from upstream. parent_doc is not on a deprecation roadmap.

Round 430 — narrative fact entity: frame.decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round A (of the A/B/C decomposition ratified with R429): the narrative fact entity lands. NarrativeFact = a claim held in exactly one epistemic frame over a canon-time extent in structure-section coordinates, with mandatory evidence provenance, recorded conflict assertion edges, and in-frame succession for time-indexed belief change — the storage half of the North Star sentence that frames are sparse non-privileged axes (a believed-fact and the ground-truth fact are distinct facts, both true, never cross-validated; absence in a frame = unrecorded, not false). Frame mechanism per the design round: frames-as-data at the SSOT log layer (a registry + an axis field), no inheritance or overlay (the multi-axis model leaves nothing to overlay); branch-KV remains the read-side projection realization when scale materializes the index. Canon closure is DERIVED: a superseded belief's effective end comes from its successor's canon_from, never written back (append-only, frozen-ledger genre). Both write paths route one shared builder (R305 parity); quote hashes are computed at write so a stored hash can never start out wrong (R404). Schema v11 to v12 is a declarative default — all four consumer stores load unchanged. Proven against the real corpus: the 27-chapter Dracula PoC store took 4 frames + 10 hand-extracted facts (3 cross-frame conflict clusters, 2 in-frame belief changes) in one atomic transaction with forward succession refs, idempotent on re-run. Round B (continuity gate) and Round C (frame-at-T projection) follow.

Round 431 — continuity gate: frame-scope.decision_summary: Phase 1A build Round B: the continuity gate lands — the validation half of the North Star sentence whose storage half was R430. scan_continuity evaluates the RECORDED conflict assertion edges frame-scoped: a same-frame pair whose DERIVED canon extents co-hold at any point is a violation; a cross-frame pair is data, counted and never gated. Effective extents are derived at scan exactly as designed (stored canon_to, cut by any in-frame successor's canon_from — nothing written back); a stored end that outlives its successor's start is itself flagged. Canon order obeys guardrail B-1: it is a DECLARED partial order (canon-order/v1 edge JSON, consumer/medium-adapter generated, cycles reject, optional sha256 pin per the R428 authority-input rule) — section-id spelling is never consulted, non-comparable pairs surface as a count and never gate, and equality needs no declaration so the gate already catches same-coordinate contradictions with no order file. Guardrail B-2 is structural: conflict scoping lives in one same_scope predicate that widens to frame-x-branch when the world-line axis lands. Opt-in via the [continuity] table (severity default reject, the content-drift rationale: a same-frame simultaneous contradiction is wrong data, never a legitimate intermediate state). Proven on the real corpus: the Dracula store's 4 recorded conflict pairs are all cross-frame = 0 violations under reject (the multi-axis thesis executing), and a fabricated same-frame overlap was caught at its exact canon point with exit 1. Round C (frame-at-T projection) remains.

Round 433 — world-line branch axis: (fra.decision_summary: AI-authoring greenlit as the live consumer; the sec 7.10 build order executes, pull 1 of 3: the world-line branch axis (sec 7.9 axis 2) lands. A branch is which-world, a frame is who-believes - the four-axis decomposition holds and the two never conflate; per-branch ground truth is the (branch, frame) composite. NarrativeFact gains an additive branch field (serde default main, the default never serializes, so every pre-branch store round-trips byte-identical; schema v12->v13, declarative default, no migration arm). Guardrail B-2 executes exactly as written at R431: same_scope widens frame -> (frame, branch) as a key-widening, not a rewrite - same-frame facts on different world-lines never conflict (cross-branch pairs are data, like cross-frame pairs), and in-frame succession never crosses a branch (world-line divergence is data, not succession; enforced at the write path and re-checked by the scan). Canon order goes branch-relative (B-1 carried): canon-order/v1 gains an optional branches map of per-world-line edge sets, each composed with the shared base - the same quest node can legitimately order differently on two branches, which a single global DAG cannot express (it would be a cycle). frame_view scopes to one world-line (--branch, default main) behind a derived fail-loud unknown-branch boundary (no registry: known = main, fact-carried, or order-declared; a typo'd branch must not read as an empty world).

Round 434 — authorial retract/amend: axi.decision_summary: Pull 2 of the sec 7.10 build order: the authorial correction path lands. The four-axis decomposition (sec 7.9) separates in-world belief change (axis 1/3: in-frame supersession, predecessor stays in the log) from author-time correction (axis 4: the claim itself was mis-written and must stop existing or change in place). Before this round a typo was permanent - any revision of a written fact divergent-rejected with NO alternative path, and the reject message actively gave WRONG advice (recommending in-frame supersession, which fabricates an in-world belief change out of an authorial slip). Two primitives close the gap: retract_fact (remove an unreferenced fact; inbound conflict edges / succession pointers block it fail-loud with the referrer list, so scan invariants never see a dangling target; mandatory reason, the remove_section audit-safeguard precedent; no tombstone - transaction time is the git history of the log per R330) and amend_fact (in-place revision keeping the id, routed through the SAME shared builder as add_fact/import_facts per the R305 parity rule, with inbound successors required to stay same-(frame, branch) so succession scope cannot be corrupted). The divergent-reject messages now advise both paths by name.

Round 438 — branch fork-point: shared-hi.decision_summary: The R433 branch axis shipped scoping without divergence semantics - the design's own justification for branch != frame was copy-on-write shared history, yet a branch view was as sparse as a frame: a story forking at chapter 30 lost chapters 1-29 on the branch view, the gate under-detected contradictions against inherited facts, and the module-doc claim that the log carries everything the index needs was false without a fork datum. This round closes that tension the way the four-axis decomposition wants it closed: Branch.forks_from records WHERE a world-line diverged (forest by construction - parents must pre-exist, forks are immutable), visibility becomes a three-state world-membership judgment (inherited-In / definitively-Out / order-cannot-decide-Unknown, surfaced never gated), holds_at evaluates in the QUERY world with successor visibility filtering (a fork's revision of an inherited belief is in-world change that never leaks back into the ancestor's view), conflicts evaluate in the pair's JOIN world (siblings share no world = data), succession may point along the lineage, and a branch's composed canon order inherits every ancestor's declared edges. forks_from = None preserves the standalone-world semantics exactly - every pre-fork store and test gates identically. For the pinion AI-first runtime this is the primitive that makes playthrough-as-branch and route-divergence authoring representable.
changes_bullets: Branch.forks_from{branch, at} (mnemosyne-core BranchFork), schema v15->v16; None = standalone world (R433 semantics preserved exactly); parent must pre-exist + fork immutable after registration = ancestry is a forest BY CONSTRUCTION, no cycle writable; build_branch_fork = the one fork-invariant place shared by add_branch and the manifest path

world visibility (3-state, B-1 honest): a fact on an ancestor branch is In iff canon_from <= that lineage's departure point, Out when comparable-and-after, Unknown when the declared order cannot decide (surfaced, never gated); holds_at is now world-relative and a successor ends a predecessor ONLY where the successor itself is visible - a fork's revision never leaks back into the ancestor's view

conflict scoping generalizes to the JOIN world: same frame + one branch on the other's lineage = evaluated in the deeper world (violation names it); siblings/unrelated = cross-scope data; succession may point along the lineage (write path + scan agree) - revising an inherited belief is in-world change

per-branch order composes the full ancestry: branch reach = closure(base + every ancestor's declared edges + own), cycle-checked per composition; load_canon_order now returns the FILE and construction happens post-store-load (ops compose_canon_order, single path for CLI/MCP)
CLI add-branch --forks-from/--forks-at + MCP add_branch fork args; lineage_of/fork_ancestry hop-capped fail-loud against out-of-band cyclic edits
verification_bullets: new semantics tests: fork inherits pre-fork facts but not later main facts (and main view unaffected), conflict with an inherited fact gates in the join world while sibling forks stay data, lineage succession revises without leak-back (route sees f-new, main still sees f-old), undecidable fork comparison surfaces as unknown, grandchild inherits ancestor branch order (deep gets route's edges, main does not)

atomic write-path tests: fork parent must pre-exist / no self-fork / fork point must be a section / immutable after registration (divergent reject) / lineage succession accepted while standalone-branch succession still rejects
ALL pre-fork tests pass unchanged - standalone-world semantics byte-preserved; full workspace suite green (773 tests, 0 failed), clippy clean, fmt clean

playthrough-as-branch (pinion save slots) is now representable; runtime read scale stays flat-scan until convergence-B pulls

gate conservatism note: an Unknown-visibility successor does not cut its predecessor (false-negative direction, consistent with B-1 unordered-never-gated); revisit only if a consumer shows a real miss

Round 439 — conflict-edge claim pins: st.decision_summary: A conflict edge is a recorded SEMANTIC judgment about claim content (sec 7.4) - but R434's amend could change the judged text out from under the judgment, leaving the gate evaluating an assertion about words that no longer exist. This round applies the codebase's own drift discipline (R404 content pins, R420 drift->Stale) to the judgment layer: every ConflictAssertion pins the target's claim sha256 at judgment time, computed by the primitives and never caller-supplied; the scan compares pins against current claims and surfaces ConflictEdgeStale demanding re-affirmation. The re-affirmation path is the amend itself - amending a fact restamps its OUTBOUND judgments (the amender freshly asserts its own edges) while INBOUND judgments go stale, which is exactly the asymmetry the axis-4 model wants: you can re-state what you believe, you cannot silently keep others' statements about your old text. Clean break v16->v17 with no compat shim (pre-release; no committed store carries an edge; the old shape fails loud). Succession deliberately stays unpinned: it relates fact identities, not wordings.
changes_bullets: NarrativeFact.conflicts_with: bare target ids -> ConflictAssertion{target, target_claim_sha256} (mnemosyne-core), schema v16->v17 - CLEAN BREAK, no compat shim (pre-release rule; no committed consumer store carries an edge; an old-shape store fails to load LOUDLY rather than silently dropping the pin)

the pin is computed by the primitives, never caller-supplied (R404): validate_fact_refs becomes validate_and_stamp_fact_refs (the one shared pass - add_fact / import_facts post-staging snapshot / amend_fact all route it); add_fact_conflict stamps from the target's current claim; FactImport keeps bare ids (the authoring face is unchanged)
amend semantics: amending a fact RESTAMPS its outbound judgments (the amender freshly asserts its own edges); inbound judgments pointing AT the amended fact go stale instead - never auto-refreshed

Round 440 — hardening: one fork walk, to.decision_summary: The second session review held R433-R439 to the lifetime-project standard and found five defects; this round pays all of them plus one live bug the fix surfaced. The deep one was a fail-loud asymmetry: the scan re-checked conflict/succession targets against out-of-band edits while trusting frame/branch/entity registry membership and section refs entirely to the write path - and the lineage lookup PANICKED on an unregistered fact branch instead of erroring. The shared gate/view boundary now re-checks the store's full referential closure (an Err, because a store that fails it is corrupt and the semantics are not evaluable - distinct from missing conflict targets, which remain evaluable data findings), making every downstream lineage lookup total by invariant. Round 441 — typed-claim/rule-gate design.decision_summary: The recorded design round R437 deferred (do-not-improvise carry honored). The typed leg: NarrativeFact gains an OPTIONAL authored TypedClaim{subject: entity-id, predicate: registered-id, object: Entity(entity-id)|Value(scalar)} beside the required prose claim - B-1 applied to typing (declared at write time in the same act as the prose, never NLP-inferred), binary predicates only, subject and entity-object must be registered AND members of the fact's entities list (the retrieval key is never silently widened). Partial coverage IS the design: probed on the 10 real Dracula claims, 3 type cleanly, 5 are compound prose where typing forces the per-claim split the prose tolerated, 2 are negative-epistemic and stay prose-only (open-world: absence = unrecorded, never false) - the deterministic gate covers the typed subset while recorded edges and the future LLM-discovery adapter cover the rest, three conflict sources one gate. Predicates are load-bearing refs (rules key off them; a typo'd predicate silently escapes its rule - the R436 write-side-typo lesson), so they become the 4th fail-loud registry carrying object_kind entity|scalar for builder shape-checking; per the R440 carry, build Round A performs the registry dedup in the same change that adds the 4th. Rules are consumer vocabulary and never enter L0: a narrative-rules/v1 declared artifact (the canon-order/R428 authority-input pattern, optional sha256 pin) with exactly TWO classes covering the named trio - exclusive{predicate, per: subject|object} (location exclusivity per subject, conservation/custody per object; same-value co-holding duplicates are consistent, not gated) and transition{predicate, allowed} riding the in-frame succession edge (succession IS the declared adjacency - adjacency over a partial canon order is ill-defined; unchained same-subject/predicate visible pairs are surfaced as a WORLD-scoped count, never gated). Evaluation lands inside scan_continuity as new violation variants and MUST reuse WorldCtx::holds_at verbatim as its third reader - the probe's binding finding: a paper interval model with an inclusive successor boundary produced 4 false positives on correctly chained real arcs; the half-open successor cut is load-bearing. Frame x branch scoping carries unchanged (cross-frame and fork-world pairs proved inert on real data), succession chains become structurally rewarded (a forgotten chain is now a caught overlap), and rule findings are derivations re-evaluated each scan - no staleness, no pins (judgments keep their R439 pins). Opt-in = authoring the rules file; violations ride the existing continuity severity knob. Design only: no schema or production code this round; build = Round A then Round B, consumer-pulled.

Round 442 — setup/payoff coverage: Chekh.decision_summary: The AAA-map item carried a name and no definition; this round derived one from two existing patterns and pinned it: narrative craft's setup/payoff discipline (an introduced device must be used) expressed in this codebase's coverage vocabulary (R389/R390 - a declared expectation plus a read-only 3-way classification), probed on real Dracula arcs BEFORE building. A fact opts in as a setup via payoff_expectation=expected (default unmarked - absence is unrecorded, never an assertion, the sparse-frame ethos on the discourse axis; the default never serializes so pre-payoff stores stay byte-stable); a later fact resolves it via pays_off backward identity edges, the supersedes_in_frame pointer shape - the setup is written first and never touched when paid, append-only by genre. Edges are deliberately UNPINNED (the R439 content pin covers judgments about claim text; succession and payoff relate fact identities, not wordings) and cross FRAMES freely (a discourse-structure relation, not an epistemic judgment - Renfield's zoophagy is set up in seward's frame and paid off in ground truth) but never credit across worlds. The report classifies per query world over the shared visibility semantics: paid / dangling / exempt plus three honesty surfaces (payoffs_to_unmarked = forgotten marking, payoff_before_setup = mystery structure surfaced never gated, unknown = B-1 undecidable). The probe's central finding drove the scoping: an inherited setup DANGLES on a fork until that world-line itself pays it - main's post-fork payoff is invisible there, so forking early surfaces all the narrative debt the new world inherits; each playthrough resolves its own guns. Dangling is deliberately never gated - a WIP story has dangling setups by definition; the dangling list IS the author's todo list, and a release-time no-dangling gate stays consumer-pull. Write-side invariants ride the one shared builder path (R305): tag parse, no self/blank/duplicate refs, fail-loud targets, inbound pays_off blocks retraction; the scan re-checks out-of-band edits as PayoffTargetMissing, an evaluable finding rather than a corruption Err per the R440 boundary doctrine.

Round 443 — session review of R441-R442:.decision_summary: The R436/R440 cadence applied to the two newest rounds: hold R441 (typed-claim/rule-gate design) and R442 (setup/payoff coverage) to the lifetime-project standard before anything builds on them. Three findings, all repaid in-session. The real one is in the R441 probe: the exclusive rule's consistency skip ('a restated fact is not a violation') was implemented one-sided - it skipped equal OBJECTS under per:subject but never skipped equal SUBJECTS under per:object, so a restated custody fact (the same holder stated twice) would false-positive as a two-holder conservation violation. The principle is now pinned symmetric - the skip applies to the NON-KEYED leg, both directions - in the probe and in design sec 7.12, so build round B inherits the rule, not the bug. Round 447 — payoff dead-edge masking fix.decision_summary: The R445 Detroit slice's Finding 3 closed: the R443 uncredited_edges surface withdrew an edge from the global dead-edge pool whenever ANY world saw EITHER endpoint as Unknown - and since parallel protagonist chains make every cross-chain fact Unknown in the other protagonist's forks, the surface went structurally silent on exactly the corpus shape that ratified it (R445 falsified this live: the genuinely dead F-K13 -> F-K05 edge was masked under the parallel-chains order and surfaced only under a discourse interleave). The fix scopes the withdrawal to worlds where the edge COULD credit: both endpoints In or Unknown with at least one Unknown - a world where either endpoint is Out is decided (the edge cannot credit there) and exempts nothing. Edges that credit nowhere but met a genuine could-credit undecidable world now surface as a new undecidable_edges report field instead of silently draining (the no-silent-caps rule: silent withdrawal reads as 'no dead edges' when it means 'could not decide'), and they are deliberately never listed as definitively dead (B-1 honesty both directions). Verified on the live Detroit store: the parallel-chains order and the discourse-interleave order now agree on the dead edge - the order declaration choice (R445 Finding 5) no longer changes whether a dead edge is visible, only how much becomes undecidable.

Round 450 — session review of R449: padd.decision_summary: The R436/R440/R443/R448 cadence applied to the rules-gate build before anything stacks on it. One real finding, falsified live before fixing: load_narrative_rules validated shape with trimmed compares and the scan boundary checked the predicate registry with .trim(), but the evaluation filtered typed facts by EXACT predicate equality — so a whitespace-padded predicate in a declared rules file passed every check and matched nothing, silently disarming the rule it declared. That is the precise silent-escape class the fail-loud predicate boundary exists to prevent (the R436 write-side-typo lesson), reproduced against the Detroit store: the padded strict vocabulary reported rules=1 violations=0 where unpadded fires 2. The fix follows the one-invariant-one-place doctrine: whitespace normalizes INTO the stored values at load (rule id, predicate, transition legs), and the scan boundary now compares EXACT so the two readers of a rule's predicate (registry check, fact filter) can never again disagree about what the rule names; a padded programmatic rule that bypassed the loader fails loud naming the padded string. Re-verified end-to-end over live MCP stdio in the same window (the R448 verification-gap lesson): the config rules_path path fires, and an override pointing at a padded declaration also fires post-normalization. Second finding: the per-world reporting contract for exclusive violations existed only in prose - now pinned by a test asserting a violating main pair inherited by a fork reports in BOTH worlds, main first (the world is part of the finding; the R441 probe's executable model). Architectural sweep found nothing else to repay: the per-world scaffolding duplication between the exclusive and unchained halves diverges in its inner logic (abstraction would be speculative), and two lenient-parse behaviors are recorded as observations rather than changed — a typo'd top-level key parses to zero rules but the count is surfaced never silent, and per-rule unchained dedup double-counts only when two transition rules name one predicate (probe-verbatim, frozen semantics).

Round 451 — Intercept converter spike: i.decision_summary: R444 build order step 3 executed: a scratch converter maps inkle's The Intercept (MIT, 30 narrative knots) onto the declared-artifact contract — section-manifest (beats) + canon-order/v1 (knot-level divert edges) — and the whole R449 stack consumes the generated artifacts UNMODIFIED through the real primitives: import-sections, import-facts (a typed custody arc + the interrogation pair), validate-continuity with rules. Inventing an order would have been the B-1 violation; instead converter honesty propagated through to gate honesty on real data. (4) The Intercept's reconvergent flag-carried variation maps to ONE world with zero branch registrations — R445 Finding 4 (carried flags are typed state, not world divergence) confirmed from the opposite direction, a choice-driven medium landing on one world + a DAG order. Negative control: stripping the custody succession fires rule_exclusive_overlap at a converted beat. Branch emission and flag-to-typed-fact extraction were deliberately not exercised; productizing the converter is consumer-pull with the SCE-A1 separate-repo precedent. No production code this round.

Round 452 — session review of R449-R451:.decision_summary: The owner restated the standing standard (textbook structure over cost, lifetime-project bar, North-Star and SSOT fidelity) and the R436-cadence review ran against the R449-R451 window. Verdict first: the architectural spine held — the rules gate is a derivation layer over the one holds_at with no second interval algebra, rule vocabulary never entered L0, the store stayed the single directly-validated SSOT (every entry through the real primitive, every scratch store gitignored), and no finding touches the North-Star axes. Three findings, all repaid in-round. The substantive one: unchained_state_pairs used the probe's direct-edge check, so a CORRECTLY chained 4-step arc permanently reported its 3 transitive pairs as unchained — an honesty surface that emits false signals on correct data is itself dishonest, and R449 had recorded this as a noise-gated revisit trigger; the owner's standard fired it on principle. Falsified live, then fixed by the R443 amendment pattern: design sec 7.12 now pins unchained = no succession PATH between the pair, succession_ancestors walks the single backward pointer chain (cycle-guarded, out-of-band-edit safe), an untyped middle fact still connects its typed endpoints (partial coverage covers the hops; the pair is chained), and the R441 probe carries the same semantics (all probes pass, real arcs at 0). The genuinely-unchained signal survives intact: the Detroit broken-chain probe still surfaces both the overlap violation and the now-truly-unchained pair. Finding 2: the per-world same-frame visible-pair sweep existed twice inside the rule loop — extracted as for_each_world_pair the moment the copy count hit two (the R440 rule), and the two coexisting scoping models are now pinned in prose: recorded edges evaluate per edge in the join world, derived findings sweep per query world, one holds-semantics under both. Finding 3: the two [continuity] pin/path validations were copy-paste twins — check_authority_pin_pair, messages preserved verbatim. Assessed and deliberately left: typed_object_key stays local with its promotion trigger; the ops envelope mirror is the R435 pattern; per-world co-hold cost is scale-gated (measure first). One inherited observation recorded for a future round: committed code cites the gitignored design doc — the store entries carry the decision substance, so the audit trail is self-contained either way.

Round 454 — T1-B Detroit visualization s.decision_summary: T1-B (design doc sec 10) answered its empirical question — does the picture yield insight the JSON rows do not — YES, four concrete instances on the Detroit slice, with zero substrate change. A one-shot gitignored generator renders existing report verbs only: report-frame-view sampled per (world, frame, node) so the holds-decision is the verb's at every cell, report-payoff-coverage for the fork-tree badges; the viz computes NO interval algebra of its own — extents are runs of sampled nodes and divergence windows are nodes where both ends of a recorded conflict edge hold, i.e. the projection-is-the-interface principle executed literally with the gate's own semantics. Friction recorded as promotion triggers, not repairs: an irony-interval verb should carry world and node-span explicitly, and the R453 violation-record asymmetry (transition has no branch field) was met again from the consumer side. Round 455 — dramatic-irony intervals: Ti.decision_summary: The first Tier-2 promotion fired on the T1-B pull (R454: the window-extent insight was the spike's strongest picture-over-rows instance, and its client-side sweep already prototyped the derivation; the owner's no-silent-fail-scripting ruling made absorbing the Python layer the same change). A literary concept becomes a deterministic derivation with nothing inferred: the irony marker is the AUTHORED cross-frame conflict edge (B-1 — same-frame edges are the gate's territory, counted and skipped), and the window is the node SET of a query world where the one holds-semantics says both ends are simultaneously in effect — WorldCtx::holds_at VERBATIM as its 4th reader (gate, frame view, rules gate, irony report; the R441 no-own-interval-algebra finding carries), node universe = store sections (the gate's co-hold idiom). Scoping is the derived-finding model of the R452 pin, necessarily: a cross-frame edge has no join world by construction, so the report sweeps every query world and a window inherited by a fork reports in both worlds (the R450 contract). The window is deliberately a node set plus starts (minimal co-hold nodes) and an open flag (the set contains a maximal node of the world's declared composed order — the R454 'belief never closes' headline as a first-class signal), never a (from,to) span: under a partial order the co-hold region need not be contiguous and a span would lie. Honesty surfaces: per-world windowless (both endpoints visible, never co-holding — a belief corrected before the truth lands is data, not absence) and undecidable (an Unknown endpoint, B-1, never classified); store-wide cross-frame/same-frame totals (no silent caps); an Out endpoint makes the edge another world's business. Never gated — irony is craft signal, not defect (the dashboards-never-gate principle), so no severity knob exists. Dogfooded live on Detroit: the spike's exact window reproduced (F-H04 concealed gun vs F-H05 'Connor is unarmed', opens at det-h-negotiation, OPEN at world-line end, inherited into both gun-fork outcome worlds — Daniel dies still holding the false belief), and the two order declarations agree on start and openness while the interleaved one honestly widens the node set with now-comparable cross-chapter beats (the R445 comparability-vs-occurrence wrinkle, now visible in a report). The spike's generate.py is deleted in the same change (no-legacy-carry; the HTML stays as frozen evidence).

Scoping is the derived-finding model of the R452 pin, necessarily: a cross-frame edge has no join world by construction, so the report sweeps every query world and a window inherited by a fork reports in both worlds (the R450 contract). The window is deliberately a node set plus starts (minimal co-hold nodes) and an open flag (the set contains a maximal node of the world's declared composed order — the R454 'belief never closes' headline as a first-class signal), never a (from,to) span: under a partial order the co-hold region need not be contiguous and a span would lie. Honesty surfaces: per-world windowless (both endpoints visible, never co-holding — a belief corrected before the truth lands is data, not absence) and undecidable (an Unknown endpoint, B-1, never classified); store-wide cross-frame/same-frame totals (no silent caps); an Out endpoint makes the edge another world's business. Never gated — irony is craft signal, not defect (the dashboards-never-gate principle), so no severity knob exists. Dogfooded live on Detroit: the spike's exact window reproduced (F-H04 concealed gun vs F-H05 'Connor is unarmed', opens at det-h-negotiation, OPEN at world-line end, inherited into both gun-fork outcome worlds — Daniel dies still holding the false belief), and the two order declarations agree on start and openness while the interleaved one honestly widens the node set with now-comparable cross-chapter beats (the R445 comparability-vs-occurrence wrinkle, now visible in a report). The spike's generate.py is deleted in the same change (no-legacy-carry; the HTML stays as frozen evidence).

Round 456 — session review of R453-R455:.decision_summary: The R436-cadence adversarial review ran against the R453-R455 window under the owner's restated standard (textbook structure over cost, lifetime-project bar, North-Star and SSOT fidelity). Verdict first: the spine held — the irony verb is a pure derivation over the one holds_at with no second interval algebra, it reads across frames but JUDGES nothing (no violation class, no severity knob: frames stay never-cross-validated, the perspectival axiom intact under a verb whose entire subject is cross-frame divergence), the store remained the single directly-validated SSOT (R455 entry substance self-contained, trap-corpus sha256 pin committed inside the R453 entry while the artifacts stay gitignored), and the trap corpus measured the system rather than bending it. Four findings, all repaid in-round. The substantive one: the R455 windowless verdict conflated two different honesty states — a pair whose starts the declared order CANNOT COMPARE was labeled windowless, asserting -the belief never overlaps the truth- where the truthful claim is -the declaration cannot order them- (under a richer declaration the same pair may be a window; the gate already encodes exactly this distinction as unordered_pairs, so the report diverged from the codebase's own idiom). Pre-fix evidence is pinned in the round itself: the R455 undecidable-fork test asserted windowless=1 on a parallel-chain pair and passed. Fixed by mirroring the gate: per-world unordered edge list, windowless now requires comparable starts. Finding 2: the WorldCtx::holds_at successors input was hand-rolled identically at three sites (scan, frame view, irony) — the R440/R452 two-copy rule fired at three; successors_index is the one builder. Finding 3: irony_intervals read CanonOrder's private reach representation to decide world-line ends — the judgment moved onto the order type as is_maximal(branch, node) with a new test pinning that isolated sections (in the store, outside the declaration) are never maximal. Finding 4: the CLI report verbs carried byte-identical flag parsing — parse_narrative_report_args extracted at the second copy. Assessed and deliberately left, recorded with reasons: the per-world lineage scaffolding across the three readers (R450 verdict carries — inner logic diverges), the gate-vs-report conflict-pair collection (shared idiom, divergent side effects — not a sweep), and the R453 branch-field asymmetry (still no consumer friction). 819 tests, Detroit live unchanged, MCP stdio re-verified with the four-way per-world shape.

Round 457 — LLM typing discovery design:.decision_summary: The owner opened the LLM-discovery gate and the design round ran R441-style (design only, build frozen, consumer-pulled). Scope refinement first: sec 7.10 gap 5 named conflict-discovery, but the R453 trap corpus quantified the real gap as TYPING - the deterministic layer misses untyped prose faults 2/2 and catches their typed twins 5/5, and typing alone is measurably sufficient (a typed double-custody gates immediately via exclusive; a typed resurrection surfaces via unchained) - so v1 is typing discovery: proposed typed legs for EXISTING untyped facts, nothing else. The B-1 crux is a reconciliation, not an exception: R441 pinned -typed legs are declared at write time, never NLP-inferred-, and discovery honors it by relocating inference OUTSIDE the store - the LLM's output is quarantined in a reviewable sha256-pinnable typing-proposals/v1 artifact, a typed leg enters only through the declared amend path where the authored act IS the review plus import, and the amend reason records provenance; -never NLP-inferred- precisely means -never SILENTLY NLP-inferred-. This is the R428 authority-input pattern's third instance (after canon-order and narrative-rules), and the substrate gains zero LLM clients: any agent session (Claude today, pinion later) reads report-typing-candidates (the one-call input package: untyped facts + claim sha256s + registered predicate/entity vocabulary - AI-first context economy, unregistered vocabulary never proposable), writes the proposals file, runs import-typing-proposals. Safety rails pinned: the R439 judgment-time content pin re-targeted (each proposal stamps the claim text it interpreted; import re-checks, so a fact amended after proposing fails loud as stale instead of silently mis-typing revised prose); all-or-nothing import with full per-proposal verdicts and --dry-run (the file is the reviewed artifact - make it fully valid, no half-applied state); every typed invariant rides the ONE R305/R446 builder site so the import path adds zero new invariant sites; fill-blanks only; no confidence scores (the reviewable substance is the rationale, not a number the model can inflate). The acceptance benchmark is pinned BEFORE build, falsifiable: the R453 trap table gains a -with discovery- column (blinded agent, V7/V8, expected MISS-to-gated and MISS-to-surfaced respectively) plus Detroit dogfood over its 11 untyped facts with the R441 partial-coverage expectation carried (compound and negative-epistemic claims STAY prose - the design, not a failure). Build = Round A (candidates report) then Round B (loader + import, CLI/MCP), consumer-pulled.

Round 458 — typing discovery Round A: re.decision_summary: Build Round A of the R457 frozen design, no drift: report-typing-candidates packages the typing-discovery input as ONE deterministic call — every untyped fact (id-sorted) carrying its claim text, the claim_sha256 the eventual proposal must stamp (the R439 judgment-time pin, import will re-check it so a fact amended after proposing fails loud as stale), frame/branch/canon_from, and its entities list, PLUS the predicate registry (the 4th registry verbatim — the ONLY vocabulary a proposal may name) and the entity registry (typed subjects/entity-objects must be registered AND members of the fact's entities list, R446). AI-first context economy is the point: the proposer (an LLM agent outside the substrate — the substrate gains no LLM client) never assembles its own context from N queries and never sees unregistered vocabulary as proposable. Order-independence is part of the contract: typing is a property of the fact, not of any canon declaration, so the verb takes no --order flag (accepting an ignored flag would be a silent lie) and the store boundary runs under the empty order — declaration-side checks vacuous, fact-side out-of-band re-checks still apply (the R440 doctrine). The R439 pin encoding (claim_sha256_hex) was inline in the gate's stale-edge check; the report became the second site and the two-copy rule extracted the one builder. Surface: CLI report-typing-candidates --json/--sidecar, MCP report_typing_candidates (52 tools) whose description carries the proposal contract. Dogfooded live on Detroit: exactly the 11 inventoried untyped facts surface with the 4-predicate/10-entity vocabulary riding. Round B (typing-proposals/v1 loader + all-or-nothing import) next, design frozen.

The typing-proposals/v1 artifact landed as designed: deny_unknown_fields types (a NEW artifact carries no lenient-parse legacy - a typo'd key fails loud instead of silently dropping a proposal field), a loader that fail-louds on schema tag and empty list and returns the file-content sha256 as the audit anchor, and import_typing_proposals - ALL-OR-NOTHING with full per-proposal verdicts and a dry-run twin that validates identically and writes nothing. Every reject class carries its own named verdict: duplicate-in-file, missing fact, already-typed target (fill-blanks only - overwrite is manual author territory), STALE claim sha (the R439 judgment-time pin re-targeted: a fact amended after proposing rejects loud instead of silently mis-typing revised prose), empty rationale (the reviewable substance is mandatory), and every typed-claim invariant via build_typed_claim - the ONE R305/R446 builder site, so the import path added zero new invariant logic by construction. Round 460 — session review of R457-R459:.decision_summary: The R436-cadence adversarial review ran against the typing-discovery window (R457 design, R458 candidates, R459 import + blind acceptance) under the owner's restated standard. Verdict first: the architectural spine held — B-1 survived its hardest test yet (an NLP-inference feature built WITHOUT the store ever ingesting un-reviewed inference: quarantined artifact, declared import, fill-blanks only), the typed invariants stayed in the one R305/R446 builder, the blind acceptance protocol measured the system rather than flattering it, and no finding touches the North-Star axes. Four findings, all repaid in-round. The substantive one: the lowercase-hex sha256 encoding existed in SIX hand-rolled implementations across four crates — including both ends of the cross-crate claim pin, stamped by report-typing-candidates in mnemosyne-validate and re-checked by import_typing_proposals in mnemosyne-atomic; an encoding change on either side would have mass-staled every proposal silently, the half-enforced-invariant class operating across crate boundaries. Consolidated to ONE mnemosyne_core::sha256_hex (with the encoding pinned by its own test: 64 lowercase hex, deterministic), converting schema's production-unused pub fn (deleted with its test), atomic's private fn plus publishable/audit hash_hex, cli's EPUB re-hash, validate's claim pin + authority-pin + catalog + confirmation hash_file, and two test-local copies; unused sha2 deps dropped from three crates; project.rs's u64 key derivation keeps direct sha2 deliberately (different encoding family). Finding 2: R459's MCP import handler hand-rolled a SECOND mutate-lock acquisition beside run_mutate — extracted with_mutate_lock so receipt-shaped and verdict-report-shaped mutates share THE one acquisition site (two lock sites are how two mutate paths drift). Finding 3, the process one: the R459 build deviated from the frozen design's apply-via-amend-acts prose for good reasons (amend restamps outbound judgment edges — the amender's-fresh-assertion semantics, wrong for a mechanical typing fill; amend reasons are validated but never persisted, the R434 transaction-time-audit model) — but the deviation went unrecorded at build time; sec 7.15 now carries the declared as-built correction, and the lesson is pinned: frozen-design deviations are recorded in the deviating round, not discovered by the next review. Finding 4: sec 7.15's V7 acceptance expectation was stale after R459 exceeded it; amended with the result. One stale doc block from the R403 deletion also fell. 824 tests, clippy clean, cross-crate pin parity verified live post-consolidation, MCP stdio re-verified through the single lock entry.

Round 461 — LLM edge discovery design: t.decision_summary: The owner pulled edge discovery v2 and the design round ran R457-style against the CORRECTED value map: R459's blind run falsified the design-time claim that a succession proposal upgrades the V7 co-hold class (alive-excl gates it with no edge when the dead state is unbounded), so v2 targets exactly three remaining classes - (1) bounded disallowed step: an explicit canon_to predecessor never co-holds (exclusive blind) and carries no succession edge (transition blind), today a gate-level miss surfaced only as the unchained count, flipped to rule_transition_invalid GATED by a proposed succession edge; (2) the V3 stripped-chain-link class, repaired back to unchained 0 / scan green; (3) sec 7.10 gap-5 conflict discovery over the R459 stays-prose residue (compound and negative-epistemic claims the registered vocabulary cannot type), flipped from no-channel to FrameConflictOverlap GATED via a proposed conflict edge. Architecture carries verbatim from sec 7.15: quarantined reviewable artifact (edge-proposals/v1), declared all-or-nothing import with full verdicts + dry-run, no confidence scores, zero LLM clients in the substrate. Two design deltas. First, the R439 judgment-time pin goes TWO-SIDED: an edge judgment interprets two claim texts, so the proposal stamps both endpoint claim sha256s and import re-checks both - either fact amended after proposing fails loud as stale; the STORED succession edge stays an unpinned identity ref (R442 doctrine: pins cover judgments about wordings; the proposal is the judgment, the edge is identity). Second, a latent succession-cycle hole rides this build after live falsification: amend_fact retargeting and import_facts forward refs BOTH close an A<->B succession cycle with exit 0 today, and the scan then reports zero violations while the cycle's facts silently never hold anywhere (each derives the other's end) - the half-enforced-invariant class exactly; fix = one shared cycle walk rejecting at every succession write site (add_fact / import_facts / amend_fact / the edge import) plus a SuccessionCycle scan violation for out-of-band plants (R440 boundary doctrine). Acceptance pinned before build, falsifiable: blinded V3 repair (unchained 1 to 0, green), new V9 bounded dead-to-alive (0 violations to rule_transition_invalid), new V10 stays-prose contradiction (no channel to FrameConflictOverlap), V0 specificity (post-import violations 0, author-review rejects recorded as over-proposals), Detroit pristine succession_gaps = 0. Store schema unchanged at v19 - the import fills fields that already exist; the new surface is the artifact plus report-edge-candidates / import-edge-proposals on both wires.

Three pins met exactly: V0 pristine control returned ZERO proposals and zero violations (specificity under the strictest reading - the agent judged every recorded transition already chained and declined to invent work); V3 stripped-link repair re-proposed the deviancy edge from the succession_gaps hint, imported it, and drove unchained 1 to 0 with the scan green; V10 stays-prose contradiction was proposed as a conflict edge from the claim texts alone (prose-only pair, no hint existed) and flipped no-channel to frame_conflict_overlap GATED. The V9 bounded-disallowed-step pin was NOT met, and the miss is the round's finding: the blind proposer deliberately declined the succession hint with a defensible reading (dead-then-alive with no narrated revival = contradiction, not one state replacing another) and proposed a conflict edge - which is gate-silent on exactly this pair, because the conflict gate requires co-holding and the trap's defining bounded extent prevents it. The pair never went silent (unchained stays 1; the edge is reviewable data), and the mechanical half was verified grader-side: importing the succession reading of the same pair fires rule_transition_invalid (alive-arc, carl, dead->alive) precisely as designed. Lesson pinned, the R459 lesson from the other direction: R459 under-predicted what the deterministic layer catches, R464 over-predicted which reading an LLM picks - acceptance pins for discovery rounds should pin the DETERMINISTIC half (given the edge the gate fires, given no edge the honesty count points) and leave which-reading-the-proposer-chooses to the author review loop, where a conflict proposal on a known state change is exactly the moment the author authors the succession edge manually. Round 466 — playthrough manuscript: Tier.decision_summary: The second Tier-2 promotion fired on two pulls: the owner question the backlog entry answers ('a human cannot read the graph' — N worlds = N linear manuscripts) and the Tier-3 A/B authoring experiment, whose blind-preference grading needs a readable per-world linearization as its consumption interface. Nothing is inferred — the manuscript is a deterministic projection of declared data. Scene sequence = the query world's GOVERNING composed order linearized (Kahn over the closure, lexicographically smallest ready node first; CanonOrder::linearize, on the order type per the R456 rule). The composed order is partial, so the emitted sequence is ONE valid reading and never claims otherwise: every adjacent emitted pair the order cannot compare surfaces as undeclared_adjacencies — the sec 7.14 span lesson carried from intervals to sequences (silently totalizing an incomparable pair would lie about what the author declared, B-1). Scene events are declared coordinates verbatim, two end kinds with distinct semantics: expired (canon_to equals the node — the fact holds AT it, through it, its last scene) vs superseded (a visible successor's canon_from equals the node, the event names the cutter); holding_count is judged by WorldCtx::holds_at VERBATIM as its 5th reader (gate, frame view, rules gate, irony report, manuscript — one semantics), so the delta story and the holds judgment cross-check each other instead of drifting into a second semantics. Honesty surfaces complete: unplaced_facts (a visible fact whose canon_from / canon_to / cutting successor's canon_from the world's order never names, with the offending field), undecidable (Vis::Unknown, never placed, never counted), sections_outside_order (isolated coordinates, R456: never scenes); no silent caps. The --world filter is the consumption unit (one manuscript per reading/grading session), fail-loud on a typo. Never gated — a manuscript is a reading surface, not a defect detector. successors_index now carries the successor's id beside the fact (the manuscript names the cutting fact): one index, every reader updated in the same change. Detroit dogfood read live scene-by-scene and produced two recorded insights: the non-interleaved order leaves fork worlds at undecidable=8 where the interleaved declaration drops to 0 (the R445 finding-5 adapter decision made legible per scene), and a fork world's manuscript can contain a NOT-TAKEN sibling route's outcome scene with zero events — base order nodes carry no branch attribution, a node-level fork cut would be the R436 heuristic class, so the substrate stays declaration-faithful and the fix (per-branch outcome declaration) is the ADAPTER's, pinned in sec 7.17. Store schema unchanged at v19; pure read projection, no new invariants, builder sites untouched.

Round 467 — session-load reads: identifi.decision_summary: A live session-load miss exposed two gaps with one root. query --term "Round 466" --scope changelog returned [] against a store whose latest entry IS Round 466 — indistinguishable from the entry being absent, the silent-miss failure mode this codebase repays on sight. Cause 1: the R292 term scan never matched identifier keys. That was an omission, not a recorded exclusion — the v1 out-of-scope list names pointer fields and enums but never IDs, no test pinned the absence, and IDs are exactly what an agent greps for at session start. Cause 2: the R410 list_changelog read model (round-number-ordered whole-ledger projection, built for the deferred Studio timeline) had no CLI or MCP surface, which is what pushed a listing need through a substring search in the first place. Both repaid in one round: identifier keys become searched fields symmetric across the three kinds under kind-qualified names (section_id / entry_id / inventory_id — one shared filter namespace, no ambiguity, opt-out via the same field filter); and the existing projection is exposed verbatim as query --list-changelog plus the list_changelog MCP tool — no new read model, wiring only. The honesty payoff: an ID-pattern search that returns 0 hits now means the ID does not exist, and the session-load question 'what are the latest rounds' is a listing verb, not a grep idiom.

Round 469 — A/B authoring experiment des.decision_summary: The sec 10 Tier-3 entry's gate fired (trap corpus R453 done, discovery verbs R458-R464 complete, owner pull 2026-06-11) and this round spends it entirely on design, because the experiment's validity floor IS the session separation: a session that designs the grading and then writes the story has contaminated both. The trial answers three questions under three disciplines. Floor (does the Mnemosyne loop reduce deterministic consistency defects in a long branching story?): two arms, identical original premise and structure quota, identical 3-session budget with fresh context per session — plain arm writes prose, loop arm authors store-first with gates at session end repairing before delivery; graded NOT on the loop's own store but on a blind re-extraction of BOTH proses under one pinned recipe, the symmetric-referee move the design considers its keystone. Ceiling (is either preferred?): per-world linear reading copies — the R466 manuscript verb's pulling consumer — judged blind by 3 fresh LLM sessions on a pinned 5-axis rubric; per the R464 V9 lesson this leg pins procedure and refuses to pin an outcome. Economics: token totals and prevented-defect counts, measured open. One pre-registered outcome only (PRED-1: plain >= 3 endpoint defects AND loop < plain); the bridge finding (judge-cited errors invisible to the D-metrics = untyped residue on live prose) connects the R453 miss-rate to real authoring. Everything an execution session will follow — premise, prompts, recipes, rubric, runbook S0-S11 — lives in one manifest whose sha256 is pinned in this entry before any execution session exists.

The instructive pair: F2 found ambiguity inside the just-pinned A/B manifest (which store backs the loop story's reading copy — an orchestrator degree of freedom is a hole in a BLIND protocol), fixed by making the blind re-extracted store the single authority for ordering BOTH arms' judge copies and re-pinning the manifest pre-execution, the pin chain itself now the tamper evidence; and F3 found this session extending the very parse-then-ignore class R466 had rejected (query-mode flags silently outranking each other), fixed by loud mutual exclusion in one parse site with unit tests. Pattern note for future reviews: every finding came from asking whether the session's artifacts obey the rules the session itself cited.
