Round 513 — warm-render posture frontier.decision_summary: R504's disclosure-craft experiment produced a split result its validated headline undersold: disclosure won the prose-quality keystone (5.00 vs plain 4.22) and tied or beat plain on all four measured axes, yet lost the holistic forced choice 2-1 on a quality the rubric undersamples — novelistic warmth. This round diagnoses that gap as render POSTURE, not missing data and not a raw model ceiling (R505's read): the same model wrote warmer prose in the plain arm from the same plot facts, so the differentiator is the JOB the prompt assigns — compliance (project this fact list under this disclosure plan, do not leak) makes the story serve the facts and reads like an outline; storytelling (tell the best story) makes the facts serve the story and reads warm. The lever is to relocate fidelity out of the author's prompt into the deterministic gates already built and proved (R507/R508/R512): render in a free storytelling posture, then gate-and-repair, so the author's job is plain's job and verification is the machine's. The round pins a controlled, measured acceptance experiment (warm render vs the reused R504 compliance render; fact base and disclosure plan held constant; posture the only varied variable) with an honest symmetric fork — a forced-choice flip proves posture was the cause, no flip proves the R476 model-craft ceiling on a clean comparison and authorizes a pivot to a different North-Star axis. Code 0; experiment execution is consent-gated.
changes_bullets: Diagnosed R504's 2-1 forced-choice loss (despite a keystone win at 5.00 vs 4.22 and parity or better on all four measured axes) as render POSTURE, refuting R505's model-craft-ceiling read: the same model wrote warmer prose in the plain arm from the same plot facts, so the differentiator is the JOB the prompt assigns — compliance fact-projection (the story serves the facts, reads like an outline) vs storytelling (the facts serve the story, reads warm) — not data and not ability.

Designed the warm-render protocol: a warm brief in narrative register carrying the SAME beats and withholds as the R504 compliance brief (no new story information, only the job re-registered, withholds encoded as story beats not fact-mode pins), then a gate-and-repair loop that runs the R508 leak and fidelity gates over a blind re-extraction and repairs only violations, scene-scoped and still in storytelling register; the lever is relocating fidelity out of the author's prompt into the gates we built and proved (R507/R508/R512). Round 516 — assemble.rs strip root-cause.decision_summary: R516 root-causes in code the R509 silent-fail that recurred during R515, repaying it the textbook way (fix-don't-workaround, pay-debt-now) instead of the inline-Python source surgery R515 used as a workaround. The R515 owner session review surfaced it: the warm render wrote fork-choice bullets WITHOUT the literal CHOICE token (the form `- **CONFRONT** ... -> sc-09a`), plus a `## World-line and ending map` appendix and an interior `---` rule, and the experiment-harness assemble step silently passed all three into the blind reading copies (it stripped only the `### CHOICE` heading line, keeping the token-less bullets, the card intro, the map, and the rule). That is exactly the silent-fail class R509 set out to end, and R515 worked around it with a throwaway Python structural strip rather than fixing the harness. The fix is a single general rule in assemble.rs reading_body: a markdown heading inside a scene body opens a trailing structural section (a fork card or the world-line map) and is never prose, since the scene's own heading is the delimiter stripped before the body, so the body is truncated at the first heading; plus interior horizontal rules (`---`/`***`/`___`) are stripped as structural separators (story.rs trims only the one trailing rule, so an interior one before a trailing appendix reaches assemble). The now-redundant heading-CHOICE branch in is_scaffolding_line is removed (headings truncate before it runs); the R500 `CHOICE:`-directive convention (no heading) keeps its line-level `A)/B)` option text unchanged. New tests model the exact token-less-bullet, world-line-map, interior-rule, and prose-`#` forms; cargo test (24+4) and clippy -D warnings pass. Proof on the real R515 data: re-running the fixed assemble over the R515 sources with the verb-derived per-world order (no Python) reproduces the judged reading copies modulo four stray `---` lines on the warm arm (the WINNING arm), provably immaterial — no judge cited a horizontal rule and the marks disfavored the winner — so the R515 3-0 craft result is unaffected. Code change is scoped to tools/experiment-harness/src/assemble.rs. The experiment-copy re-validation (regenerate the canonical post-R516 copies and re-judge on them) and the remaining textbook items (PIN-W1 as a genuine per-world reading-copy re-extraction; replacing the inline-Python order/heading normalization with the report-playthrough-manuscript verb, whose per-world paths were verified byte-equal to the Python walk) are staged as the next rounds.

Round 517 — pre-commit Gate 5b: fmt + cl.decision_summary: R517 closes a pre-commit gate gap surfaced during R516: the in-repo crates that carry their OWN [workspace] table (tools/experiment-harness, bench/, studio/ — split out deliberately so the root workspace build/CI/pre-commit never compiles them, the build-speed reason) are never reached by the pre-commit fmt/clippy gates, which run cargo fmt --all and cargo clippy --workspace and therefore see only root members. The consequence bit in R516: the assemble.rs fix committed unformatted because no gate checked it (caught only by a manual cargo fmt --check afterward and amended). That is precisely the silent-fail class this repo bans — a gate that does not gate part of the codebase — and it is doubly pointed because the experiment-harness header calls the crate the repayment for the silent-fail Python it replaced, yet the crate itself was ungated. The fix is a new pre-commit Gate 5b that is structural, not hardcoded: for each staged .rs it walks up to the file's owning [workspace] root and, for any root other than the repo root, runs cargo fmt --manifest-path <ws>/Cargo.toml --check (loud reject on failure) and cargo clippy --manifest-path <ws>/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings on that workspace. It runs ONLY when such a file is staged, so the root gate stays fast and the build-speed rationale for splitting these crates out is preserved; and because it derives the workspace from structure, a future tools/<crate> with its own [workspace] is covered automatically (no list to maintain). pre-push is deliberately left root-only: it validates the publishable production workspace before publishing, while Gate 5b keeps all committed Rust — production and dev/experiment tools alike — clean at commit time. Validated end to end: the detection picks tools/experiment-harness + bench and skips root crates and non-.rs files; a deliberately fmt-dirty harness line, staged and run through the real hook, was REJECTED at Gate 5b (exit 1) with the manifest-scoped fix hint, then reverted clean. Recorded (not this round's scope): bench/ and studio/ carry pre-existing fmt drift the new gate will surface the next time either is edited — correct lazy enforcement, not a regression.

A single blind author subagent, given ONLY the fresh premise The Saltmarsh Bell + the mutate-API author contract (NO facts), authored a 14-scene / 36-fact / 3-frame branching story with one fork into 3 terminal world-lines, running its OWN write-gate-read-repair loop (3 iterations) to gate-clean — the first end-to-end test of the upstream authoring step every prior experiment (R500/R504/R512/R514) skipped by hand-authoring the base. The orchestrator (this lineage; R469 firewall — authored no fact, judged nothing) ran the two deterministic pins independently of the author's claim: PIN-A1 convergence HELD (reproduces into a fresh seed with 0 import errors; validate-continuity 0 structural / 0 interval, the 3 belief-vs-truth pairs registering as cross-frame data not conflicts; every terminal world places all its facts) and PIN-A2 structural floor HELD (every terminal world dangling=0, fork-tree 1 fork / 0 unplaced / 3 children / all terminal, 0 timeline gaps, 0 off-branch succession) — verified against the hand-authored Meridian reference base, whose pre-fork main-stub dangling shape is identical and the AI base cleaner (1 vs 8). 3 blind judges (fresh context, only the rubric + neutral per-world manuscripts) scored causal coherence: unanimous 5/5 overall, 5/5 coherence / relevance / branch-integrity, completeness 5/4/4, all three independently calling it a genuinely authored story not an internally-consistent pile of facts — the scale-floor store-consistency-versus-causal-coherence did NOT reproduce at 14 scenes. The only flagged items (a late-introduced harbourmaster at sc-07e; a cross-branch backreference at sc-07a) are completeness blemishes, not logic breaks, and are exactly the semantic gaps the gates cannot catch by construction = the R476 ceiling surfacing where R518 predicted completeness-beyond-structure is judge-only. By the pre-committed decision rule, both pins hold + judged coherent means AI-self-authoring is REACHABLE at small scale and the next axis is SCALE (the scale-floor rematch at 60+ scenes where the prose-first loop lost). Honesty: n=1 premise / 14 scenes is the baseline not a scale claim; causal coherence is judge-derived (one model family, 3 independent blind sessions); the 2 blemishes would compound at scale. Round 521 — top-down authoring + structu.decision_summary: From the post-R520 owner dialogue. R520 proved AI-self-authoring reachable at small scale but surfaced 2 blemishes the gates did not catch (a late-reveal harbourmaster sc-07e; a cross-branch prose allusion sc-07a), and R520 grouped both as the R476 ceiling. The owner punctured that on both counts, and this code-0 design round formalizes the corrections as the authoring discipline the SCALE axis requires. Honest refinement (append-only, R520 NOT mutated, the R502/R505 pattern): only case-1 (a MISSING setup) is the true ceiling — you cannot deterministically detect the absence of a fact whose necessity is a judgment; case-2 (a reference to a fact living only in a sibling world-line) is exactly the cross-branch reachability that R488 FactCanonOffBranch already decides for canon_from, and it slipped only because the allusion was free prose (no structural edge) and because evidence references are existence-checked but NOT reachability-checked (verified in code: continuity.rs:1165 existence-only vs the le() reachability at :126 applied to canon_from at the FactCanonOffBranch check). Piece A = the top-down authoring contract: redesign the bottom-up author-brief into phased top-down (scope + skeleton tentpoles first — each world-line's ending, the load-bearing entities, the fork, the major reveals AND their setups together — then detail fill); the substrate already supports any authoring order (facts placed by canon_from), so it is a CONTRACT change not a build; it seeds case-1 (the proof mechanism becomes a tentpole) and makes salience EMERGENT (the skeleton IS the load-bearing declaration, a second mechanism for the R505/R506 salience-is-emergent conclusion). Piece B = the structural backreference discipline: a claim may not allude in free prose; a backreference must cite the establishing scene in evidence, and the one small buildable lever is extending the R488 le() reachability check from canon_from to evidence (deterministic, AI-out-of-gate, same kind as FactCanonOffBranch — spine evidence passes, sibling-branch evidence fails), which catches case-2; built WITH the scale experiment per YAGNI, not now. Combined they fix both blemishes with no new substrate. This is the SCALE-axis input: the scale experiment authors at 60+ scenes under this contract, with the two known failure modes mitigated by construction so a coherence failure at scale would be a deeper finding.

Round 526 — precondition back-propagatio.decision_summary: The owner challenged R524's lone blemish — 'top-down should already have known what the branch needed.' The store bears the owner out, and this code-0 design round formalizes the precise failure as a refinement of the R521 top-down contract. The act-dig survivor was KNOWN at the skeleton stage (the Phase-0 tentpole f-071 reads 'the survivor confirms…'); the entity theo was spine-grounded (sc-08); what slipped is a new STATE (Theo alive) that answers a question gt left silent — the spine carries the gang's death only as a vigil (mood) and a town-belief, never as a ground-truth fact, so the reveal contradicts nothing (coherence 5/5) yet resolves an unplanted question. R521's contract modeled the reveal's PAYOFF relationship (f-071 pays off the seeded warning) but had no slot for the new state the reveal INTRODUCES. The refinement (Piece A v2): in Phase 0, for each reveal, decompose every fact it asserts and SEED every new precondition — a new entity gets an establishing beat, a new state/answer gets its question opened earlier as a payoff_expectation:expected setup the reveal pays_off, and gt must take a position (or mark open) any question a belief frame raises. Recognized preconditions, modeled as setup->payoff pairs, ride the EXISTING report-payoff-coverage gate (no new gate), shrinking the R476 ceiling to preconditions the author never recognizes. A new entity-first-appearance gate was REFUTED (the slip was a state not an entity; foreshadowing-necessity is the R476 judgment ceiling). No build; the clause is the verbatim Phase-0 text the next authoring run's author-brief instantiates.
changes_bullets: design-doc sec 7.28 = the Piece A v2 contract clause (precondition back-propagation) — the verbatim Phase-0 text the next top-down author-brief adds.

Honest refinement of R524 (append-only, R524 NOT mutated): the act-dig survivor was NOT a late discovery — the Phase-0 ending tentpole f-071 literally names "the survivor", and the entity theo (Margaret's brother) was spine-grounded at sc-08 (her vigil). What slipped is a NEW STATE ("Theo is alive") that ANSWERS a question the spine left silently open: gt never asserts the gang dead (only f-103 gt vigil + f-111 town-belief), so the survivor contradicts no fact (0 violations, coherence 5/5) but resolves an unplanted question. R521's setup->payoff framing has no slot for an enabling precondition = the leak path.

The rule: in Phase 0, for each reveal tentpole, decompose every asserted fact into (a) a setup it pays off / (b) already-established or reader-derivable / (c) a NEW precondition (a new entity OR a new world-state resolving a question / cutting against the reader's assumption). Every (c) is seeded before the reveal — a new ENTITY gets an establishing beat, a new STATE/ANSWER gets its QUESTION opened earlier as a payoff_expectation:expected setup the reveal pays_off. Frame corollary: if gt is silent on a question a belief frame raises, gt must take a position or mark it open.

Round 528 — convergence-JOIN model DESIG.decision_summary: The convergence-JOIN DESIGN round (the owner said 'start the convergence-JOIN design round'). Answers the five questions sec 7.29/R527 scoped — code 0, refute-new-substrate-first (R493). The headline code finding sharpens every answer: the order ALGEBRA — closure_of's transitive closure, le() reachability, linearize()'s Kahn topo-sort, is_maximal/names — is ALREADY a general DAG machine (continuity.rs:263 states the closure of a DAG topo-sorts identically to it), so the 'forest by construction' constraint does NOT live in the order layer; it lives in exactly three named places: the single-parent Branch.forks_from (narrative.rs:82), the chain-shaped fork_chain/fork_ancestry (narrative.rs:104 / continuity.rs:991), and the single-lineage visibility/join_world (continuity.rs:1019/1042). A world-line JOIN is therefore a BOUNDED generalization of the ANCESTRY layer, not a rewrite of the order algebra. Scoped to the exclusive-OR diamond, the JOIN is a write-once SHARED continuation (a path-dependent prefix plus a suffix authored once), NOT a state-merge; its soundness is the R488/R522 reachability family checked per-incoming-parent ('no unreconciled dependency across a confluence'), with explicit reconciliation expressed by a bounded cross-confluence extension of supersedes_in_frame succession. Concurrency / free-order / availability-gating is a DISTINCT future substrate axis, not folded in. Build YAGNI-deferred behind an authoring run that needs it (the R495/R518/R521 'experiment is the test' discipline). Working term 'confluence' sidesteps both code collisions (join_world lattice-meet; persistence convergence-B index).
changes_bullets: Q1 REFUTE-FIRST — gap CONFIRMED: three existing-means candidates all fail. (a) a within-ONE-branch canon diamond (a->b, a->c, b->d, c->d) is handled by le() but b AND c both occur in EVERY playthrough of that branch = concurrency-within-a-world, not exclusive reconvergence. (b) duplicating the continuation onto both branches yields two DISTINCT facts (NarrativeFact.branch is a single String, narrative.rs:336) = no shared node identity, the fork-tree shows two leaves not a merge, payoff/continuity gates treat them independently = defeats write-once. (c) a third branch forks_from one parent inherits ONLY that one parent. The single immutable forks_from is the hard blocker; the gap is real (matches R527).

Q2 REPRESENTATION — a world-line gains a MULTI-parent merge declaration (working term `confluence`: the BranchFork {branch, at} shape as a SET, not Option-singular). SURVIVES UNCHANGED (the order algebra is already DAG-general): closure_of / le() / comparable / linearize (Kahn) / is_maximal / names. MUST GENERALIZE chain->DAG: fork_chain (single-parent walk -> ancestor-SET collection, the hop-cap stays as the DAG acyclicity guard); fork_ancestry (Vec chain -> transitive ancestor set); CanonOrder::from_declaration's composition loop (already iterates ancestry as a collection, so it generalizes for free once ancestry yields the full set); visibility / Lineage.cut (one cut -> a cut per parent path); join_world (lattice-meet over a DAG). The acyclic invariant is preserved: a confluence may not merge a branch into its own ancestor.

Q3 SEMANTICS (the crux) — SCOPE to the exclusive-OR diamond ==> a JOIN is a PATH-DEPENDENT continuation that SHARES authored facts, NOT a state-merge. Any single playthrough traverses EXACTLY ONE incoming line, so "what holds at the confluence" is W1's-prefix OR W2's-prefix plus the shared suffix authored ONCE. The primitive buys WRITE-ONCE shared continuation (author the ending once, both lines inherit) = directly attacks the forest's duplication tax (all-roads-lead-to-the-ending without authoring it N times). The soundness GATE (the R488/R522 le() analog) = "no unreconciled dependency across a confluence": every fact visible in the shared continuation must have its support (evidence / pays_off targets / referenced entity-state) reachable from EVERY incoming parent via le() checked PER-PARENT; a continuation fact depending on a prefix present on only SOME entries = the false-merge bug = REJECT (deterministic, AI-out-of-gate, the R502 family).

Q3 cont. RECONCILIATION — where content MUST differ by entry, you do NOT converge (stay forked) OR author an explicit reconciliation at the confluence: the EXISTING supersedes_in_frame succession with ONE bounded exception — succession may cross INTO a confluence node from its parents (today SuccessionCrossBranch, continuity.rs:840, rejects ALL cross-branch succession; the confluence is the single principled exception, a successor there supersedes each parent's divergent belief). No state-reconciliation ENGINE and no auto-merge logic (that = the R476 ceiling / world-simulation / pinion territory, deliberately out).

Q4 FREE ALTERNATION — fork->join->fork->join GENERALIZES to a series-parallel DAG, CONDITIONAL on Q2's multi-parent ancestry. Kahn linearize() already topo-sorts any DAG (continuity.rs:263 "the closure of a DAG topo-sorts identically to it"); le() answers cross-lattice reachability once from_declaration composes over the ancestor SET. The ancestor-CHAIN is the ONLY thing replaced. Multi-parent ancestry is MORE general than series-parallel (allows arbitrary acyclic merges); an optional "well-formed diamond" structural surface (every confluence's parents share a fork ancestor; the R442/R488 report-not-gate family) is DEFERRED — do not constrain mechanically up front.

Q5 JOIN vs CONCURRENCY — SEPARATE AXES, do NOT fold in. Convergence-JOIN = the exclusive-OR diamond (one path per playthrough -> tractable as sharing + per-parent reachability, this scope). Concurrency / quest-graph = AND-threads, author-free interleaving, availability GATING, state COMBINED (real conflicts), a quest unit (R527 open-world gaps #1/#2/#3) = the combinatorial explosion; it needs a different model (an independence/concurrency relation — event-structure / Mazurkiewicz-trace shape — plus a gating/precondition layer), its own future R518-style scope round. Folding it in would import the explosion into an otherwise clean bounded generalization.

BUILD DECISION — DESIGN captured, BUILD DEFERRED behind an authoring run that HITS the wall (the R493/R495/R518/R521 doctrine: build only when an experiment shows pull; R524 SCALED to 70 scenes inside the forest with NO merge needed, so there is no pull yet). The next authoring/scale run's brief gains a many-world-lines-converge-to-one-ending requirement; if the forest forces ugly duplication or the author cannot express the shared continuation, THAT failure is the build trigger (exactly how R521's contract -> R524's scale run worked). Naming-guard carried: `confluence` (narrative world-line merge) != join_world (the conflict-scope lattice-meet, continuity.rs:1042) != persistence convergence-B index (narrative.rs:142); the final identifier is a build-time decision.

The forest constraint READ at narrative.rs:81-82 (forks_from: Option<BranchFork>), narrative.rs:104-120 (fork_chain single-parent walk), continuity.rs:991-1005 (fork_ancestry -> Vec chain), continuity.rs:1019-1060 (visibility / join_world single-lineage); the cross-branch-succession reject at continuity.rs:838-845 (SuccessionCrossBranch). The conclusion "the forest lives in three named places, not the order layer" is a read finding.

Refute-first applied (the R493 discipline): each Q1 candidate tested against the actual types (NarrativeFact.branch is a single String at narrative.rs:336-337; Branch.forks_from is Option-singular at narrative.rs:81-82) before concluding the gap is real, rather than asserting it from R527.

The primitive buys WRITE-ONCE shared continuation (author the ending once, both lines inherit) = directly attacks the forest's duplication tax (all-roads-lead-to-the-ending without authoring it N times). The soundness GATE (the R488/R522 le() analog) = "no unreconciled dependency across a confluence": every fact visible in the shared continuation must have its support (evidence / pays_off targets / referenced entity-state) reachable from EVERY incoming parent via le() checked PER-PARENT; a continuation fact depending on a prefix present on only SOME entries = the false-merge bug = REJECT (deterministic, AI-out-of-gate, the R502 family).

Q3 cont. RECONCILIATION — where content MUST differ by entry, you do NOT converge (stay forked) OR author an explicit reconciliation at the confluence: the EXISTING supersedes_in_frame succession with ONE bounded exception — succession may cross INTO a confluence node from its parents (today SuccessionCrossBranch, continuity.rs:840, rejects ALL cross-branch succession; the confluence is the single principled exception, a successor there supersedes each parent's divergent belief). No state-reconciliation ENGINE and no auto-merge logic (that = the R476 ceiling / world-simulation / pinion territory, deliberately out).

Q4 FREE ALTERNATION — fork->join->fork->join GENERALIZES to a series-parallel DAG, CONDITIONAL on Q2's multi-parent ancestry. Kahn linearize() already topo-sorts any DAG (continuity.rs:263 "the closure of a DAG topo-sorts identically to it"); le() answers cross-lattice reachability once from_declaration composes over the ancestor SET. The ancestor-CHAIN is the ONLY thing replaced. Multi-parent ancestry is MORE general than series-parallel (allows arbitrary acyclic merges); an optional "well-formed diamond" structural surface (every confluence's parents share a fork ancestor; the R442/R488 report-not-gate family) is DEFERRED — do not constrain mechanically up front.

Q5 JOIN vs CONCURRENCY — SEPARATE AXES, do NOT fold in. Convergence-JOIN = the exclusive-OR diamond (one path per playthrough -> tractable as sharing + per-parent reachability, this scope). Concurrency / quest-graph = AND-threads, author-free interleaving, availability GATING, state COMBINED (real conflicts), a quest unit (R527 open-world gaps #1/#2/#3) = the combinatorial explosion; it needs a different model (an independence/concurrency relation — event-structure / Mazurkiewicz-trace shape — plus a gating/precondition layer), its own future R518-style scope round. Folding it in would import the explosion into an otherwise clean bounded generalization.

BUILD DECISION — DESIGN captured, BUILD DEFERRED behind an authoring run that HITS the wall (the R493/R495/R518/R521 doctrine: build only when an experiment shows pull; R524 SCALED to 70 scenes inside the forest with NO merge needed, so there is no pull yet). The next authoring/scale run's brief gains a many-world-lines-converge-to-one-ending requirement; if the forest forces ugly duplication or the author cannot express the shared continuation, THAT failure is the build trigger (exactly how R521's contract -> R524's scale run worked). A blind fresh-context author (R469 bound), given ONLY the premise + the proven R520/R524 top-down contract with NO convergence instruction, authored an 18-scene / 39-fact / 2-world-line convergence story ('The Reckoning at Harlow Mill') on the current forest substrate. RESULT = OUTCOME-1 (hard pull). A reader of branches[] alone would not see it ... the same dawn beat had to be authored as TWO parallel fact sets ... That duplication is unavoidable given the model: a fact belongs to exactly one branch."

R528 DESIGN field-validated + refined (append-only): the author found that sharing a scene-id at the tail of BOTH branch orders (sc-reckoning in both chains) is "legal and clean" — the canon-ORDER already TOLERATES a shared tail node, gate-clean. The confluence design targets precisely these two, not the order algebra = aimed correctly.

Secondary (orthogonal to convergence, recorded for a future look): report-payoff-substantiation forced the author to re-model "Sela IS the keeper" (a constant) as a transition contested->affirmed to discharge a typed setup->payoff — a tool-shaping pressure on how a true constant is stated.

DECISION (pre-committed R530 rule): OUTCOME-1 => PULL the convergence-JOIN BUILD (R528 confluence: multi-parent branch ancestry + the per-parent "no unreconciled dependency across a confluence" gate + bounded cross-confluence succession). The measured tax the build removes = the whole shared ending duplicated 2x (6 beats / 12 facts) + the structural invisibility (fork-tree cannot show the merge) + the silent-drift maintenance cost (nothing links f-300a to f-300b). After the build, re-run THIS premise on the new substrate = the full fork->join validation.

Round 532 — convergence-JOIN build step.decision_summary: Step 1 of the R528/sec-7.30 convergence-JOIN build, pull-justified by R531's OUTCOME-1 (the blind author was forced to duplicate the shared ending 2x and named the gap 'convergence is expressed, not declared; a reader of branches[] alone would not see it'). This round makes a world-line MERGE declarable + structurally visible WITHOUT touching the load-bearing visibility/holds_at predicate (no semantic risk): Branch gains converges_from: Vec<BranchFork> (the inverse of forks_from — the parents that converge into this shared continuation), with the mutate primitive validating >= 2 distinct pre-existing parents + real merge-section coordinates + the fork-XOR-confluence rule (a single shared build_branch_candidate for add_branch + import-facts); report-fork-tree's ForkTreeBranch gains a converges array, surfacing the merge with each coordinate resolved vs the parent's composed order. CLI --converges <parent>=<section> (repeatable) + MCP converges_from carry it; schema 22->23. End-to-end CLI smoke proven (declare a 2-parent confluence, fork-tree shows both merges). The fact-sharing composition (author once, both parent worlds inherit — removes the measured 2x duplication tax) and the per-parent 'no unreconciled dependency across a confluence' gate are the explicit next steps (R533/R534), not half-done here. Full atomic+validate suites green; clippy -D + fmt green.
changes_bullets: The convergence-JOIN BUILD, step 1 of R528/sec 7.30 (pull-justified by R531's OUTCOME-1): make a world-line MERGE declarable + structurally visible — the exact gap R531's blind author named ("convergence is expressed, not declared; a reader of branches[] alone would not see it"). Code round, the first in this arc.

SCHEMA (mnemosyne-core narrative.rs): Branch gains `converges_from: Vec<BranchFork>` (skip-if-empty, byte-stable), the inverse of `forks_from` — the parents that CONVERGE into this shared continuation, each {branch, at} = a parent + its merge coordinate. CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 22 -> 23.

MUTATE (mnemosyne-atomic): new `build_branch_converges` (mirrors build_branch_fork — each parent must pre-exist + be a registered/main branch, each merge point a real section, no self-merge, no duplicate parent, >= 2 parents since a 1-parent merge is just a fork) + a shared `build_branch_candidate` enforcing the fork-XOR-confluence rule (a world-line is a fork-child OR a confluence, never both); add_branch gains a `converges_from: &[(&str,&str)]` arg; import-facts BranchImport gains a `converges_from: Vec<BranchConvergeImport>` field (mutually exclusive with forks). Divergent-reject covers converges_from (Branch derives PartialEq).

SURFACE (mnemosyne-validate report-fork-tree): ForkTreeBranch gains `converges: Vec<ForkTreeEdge>`; fork_tree populates it (same parent-registered fail-loud as the fork side; each merge coordinate resolved vs the PARENT's composed order via CanonOrder::names; unplaced merge points land in unplaced_fork_points, deduped). The merge the fork tree alone could never show is now declared and visible.

CARRIERS: CLI `add-branch --converges <parent>=<merge-section>` (repeatable); the report-fork-tree text/JSON shows "X converges from Y at Z" (a confluence no longer mis-prints as "standalone world"); MCP add_branch gains `converges_from: [{branch, at}]`. End-to-end CLI smoke proven: declare a 2-parent confluence, report-fork-tree shows both incoming merges with at_placed=true.

SCOPE (this step): convergence is now DECLARABLE + VISIBLE. NOT yet built (the next steps): the visibility/order-composition that lets a confluence's facts be authored ONCE and SHARED by both parent worlds (removes R531's 2x duplication tax), and the per-parent "no unreconciled dependency across a confluence" gate. The load-bearing visibility/holds_at predicate is UNCHANGED this round (no semantic risk); a confluence with no facts on it is a valid structural declaration.

Round 533 — convergence-JOIN build step.decision_summary: Build step 2 of the R528/sec-7.30 convergence-JOIN arc, pull-justified by R531's OUTCOME-1 (the blind author was forced to duplicate the shared ending 6 beats x2 because a fact carries one branch and the forest has no native join node). The MODEL, decided in R528 Q3 and field-confirmed by R531: the order algebra (closure_of/le/linearize, Kahn) is ALREADY a general DAG machine, so 'forest by construction' lived only in the ANCESTRY layer (single-parent fork_chain + single-lineage visibility) — a JOIN is a bounded generalization of that layer, NOT an order-algebra rewrite. A query world W's composition = its backward fork ancestors (fork_chain) union {W} union its FORWARD confluence-suffixes (every confluence C where W is transitively in C.converges_from). A fact authored ONCE on C is visible (holds_at) in EVERY converging parent world past the merge and not before (visibility is structural membership; the composed order bounds the timing) — so R531's 2x duplication is removed by construction (12 shared-tail facts become 6). The confluence itself is not a query world (exclusive-OR: one playthrough = one parent path + the shared suffix; querying the merge as a standalone world would union nothing useful and surface false dangling-payoff findings). Cross-merge conflict reconciliation (a suffix fact vs a parent-middle fact, and cross-confluence succession) is the explicit R534 scope, not this round — confluence is new substrate, so deferring it is a staged build, not a regression or a half-enforced invariant.
changes_bullets: core::forward_confluences — the forward dual of fork_chain: a BFS over the converges_from reverse edges returning every confluence a query world flows INTO transitively (the shared continuations downstream of a merge); BTreeSet-dedup makes termination structural, so no hop cap (unlike fork_chain's non-deduped linear walk).

continuity Lineage gains a forward set beside the backward cut; lineage_of populates both; visibility() now returns In for a fact on a forward confluence-suffix UNCONDITIONALLY (the confluence is shared downstream of every parent — WHEN it holds is the order's job, not visibility's), the dual asymmetry of the fork-cut bound.

CanonOrder::from_declaration takes a forward map beside ancestry; a world's composed order unions backward-ancestor AND forward-suffix edge sets (closure_of topo-closes the resulting DAG unchanged — the order algebra was already DAG-general); new fork_confluences map mirrors fork_ancestry; compose_canon_order (the single read-side order path) builds both, so every CLI/MCP report composes the suffix.

query_worlds excludes confluences from the per-world sweep (timeline-gaps / rule gate / payoff coverage / irony / edge-candidates / manuscript default) — a confluence is a structural merge, not a playthrough, and sweeping it as its own world would render a prefix-less fragment and surface false per-world findings (a suffix setup paying off in a parent middle would read as dangling there); query_world_lineages still keys EVERY branch (join_world indexes it by any fact's branch); explicit --world still renders a confluence fragment for inspection.

Round 534 — session review (owner-reques.decision_summary: Owner asked for a textbook session review of R533 (hack/smell-free? long-term-correct structure? North Star? SSOT?) — the R510 review pattern. Honest verdict: R533 is correct, tested, squarely on the North Star (convergence/JOIN = the L1 structural-join substrate the open-world AAA-narrative goal needs), and it IMPROVED SSOT — query_worlds extracted six duplicated per-world sweep constructions into one source, the holds_at/visibility predicate changed exactly once (R390), and the forward walk is single-sourced in core::forward_confluences mirroring fork_chain. ONE genuine structural smell: CanonOrder::from_declaration is a medium-agnostic order-closure algebra, but R533 passed it TWO maps (backward ancestry, forward confluence-suffixes) that it merged identically — leaking the narrative backward/forward distinction into the algebra, plus an include-all-vs-filter asymmetry between fork_ancestry and fork_confluences. Fixed: one generic composition map (world_order_composition), the direction distinction kept ONLY where it is load-bearing (Lineage, for visibility). The conflict-gate cross-merge gap is NOT a silent-fail (it is counted as cross_scope_pairs) but IS a momentary inconsistency with the new visibility — recorded as the explicit R535 reconciliation scope, not half-built here (the general case needs an In-set intersection). Verdict after the fix: textbook to the owner's bar; SSOT clean on data/logic; North Star confirmed.
changes_bullets: SMELL FIXED (layering / SSOT) — CanonOrder::from_declaration took TWO maps (backward `ancestry` + forward `forward`) that it merged IDENTICALLY, leaking the narrative backward/forward distinction into what should be a medium-agnostic order-closure algebra. Collapsed to a single generic `composition` param; the algebra never sees why a branch contributes edges, only that it does.

fork_ancestry + fork_confluences (both only ever fed from_declaration, one filtering empties and one not — an asymmetry) collapsed into ONE `world_order_composition(branches)` = per world, its backward fork ancestors ∪ forward confluence-suffixes. The backward/forward distinction now lives in exactly ONE place — `Lineage` (cut vs forward) — where it is load-bearing for visibility; nowhere else.

Behavior-preserving (omitting empty-contributor worlds is identical to the prior include-all: an empty composition closes to `base`, which `reach_for` already falls back to). Full suite + clippy + fmt + e2e CLI smoke re-run green; the R533 manuscript/holds_at results are byte-identical.

THREE parts over the existing order algebra (no schema change — R532's converges_from suffices): (a) CONFLICT scoping — join_world generalized with a FORWARD case: when one fact is on a confluence the other's branch flows INTO (Lineage.forward), the JOIN world is the PARENT (the suffix is visible there), so a suffix-vs-parent-middle conflict co-holds and is caught — the pair R533/R534 left bucketed as cross_scope_pairs; the sibling-confluence-common-parent case stays unscoped (the deferred series-parallel generalization, surfaced not silent). (b) SUCCESSION reconciliation — cross-branch supersedes_in_frame is now legitimate in TWO inheritance directions via a SINGLE new core predicate mnemosyne_core::succession_branch_inherits (predecessor a backward fork-ancestor OR successor a forward confluence-suffix), called by BOTH enforcement points (the write-path check_succession_edge in mnemosyne-atomic AND the scan re-check in continuity.rs) so the multi-write-path invariant cannot drift (the two-write-path-one-invariant discipline; the prior backward-only write-path stayed stricter than the relaxed scan, which a failing test caught — the relaxation would have been dead code); bounded — it authorizes the edge, computes no merged state (no auto-merge engine). (c) the per-parent dependency GATE — the R488/R522 le() evidence-reachability, for a fact on a confluence, checked from EVERY incoming parent against the fact's own canon_from (which routes through that parent's merge coordinate in its composed order — NOT converges_from.at, so suffix-internal evidence reaches correctly), emitting a NEW ConfluenceEvidenceUnreconciled when evidence is reachable from only one parent; this ALSO fixes a latent false-positive (a confluence's own order is prefix-less, so the pre-R535 le(confluence, ...) wrongly flagged legitimate trunk/shared evidence). Byte-stable for pre-confluence stores (the non-confluence path is byte-identical to R522; forward sets are empty). VERIFIED: 4 new tests (the core predicate 4-direction parity unit test = the invariant SSOT; conflict-scopes-to-parent; succession reconcile-accepted/sibling-rejected; evidence reconciled-per-parent) + full suite (atomic 184 / validate 259 / workspace green) + clippy -D + fmt + live-store validate clean (281, byte-stable) + an end-to-end CLI smoke (a Harlow Mill diamond built via add-branch --converges; validate-continuity --json surfaced exactly the one confluence_evidence_unreconciled with parent=ride, cross_scope_pairs=0). NEXT (R536) = re-run convergence-probe/v2 (the fork->join validation: the shared ending authored ONCE, the merge gate exercised, the R531 12->6 duplication tax confirmed removed).

Round 538 — explicit CLI path overrides.decision_summary: Round 538 — explicit CLI path overrides resolve CWD-relative (the textbook fix surfaced by R537's de-risk; foundation primitive, owner-requested cost-no-object review). The convergence-probe/v2 de-risk surfaced that a relative --sidecar / --order CLI override resolved against the WORKSPACE ROOT (cascade::resolve_sidecar joined the anchor = the discovered root the CLI feeds via workspace_anchor), NOT the CWD — so an explicit relative --sidecar from a subdirectory silently planted a store at the repo root, AND the code VIOLATED its own doc comment ('a relative override joins the dir the command was invoked against' = CWD). The textbook root-cause fix (the R510/R534 review bar): an EXPLICIT CLI path argument is CWD-relative (the universal CLI convention, least surprise — like --manifest and every standard tool), while a config-DECLARED path ([atomic] sidecar_path / [continuity] canon_order_path) stays workspace-root-relative (a project-level declaration). SSOT restored: ONE new pure rule resolve_explicit_cli_path(cwd, raw) shared by BOTH --sidecar (resolve_sidecar) and --order (resolve_canon_order_file) so the two cannot drift to different anchors; a functional-core / imperative-shell split (the pure resolve_sidecar_in + resolve_explicit_cli_path are unit-tested, the thin resolve_sidecar / resolve_canon_order_file shells inject the process CWD). Blast radius = 0 regression (no hook/script passes an explicit relative --sidecar/--order; repo-root invocations have CWD == workspace_root, identical), verified by full suite + clippy -D + fmt + an e2e smoke (a relative --sidecar from a subdir now lands in the CWD, repo-root pollution gone). On-axis: a mutate-API-safety / tool-ergonomics fix that also removes the absolute-path crutch the R537 author-brief had to carry.

Round 542 — the prose-ghost precondition.decision_summary: A code-0 design/refutation round (the R518/R496 refute-first pattern) formalizing the owner-dialogue conclusion to the R541 sc-32 hole. The hole-class (R541 sc-32 + R524 act-dig): a load-bearing object/state existing ONLY in a fact's free-text claim, never a registered node — the deterministic gates pass because every DECLARED link is valid and the ghost is not a node, so nothing dangles. Diagnosis: soft rules are ignorable (R526 sec-7.28 was ignored at R541), only hard gates count, and a hard gate can read only structure not prose (AI-out-of-the-gate). Refute-first on the REAL R541 base REFUTES the cheap gate (force a typed claim at payoff facts + ground the typed-object): 11 of 14 payoff facts are legitimately prose-only (79% false-positive flood, the R526 noise reconfirmed on data), AND f-hold-04 is structurally identical to a legitimate reveal (entities [wend, deed_bond] both real), so a forced-typed author evades by naming the real grounded entity and the ghost relocates to a POSSESSION error structure cannot see. The hole-class's true nature is a possession/state error (the bond in the wrong hands on this branch), whose deterministic catch needs per-branch possession/location state + predicate exclusivity = WORLD-STATE SIMULATION = the R527 'world-state recorded-not-simulated' axis = a large axis, not a small gate. DECISION: the cheap prose-ghost gate REFUTED (do not build, noisy + evadable); the real lever deferred to its own R527 world-state scope round behind real pull (n=2 is not it); for now the blind judge is the floor's backstop (caught sc-32 3/3) and the R526 soft clause stays as incidence-reducing guidance. The deliverable = naming, on data, the IRREDUCIBLE residue of 'store-consistency != causal coherence' that no AI-out-of-gate check removes without world-state simulation — the true boundary of the deterministic floor. SSOT = design-doc sec 7.33 + this entry.

(b) MapLocator carries fact_id (the R556 field sketch omitted it) — a locator without its fact id cannot be dereferenced to content, so it is load-bearing not decorative. Round 559 — fact-to-quest leg DESIGN: a.decision_summary: R559 = the DESIGN round for the fact-to-quest leg (the owner's R559 scope-fork choice B: deepen the Mnemosyne seam; code 0, the R496/R556 design-round pattern). The fact-to-quest leg is the MIDDLE of the North-Star pipeline fact-to-story-to-quest-to-map/surface: the story leg is the manuscript/disclosure render (R466/R506-515), the map/surface leg is the playable-world projection (R556-558), and quest is the goal-structure between them. ONTOLOGY (North-Star framing): a quest is a goal-directed OBLIGATION — an objective with a completion condition, prerequisites, outcomes, and availability — and in the spec-is-one-instance-of-narrative model it is the NARRATIVE instance of the substrate's universal TRACKED-OBLIGATION pattern, exactly as a requirement / verification-expectation is the spec instance (code-grounded: PayoffExpectation is documented in narrative.rs as the narrative mirror of the spec CoverageExpectation). REFUTE-FIRST substrate audit (the R493/R547 discipline) maps every part of a quest to an EXISTING primitive: objective identity + actor + steps = an Entity of kind quest (Entity.kind is consumer-defined per ARCHITECTURE sec 6 inv4) + TypedClaims (pursues / completed_by / requires), the R547 authoring-contract-over-existing-primitives pattern; the open/closed obligation = PayoffExpectation Expected (a setup = the quest given) discharged by pays_off (= completed), with per-world DANGLING (report-payoff-coverage, R442) = the quest still OPEN in that world-line; prerequisites = the canon-order partial order; outcomes / branching = the fork tree (R497) + converge (R532); completion evaluation = holds_at (R466) per world; availability surfacing = disclosure (R506) + the MapLocator (R557) — a quest becomes available when its giving fact is disclosed at a surface = a map locator, so the fact-to-quest and map/surface legs INTERLOCK over one substrate. CONCLUSION: no part of a quest needs new authoritative substrate. The GENUINE boundary (not downplayed): the EXECUTABLE quest logic — the runtime lifecycle available-active-done-failed, complex / disjunctive completion guards, the quest state machine — is NOT Mnemosyne's; it is the R546 declarative-vs-executable line. Mnemosyne models the DECLARATIVE quest STRUCTURE (the facts: objectives, prerequisites, outcomes, completion conditions); SCE / pinion EXECUTE it (SCE = what the system does = the SCXML state machine, the ARCHITECTURE sec 1 sibling split; the same layer-split as R546/R547/R549). Quest STATE is DERIVED per world-line (a projection over holds_at + disclosure + payoff), never stored. DECISION: the fact-to-quest leg = (a) an AUTHORING CONTRACT (a kind-quest entity + the pursues/completed_by/requires typed claims; the giving fact marked payoff_expectation Expected; the completion fact pays_off it) = zero new substrate, the R547 clause pattern; (b) a PULL-GATED read projection report-quest-graph (sibling of report-playable-world) composing payoff + canon prerequisites + fork outcomes + holds_at completion + disclosure availability into a per-world quest graph (QuestNode = objective, actor, derived per-world state, prerequisites, outcomes, completion fact, surface locator). NOT built this round (code 0). NOT built until a pinion / authoring consumer pulls it (ARCHITECTURE sec 6 inv3 / the R556 discipline). The R558 lesson is carried forward into the staged build: reuse the existing per-world reports VERBATIM, carry their honesty surfaces, no re-projection, no silent drop. Honest scope: like R547/R556 the substrate is already sufficient; the contribution is the framing + the authoring contract + a staged projection, and the smallness IS the finding (the obligation pattern already covers quests). NEXT = R560 owner cadence.

CORRECTION 1: the dividing axis is DECLARATIVE-TRUTH vs EXECUTION, NOT simple-vs-complex. A guard CONDITION, however complex (nested AND/OR over facts, e.g. (A and B) or C), is a statement of world-state = Mnemosyne, projecting to an SCXML cond (R546 placed cond guards on the world-state side, R547). Only the side-effecting executable content (assign / script / send / the running interpreter) is SCE. I had loosely said complex guard = SCE; complexity is not the line, truth-vs-execution is. CORRECTION 2: PLAYING is NAVIGATION / SELECTION over the frozen map, not a time-flowing execution engine. The binding model is the memory's frozen-substrate pointer projection, NOT frame accumulation (CQRS read-side): the player's choice-path selects a world-line, and pinion / the visualizer looks up Mnemosyne's PRE-COMPUTED per-world-line projection (R557 playable-world, R559 quest-graph) and renders it. The visualizer is a cursor + renderer (a preview / test affordance for the author or AI, and the ship-time player path is the same), holding only the choice-path; there is NO executing engine in the discrete branching-narrative core, and quest STATE is DERIVED per world-line (holds_at + disclosure + payoff), never stored. I had overstated this as SCE/pinion executing flowing-time play. WHEN SCXML IS GENUINELY NEEDED (so the correction does not erase it): only at the EXECUTION edge — (1) concurrency / parallel (SCXML parallel regions + event queue + join: the R549 / R546 interfering-AND-thread edge that the exclusive-OR fork tree cannot express); (2) event-driven / real-time reaction (send / timers / invoke); (3) AOT codegen to a target language or formal verification (reachability / model-check) = SCE's stated purpose. The discrete branching core needs NO SCXML (KISS; SCXML there is over-engineering); whole-narrative-as-SCXML is POSSIBLE but only NEEDED where execution semantics buy something. Mnemosyne FEEDS SCXML (fork_tree to topology, world-state to cond) but does not store or execute it; the facts-to-SCXML adapter is R546-designed and unbuilt (pull-gated); executable SCXML is SCE. This split is symmetric for spec and narrative (one substrate, spec is one instance of narrative) — the only narrative-extra is a live PLAYTHROUGH a static spec lacks, and even that is navigation + an optional continuous-state edge (accumulating counters / inventories with combinatorial guards / R549 live contention) that is pinion-side, optional, deferred, not Mnemosyne's role and not required for the core. Round 567.decision_summary: R567 = the EXECUTION of dnd-quest-experiment/v3 (the R566 manifest, owner choice A0; the R469 blind family). OUTCOME = close_proven, with one intrinsic nuance the experiment was designed to surface. It tested whether a REAL story expansion (authoring the dead delver's investigation as on-page PROLOGUE scenes) closes the R564 D1 residual (the villain's identification was summarized off-page backstory) without leaking the withheld villain identity and without reading as merely longer — the empirical test of whether D1 was a scope choice or a substrate wall. The blind author added a 4-scene prologue (sc-00a-d, prepended before sc-01) + a new delver frame + 13 facts (Coombe marks the fresh tithes, watches a robed figure tip bodies into the sluice, follows the trail up toward the "holy quarter", records it leaving the name a deliberate blank, and drowns cut off), and re-pointed the journal fact f-130 to also pay off f-005 (the shown tracking); 52->56 scenes, the diff vs v2 = 13 facts added + ONLY f-130 changed + 1 frame + 4 sections (exactly the R565-priced expansion). PIN-1 + the LEAK RE-PROVE PASS (the load-bearing result): fresh rebuild 0-error, continuity 0/0, fork placed/terminal, terminal danglings IDENTICAL to v2, quest contract + map preserved; the leak gate over a blind re-extraction = leaks=0, vocabulary_shared=20, with f-004 (Vane is the cause) STILL first re-extractable at sc-14 not the prologue — the withhold-split WORKS, the deed is shown on-page without leaking the who (the renderer avoided even the word "shrine", rendering the trail's end as "the quarter where the ground was holy"; static + render greps and the blind extractor independently confirm the figure is never identifiable from the prologue). PIN-2 D1-closed = PARTIAL, and the partiality is INTRINSIC (the key finding): the blind extractor confirms the investigation is now SHOWN ("the journal is no longer pure off-page assertion") = the close of D1-as-originally-stated, BUT the sc-14 naming step ("it led him to the shrine-keeper, Brother Vane") is exactly the step the prologue says Coombe NEVER took (he left the name blank), so the NAME still arrives one step past where the shown hunt stopped — and this is NOT fixable, because showing Coombe confirm it is Vane would LEAK f-004 and fail PIN-1. The withhold and a literal full-closure are in DIRECT TENSION: a mystery that withholds the villain's identity cannot SHOW the identification without spoiling itself; the correct resolution is exactly what v3 does (show the investigation, keep the naming as the sc-14 reveal). 3 blind A/B judges (v2 no-prologue vs v3 with-prologue, randomized, sealed label-map): keep-the-prologue 3-0 KEEP (unanimous); knowledge-realism v3 2-1 (judge-2 narrowly for v2, flagging the prologue's "holy quarter" steering); more-finished-overall v3 3-0; overall v3 5/5/5 vs v2 4/5/4 (v3 >= v2 all three, strictly higher on two) — the named-from-a-document loophole the v1/v2 extractor flagged is closed by the prologue's triangulation. The sharpest carry: some "acquisition gaps" are not gaps to CLOSE but reveals to TIME — a refinement of the store-consistency != causal-coherence residue. Round 569 — report-quest-graph strict-co.decision_summary: R569 = textbook review of the R568 report-quest-graph build + the corrections it found, all fixed this round. The review (one adversarial reviewer + owner-grade self-audit) raised 7 findings. F1 (the headline, correctness+drift): the giving-setup binding used a scene-proximity FALLBACK (bind to any Expected setup paid at the completion scene when the completed_by fact carried no pays_off edge) — a drift from the sec 7.38 contract ("the completion fact pays_off it"), self-admittedly able to BLEED givings across two quests completing at one scene, and unit-untested (every fixture was combined). FIX = strict-combined ONLY: a quest's giving setups are the Expected facts its OWN completed_by facts pay off; an author who splits completion from payoff gets an honest unresolved, never an inferred binding — cross-quest bleed is now structurally impossible. F2/F3/F6 (drift + doc-honesty) dissolve under the same fix: open/done AND completion beats now read STRAIGHT from R442 payoff coverage (PaidSetup.payoffs), so the local visibility re-derivation (lineages + visibility(), with its false "holds_at" comment) is DELETED — the QuestCompletion doc ("read from the R442 paid list") is now true and "no re-derivation" is now literal. F4: QuestState::Unknown is documented as ONE definition (not-on-this-road); orphan quests are additionally listed in unresolved_quests, read the two together. F7 (typed-claim entity-ref boundary check) DEFERRED — a general boundary concern across all typed claims, not quest-specific; a global change risks continuity-gate regressions, so it is recorded not taken (scope discipline). FROZEN-LEDGER respected: the R562 v1 store is NOT re-authored (experiment reproducibility) — strict surfaces q-main (encoded split, completed_by facts f-305/f-404/f-505 carry no pays_off) as unresolved while the 3 combined quests (q-key/q-delver/q-reliquary) resolve EXACTLY (per-road divergence intact, all 4 giver locators resolved) = strict honesty over heuristic rescue, proven on the real store. R568's "q-main done all roads" was the fallback's doing; the strict result is the honest one. No new substrate, no production gate touched; the R568 commit is unpushed so the build + correction land as one clean history.

HEADLINE FINDING (the refute-first R493/R547/R556 discipline, RESOLVED on code before pinning): the design question "is same-place-two-eras a FRAME, a BRANCH, or a canon-ORDER coordinate?" is RESOLVED — ERA = a canon-ORDER coordinate on ONE world-line. The in-world TIME position is the orthogonal canon-order partial-order coordinate (R466 partial order, R560 canon order is partial). So the two ages = per-era SCENES ordered past<future on one world-line; same place = a shared Entity + the R557 MapLocator object stable across eras; past->future causation = R442 setup/payoff across time-distance + R547 exclusive succession (holds_at + supersedes_in_frame); the wend-pipe time-toggle = PLAY navigation over the frozen substrate (R560), not execution; the one optional past act = a Branch fork into two futures; multiple characters = the frame axis (R541); different regions = distinct scenes/locators; cross-region causation = pays_off crossing FRAMES freely but never WORLDS (continuity.rs:2442-2444) + R547 succession. Round 573 — time-travel-experiment/v2 ex.decision_summary: R573 = EXECUTED time-travel-experiment/v2 (the owner's experiment word; the R553 controlled-re-render discipline), closing R571's one honest blemish. OUTCOME: PIN-M1 HOLDS and the MYSTERY render wins the blind A/B 3-0. A CONTROLLED RE-RENDER of v1's FROZEN gate-clean base — NO new author (the frozen-ledger rule), ONLY the discourse order changed — in a WITHERING-FIRST (mystery) telling passes the leak gate (leak=0) that v1's Founding-first IRONY render FAILED (leak=1). Firewall R469 (14th use): the orchestrator ran the rebuild / outline / gates / A-B assembly; blind subagents re-rendered, re-extracted, and judged. PIN-M1 (the headline): the MYSTERY render's validate-disclosure-leak = leaks 0 (vocabulary_shared 15, the R510 F5 non-vacuous guard) + validate-render-fidelity off_path 0 reached_terminal true; the IRONY render re-confirmed leak 1 (f-seal-vent @ sc-04) on the SAME rebuilt base — same facts, same disclosure plan, same world-line, ONLY the reading order, flipping leak 1 -> 0. The blind re-extractor (independent re-read of the mystery prose) confirmed the mechanism on the page: both Founding causes (the cistern seal, the ford marking) are first stated as ground truth ONLY at sc-39p; the Withering scenes (sc-27p..sc-38p) render the clean water and firm crossing as unexplained wonders with explicit not-knowing. WHY IT PASSES (design verified in disclosure.rs:211-278 BEFORE pinning, the refute-first discipline): the leak gate reads each withheld fact's re-extracted canon_from (the prose's OWN ## sc-NN heading) and flags a typed-tuple match at-or-before the pin in canon order; the mystery render states no withheld cause under any heading before sc-39p, so the cause first-discloses AT the pin => leak 0. The existing substrate HONORS a discourse-order reveal — no new axis needed. Judged A/B (3 blind judges, arm positions varied per judge, label-map recorded): MYSTERY wins OVERALL 3-0 and REVEAL-IMPACT 3-0 (5 vs 2 every time); IRONY wins ERA-TEXTURE 3-0 (5 vs 2-3, exactly the preregistered trade); all three independently named the SAME reason unprompted — IRONY shows the seal (sc-04) and stone (sc-11) up front so its 'reveal' only RESTATES what the reader already saw, while MYSTERY withholds until the cross so the why lands as EARNED DISCOVERY. LOAD-BEARING FINDING: the mechanical leak gate's flag on v1 was NOT over-strictness — it tracked a REAL craft weakness the readers also feel; here the disclosure gate and craft AGREE (the contrast with R500's fidelity != craft). Decision rule mystery_leak_clean_and_judged FIRES: future-first is EXPRESSIBLE on the EXISTING substrate via render discipline AND reads as the better time-travel game. THE (ga)->(na) INPUT: PIN-M1 PASS => the (na) question narrows from 'is future-first expressible?' to 'should a first-class discourse-order axis be ENFORCED?', and the (ga) evidence leans strongly NO-ADD — the leak gate ALREADY enforces disclosure-order coherence (it FLAGGED v1's wrong-order render leak 1 and PASSED v2's right-order render leak 0; the gate IS the discourse-order check); what v1 lacked was render DISCIPLINE (heed the gate; treat leak>0 as 'your reveal order is wrong'), NOT a substrate feature; a positive 'declare the telling is Withering-first' axis would be redundant. So the (na) round's likely conclusion is a refute-first NO-ADD, recorded as the R573 finding for (na) to formalize or refute. HONEST RESIDUE (not downplayed, feedback_dont_downplay_experiment_flaws): MYSTERY LOSES era-texture 3-0 — the genuine cost, named pre-execution: the Founding age is lived-in-full in IRONY and glimpsed-only-at-the-reveal in MYSTERY; the gate-clean mystery form is NOT strictly better, it TRADES the lived-in past for the earned reveal; a full game might want BOTH (a base where the bearer's first Founding visit withholds the CAUSAL significance) = a craft/structure design not tested here; n=1 on ONE base (the discourse-order variable only); the A/B is structurally tilted on era-texture (IRONY renders the Founding trunk, MYSTERY does not) — named pre-execution; the bridge-tree's planting cause is shown in neither arm's reveal (a minor slice-scope gap the extractor flagged). DECISION = NO Mnemosyne build (substrate sufficient — the leak gate already enforces disclosure order); committed; push withheld. SSOT = v2/report.md + this entry.

Round 576 — ratify the structured-fact S.decision_summary: Ratify the structured-fact SSOT structure as the textbook fix for the pinion R1013.1 class (prose acting as a write-side source of store-homed facts: false supersede/decided/bundled claims that passed every gate). A structured fact (relation/status/binding) lives once in the store; current-state prose may only point/project, never restate; a syntactic lint forbids fact-assertion verbs beside a section ref in current-state surfaces, changelog audit-narrative exempt. Verification was the wrong frame (it presupposes two copies; SSOT forbids the second), so the prior claim-substantiation-gate draft is superseded. Reuse existing homes and verification (decision_status/superseded_by, BindingKind + max-rigor, R342/R574); typed relations are SSOT completion scoped to used relation verbs, not a speculative ontology. Design-only; build deferred pending open items (notably an open-question state has no DecisionStatus home).
changes_bullets: Authored claudedocs/structured-fact-ssot-design.md and deleted the superseded claim-substantiation-gate-design.md draft (verification-as-frame was the smell).

Ratify the structure: a structured fact (relation/status/binding) has one store home; current-state prose (code comments, section caveats/intent/rationale/body) may only point or project, never restate; the changelog audit-narrative is exempt.

The only new mechanism is a syntactic lint (a fact-assertion verb beside a section ref in current-state surfaces); everything else reuses existing homes and verification (decision_status/superseded_by, BindingKind + max-rigor R413-R428, supersede invariant R342/R574).
Reframe typed relations as SSOT completion: every used relation needs one home so prose can project it; build per used verb only, never a speculative ontology.

Design composes with existing mechanisms (R342/R574 supersede invariant, max-rigor R413-R428 bindings, R400 SSOT/projection precedent); no new verification subsystem is introduced.

Round 577 — implement v1 of the structur.decision_summary: Build v1 of the structured-fact SSOT design (ratified R576): a new opt-in prose-fact-assertion axis in validate-code-refs that flags a current-state code comment which RESTATES a structured fact (a relation/status verb adjacent to a §<id>) instead of pointing to it. The fact has a single store home (decision_status/superseded_by/bindings, authored via the mutate API); prose only projects. Deterministic and AI-free; opt-in via severity_prose_fact_assertion (None=off). Scoped to used relation/status verbs; implements excluded (binding idiom). The design acceptance test — the real R1013.1 comment shape — is rejected by the lint. Section-body surface, open/deferred-state verbs, and a CLI override are deferred per design sec 12.
changes_bullets: Add the prose-fact-assertion axis to validate-code-refs (mnemosyne-validate): a current-state code comment that RESTATES a structured fact — a relation/status verb adjacent to a §<id> citation — is flagged ProseFactAssertion, because the fact has a single store home and prose must only point to it.

New ViolationKind::ProseFactAssertion + DefectClass::ProseFactAssertion + extract_prose_fact_assertions helper (closed verb set, backtick-skipped, one hit per line, independent of whether the cited id resolves).

New opt-in config axis severity_prose_fact_assertion (Option<Severity>, None = off), wired through the cli tally / summary line / JSON / reject gate exactly like severity_verification and severity_blanket.

Scope: relation/status verbs in use (supersede, decided in, ratified in, deferred to, depends on, refines, conflicts with, plus Korean 폐기/대체); implements is excluded (binding idiom, already governed by the binding axis + max-rigor).
verification_bullets: New unit tests pass: prose_fact_assertion_flags_verb_beside_section_ref (positive + 'see §X' pointer / bare pointer / backtick-example negatives) and prose_fact_assertion_rejects_the_r1013_1_comment_shape (the design acceptance test on the real R1013.1 comment text — both 'decided in §5.37' and 'supersedes §5.36' lines flag).

Round 578 — add DecisionStatus::Open to.decision_summary: Implement design sec 12a (the open-question SSOT home): add DecisionStatus::Open, the not-yet-decided lifecycle state the enum was missing (it had only Active/Superseded/Removed). Open joins Removed as axiom-exempt (no in-force decision to back) via a new is_axiom_exempt() helper that is the single source for the coverage/verification/confirmation/spec-drift exemption set, replacing 6 inline == Removed checks (closing the half-enforced-invariant risk). Wired through the fact codec (discriminator 4), as_str, the CLI set-section-decision-status parser, and superseded_by handling (Open carries none). This lets prose POINT at an open question (a section in Open state) instead of restating it. Does NOT yet enable the lint open/deferred verbs (downstream: needs the deferred-to typed relation per sec 6).
changes_bullets: Add DecisionStatus::Open (4th state, appended to preserve the existing Ord) — the not-yet-decided lifecycle state the enum was missing; Open resolves to Active or is withdrawn to Removed, never Superseded.

Add DecisionStatus::is_axiom_exempt() (Removed | Open) as the single source for the decision-backing exemption, replacing the 6 inline == Removed checks across coverage / verification / misclassification / blanket / verifies-linkage / confirmation (closes the half-enforced-invariant risk).
Exempt Open from spec rev-drift (an Open question is not a ratified live mirror) alongside Superseded/Removed.

Wire Open through the fact codec (discriminator 4), as_str ("open"), the CLI set-section-decision-status parser + help text, and set_section_decision_status (an Open section carries no superseded_by).

Round 579 — resolved_by forward-pointer.decision_summary: Build SSOT design sec 12a/sec 6 step 2 in one round. (A) Add resolved_by — the open-question SSOT home for 'deferred to §Y', symmetric with superseded_by (dedicated cardinality-1 forward-pointer, set only when Open, own invariant; projected as a resolved_by cross-ref so it is orphan-checked; deliberately NOT a premature general relation store, which would risk a shared-field half-enforced invariant). set_section_decision_status gains a resolving param; the CLI gains --resolving guarded to --status open. (B) Curate the prose-fact-assertion lint to 'lint a verb iff its fact has a store home': add deferred to / open question / still open; remove depends on / refines / conflicts with (no home yet — R577 over-included them = alternative-less ban); keep bare 'open' out (noise).
changes_bullets: Add AtomicSection.resolved_by (Option<String>, serde-default) — the open-question forward-pointer to its expected resolver, symmetric with superseded_by: a dedicated cardinality-1 field set only when decision_status==Open (optional there), each lifecycle pointer keeping its own invariant (no general relation bag = no half-enforced-invariant risk).
set_section_decision_status gains a `resolving` param (sets resolved_by for Open, clears it on every other transition); the CLI gains `--resolving §<M>` guarded to `--status open`, plus help text.

Project resolved_by as a `resolved_by`-kind cross-ref so it is orphan-checked through the existing machinery — no new validator (parity with superseded_by, which also has no reverse-direction out-of-band check).

Correct the MSRV to the field-proven floor 1.88. To keep the claim continuously verified (not another unverified declaration — the same accuracy principle the prose-fact lint enforces) add a msrv CI job that reads rust-version from Cargo.toml (single source, no drift) and runs cargo check --workspace on that toolchain via RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, overriding the rust-toolchain.toml dev pin of 1.94.1 (dev-on-latest, support-down-to-MSRV). Discovered while doing so: mnemosyne-validate.yml was malformed (unparseable indentation) so the GitHub CI had been silently non-running; rewrote it into valid YAML in the same change. The cargo install --git adoption commands in README/SCHEMA_GUIDE are correct (they include mnemosyne-cli); the missing-package error was only in this session's chat advisory.

Rejected option (b) (a caveat remove/replace primitive) as a frozen-ledger violation. The lint now scans only the settable current-state fields, where a flagged assertion can actually be remediated via its setter. This confirms the sec 9 irreducible-residual classification with the concrete append-only mechanism.

Round 586.decision_summary: Extend the R585 AI-first-authoring support debt with the spatial support surface: relational (not metric) space needs a place-graph projection report plus deterministic spatial-integrity and spatial-fidelity gates, so text/2D/3D renderers project one topological SSOT and cannot drift from it. Storing and projecting works today with user predicates; only the deterministic guarantee is the debt.
changes_bullets: place-graph report: project the containment hierarchy + adjacency for a renderer (the spatial analogue of report-quest-graph)
spatial-integrity gate (Validator plugin): containment cycle-free, no orphan place, no mutually-exclusive double-containment, adjacency consistency
spatial render-fidelity gate: a rendered description must not contradict declared spatial relations (extend the R505 render-fidelity pattern to spatial predicates)
convention (no feature needed to store): relational space via user predicates located-in / part-of / adjacent-to / direction-of as typed entity relations; no metric coordinates
verification_bullets: extends the R585 support-surface debt with the spatial axis

carry_forward_bullets: start now with no feature: author relational space as user predicates + facts; a renderer reads them via query (report-entity / query --term) and projects
promote when load-bearing: place-graph report + spatial-integrity gate + spatial-fidelity gate (deterministic and medium-neutral, so in-core Validator + report, not the external harness)
invariant: relations are the stable SSOT; metric coordinates are renderer-local, volatile, untracked; each renderer solves coordinates to satisfy the declared relations

changes_bullets: describe-schema: new SchemaContract.disclosure_encoding field — the withhold+first_at per-world reveal idiom (a per-road secret stays mode=withhold with a first_at pin on the reveal-road only; mode=state/hint/imply is world-independent and discloses on EVERY world-line, so it leaks), plus the caveat that a clean report-authoring-frontier does NOT certify a correct telling (a premature leak/early-reveal is a render property, caught only by the disclosure leak gate + report-playthrough-manuscript over re-extracted prose).

describe-schema: the branches registry description documents the FORK-LINEAGE TRAP two independent loop agents hit — a fork inherits the parent prefix, but bare main stays its own dead-prefix world-line still carrying the trunk setups; forking both roads off main and never continuing bare main leaves those expected setups dangling on main. Fix recorded: continue main AS one road, or pay the trunk setups off before the fork.

Round 607 — check_store_boundary exempts.decision_summary: A consumer (the-tide-that-counts, adapting a novel into a branching game) hit a false reject: add-branch <C> --converges main=<sec> --converges <fork>=<sec> succeeds at mutate, but every canon-order consumer (validate-continuity / report-fork-tree / report-payoff-coverage / manuscript) then fails with 'canon-order declares an edge set for branch main, which is not in the branch registry'. Root cause: check_store_boundary's declared-branch loop was the only one of four sibling registry checks missing the MAIN_BRANCH exemption. world_order_composition keys MAIN_BRANCH when main is a confluence PARENT (its own docstring: 'a confluence parent may be main'), that key flows through from_declaration into branch_reach, and declared_branches() then yields main — which the unguarded loop rejects because main is never registered. The fix adds the b != MAIN_BRANCH guard, identical to the fact / branch / world siblings in the same function. This unblocks the documented main-as-confluence-parent topology, letting a completed main trunk be re-woven with a forked braid without shattering the canon trunk into a dead prefix (the R601 fork-lineage trap).

Round 608 — the continuity gate scopes m.decision_summary: An adversarial self-review of R607 found the boundary fix was necessary but NOT total; R607's own carry-forward claimed 'every canon consumer unblocked / the fix is total', which is false. query_world_lineages — the lineage map consumed by scan_continuity, timeline_gaps, and edge_candidates — hardcoded main to Lineage::default() (empty forward) and computed lineage_of only for registered branches, and main is never a registered branch. The READ surfaces (payoff_coverage / frame_view / irony_intervals / playthrough_manuscript) instead call lineage_of per world, which computes forward = forward_confluences(world). So for a main-as-confluence-parent store the gate saw main.forward = {} while the view saw main.forward = {the confluence}. Consequence: a conflict between a main-exclusive-middle fact and a confluence-suffix fact returns None from join_world (the R535 forward arm lineages[main].forward.contains(suffix) is false), drops into cross_scope_pairs, and is NEVER checked — a silent false-negative in the flagship validate-continuity gate, for exactly the topology R607 unblocked. The gate and the view drifted, violating the 'holds_at is THE single holds-semantics shared by gate and view' invariant. Fix: query_world_lineages now flows main through the same lineage_of walk as every branch (main is no longer special-cased), making it genuinely 'THE single construction' its docstring claims. Byte-stable for pre-confluence stores, where forward_confluences(main) is empty so lineage_of(main) equals Lineage::default().

Round 609 — is_known_world single-source.decision_summary: The R607 review's MEDIUM finding: the guard 'a valid world-line reference is MAIN_BRANCH or a registered branch' was hand-copied as world != MAIN_BRANCH && !branches.contains_key(world) at 12 sites across mnemosyne-core's consumers (mnemosyne-validate continuity x6, mnemosyne-atomic write path x4, mnemosyne-ops x2), with no single source. That un-single-sourced invariant IS the R607 bug's root: one site (the declared-branch loop) was added without the guard because nothing named or forced the concept. Fix: a single primitive mnemosyne_core::is_known_world(branches, world) beside its world-line siblings (fork_chain / forward_confluences / MAIN_BRANCH), with all 12 sites routed through !is_known_world(...). Pure refactor: !(world == MAIN || contains(world)) is (world != MAIN && !contains(world)) by De Morgan, and each call site keeps its own bespoke fail-loud message. Now a 13th world-ref guard cannot silently drop the main exemption — the concept has one name and one definition.

Round 611 — a fork off a confluence-chai.decision_summary: MNEMO-GAP-003, filed by the-tide-that-counts (the game-adaptation consumer) as the next step after GAP-002/R607: once the canon trunk becomes a CHAIN of confluences — which any upstream re-convergence braid creates — a DIVERGENT line forking off that trunk stops seeing the mid-trunk facts the merge displaced onto the confluence, even facts at-or-before its own fork point. Reproduced on the installed R609 CLI: with a braid re-converging into `weave` (which then OWNS the s3-s4 suffix), an `ending` forking off main@s3 lost `f-mid`@s3 — while `main` and the braid walked the full trunk correctly, so the re-convergence itself was never broken; only the fork off it was. ROOT CAUSE: fork inheritance was solved against the ancestor's OWNED facts rather than the ancestor's COMPOSED walk — `visibility`'s backward arm read only `fork_chain` (`cut`) and never the `forward_confluences` those ancestors flow into, so a re-convergence that moved a trunk segment onto a confluence made that segment invisible to anything forking off the trunk. The engine had already named this the deferred series-parallel generalization (the `join_world` docstring). DECISION: extend fork inheritance from "the ancestor's own facts" to "the ancestor's composed walk", BOUNDED at the departure — a third lineage relation `cut_forward` (a confluence an ancestor flows into -> that ancestor's departure point), resolved through the SAME bounded ladder `cut` uses. Three legs, because any one alone is a half-invariant: visibility (one fix point for every read surface), order composition (so the divergent world can compare a displaced coordinate to its fork), and join_world (so recorded-conflict scoping tracks the visibility instead of silently bucketing a co-holding pair as cross-scope). The BOUND is what stops a divergent ending from stealing the SHARED tail: it inherits the trunk prefix only up to its fork; the re-convergence suffix past it stays Out. Transitivity is free — `forward_confluences` is already a transitive closure, so a fork off a two-link chain inherits BOTH links (the consumer's real F1+F2+F4 topology). Byte-invariant for fork-only and single-confluence stores.
changes_bullets: Lineage gains cut_forward (a confluence a fork ANCESTOR flows into -> that ancestor's departure bound), built in lineage_of from fork_chain x forward_confluences; bounded_visibility extracted so the cut and cut_forward arms share ONE ladder and cannot drift

visibility gains the bounded backward-then-forward arm — one fix point for every read surface (payoff/dangling, playthrough manuscript, frame-at-T, irony intervals, the typed-rule world sweep all route through visibility)
