Round 611 — a fork off a confluence-chai.publishable_decision_summary: MNEMO-GAP-003, filed by the-tide-that-counts (the game-adaptation consumer) as the next step after GAP-002/R607: once the canon trunk becomes a CHAIN of confluences — which any upstream re-convergence braid creates — a DIVERGENT line forking off that trunk stops seeing the mid-trunk facts the merge displaced onto the confluence, even facts at-or-before its own fork point. Reproduced on the installed R609 CLI: with a braid re-converging into `weave` (which then OWNS the s3-s4 suffix), an `ending` forking off main@s3 lost `f-mid`@s3 — while `main` and the braid walked the full trunk correctly, so the re-convergence itself was never broken; only the fork off it was. ROOT CAUSE: fork inheritance was solved against the ancestor's OWNED facts rather than the ancestor's COMPOSED walk — `visibility`'s backward arm read only `fork_chain` (`cut`) and never the `forward_confluences` those ancestors flow into, so a re-convergence that moved a trunk segment onto a confluence made that segment invisible to anything forking off the trunk. The engine had already named this the deferred series-parallel generalization (the `join_world` docstring). DECISION: extend fork inheritance from "the ancestor's own facts" to "the ancestor's composed walk", BOUNDED at the departure — a third lineage relation `cut_forward` (a confluence an ancestor flows into -> that ancestor's departure point), resolved through the SAME bounded ladder `cut` uses. Three legs, because any one alone is a half-invariant: visibility (one fix point for every read surface), order composition (so the divergent world can compare a displaced coordinate to its fork), and join_world (so recorded-conflict scoping tracks the visibility instead of silently bucketing a co-holding pair as cross-scope). The BOUND is what stops a divergent ending from stealing the SHARED tail: it inherits the trunk prefix only up to its fork; the re-convergence suffix past it stays Out. Transitivity is free — `forward_confluences` is already a transitive closure, so a fork off a two-link chain inherits BOTH links (the consumer's real F1+F2+F4 topology). Byte-invariant for fork-only and single-confluence stores.

Round 612 — world-line membership is ONE.decision_summary: A cost-no-object review of R611 (three INDEPENDENT adversarial reviewers, the discipline the memory prescribes and that R611 skipped) returned a verdict I accept: cut_forward was a PATCH, not the model. R438 added one lineage relation, R533 a second, R611 a third — and each round the enumeration missed a case the next one would have to bolt on. The reviewers proved the miss is not hypothetical: a fork off a CONFLUENCE (the second link of every subway-braid chain, i.e. the consumer's actual F1+F2+F4 topology) lost the ENTIRE pre-merge trunk, silently; a non-monotone fork chain leaked; a confluence world returned a prefix-less fragment; and R611 left succession at the OLD width, so the gate would report a contradiction in a divergent world and then reject the only sanctioned way to fix it. DECISION: replace the enumerated relations with the series-parallel LATTICE the gap report itself pointed at. World-line membership is a map from branch to the departure coordinates a fact must be at-or-before — ALL of them, conjoined. FORK = conjoin a bound. MERGE = INTERSECT the parents. That is closed: a fork off a confluence, a fork off a fork off a confluence, nested confluences, a confluence whose parent is a confluence all fall out of those two rules, so there is no fourth relation to add, ever. Two consequences make it more than a refactor. (a) Carrying the bound as a SET rather than folding it into a `min` keeps the lattice ORDER-FREE, which is what finally lets the write path (succession) and the read path (visibility) share ONE definition instead of three that drift — the canon order compares against each bound later, at visibility time. (b) The intersection at a merge is a genuinely new and provably right semantics: a confluence continues only what EVERY incoming road carried, so the path-independent trunk survives while each parent's exclusive middle is dropped — which is exactly why a fork off it now inherits the trunk. join_world stops being a hand-enumerated relation and becomes the bounded visibility itself ("a world where BOTH facts are In"), which as a side effect CLOSES the sibling-confluence-common-parent case deferred since R533 — it literally is the "In-set intersection over the query worlds" that docstring said would be needed. HONEST BOUNDARY, stated so this entry cannot be misread: R612 fixes the FACT axis only. The COORDINATE axis (CanonOrder::names / linearize / is_maximal read R611's unbounded order widening) is STILL BROKEN — render-fidelity is blind for divergent worlds, the R488 wrong-branch guard is silent past the fork, and the pinion seam emits phantom scenes. Verified still reproducing after this round. That is the next round, and it must first answer a substrate question this arc exposed: a world-line has no declarable END.

Round 613 — the COORDINATE axis designed.decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, designed — and the design ROUND is the finding, because my first design was REFUTED before it could be built. Setting: R611 fixed the FACT axis by silently widening the COORDINATE axis, which BLINDED two deterministic gates (validate-render-fidelity for a divergent world now REWARDS a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAGS the faithful one; R488's wrong-world-line guard goes silent past the fork) and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R612 fixed the fact axis properly with the membership lattice and deliberately did not touch this. So: `CanonOrder` is asked TWO different questions and answers both from one derived node set — PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?", which must stay GENEROUS: R611's widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, and both reviewers confirm no case needs it narrowed) and ROAD ("which coordinates does this world TRAVEL, and where does it END?", which must be BOUNDED). Splitting them is the round's surviving thesis. THE DRAFT I WROTE derived the road from the R612 membership lattice. Two independent adversarial reviewers implemented it against the real crates and ran it over all 46 store-times-order pairs in the repo, and it is WRONG — not marginally: its own seed clause re-admitted the exact leak it was written to block; applying the FACT bound to EDGES collapsed a playable world's road to a single node, turning its own facts into false positives; on a REAL store it silently made a world's ENDING the story's OPENING scene, so the terminal gate would pass prose that renders only the briefing — a silent wrong answer from the gate that exists to catch silent wrong answers; and it would newly reject 381 facts across 13 pairs in four breakage classes where I had admitted one, INCLUDING the confluence's own facts, which are the very subject of MNEMO-GAP-003. THE LAW THAT EXPLAINS ALL OF IT, and the reason no patch to the draft can work: FACTS INTERSECT AT A MERGE, ROADS UNION AT A MERGE. They are DUALS. A fork CUTS facts (conjoin a bound) but OVERRIDES the road (its own out-edge at the departure coordinate replaces the inherited one). R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — that is what makes the fact axis right — so for any world whose prefix runs through a merge, the member edge set no longer holds the edges that carry the road. One lattice cannot serve both axes. THE MODEL: road = an OVERRIDE WALK. A coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge into it leaves a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there (own beats nearest fork ancestor beats the base). No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all — which is precisely why it neither collapses nor forces the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain (the R456 incomparable-is-first-class idiom the draft violated). Validated against every topology in the repo, including the two real stores the draft broke, which it leaves PASSING. THE SUBSTRATE FINDING (and the correction of my own false refute-first): the store CANNOT distinguish "W forks in FACTS ONLY and continues down the trunk" from "W forks and ENDS at its own beat" — both encode as forks_from with no edge set, and my draft silently reinterpreted the first as the second, which IS the 381. The resolution is not a new field but a DECLARATION-COMPLETENESS fail-loud that NAMES the ambiguity and hands the author the lever, so the default (undeclared = the trunk) is both correct and loudly named. That converts a LYING gate into an honest one at zero migration cost. Code 0. The build is R614, gated on ratification.

Round 613 — the COORDINATE axis designed.publishable_decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, designed — and the design ROUND is the finding, because my first design was REFUTED before it could be built. Setting: R611 fixed the FACT axis by silently widening the COORDINATE axis, which BLINDED two deterministic gates (validate-render-fidelity for a divergent world now REWARDS a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAGS the faithful one; R488's wrong-world-line guard goes silent past the fork) and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R612 fixed the fact axis properly with the membership lattice and deliberately did not touch this. So: `CanonOrder` is asked TWO different questions and answers both from one derived node set — PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?", which must stay GENEROUS: R611's widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, and both reviewers confirm no case needs it narrowed) and ROAD ("which coordinates does this world TRAVEL, and where does it END?", which must be BOUNDED). Splitting them is the round's surviving thesis. THE DRAFT I WROTE derived the road from the R612 membership lattice. Two independent adversarial reviewers implemented it against the real crates and ran it over all 46 store-times-order pairs in the repo, and it is WRONG — not marginally: its own seed clause re-admitted the exact leak it was written to block; applying the FACT bound to EDGES collapsed a playable world's road to a single node, turning its own facts into false positives; on a REAL store it silently made a world's ENDING the story's OPENING scene, so the terminal gate would pass prose that renders only the briefing — a silent wrong answer from the gate that exists to catch silent wrong answers; and it would newly reject 381 facts across 13 pairs in four breakage classes where I had admitted one, INCLUDING the confluence's own facts, which are the very subject of MNEMO-GAP-003. THE LAW THAT EXPLAINS ALL OF IT, and the reason no patch to the draft can work: FACTS INTERSECT AT A MERGE, ROADS UNION AT A MERGE. They are DUALS. A fork CUTS facts (conjoin a bound) but OVERRIDES the road (its own out-edge at the departure coordinate replaces the inherited one). R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — that is what makes the fact axis right — so for any world whose prefix runs through a merge, the member edge set no longer holds the edges that carry the road. One lattice cannot serve both axes. THE MODEL: road = an OVERRIDE WALK. A coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge into it leaves a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there (own beats nearest fork ancestor beats the base). No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all — which is precisely why it neither collapses nor forces the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain (the R456 incomparable-is-first-class idiom the draft violated). Validated against every topology in the repo, including the two real stores the draft broke, which it leaves PASSING. THE SUBSTRATE FINDING (and the correction of my own false refute-first): the store CANNOT distinguish "W forks in FACTS ONLY and continues down the trunk" from "W forks and ENDS at its own beat" — both encode as forks_from with no edge set, and my draft silently reinterpreted the first as the second, which IS the 381. The resolution is not a new field but a DECLARATION-COMPLETENESS fail-loud that NAMES the ambiguity and hands the author the lever, so the default (undeclared = the trunk) is both correct and loudly named. That converts a LYING gate into an honest one at zero migration cost. Code 0. The build is R614, gated on ratification.

Round 614 — the ROAD axis built: names/l.decision_summary: The COORDINATE axis, BUILT to the R613 design — and the three deterministic gates R611 blinded are measurably un-blinded. `CanonOrder` was answering TWO different questions from one derived node set: PRECEDENCE ("can this world's order COMPARE a and b?") and ROAD ("which coordinates does it TRAVEL, and where does it END?"). R611 had to widen the first — that widening is MEASURED to have repaired four gates, including a disclosure leak that was passing at exit 0 — and in doing so it silently widened the second, which is what made `validate-render-fidelity` REWARD a render that delivered the trunk's ending and FLAG the faithful one, silenced R488's wrong-world-line guard past a fork, and put phantom scenes on the pinion seam. R614 splits them: `reach` keeps powering `le`/`comparable`, UNCHANGED and generous; a new `road` powers `names`/`linearize`/`is_maximal`, bounded. THE ROAD IS AN OVERRIDE WALK, not a bound: a coordinate is on W's road iff it is a declared SEED, or an edge reaches it FROM a coordinate ALREADY on the road, declared by the CLOSEST member branch declaring an out-edge there. A branch that declares its own successor at a shared coordinate REPLACES the inherited one; a branch that declares nothing CONTINUES its lineage's road. The `u is already on the road` requirement is what refuses the leak: a confluence legitimately declares a merge edge from EACH parent, so a SIBLING's exclusive coordinate is NAMED by a branch every downstream world belongs to — under a node-set union it leaks (the R611 defect, and the R613 draft's seed clause re-admitted it); under the override walk the edge simply cannot fire from a source the world never reaches. CRUCIALLY the road lineage is NOT `world_membership`: facts INTERSECT at a merge, roads UNION, and R612's intersect deletes the parents from a confluence's membership BY DESIGN — deriving the road from the fact lattice is what collapsed the refuted draft. No fact-bound is consulted on the road axis at all, which is also why it never asks the order to compare coordinates on a parallel chain, where they are legitimately incomparable rather than past. THE SUBSTRATE AMBIGUITY IS NAMED, NOT GUESSED: a branch that declares no road rides its lineage's road on, so its ENDING is the trunk's — correct for a world-line diverging only in FACTS, wrong for a divergent ending whose road was never declared, and the store cannot tell them apart. So `undeclared_roads` + a CLI NOTICE hands the author the lever instead of silently picking a reading. That is what keeps this NON-BREAKING: measured over 70 real store-times-order pairs, ZERO newly-rejecting — against 381 newly-rejected facts for the refuted draft on the same corpus. `is_maximal` now reads the road and `terminals()` returns the END SET, because a world-line legitimately has several ends.

Round 615 — evidence is a ROAD question:.decision_summary: Paying the debt R614 itself created, and closing the R613 review carry. R614 moved the R488 wrong-world-line guard onto the ROAD axis but left EVIDENCE reachability on `le` alone — and the two are ONE principle ("could this world have SEEN that scene?"), so a single rule was left carrying two different invariants: exactly the half-enforced-invariant trap this project forbids, and I introduced it one round earlier. PROVEN exploitable before fixing, not assumed: on the shipped R614 binary a fact on a divergent `ending` cited a scene that only its SIBLING travels, and the gate returned 0 violations — the generous precedence order still connects that scene, because a confluence declares a merge edge from EVERY parent. Both halves now ask the road. The naive tightening then DOUBLED the violation count on two real stores while naming ZERO additional facts, so the round also fixes the reporting: a fact whose OWN coordinate is off-road is already named by FactCanonOffBranch, and there is no world in which to ask "could it have seen that" when the beat itself is not on the road — the evidence axis stays quiet about it. Also closed: an ORPHANED ROAD EDGE (a declared edge whose source the branch never reaches) now fails LOUD instead of silently truncating a world-line, possibly at its own ending — 0 of 83 real pairs trip it, including the detroit store whose branch legitimately declares a road segment starting BEFORE its fork point. And the AUTHORING CONTRACT: describe-schema's `branches` registry now carries the world-line model a blind author cannot otherwise self-serve — the two axes and their DUAL merge behaviour (facts INTERSECT, roads UNION), that authoring a MERGE RELOCATES TRUNK OWNERSHIP onto the confluence, that the base `edges` ARE main's road while each `branches` entry is that world-line's own road segment, that a branch declaring no road inherits the TRUNK'S ENDING and what that costs at the render-fidelity gate, and that evidence is a road question — with a concept-pin test so the prose cannot drift off the code again, which is precisely how R611 and R614 went wrong. Finally, the R613 review asked for the merge-edge convention to be PINNED; having built the walk, the honest answer is that no pin is needed — the "you must GET there" requirement makes the choice unobservable — and the contract now says so rather than inventing a rule.

Round 615 — evidence is a ROAD question:.publishable_decision_summary: Paying the debt R614 itself created, and closing the R613 review carry. R614 moved the R488 wrong-world-line guard onto the ROAD axis but left EVIDENCE reachability on `le` alone — and the two are ONE principle ("could this world have SEEN that scene?"), so a single rule was left carrying two different invariants: exactly the half-enforced-invariant trap this project forbids, and I introduced it one round earlier. PROVEN exploitable before fixing, not assumed: on the shipped R614 binary a fact on a divergent `ending` cited a scene that only its SIBLING travels, and the gate returned 0 violations — the generous precedence order still connects that scene, because a confluence declares a merge edge from EVERY parent. Both halves now ask the road. The naive tightening then DOUBLED the violation count on two real stores while naming ZERO additional facts, so the round also fixes the reporting: a fact whose OWN coordinate is off-road is already named by FactCanonOffBranch, and there is no world in which to ask "could it have seen that" when the beat itself is not on the road — the evidence axis stays quiet about it. Round 616 — MNEMO-GAP-005 reviewed: both.decision_summary: MNEMO-GAP-005 (from the-tide-that-counts) asked for two things: a per-fact provenance facet (Canon/Invented/Structural) and a branch-owned-density projection. A cost-no-object review (three independent adversarial reviewers plus measurement against the real 827-fact consumer store) refuted BOTH designs before any build — the R613 pattern, where the refutation is the round's most valuable output. Density: the proposed denominator (own segment = road(B) minus the union of parent roads) collapses to EMPTY on every confluence, because a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix, so it is a divide-by-zero on a legal store — proven on the real R614 fixture. Provenance: measured against the real store, the trichotomy is the wrong shape because its two axes have opposite derivability and opposite granularity. STRUCTURAL (quest plumbing) is per-fact and fully derivable (typed quest predicates unioned with the completed_by->pays_off giving-setup binding the quest graph already computes) — verified to reproduce all 80 plumbing facts exactly with zero false-positives — so storing it would only duplicate the quest structure. CANON-vs-INVENTED is per-branch and genuinely NOT derivable (branch != main mislabels the 543 canonical weave confluence facts, 66 percent of the store), but it is adaptation-fidelity metadata — vacuous for an original work and the same class the gap itself defers as out-of-charter for its canon-manifest denominator. Owner decision C: derive structural natively (zero schema) and keep canon-vs-invented consumer-side, consistent with the north-star (original-work authoring; adaptation fidelity is a consumer concern like SCE). The per-fact trichotomy is dropped; density lands corrected (own-declared-segment denominator, road-consistent numerator, Option for the empty-own-segment signal). This is a code-0 design round; R617 builds density and R618 builds the derived structural coverage split.
changes_bullets: REJECTED the gap's per-fact provenance facet (`NarrativeFact.provenance {Canon,Invented,Structural}`): three independent adversarial reviewers plus measurement against the real 827-fact consumer store converged that it is the wrong shape — it stores the one thing that is fully derivable and mis-locates the one thing that is not, per-fact, with a `canon_from` naming collision. No `NarrativeFact` schema change lands.

STRUCTURAL (quest plumbing) is DERIVED, not stored: `structural = (typed.predicate in {pursues,requires,completed_by}) UNION (an Expected fact paid off by a completed_by-typed fact)` — the same completed_by->pays_off giving-setup binding `quest_graph` already computes (R559/R568). Storing it would duplicate the quest structure and could drift; deriving it is exact.

CANON-vs-INVENTED stays CONSUMER-SIDE (owner decision C): it is a real per-world-line property but genuinely NOT soundly derivable, and it is adaptation-fidelity metadata (vacuous for an original work) — the same class the gap itself defers as out-of-charter in its canon-manifest denominator. Charter = original-work authoring; adaptation fidelity is a consumer concern (the SCE precedent). Considered and set aside: `Branch.canonical: bool` (a per-branch, byte-stable native home) — declined as out-of-charter under decision C, recorded for revisit if the charter scope changes.

The §3b density projection is corrected before build: the gap's denominator (own segment = `road(B) \ union(parent roads)`) collapses to EMPTY on every confluence (a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix, so `road(C)` is a subset of the parents' union), which is a divide-by-zero on a legal store. Ratified replacement: denominator = the world's OWN DECLARED road segment (a new `CanonOrder` field + `own_road_segment` accessor over the private per-branch edge set), numerator road-consistent (facts with `branch==B` whose `canon_from` is in that own segment), `density: Option<f64>` = None for an empty own segment (a facts-only / undeclared-road divergence that rides the trunk — a signal, never 0 or infinity), main as the baseline.

AFFIRMED: no `set-fact-provenance` (or any per-field fact setter) — facts have no per-field setters; add/import/amend all route the single `build_candidate_fact` (R305 parity), and a setter would be a second write path bypassing it.
verification_bullets: The density divide-by-zero was PROVEN, not assumed: computed the gap's `road(B) \ parent-roads` against the real R614 fixture `road_axis_override_walk_bounds_each_world_line` — the confluences `weave1` and `weave2` both yield an EMPTY own segment (their entire road is inherited from parents), so `owned/0.0` = NaN/inf, a serialize-or-lie failure on a valid store (the R613 failure mode: the gate that exists to catch silent wrong answers producing one).

STRUCTURAL derivation verified against the real consumer store (the-tide-that-counts, 827 facts): the derived predicate reproduces all 80 id-regex plumbing facts EXACTLY — 0 missed, 0 false-positive; and of 43 `Expected` setups, the 22 give-setups classify structural while the 21 genuine Chekhov setups do not. So deriving structural is exact, no schema needed.

CANON-vs-INVENTED non-derivability verified on the same store: `branch != main` = 639 facts but the consumer's invented set = 96 (braid + ending); the 543 `weave-*` facts are `converges_from` confluences = CANONICAL re-convergent threads, so a branch-based derivation would mislabel 66% of the store. Fork-vs-confluence topology aligns today but is fragile (`weave-firstcall` converges FROM the invented `braid-firstcall`), so it is not a sound derivation either — the axis must be declared, not inferred.

Three independent adversarial reviewers converged separately (charter/provenance, density road-model, derivation-sufficiency), each citing real source and, for the store measurements, the real consumer store; the two store measurements above were re-verified independently before this entry.
carry_forward_bullets: NEXT R617 = BUILD the corrected §3b density: the `own_road_segment` accessor (new `CanonOrder` field computed in `from_declaration`), the `BranchDensity` report carrying owned_facts / own_scene_facts / own_road_scenes / `density: Option<f64>` beside the `undeclared_roads` flag, wired into `authoring_frontier_report`; regression-locked on the R614 road fixtures (every confluence gets a non-empty own segment or an honest None, never a divide-by-zero).

NEXT R618 = BUILD the derived §3a coverage split: `scene_coverage` gains a derived `structural` count (typed-quest UNION completed_by->pays_off) beside `fact_count`; canon-vs-invented is NOT added (decision C — consumer-side). Zero `NarrativeFact` schema change.

CONSUMER REPORT (the-tide-that-counts): the provenance facet is declined (structural is derivable exactly; canon-vs-invented is out-of-charter adaptation fidelity, kept consumer-side); the coverage-honesty need is served by the derived structural split; the density projection lands corrected (own-declared-segment + Option) and is NOT claimed to match the external coverage.py divisor (that tool was not shared).

Round 617 — branch-owned density built:.decision_summary: Builds the corrected §3b density from R616's ratified design. The frontier now reports, per world-line, how much it OWNS on the road it DECLARED itself (own_scene_facts / own_road_scenes) versus the prefix it inherits — so a divergent world that looks full by inheritance but owns little is visible. The denominator is the world's own declared road segment (a new CanonOrder field + own_road_segment accessor), NOT the gap's road(B) minus the union of parent roads, which collapses every confluence to empty (a converging parent forward-inherits the merge suffix) and divides by zero on a legal store. The numerator is scoped to that same own segment, so a fact at the shared fork coordinate is counted in owned_facts but never inflates the density (the R613 fact/road dual-axis trap). An empty own segment yields density None (a facts-only or undeclared-road divergence riding the trunk — a signal, never 0 or infinity), distinguished by own_road_declared. Proven end-to-end on the real merged consumer store: no divide-by-zero, main a 3.62 baseline over the divergent endings' 0.83-2.08, weave-ledger 15.42 versus a facts-only weave-firstcall reporting None. The numbers are honest per world but are deliberately NOT claimed to match the consumer's external coverage.py divisor (that tool was not shared).

A subset of the road, computed in `from_declaration` beside it, EMPTY for a branch that declares no road (an undeclared_roads world riding the trunk).

AuthoringFrontierReport gains `branch_owned_density: BTreeMap<String, BranchDensity>` (main + every registered branch): owned_facts (all facts branch==B), own_scene_facts (branch==B AND canon_from on the OWN segment — road-consistent, so an inherited-prefix or shared-fork-coordinate fact never inflates it), own_road_scenes (own segment size), density = Option<f64> (own_scene_facts / own_road_scenes, None when the own segment is empty), own_road_declared. A pure read, not fed into total_gaps.

Round 619 — cost-no-object review of R61.decision_summary: An owner-requested cost-no-object review (three independent adversarial reviewers — SSOT/structure, north-star/cost, correctness/silent-fail — plus self-audit) held R617-R618 to the lifetime-portfolio bar where a smell or silent-fail is a defect. It found real defects a solo self-review had passed clean. Sharpest: the R617 density metric measured the WRONG question — its own-declared-segment denominator hid the very 'looks full by inheritance' dilution the gap was filed to surface (on the real store the divergent endings read nearly as dense as the trunk, and a fact-rich facts-only world read a confusing None), and it carried a correctness bug (a branch declaring an edge into its inherited attach coordinate counted that coordinate as own, a silent 2x error on a legal store). Both are fixed by dividing owned facts by the FULL traversed road instead, which also let the entire own_road machinery be deleted (net -304 lines). Second: structural_fact_ids duplicated quest_graph's giving-setup rule and had ALREADY diverged (flat vs kind:quest-gated) — fixed by extracting one shared kernel quest_giving_setups both call. Also: the structural coverage is now exposed as a flat fact-id set (not only a per-scene count) so the consumer can join it per-fact and retire its heuristic; the R618 structural test was vacuous on the Expected guard and is rewritten to lock all three guards; the MCP tool description is updated. Verified end-to-end on the real store: divergent forks now read low (0.12-0.47) against main 2.94, structural_facts = 80 matching the consumer's plumbing set. R617's committed entry stays as the audit trail of what was first built; this records the correction.
changes_bullets: Density denominator corrected: `owned_facts / |full road traversed|` (`linearize(B).len()`) replaces R617's own-declared-segment. The own-segment version measured the WRONG question — it divided by the handful of scenes a world declared, hiding the long inherited span that IS the "looks full by inheritance" dilution the gap wanted flagged (a divergent world read nearly as dense as the trunk; a fact-rich facts-only world read a confusing "rides the trunk" None). The full traversed road surfaces dilution (a world riding a long road owning little reads LOW) and is bug-free.

REMOVED the own_road machinery entirely (field + own_road_of + own_road_segment accessor + its test): besides measuring the wrong signal it had a correctness bug — a branch declaring an edge INTO its inherited attach coordinate (the shape R615's own error message invites) counted that inherited coordinate as own, a silent 2x error on a legal store. The full-road denominator needs none of it. BranchDensity is now {owned_facts, road_scenes, density: Option<f64>} (None only for a store with no order).

SSOT: extracted `quest_giving_setups` as the SINGLE home of "a quest's giving setup is an Expected fact its own completed_by fact pays off (gated on kind:quest)". `quest_graph` (per-quest index) and `structural_fact_ids` (union) both read it, so they can no longer disagree — the R618 duplication had ALREADY diverged (structural was flat, quest_graph gated on kind:quest), a real "one semantic, two resolvers, divergent answers" defect.

`structural_facts` (the flat structural fact-id set) now rides the frontier report beside the per-scene `scene_coverage.structural` count, so a consumer can JOIN it to each fact's branch and actually RETIRE its external id-prefix heuristic (a per-scene aggregate alone could not be joined per-fact). MCP tool description updated for the new report fields.
verification_bullets: Density on the REAL consumer store (827 facts) now surfaces the gap's signal: the divergent forks read LOW (braid 0.12-0.17, ending 0.27-0.47) against main 2.94 — a 6-10x deficit where R617's own-segment version read a signal-hiding 2-4x; the fact-rich confluence weave-firstcall reads 3.78, not the confusing "n/a rides trunk". structural_facts = 80, matching the per-scene structural sum exactly (the consumer's id-regex plumbing set).

Rewritten ops density test locks the R619 shape end-to-end through authoring_frontier_report: main density > 1.0 (facts-per-scene, legitimate), a CONFLUENCE gets a real Some density (the own-segment version's fatal divide-by-zero case), a facts-only/undeclared divergence gets a real Some density (never the confusing None).

Rewritten structural test locks the THREE guards the R618 test missed (it was vacuous on the Expected guard): an Unmarked fact a completion pays off is NOT a giving (Expected guard), a completed_by fact whose subject is not a registered quest binds no giving (kind:quest gate = the shared kernel, so structural agrees with quest_graph), and a genuine Chekhov setup is not structural. The 3 quest_graph tests still pass (the SSOT refactor is behaviour-preserving).
The fix SIMPLIFIED the code: -304 / +183 lines. green: mnemosyne-validate 293 lib, cargo test --workspace, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, fmt --all --check.
carry_forward_bullets: The cost-no-object review was done by THREE independent adversarial reviewers (SSOT/structure, north-star/cost, correctness/silent-fail) plus self-audit — and they found real defects a solo self-review had passed clean (the wrong-question density, the own_road bug, the SSOT divergence, the vacuous test). This is the standing lesson: independent adversarial review is required at this bar, not optional.

Round 620 — discoverability defects: the.decision_summary: The first playable consumer (the-tide-that-counts: 852-fact store, running branching VN) filed a field report concluding Mnemosyne lacked world-state, player projection, carrier semantics, open predicates, and a map — and was wrong 7/7, rebuilding ~1,100 lines of Python outside the store. Reviewed adversarially: the count is 9, not 7 (the report also missed QUEST_PRED_REQUIRES = the declarative prerequisite, and its own claim that no round ever discussed fact-to-fact derivation is refuted by R493, which PoC-tested a causes edge and REFUTED it on data). The report's thesis is therefore CONFIRMED and its evidence is the proof: this is a DISCOVERABILITY failure, not a capability gap. Measured causes, all Mnemosyne-side and all mechanical: (1) the CLI bare-invocation usage string was a second hand-maintained command list that had drifted to omit every narrative verb (validate-continuity, describe-schema, report-playable-world, report-quest-graph, report-typing-candidates) while still naming 52, so it read exhaustive; (2) the auto-loaded MCP onboarding resources affirmatively taught that the store has 4 closed-form entity types, citing a Round 60 that is off-main, a claim already stale by R273; (3) CLAUDE.md's own citation-hygiene protocol told agents to prefix-match round-NNN-- against list_sections, which returns spec sections only, so it answers does-not-exist for all 366 rounds; (4) README framed the narrative half as deferred future work and speculated primitives that were never built. The consumer was not careless: the documented onboarding path told them the substrate did not exist. DECISION: fix the front door, and kill the drift class rather than refresh its instances — no restated counts, point at describe-schema. R585 built describe-schema because THIS consumer reported THIS gap; it still did not reach them, so the fix is routing, not another artifact.

Round 623 — the doc gate: a documented v.decision_summary: The generalization R620 named and did not build, and R622 carried: a gate for the docs. R620 and R622 fixed real doc defects — a config key dead since Round 400 shipping in five copy-paste blocks ~220 rounds later, both READMEs' quickstart failing to parse, a CI example invoking a verb deleted with GENERATED.md, a _vN-banned identifier living inside two docs — and every one of them was found by a person reading. That is the same posture that let them rot in the first place, so the round is not done until the question is decided by a machine. Two questions about tracked docs are decidable and are now gated: a verb a reader is told to run must dispatch, and a mnemosyne.toml a reader is told to paste must parse through the real loader. The verb oracle is --help, which R622 made a projection of the COMMANDS table, so the gate cannot drift from dispatch. IT IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITSELF: both READMEs documented a CLI commit verb recording design-doc transactions to RocksDB column families — it has never dispatched, and mnemosyne-store is not even a CLI dependency. Three independent adversarial reviewers and two rounds of hand-sweeping missed it; the gate named it in one run. Getting it precise mattered more than getting it built: the first parser read cargo's own --force as a verb, the second cut --help to help, the third mis-paired fence backticks with prose, and the fourth silently MISSED the English commit mention because the inline span wrapped a line while catching the Korean one — an under-detecting verification path, the exact failure this arc condemns. A gate that cries wolf gets ignored and a gate that under-detects is worse than none, so both floors are counted and the non-vacuity is proven by injection.

Precision was again the hard part and again caught before landing: the first check would have falsely flagged [plugins] (documented as its subtable) and the two Vec sections (written [[name]]), and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored as surely as one that under-detects. Membership assertions are now tautological (the producer derives), so they are DELETED rather than re-pinned in the test — moving a hand-list from production into a test is not a fix. What is pinned instead is NOT tautological: vocabularies are non-empty (vacuity), every published class round-trips through serde, and every enum's `as_str()` AGREES with the serde tag the contract publishes — a live production mirror (receipts, CLI/MCP json) whose doc claims parity that nothing enforced until now.

Round 636 — the drift claim R631 made an.decision_summary: R636 pays the LAST defect from the owner's cost-no-object session review, and it is the one that stings most: R631 reintroduced the exact anti-pattern R629 had been paid to delete THREE ROUNDS EARLIER. R631 stated the quest object rule TWICE in the published contract — object_shape (prose) and required_object_kind (machine) — and asserted in a doc comment that "the two cannot drift" while binding them with NOTHING; R629's entire content was deleting three comments that claimed a drift-safety the code lacked. The drift is not cosmetic: describe-schema is the authority R620 designated after a consumer concluded seven present capabilities were absent, so prose reading "scalar" while the machine enforces entity teaches a shape the guard rejects — the same misleading-contract mechanism, same surface, same reason. FIXED BY A TEST THAT MAKES THE CLAIM TRUE rather than by softening the comment: quest_object_shape_prose_matches_the_enforced_kind asserts the prose NAMES the enforced kind, and for the None case (completed_by accepts entity OR scalar) that it names BOTH, so that arm is not half-vacuous. That limit is now in the code instead of hidden behind "by construction". The session review is fully paid (R634 R630's half-measure, R635 DEBT-H, R636 this). 960 tests, clippy-D 0, fmt.

MY THREE CLAIMS, ALL REFUTED BY EXPERIMENT, recorded because the refutation is the deliverable. (1) "FORCED": they use `withhold` ZERO times in all four plans (the default already withholds, so the arm never bound), and at the 5 TYPED player facts — where `first_at` was fully legal — they wrote the identical bare `state`. (2) "the disease is typed coverage": the leak gate's coverage of `player` is EXACTLY ZERO (`targeted=0`, since targeting is `withhold || first_at`), so typing all 852 facts moves it from 0 to 0; and `first_at` ("where the reader FIRST LEARNS it") is semantically inapplicable when the player's action decides when a fact is learned. (3) "a telling needs a render": three of five telling-consumers take one store with no re-extraction, the MCP contract calls playable-world render-free BY DESIGN, and they DID render it (`i18n.py:91-130`).

WHAT SURVIVES FROM MY RULING, and it is precise: the write predicate `mode == Withhold || has_first_at` (`atomic/lib.rs:5210-5212`) is the IDENTICAL boolean to the leak gate's targeting (`disclosure.rs:214`). The set of decisions the write path lets an untyped fact carry IS the set the gate skips. But the counterfactual refutes the causal reading — bypass the invariant, author an untyped `withhold`, and the gate STILL errors "un-gateable". The invariant is a messenger, not a cause; un-gateability is intrinsic to untypedness.

THEIR THREE OPTIONS, RULED: (a) a fifth `dug` mode — REFUTED, `imply` already IS that mode ("realised via an object/environment — the Dark-Souls item-text"), and the store's own numbers show the idiom split in half (21 `imply` uses across the reader plans with ZERO carriers; 11 carriers exclusively in `player`, which uses `imply` zero times). (c) "maybe it isn't a disclosure plan" — REFUTED on the premise, above. (b) a telling-level ACCESS/AGENCY flag — SURVIVES: mode (how plainly the telling commits) and access (must the audience act to get it?) are orthogonal axes the reader-centric vocabulary conflates. No measured fault forces it yet, so it is not licensed — recorded, not queued.

TWO LIVE DEFECTS, OURS, found independently by BOTH reviewers and reproduced by me: (1) a `withhold` override carrying a surface EMITS A LOCATOR with `mode: "withhold"` (verified: 7 locators for `f-original-sin`, `scene_ordinal: 17`) — no mode filter at the emission site. Their engine DELETED its withhold filter (17c1340, "Withheld facts emit no locator"), a premise true only because nobody has yet surfaced a withheld fact — so the story's core truth would print to the game screen through the map seam, past the leak gate. (2) `continuity.rs:3915` documents `locators` as "in walk order"; they are ordered by `canon_from` while each `scene_ordinal` is the surface's — an injected divergence inverted them (53→17). Both arm the moment `surface` is used for the carrier design it exists for.

THE DESIGN, licensed by measured fault, NOT BUILT THIS ROUND (code 0 by contract): derive the locator scene from `canon_from` when no surface is authored, gated on `mode != withhold`. It collapses 1,099 hand-copies to the 11 real carriers, makes all 7 of their historical drifts UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely detectable (R622: derivation, not detection), restores `surface` to the sparse override its own doc describes, and closes defect (1) in the same move.

REFUTED AS BUILDS, each measured rather than argued: `surface.object ∈ fact.entities` fires on 4 of 11 and its hits are the MOST correct uses (`ent-bunok` is the store's own designed leaker) — it would forbid the Dark-Souls model the field exists for; `surface == canon_from` as a GATE forbids the design it is meant to protect; scene-is-a-section and object-is-registered are already write-path invariants; off-road-surface is vacuous here (all 7 roads span all 66 scenes). It now says what it is and names the sort for anyone needing encounter order. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, named rather than implied: it does not answer the consumer's vocabulary question — `state` still means "the prose tells it" in a reader telling and "the audience digs it" in a player telling, and R642 ruled that unlicensed (no measured fault forces it; the access/agency axis stays recorded). Round 645 — DEBT-C ruled: typing the rej.decision_summary: R645 rules DEBT-C at code 0, and the ruling is that DEBT-C's own scoping — Round 629's "type the reject path, then invariants() DERIVES like the other five vocabularies" — is CATEGORY-CONFUSED. Two independent adversarial reviewers refuted my candidate typed-enum design before any build, converging on the same measured verdict from different angles, and I re-ran every load-bearing number. THE PARTITION KILLS THE DERIVE PREMISE. describe-schema publishes 13 named invariants; the write path carries ~150 distinct reject messages through AtomicMutateError::Validation (measured: 141 direct Validation construction sites + 72 Result<_,String> helper rejects funnelled in at the primitive boundary via .map_err(Validation)). The mapping is many-to-one AND two-thirds unmapped: ~30-40 narrative-fact ref-integrity messages fold into the 13 (evidence-provenance alone renders 7 distinct messages; registered-entities 3; pays-off-exists 4), while ~110 messages have NO invariant home at all (the ~10 --reason audit gates, ~13 section field-caps + Round-298 gates + mandatory fields, 8 binding-file path-normalization rules, entry_id/inventory/confirmation/normative_excerpt conformance, and the manifest wrappers that are recursive pass-throughs of an inner error). So the two horns are: a 13-variant enum whose Display cannot reproduce 150 messages (each variant becomes a sub-discriminated field-bag) and leaves ~110 sites on a catch-all String — reintroducing the stringly-typed reject for two-thirds of the surface; or a ~150-variant enum whose serde_variants yields 150 implementation-detail tags that are NOT the 13 curated kebab names, ballooning the contract from 13 teaching guarantees to 150 path-normalization rules and destroying its purpose. Neither is the five-vocabulary shape. THE CATEGORY ERROR, which is the real finding: for disclosure_mode/payoff_expectation/predicate_object_kind/rule_class/quest-predicates, THE ENUM IS THE DOMAIN — a field of that type can hold nothing but a variant, so serde_variants::<T>() is authoritative by construction, the type's inhabitants ARE the value set. There is NO type whose inhabitants are the invariants; the set being enumerated is "the conditions the write path chooses to reject," which lives in imperative control flow (the if cond { return Err } statements), not in any data type. An InvariantViolation enum is a labelling scheme laid over that control flow by hand — its variants are names an author HOPES correspond 1:1 to reject sites, and no compiler law forces either (i) every return Err to carry a distinct variant, or (ii) a variant's prose to match the condition it is attached to. Proven: a reviewer injected a genuinely new write-time reject (a SENTINEL check in build_candidate_fact) — it compiled clean, describe-schema stayed at 13 invariants, and the whole suite stayed green; but under the typed design the same reject could reuse any existing variant and escape identically, because nothing ties a variant's meaning to the if it tests. Typing the reject path would RELOCATE R629's "second mirror the compiler claims to force but doesn't" one level up, at ~150-site cost, while looking MORE authoritative because it is typed. Round 629 fixed the EASY case where the type was the domain; DEBT-C tried to generalize it to a case where the analogy breaks. THE GAP IS REAL BUT NOT R493-LICENSED FOR A BUILD. The reviewer's injection is redundant with the current state: the store already enforces ~150 rejects while publishing 13, and ~110 reject classes are already unpublished with the repo green — that is not a regression to catch, it is the standing shape of a curated contract. invariants() has drifted ZERO times: two deliberate edits in its life (R587 birth, R627 fix), never an accidental omission. The harm is bounded — every unlisted reject is FAIL-LOUD with an actionable message (surprise, not the silent wrong-vocabulary corruption R629 fixed) — and NO production code branches on the reject KIND: ops/lib.rs:424 binds Validation(msg) and wraps it verbatim, atomic_cli.rs:88 maps Validation(_) to "validation" and displays, and a grep for any .contains()/== on a Validation message is empty. So typing has zero measured consumer, and the classification motive (make it derive like the five) is category-confused. Both motives fail. THE RULING: DEBT-C as scoped is REJECTED and RE-SCOPED toward closure, not build. invariants() being hand-maintained is CORRECT for its kind — a curated documentation contract, categorically unlike the five closed-enum vocabularies — and Round 629's "then derive the invariant list" was the mis-generalization. IF drift-catching is later wanted, the honest artifact is NOT a typed enum and NOT sold as derivation: it is a small fail-loud pin giving the ~13 reference-integrity invariants a canonical id and asserting each reaches a live enforcement path (the continuity gate already re-checks these same refs out-of-band per invariant_enforcement, so that mapping has a second home) — ~13 lines, inherently hand-maintained, honest about being a behavioural guard over a curated summary rather than a derivation from a type. That pin is itself unlicensed today (zero measured drift) and is recorded, not built. The R305 field-invariant-parity discipline (two write paths on one field must enforce the same invariant set) is untouched and remains the real structural guard on the reject path; DEBT-C was never about that.

Round 646 — C1 refuted: a requires-cycle.decision_summary: R646 rules R637's catalogue item C1 (a quest-prerequisite acyclicity check) at code 0: REFUTE-AND-CLOSE as a validate-continuity gate. An independent adversarial reviewer refuted my candidate BUILD ruling before any build — the eighth first-design refutation of this arc — and the refutation is stronger than my case, because it convicts R637's own framing, which I had inherited. THE CATEGORY ARGUMENT R637 USED IS WRONG FOR requires, and that is the load-bearing finding. R637 said "a cycle is a contradiction (never legitimate, not even mid-draft)" and placed C1 in validate-continuity by the same line that puts SuccessionCycle there. But that intuition is succession's, borrowed without re-deriving it from requires' semantics. A SUCCESSION cycle is truth-corruption: supersedes_in_frame means "the older fact no longer holds", so A supersedes B and B supersedes A makes both facts simultaneously superseded — they sit in the store live-and-latest while silently never holding anywhere (continuity.rs:1244). There is no coherent authoring waypoint where that is valid; it is a genuine contradiction, and continuity gates it. A REQUIRES cycle is well-defined unsatisfiability, verified in source: requires is surfaced ONLY as `prerequisites` metadata on the quest node (continuity.rs:4446), and it does NOT feed quest-state computation — per-world state derives from giving-fact payoff coverage (:4416), and unresolved_quests fires only when a quest has no giving setup at all (:4374). So a requires-cycle where each quest has a discharger produces a completely uncorrupted result: the quests get their normal states and the cycle sits as declared-but-unsatisfiable prerequisite metadata. That is exactly why R637's own injection measured validate-continuity violations 0 AND why my minimal 2-cycle reproduction (q-a requires q-b, q-b requires q-a) exits 0 — nothing is silently false, the store's meaning is simply "these quests are mutually blocked / never openable", which is unsatisfiability, the same genus as a dangling prerequisite that continuity DELIBERATELY tolerates ("a WIP story has dangling setups by definition", :2903). By continuity's OWN stated line — GATES CONTRADICTIONS and REPORTS INCOMPLETENESS — a requires-cycle falls on the REPORT side. R637 put it on the gate side by misclassifying it, and its ruling is internally contradictory: R637 says the play-readiness class (C2 obligation-with-no-discharger, C4 unsatisfiable-precondition) cannot be folded into validate-continuity without breaking the WIP-green contract, yet says C1 belongs in validate-continuity today — the ONLY distinguisher is "cycle = contradiction", and removing it relocates C1 next to C2/C4 in the unbuilt play-readiness class. A requires-cycle ("these quests can't open") is a strict sibling of C2 ("this quest can't be discharged"); gating one while parking the other outside is incoherent. R493 ALREADY RULED THIS EXACT CLASS, and it postdates the sibling precedent: "The only net-new piece (a causal cycle among non-succession facts) is unmeasured, YAGNI" — verbatim in the Round 493 entry. A requires-cycle is a causal cycle among non-succession facts; R493 governs it directly and defers it. The sibling-precedent ground fails too: canon-order and the branch forest are acyclic BY CONSTRUCTION (the mutate API literally cannot express the bad state — continuity.rs:145 "a cyclic declaration is no order"; forks immutable), which is impossible-states-unrepresentable at the type/construction level, not a runtime gate; requires is the opposite, a free-form author-drawn edge the API is designed to let you write (R637's own "the only one an author draws freely"). Making it unrepresentable needs a runtime gate that fires DURING authoring, colliding with the WIP-green contract. And a mid-draft requires-cycle is plausible in a way a mid-draft succession-cycle is not: an author wiring q-a requires q-b, then adding q-b requires q-a while restructuring a mutual dependency, produces a momentary loop = "neither opens yet" = incomplete wiring, not a contradiction. THE RULING: C1 as a validate-continuity acyclicity gate is REFUTED and CLOSED. It is not a contradiction (metadata-only, uncorrupted), it breaks WIP-green (fires during authoring), R493's measured-fault clause is unmet (zero cycles in the sole consumer's 852-fact store; their own knots.py already carries the check, so building it in Mnemosyne unblocks no one), and it fails even by R637's own contradiction-vs-incompleteness line. If anything is ever built it is a REPORT in the play-readiness class — surface a mutually-blocked prerequisite set as an unsatisfiability finding in report-quest-graph, alongside C2/C4 — designed as that named class when an author-claims-DONE gate is actually wanted, never a continuity reject and not as a one-off ahead of the class it belongs to (the scattershot "fix the next thing we tripped over" R633/R637 warned against). One correction to R637's catalogue, forward (R637 is frozen): its C1 row calls the requires-cycle "total silence — write path ACCEPTS, validate-continuity exit 0, report-quest-graph unresolved_quests=[]". The silence is not total: a cyclic quest with no discharger already surfaces in unresolved_quests, and even with dischargers the prerequisites metadata is present in report-quest-graph — what is absent is a NAMING of the cycle qua cycle, which is a report-shaped gap in the unbuilt play-readiness class, not a missing continuity gate.

THE CAUSE: Rust's exhaustiveness only fires on a `match` OVER the type. `TypedObject::from_exclusive_args` (narrative.rs:453) matches `(Option<String>, Option<String>)`, NOT `TypedObject` — it CONSTRUCTS the enum, so its input never changes when a variant is added and its 2x2 match stays exhaustive and green. The arity `2` is a HAND COPY of the variant count, and it is the exact shape R448 consolidated ("both surfaces had hand-rolled copies") without ever DERIVING. So the compiler forces every READER and zero WRITERS, and the write surface (CLI flag, MCP field, published JsonSchema) is where a leg's whole value lives. Round 665 — the charter ruling refuted 3.decision_summary: R665 IS THE CHARTER RULING R663 DEMANDED, WRITTEN, SENT TO THREE INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWERS, AND REFUTED 3/3 — my third design killed before build in this arc (R625's ancestor, R659, this), and the third time I was confident. THE REFUTATION IS THE ROUND; the ruling is not repaired here because what killed it is worth more than what it claimed. THE DRAFT SAID: R663's question ("do closed-world assertions belong in the substrate, or does the sparse-frame ethos forbid them?") carries a false premise — the ethos is scoped to facts-in-a-frame, registries are already closed-world, invariant 4 routes rather than bans, and the hole is one missing primitive, DECLARED COMPLETENESS. Five of its six claims fell, from three lenses that never spoke to each other. CLAIM 1 IS REFUTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN WORDS, in the SSOT: R442 generalised the ethos to the DISCOURSE axis BY NAME — `narrative.rs:498-500` "absence of marking is unrecorded, never an assertion that the fact is not a setup (the sparse-frame ethos applied to the discourse axis)", echoed at `narrative.rs:634-636` for disclosure, and R442's own ledger says "the sparse-frame ethos on the discourse axis". My narrow reading was of a sentence the project had already generalised in core, twice. R663 WAS DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT AND CITED THE WRONG SENTENCE — the ethos is real and broader than the sparse-frame line, and correcting the citation does not touch the finding. CLAIM 3 IS AN EQUIVOCATION AND MONOTONICITY KILLS IT: the closed-world assumption is NON-monotonic (an eighth knot must retract "exactly seven"); a registry is MONOTONIC (`add-entity` never invalidates a passing store), and the reject message itself says "add-frame first" — a set whose own violation tells you to extend it on demand is not closed. I also cherry-picked "[load-bearing]" as though it qualified all registries: `entities` is `load_bearing: false` (`schema.rs:556`), and entities is exactly the registry "exactly seven knots" and "every object has a name" run through. CLAIM 5 DIED THREE WAYS — I found it myself before the reviewers reported, and both of them found it independently: the `exclusive` arm (`continuity.rs:2565-2600`) fires only when TWO PRESENT FACTS co-hold, so "at most one" is MAX-cardinality, satisfied VACUOUSLY BY THE EMPTY SET, while every assertion the consumer needs is MIN-cardinality (exactly-seven, every-knot-has-a-mouth). R449 is precedent for the opposite half, and its own interval sibling is precedent AGAINST me: an absent operand returns `Unverifiable`, never `Violated`. MY OPERATIVE CLAUSE WOULD HAVE FORECLOSED WHAT ALREADY SHIPS: I ruled the declaration must live in "a DECLARED artifact naming registry ids, never as core schema" — but `CoverageExpectation` and `PayoffExpectation` are BOTH L0 core schema enums and inv4 holds for both. The charter's real test is MEDIUM-NEUTRALITY, not artifact-externality; my ruling would have banned the shape two of the three shipped instances use. CLAIM 4 SURVIVED, and it is the only survivor: all nine inv4 citations route or scope, none bans — `continuity.rs:655-658` "Rule semantics are game/world vocabulary and never enter L0 … the artifact arrives declared" is a destination. AND THE PREMISE UNDER ALL OF IT IS FACTUALLY FALSE, WHICH IS THE FINDING: "we record only PRESENCE" has been untrue since ROUND 269. `CoverageExpectation::Normative` (an L0 core enum) + no covering binding => `NormativeGap` => `ImplementationMissing` => `severity_coverage.unwrap_or(severity_binding)` => default REJECT. That is negation-as-failure, gated, default-reject, running for ~400 rounds; R589's `zero_fact_scenes` ("sections with no fact anchored") is the absent-REFERENCE class over the section registry, also shipped. The declared-expectation-plus-coverage family has shipped THREE TIMES and the code counts them itself (`disclosure.rs:36-40`: "the THIRD coverage instance after the spec axiom (R389/R390) and payoff (R442)"), and R663's own carry NAMED the primitive in a parenthetical I never cited ("a declared-completeness primitive: 'these are all of them, and the gate enforces it'"). THE FINDING MY DRAFT NEVER REACHED, and the reason this round is worth its commit: R442 ALREADY CONTEMPLATED THIS EXACT GATE AND PARKED IT AS A RECORDED REVISIT TRIGGER — verbatim, "Dangling is deliberately never gated — a WIP story has dangling setups by definition; the dangling list IS the author's todo list, and A RELEASE-TIME NO-DANGLING GATE STAYS CONSUMER-PULL", repeated by R449 ("release-time gates stay consumer-pull"). SO THE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, ON THE TWO AXES: spec coverage GATES at default-reject (R269, "Active = backed by code"); narrative coverage REPORTS (R442, "a WIP story has dangling setups by definition"). Same shape, opposite enforcement, two published rationales that cannot both be the principle. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE CHARTER CONFLICT, and my draft declared it nonexistent while walking past it. R663'S GAME IS THE RELEASE-TIME CONSUMER R442 NAMED, so the parking condition is FIRED — but note the trap before anyone rules on it: parking the NORTH STAR behind "consumer-pull" is itself the mis-framing this project has recorded as a recurring error (the game is the north star, not an external consumer we wait on). RECORDED, NOT RULED. AND THE MEASURED FINDING THAT RE-PRICES THE BOARD, a reviewer's and new: THE CONSUMER ALREADY BUILT R662's CANDIDATE RESOLUTION THEMSELVES — `map.json` as the source, a DERIVED `narrative-rules.json` naming only entity ids, gated by our substrate, their `map.json` law reading "노드는 잎만이다" because `exclusive(per:subject)` breaks with containers — AND IT HAS NEVER RUN ONCE: `rules_path` grep = 0 in their toml, no real `validate-continuity` call in their build, `.githooks/` = `commit-msg` only. THE CHARTER WAS NEVER THEIR BLOCKER. ONE TOML LINE WAS. And the route I called "paved twice" has ZERO live adopters including US: our own `mnemosyne.toml` has no `[continuity]` table and no hook or CI wires `validate-continuity` — a fact I ran and READ during R664 without seeing it. THE BOTTLENECK IS ADOPTION AND NON-VACUITY, NOT PERMISSION. Finally, the hand-list trap I nearly walked into: "exactly seven knots" is DERIVED from the store today by the consumer ("knots.py 가 스토어에서 도출한다"), so my declared-completeness artifact would have replaced a DERIVED ORACLE WITH A HAND-LIST — the anti-pattern this project already rules against and whose rot R663 measured on `cast-aliases.json`. Code 0.

My draft claimed road coverage already shipped as R596's `unordered_scenes` and the build would be a duplicate. It does not. R596 filters `n > 0` (FACT-BEARING; its question is renderability, so an empty unplaced scene is deliberately out), and `zero_fact_scenes` filters on content with NO placement predicate at all — so an EMPTY unplaced section was computed NOWHERE and sat in `zero_fact_scenes` indistinguishable from a PLACED empty. R663 injected a BARE `add-section`; I injected one WITH A FACT, got `unordered scenes (1)`, and declared the prior round wrong. On R663's own store with R663's own injection the frontier answers `unordered_scenes = []`. THE REFUTATION WAS IN MY OWN FIRST MEASUREMENT — I ran the bare case, read `unordered scenes: none` beside `zero-fact scenes (1): sc-orphan`, and counted the zero-fact hit as "the capability exists". It is not: `zero_fact_scenes` has no placement axis (proven — `pro-part1`/`pro-part2` are order nodes and sit in the same bucket). THE BUILD: `AuthoringFrontierReport.unplaced_scenes` = `section ∈ registry ∧ ∉ order.nodes()`, content-independent, the placement axis that had no owner; `unordered_scenes` is now DERIVED from it (one resolver); NOT in `total_gaps` (`zero_fact` ⊎ `unordered` partition on `fact_count` and their union covers it — adding it would double-count). Plus `ContinuityReport.sections`, so `validate-continuity` prints `order_nodes=66/67 sections` instead of the lone number that misled R663, with a notice pointing at `unplaced scenes`. REPORT, NOT GATE, and NOT on R442's consumer-pull parking (which R666 buried and my draft reinstated): `FactCanonOffBranch` tolerates the orderless/forward-declared mode over the SAME predicate — a fact sitting AT an unpositioned coordinate is deliberately not flagged, so rejecting the store FOR that section being unplaced would be incoherent. The opposite direction rejecting (`check_store_boundary`) is not a counter: the code says why at its own site — a dangling reference makes the store UNEVALUABLE (`Err`, not a violation), while an unplaced section is INCOMPLETE and nothing breaks. TWO REVIEWERS, TWO KILLS, BOTH MINE TO OWN. Cut 1's notice counted 3 and pointed at a report showing 1 ("its counts are narrower" — false, 3 > 1); I generalised its wording from `belvoir-loop`, whose `zero_fact_scenes = []` makes the split look exact BY CONFOUND. Cut 2 fired on MNEMOSYNE'S OWN SPEC STORE — "5 sit on no declared road", 100% of sections, under a gate the line above declares DISABLED, for a store with no scenes; SCE's ~370 spec sections are the same shape. Both siblings are self-limiting (R614 needs a registered branch, R491 a declared interval rule); mine had no guard. I measured four FINISHED NARRATIVE stores and never ran the probe against the SPEC half of the co-equal north star — the same measurement blind spot twice, relocated from the notice's pointer to its audience. NAME: `off_road_scenes` was wrong and a reviewer caught it — this reads `order.nodes()`, the PRECEDENCE union, and reading a road off that node set IS the R611 defect; worse, `WorldManuscript.sections_off_road` (R456/R615) already owns "off road" for the PER-WORLD axis (`linearize`), so the two would have collided head-on. `unplaced` matches the code's own word (`positioned`). AND R663's LABEL WAS LOOSE: sections are "the medium's DISCOURSE order" (`describe-schema`), while the game's GEOGRAPHY is DEBT-J's weighted spatial map over entity-places, which R662 measured absent ("`MapLocator` IS NOT A SPATIAL MAP AND ITS NAME MISLEADS"). This closes a real hole; it is not the geography fault.

THE WIRE IS DELIBERATELY NOT deny_unknown_fields, AND THIS IS WHERE R668 DIED: the real map.json's FIRST key is `note`, and it carries `law`/`modes`/`unit`/`open` — prose plus DEBT-J cost vocabulary this gate does not read. Round 673.decision_summary: R673 removes the file-based map gate of R670-672 and records the ruling that supersedes it. A cost-no-object review (four independent adversarial reviewers + consumer e2e, per the owner's standing preference) found the map gate built on the wrong foundation: a separate map.json file the store cannot reconstruct, holding adjacency the substrate already models as entity-to-entity typed facts, and porting only the gates while leaving build-map.py's derivation (edges to transition rules) unported — so a consumer would still have to run the Python. The owner ruled: everything the map holds (adjacency, entrance, containers) must be STORE FACTS, no Python, no derived file, enforced as store invariants. Feasibility measured before removing: adjacency is the identical shape to the store's existing requires/pursues/pred-at facts and needs no new substrate. The R670-672 ledger entries are left standing (frozen, append-only); this supersedes them in prose. The store-native rebuild follows, each round measured against the real store.

WHY THE FILE MODEL WAS THE WRONG FOUNDATION (the SSOT reviewer's finding, verified): the North Star is that every artifact is a PROJECTION of the one fact substrate, never a second authoritative store. `map.json` was the opposite — a hand-authored primary input the store cannot reconstruct, holding adjacency that the substrate ALREADY models (entity→entity typed facts: `requires`/`pursues`/`pred-at` are exactly this shape today). Adjacency `adjacent(place, place)` is the identical shape and needs NO new substrate — it goes into the store today.

Round 678.decision_summary: R678 closes cost-audit retreat #3 — the CLI-to-MCP authoring-surface parity gap. A full diff (not the truncated spot-check) found the AI-first MCP surface missing two MUTATE verbs the CLI has: remove-section and set-section-decision-status, so an MCP-only agent (the Phase-0 north star) could create and edit sections but neither remove one nor transition its lifecycle. Adding set-section-decision-status surfaced a deeper defect: its two forward-pointer guards (superseding only for superseded, resolving only for open) lived ONLY in the CLI while the atomic write path silently dropped a mismatched pointer — so the new MCP path would have been LOOSER than the CLI (the two-write-paths-different-invariants anti-pattern). This round homes both guards in atomic::set_section_decision_status so both surfaces enforce the identical set, adds a shared DecisionStatus::from_tag so CLI and MCP parse the status vocabulary through one resolver, adds the two MCP tools, and pins the guard parity with an atomic test. The remaining CLI-only verbs (validate-*, import-epub-*, import-sections, propose-implementations, spec-side report-*) are dev/ops/spec-pipeline, not the narrative-authoring surface — CLI-only by design. #2 (migration verb) and #4 (MCP integration smoke) remain.

changes_bullets: handle_result (atomic_cli.rs) error branch: was `print_error(&e, json); Err(anyhow!("{}", e))` — the detail printed here AND reprinted by the top-level anyhow handler in main. Now `print_error(&e, json); Err(AlreadyReported.into())`: print_error stays the SOLE formatter (json blob, or the FAILED header + detail).

New `pub struct AlreadyReported` marker error in atomic_cli — carries no message, impls Display/Error; its only role is to be recognised by `downcast_ref` so the top-level handler suppresses its generic reprint while the process still exits non-zero. The standard "already reported" CLI pattern: one owner of the mutate error print, not a fragile empty-string sentinel.

main error arm: prints `error: {:#}` only when `downcast_ref::<atomic_cli::AlreadyReported>()` is None. Every NON-mutate error path (arg parse, config lookup, store load) is unchanged and still prints through main.

changes_bullets: New MCP tools import_facts + import_sections (mnemosyne-mcp) — the transactional batch authoring the surface lacked. import_facts parses a FactsManifest, import_sections a JSON array of SectionImport, then each runs the ONE atomic primitive (atomic::import_facts / import_sections) inside run_mutate, so an MCP-only agent authors a whole scene all-or-nothing; N separate add_* calls are non-atomic and a mid-sequence failure leaves a partial store.

The manifest is passed as a JSON STRING (ImportFactsArgs.manifest_json / ImportSectionsArgs.manifest_json), not a typed schemars field, so the atomic crate keeps its serde-only manifest types and takes NO schemars dependency (correct layering — schemars lives only in mnemosyne-mcp). The tool parses the same shape the CLI import-facts / import-sections read.

Parse failures map to AtomicMutateError::Validation with a shape hint; the atomic primitive owns every content invariant (per-row validation, divergent-rejects-whole-manifest atomicity) exactly as on the CLI.

Round 688.decision_summary: R688 pays DEBT-DUP-REGISTRY (registered R683): fact registry-ref validation was two hand-maintained copies (the write path build_candidate_fact/build_typed_claim, and the out-of-band detector store_registry_violations). A shared fact_ref_resolves (the one place that knows how each facet resolves) and fact_registry_refs (the one enumeration) are now single-copy; the detector iterates them and the write path resolves through the same resolver. FactRefFacet::ALL plus three tests (an enumeration-completeness test and both parity tests asserting their cases cover ALL) bind the write path's hand-enumeration to the enumeration, so a new ref cannot land on one path and silently skip the other — the drift is caught structurally. An independent adversarial reviewer ran BEFORE commit and found the first cut OVERCLAIMED the drift-kill (write path did not consume the enumeration; the parity tests were hand-listed and the test comment was false) plus a LOW within-fact ordering shift; both fixed here, not downplayed. Round 5 of the owner sweep.
changes_bullets: New shared `fact_registry_refs(&NarrativeFact) -> Vec<(FactRefFacet, String)>` — the ONE enumeration of every registry ref a fact carries (frame, branch, entities, canon_from, canon_to, evidence, and the typed predicate/subject/object legs) — plus `fact_ref_resolves(store, facet, value)`, the ONE place that knows HOW each facet resolves (branch via is_known_world, canon/evidence against sections, predicate against the predicate registry). The resolver was "how each facet resolves" duplicated across the write path and the detector; it is now single-copy.

store_registry_violations (the out-of-band detector) rewritten to iterate fact_registry_refs + fact_ref_resolves, its byte-stable messages moved to store_registry_ref_message. The two non-resolution structural checks (evidence non-empty; a typed entity leg listed in entities) stay explicit.

The write path (build_candidate_fact + build_typed_claim's check_entity_leg) resolves frame / branch / entities / canon_from / canon_to / evidence / typed subject+object through the SAME fact_ref_resolves instead of raw contains_key / is_known_world. Author-guiding messages unchanged. The typed predicate keeps its inline `.get()` (needs the declaration for the object-shape check); fact_ref_resolves(TypedPredicate) is its parity-guarded twin.

FactRefFacet::ALL is the facet authority. Three tests bind the two paths to it structurally (not by discipline — the fix for the review's overclaim finding): fact_registry_refs_enumerates_every_facet asserts a fully-populated fact emits every facet; both parity tests (detector + write-path) assert their corruption cases cover exactly ALL. A variant added to the enum forces an exhaustive resolver arm + message arm (compile) AND a push in fact_registry_refs (enumeration test) AND a case in BOTH parity tests — so a ref cannot land on one path and silently skip the other.

fact_registry_refs emits in the pre-Round-688 detector order (frame, branch, entities, canon_from, canon_to, evidence, typed) so the first-violation slice check_store_boundary surfaces is unchanged for a single-corruption fact (the review's LOW ordering finding).
verification_bullets: An INDEPENDENT adversarial reviewer read the diff byte-for-byte against the removed lines, traced both consumers (check_store_boundary, validate_workspace), and ran the parity tests. Verdict: NO runtime correctness bug — no loosening (every write-path resolution rerouted 1:1, no check dropped), no missed corruption (the membership decomposition reproduces the old set exactly), no message drift (detector arms byte-identical, write-path messages untouched). It also found TWO real things, both addressed here rather than downplayed.

FINDING 1 (the substantive one): my first cut OVERCLAIMED the drift-kill. The write path does not consume fact_registry_refs (it hand-enumerates each facet so it can build with author-guiding messages), and the two parity tests used hand-written case vectors — so the test comment "add a ref and a test fails" was FALSE. FIXED structurally: FactRefFacet::ALL is the facet authority; both parity tests now assert their cases cover exactly ALL, and a new fact_registry_refs_enumerates_every_facet test asserts a fully-populated fact emits every facet. Adding a variant now fails compile (exhaustive resolver+message matches) OR the enumeration test OR both parity tests until every path covers it — discipline turned into structure.

FINDING 2 (LOW): the within-fact emission order shifted. RESTORED the resolution-ref order (entities before canon_from) to match the pre-R688 detector, so the first-violation slice check_store_boundary surfaces is unchanged for a single-corruption fact. Residual: the structural checks (evidence-empty, typed membership) now emit after all resolution, so a fact with MULTIPLE simultaneous out-of-band violations may surface a different message first — diagnostic text only, the detected set / count / pass-fail verdict are identical, and out-of-band multi-violation is not a write-path-reachable state.

NOT IN SCOPE (pre-existing, unchanged): the detector does not check the typed-object SHAPE invariant (object_kind vs Entity/Value) that the write path enforces; the shared machinery covers ref RESOLUTION only. Neither introduced nor worsened here.

TESTS: mnemosyne-atomic green (lib incl. both parity tests + the new enumeration test); mnemosyne-validate 309 + mnemosyne-ops 18 green; real validate-workspace clean (store registry integrity: 0); clippy -D warnings 0 on atomic.
CITATION HYGIENE (R255): R677 (whole-store-registry), R681 (typed-leg gate) verified PRESENT; R688 is this entry.

The resolver and the detector's enumeration are single-copy; FactRefFacet::ALL + three tests bind the write path's hand-enumeration to it, so the two-copies drift is caught structurally. The reopen trigger (a new fact-registry ref) now fails compile-or-test until both paths cover it.

changes_bullets: DEBT-FACT-REFS-CLONE: fact_registry_refs now returns Vec<(FactRefFacet, &str)> borrowing from the fact instead of Vec<(FactRefFacet, String)> cloning every ref value. The detector (store_registry_violations, the only consumer) passes each straight to fact_ref_resolves(&str) / store_registry_ref_message(&str), and the NarrativeFact outlives the enumeration — so N allocations per fact per validate-workspace scan are gone with no behavior change.

DEBT-PREDICATE-RESOLVE-SPLIT: new resolve_predicate(store, id) -> Option<&Predicate> — the ONE predicate lookup both the resolver (fact_ref_resolves' TypedPredicate arm, via .is_some()) and the write path (build_typed_claim, which needs the declaration for the object-shape check) now call. Predicate resolution was the one facet whose lookup lived in two hand-written expressions (.contains_key() vs .get()); it is now single-copy, so "one resolver" holds for every facet including predicate (the R688 residual the review flagged).

Round 697.decision_summary: R697 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 2): the narrative-continuity transition rule reads the map's edges from STORE FACTS, not a file allowed pair list. NarrativeRuleSpec::Transition { allowed: Vec<[String;2]> } becomes { adjacency: String, undirected: bool }: adjacency names the predicate whose facts ARE the edges, and scan_continuity derives the allowed step set from the store (an adjacent(a,b) fact admits (a,b); when undirected, also (b,a)). The file allowed leg and build-map.py's derive() disappear — the 룰로 박아 core. MID-BUILD design fix (not in R696, which said blanket-symmetrize): measured across the real experiment rules, most transition rules are ONE-WAY state machines (alive→dead, operational→destroyed, machine→deviant — irreversible), so a blanket symmetrize would silently admit the reverse; directedness is preserved (undirected default false, an explicit declared symmetry), only the MAP declares undirected:true. Measured first, then an independent adversarial reviewer on the diff (verdict SAFE-TO-COMMIT). Overclaim caught + fixed not downplayed: directed reproduces the old ALLOWED SET exactly, but end-to-end store-native adjacency requires the fact subject to be a registered entity, so a directed SCALAR state machine must model its states as entities (the old file list did not) — free for the entity-place MAP, verified, recorded. Proven: 1000 workspace tests green, clippy clean, and a CLI e2e dogfood on the real tide store (20 adjacent facts imported; walk dyke-mouth→dike→village admitted 0 violations; non-adjacent village→mulmok caught; reverse village→dike rejected directed / admitted undirected). Design doc claudedocs/store-native-map-design.md sec 3.
