Round 701.decision_summary: R701 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 4 — endpoint kinds predicate-declared + write-path enforced): implements the R700 design. `Predicate` gains two optional registered-`entity_kinds` refs — `subject_kind` (subject leg, new) and `object_entity_kind` (an entity-shaped object leg) — declaring the entity KIND each endpoint must be. The fact write path (`build_typed_claim`, the SOLE typed-fact builder that add_fact / import / amend / import_typing_proposals all route through) REJECTS a fact whose endpoint entity is not the declared kind, at write time — so `adjacent(place, object)` (a road to a non-place) is unrepresentable via the mutate API. This is the spatial-map G1 (DEBT-MAP-G1-KIND) enforced by construction, moved from a read-side continuity check (which would have violated invariant 4 by hardcoding `place`) to a write-path predicate invariant; the required kind is a consumer-declared registered ref, never hardcoded in core. THREE enforcement sites keep it from being half-enforced (the R295 trap): `build_typed_claim` (both legs); `set_predicate` re-type (a full-declaration offender check — object shape AND endpoint kinds — via a new `use_satisfies_declaration` twin, closing the R700-review-#1 gap where re-type guarded object shape only, so a tighten over an off-kind use could silently break the store); and `build_predicate`'s combo guard (`object_kind=scalar` + `object_entity_kind` rejects) plus `validate_predicate_kind_refs` (registered-ref, fail-loud) shared by add_predicate / set_predicate / manifest. DEVIATION from the design's enum-enrichment PIN, measured first (수치≠추론): `PredicateObjectKind` is `Copy`, matched 30+ sites, serialized as a bare tag in every predicate — enriching it drops `Copy`, churns all sites, and forces an on-disk migration; the flat-field + guard variant (which the R700 review #5 explicitly sanctioned) achieves the identical invariant with automatic backward-compat, so BUILD took it. schema_version 24 to 25 (additive-optional; a pre-v25 predicate loads as `None` = no constraint; the bump guards against a stale older binary silently dropping the fields on save and erasing the gate). CLI `--subject-kind` / `--object-entity-kind` on add/set-predicate, MCP args + descriptions, describe-schema manifest keys. An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) returned COMMIT-WITH-FIXES; both findings folded, none downplayed: #1 MED the schema_version bump was missing (FIXED to 25 with the v24 to v25 comment; the reviewer supplied the concrete stale-binary silent-erase scenario), #2 LOW the MCP tool descriptions were stale (FIXED). Confirmed sound: no write-path bypass, add/set declaration-guard parity, invariant 4 preserved, write-path and retype-twin agree (non-vacuous parity test), backward-compat, empty-kind correctly rejects a Some constraint. Proven: full workspace tests green, clippy -D clean, 4 new unit tests + a COMMITTED CLI e2e smoke (`predicate_endpoint_kind_smoke.rs`, real binary). The map.json to store migration G1 gate-release is now MET. NEXT = R702. Design doc claudedocs/store-native-map-design.md sec 10-12.

Round 702.decision_summary: R702 BUILD (store-native map, arc step 5 — G4 map connectivity): the read-side invariant that an UNDIRECTED transition rule's `adjacent` facts form a SINGLE connected component. A new `ContinuityViolation::MapDisconnected` in `scan_continuity`'s transition arm symmetrizes the R699 one-edge model into an undirected adjacency list, DFS-walks from an arbitrary node, and flags any places NOT reached (an island off the map), naming the unreached nodes. Root-independent for an undirected graph (design sec 4.G4) — connectivity's PASS/FAIL does not depend on the start node, so NO entrance/`outside` node is needed to decide it. Scoped to UNDIRECTED (spatial) rules ONLY: a directed state machine's reachability is a different question (forcing single-component on a one-way lifecycle alive->dead would false-positive), and the reviewer confirmed this scope is correct, not a gap. `ViolationLocus` gains an `entities` field (serde-default, skip-if-empty, byte-identical output for existing violations) because a graph-level violation anchors on the unreachable PLACES, not a single fact — the actionable model previously assumed fact-anchored violations; a future G2 "invented place off the map" check will reuse the same entity anchor. An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) returned COMMIT-READY, NO correctness defect: it verified the edge cases (0/1 edge, self-loop already excluded R699, connected, two-component — no false-flag, no miss), the undirected-only scope, determinism (BTreeMap/BTreeSet -> stable unreached order, the exact-order test assertion guaranteed), and serialized backward-compat (grep found no other ViolationLocus literals, no golden/snapshot tests, the one non-test locus.facts consumer is is_empty-guarded). Named deferrals it surfaced (both legitimate, neither introduced here): the edge graph is flat / un-scoped across branches (inherited from R697-699, R696 review finding #6); the entrance-bit capture (design pairs it with G4 but it is a separate concern). Proven: full workspace tests green (mnemosyne-validate 312/312), clippy -D clean, fmt clean; a unit test (connected map clean; disconnected flags the exact island reached=2/total=4/unreached=[ent-c,ent-d]) + the COMMITTED CLI e2e `store_native_map_transition_gates_end_to_end` extended with case F (map_disconnected fires, exit 1, through the real binary). Round 704.decision_summary: R704 DESIGN (object-shape closure / DEBT-I, code 0) — the answer to the owner's "cost aside, what is the most long-term-correct thing": REMOVE the free-text typed-object slot `TypedObject::Value{String}` — the ONE unregistered, unenumerable slot in a store whose frames/branches/entities/predicates/sections/disclosure are ALL registered fail-loud — and replace it with FOUR registered shapes: `Entity{id}` (today), `Token{token}` (a CLOSED vocabulary declared ON THE PREDICATE), `Quantity{n, unit}` (a number + a REGISTERED unit), `Fact{id}` (a fact ref with two-way referential integrity). Prose keeps its home in `claim`; free text is ZERO in the machine slot. This is the owner's own four-shapes (R661), which was NOT LICENSED TO BUILD without a design round + adversarial review because two designs in this family died before build when the author was confident (R625, R659). MEASURED FIRST (R668 — the falsification test R661 left open, "does every real use decompose into the four shapes"): every `TypedObject::Value` across 69 real stores (live tide 866 facts + 40+ phase-1 experiments + the workspace), authored-SSOT split from re-extraction. RESULT: authored values = 522 Token + 16 Fact + 6 Quantity + 8 genuine prose (all tide) — 97.5% decompose cleanly; the 8 tide prose are the DEFECT R661 names (Korean descriptions leaked into the machine slot, each belongs in `claim` or reifies onto an entity/fact), NOT a counterexample. The four-shapes SURVIVES falsification: no authored typed value legitimately needs free text. Re-extraction stores hold ~100 prose — the AI dumping sentences into the value slot because nothing forced a closed token; that is the POSITIVE proof of Token's value (the same predicate is clean vocab when authored, prose when re-extracted). LOAD-BEARING REFRAME (수치≠추론): the value is overwhelmingly TOKEN (self-extraction non-blindness), NOT Quantity; cost (DEBT-J, the original ask) is a rare Quantity use (6) AND a SEPARATE reification axis (an edge cost is a relationship property, a fact is binary — sec 5). An independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, not a fork) RE-RAN the measurement (confirmed 522/16/6/8 to the unit, all 8 remodelable) and returned COMMIT-WITH-FIXES; all 6 findings folded, none downplayed: #1 HIGH the Fact existence check must be PHASE 2, not phase-1 `build_typed_claim` (a phase-1 check rejects a legal same-manifest forward ref pinned by a test, and `import_typing_proposals` must route through phase 2 — R659's proven placement); #2 MED-HIGH the write/arg surface has no compiler forcing function so a variant addition half-wires green (the R625/R659 killer) so the constructor must be a compiler-forced destructure before any variant lands; #3 MED all 522 Token/6 Quantity are in EPHEMERAL experiment fixtures — the live tide store uses ZERO tokens (state via fact-refs + prose), so Token's warrant is representative-workload not live demand and the live migration surface is tide's 24 facts, not 552; #4 MED the cross-predicate-token-disjoint claim was false (open/dead/alive recur across predicates, which STRENGTHENS on-the-predicate); #5 MED a units registry for 2 units is challenged as YAGNI so it is justified on INVARIANT 4 (units are consumer vocabulary, core must not enumerate them — the R700 place-kind lesson) + n must be an exact integer/decimal, not f64; #6/#7 the edge-cost reification and the 8-prose migration were understated so both are flagged unvalidated / needing new registry objects. Code 0: no crate/schema/gate/test touched; the deliverable is this self-contained entry + the design doc claudedocs/object-shape-closure-design.md. NOT LICENSED TO BUILD as one lump; sequencing in carry.

Token{token}: a closed vocabulary declared ON THE PREDICATE (the R701 per-leg pattern), fail-loud at the write path, extended via set-predicate (R658). The load-bearing shape — 522 authored uses + the ~100 re-extraction leaks it would catch (self-extraction stops being blind).

Quantity{n, unit}: a number + a REGISTERED unit (a new units registry), justified on INVARIANT 4 — units are consumer vocabulary, core must not enumerate them (the R700 place-kind lesson), not a core enum. n is an exact integer/decimal, never f64 (all 6 live uses are integer counts; float-fuzz).

Value{String} removal: a schema removal with a reject-loud migration arm (no silent drop — the R625 brick lesson); schema_version bumps. Read sites are compiler-safe (exhaustive match breaks each); the WRITE/arg surface is NOT (reviewer #2 precondition).

Edge-cost (DEBT-J) scoped SEPARATE: Quantity gives cost its number, but the edge attachment needs SUBJECT-leg reification (a relationship property on a binary fact) — a distinct follow-on, not closed here.

Round 706.decision_summary: R706 BUILD (object-shape closure, step 2 — the Quantity shape + a units registry): adds a FOURTH typed-object shape `TypedObject::Quantity { n: i64, unit: String }` beside `Entity{id}`, free-text `Value{value}`, and `Token{token}` (Value NOT removed — that is step 4). `n` is an EXACT integer (all measured live uses are integer counts; f64 is deliberately avoided — it reintroduces 10-vs-10.0 serialization and equality fuzz). `unit` is a REGISTERED ref into a NEW top-level `units` registry (`AtomicStore.units`, keyed by unit id), fail-loud — never free text (invariant 4, the R700 place-kind lesson one axis over: a game measures minute, a legal store day; core must not enumerate them, a bare unit string would drift min/minute/분). The registry is NEW substrate mirroring entity_kinds (R661): a `Unit` struct, an `add_unit` primitive, `add-unit` CLI + MCP, a `UnitImport` manifest kind staged before facts, and a `unit_registered` verdict. DECISION (design sub-fork): the unit lives on the OBJECT only (registry-checked per fact), NOT pinned per-predicate — so add_predicate/set_predicate stay at their current arity and no PredicateDecl bundle is forced this round. The unit check is wired through the R688 shared registry-ref system: a new `FactRefFacet::TypedUnit` (resolved against `units` via the one `fact_ref_resolves`), so the write path (`build_typed_claim`) and the out-of-band detector (`store_registry_violations`) enforce the SAME "is a registered unit" verdict from one enumeration — a half-enforced invariant is structurally impossible (the EnumIter completeness tests force the variant into fact_registry_refs + both parity lists). Unlike entity_kinds (an entity-level ref that needs its own detector), the unit is a FACT-level ref already covered by the facet, so NO standalone detector was added (the R705 precedent added no unregistered_tokens; an independent review caught and removed an early redundant `unregistered_units` that carried a false "the ONE detector both gates call" comment — the R636 overstatement correction). The R660 oracle (`every_declared_object_kind_is_satisfiable_from_the_arg_surface`) FORCED the CLI wiring: adding `PredicateObjectKind::Quantity` failed that test until `from_exclusive_args` gained a `quantity: Option<(i64,String)>` parameter, whose arity change broke every CLI call site (the R625/R659 half-wired-green defense; the build_typed_claim / object_matches_kind / conforms matches are wildcard-free, so the variant broke every one). The interval evaluator (R489) reads a Quantity's exact `n` via a new `typed_object_scalar` (the legacy single-string shapes still parse); a new `typed_object_display` gives the collision-free identity a Quantity needs for the exclusive-rule leg key (n AND unit must match), and the state-change discharge now compares `TypedObject` structurally (it is Eq). schema v26→v27. Wired end-to-end: CLI `--typed-object-quantity-n` + `--typed-object-quantity-unit` (paired both-or-neither, n parsed fail-loud as i64) + `add-unit --unit`; MCP `add_unit` tool + `AddUnitArgs`, the `TypedObject` JsonSchema auto-exposes the Quantity variant (R692); describe-schema object_kind gloss, typed_object_wire (4 variants), a `units` RegistrySpec. Quantity has NO live consumer yet (R704: the 6 measured uses are ephemeral timeline fixtures; the live tide store uses 0 quantities) — the shape is licensed by the north-star self-consistency hole (R661), and it unblocks DEBT-J's number half (edge cost is a separate reification axis, not closed here). Round 709.decision_summary: R709 DESIGN (DEBT-J — reified edge-cost, code 0): the design round that decides HOW the map edge cost (walk minutes, living only in map.json today — the R696 carry) moves into the store. The object-shape arc gave cost its NUMBER shape (Quantity{n,unit}, R706); DEBT-J gives the number a HOME on the edge. MEASURED FIRST (R668 — read build-map.py's LOGIC, not just map.json): the cost is a SINGLE EXACT integer in MINUTES per edge (20 edges, unit=minute → Quantity{i64, minute} verbatim), SYMMETRIC (map.json stores one `walk` per undirected edge, so it cannot be directionally asymmetric by construction — this RESOLVES the object-shape design's flagged open question about the b→a direction: one cost per undirected R698 adjacent fact covers both ways), and FRAME-INVARIANT ground truth (the owner INVENTED the numbers — map.json `open`: "걷는 분을 내가 지어 넣었다" — so there is no section evidence, no per-frame/per-branch variation, and future revision is game-parameter re-tuning that git history covers). Its only consumer is a DERIVED read (minutes-within-a-tide = tide_budget − Σ movement-cost; build-map.py lines 34-40: stay-time is DERIVED from map+chain+tide-length, never authored). THE DESIGN FORK the measurement exposed, adjudicated by an independent adversarial reviewer (fresh subagent, DESIGN review before any code): (A) REIFICATION — a cost fact whose SUBJECT is the adjacent fact, requiring `TypedClaim.subject` be generalized from a bare String to a `TypedSubject{Entity|Fact}` enum (the arc's biggest substrate change, ~38 sites + a facet split + the R707 phase-2/delete-guard mirror on the subject leg); vs (B) SIDE-TABLE — a top-level `AtomicStore.edge_costs: BTreeMap<fact_id, Quantity>` registry keyed by the adjacent fact id, no subject-leg change. DECISION = (B), DECISIVELY. The cost has NONE of the four properties fact machinery serves (frame/branch/evidence/supersession), so (A) buys ZERO measured capability while (a) being the arc's largest change and (b) opening a NEW structural hole the reviewer named HIGH: `check_entity_leg` forces a subject to be a registered entity IN the fact's `entities` list ("the entities list is THE retrieval key"), and a `Fact{id}` subject fails both — exempting it (unlike the R707 OBJECT-Fact, tolerable because objects were never guaranteed entities) yields a fact with NO forced entity retrieval key, a hole needing yet MORE machinery atop the 38-site change. No clean third option exists (object-leg Fact can't carry both the edge-ref and the Quantity in one binary object slot; subject=endpoint-entity can't name both neighbor and cost; a `NarrativeFact.edge_cost` field pollutes the universal struct on every fact). A future PERSPECTIVAL cost (a character's mistaken belief about travel time) is a SEPARATE fact (subject=character, believes-cost predicate), NOT a reification — so nothing ever forces the edge's ground-truth cost to become a reified fact. (A) stays a NAMED, UN-BUILT capability (R661 licensing — build it only when a genuinely evidenced/perspectival edge attribute is measured). (B) mirrors the units/entity_kinds top-level `BTreeMap<String,_>` registries exactly, with Quantity{i64,unit} the R706 shape. Reviewer verdict (B) with 3 corrections FOLDED into this decision (below). code 0; the committed SSOT is this entry (design doc claudedocs/debt-j-edge-cost-design.md is gitignored scratch). changes_bullets: DECISION (B) SIDE-TABLE: a new top-level `AtomicStore.edge_costs: BTreeMap<String, Quantity>` registry, keyed by the ADJACENT FACT ID (the R698 fact's primary key — an author-assigned key, NOT the R702 canonical a<b walk order, which is only the connectivity traversal order and does not form the id), value = `Quantity{n:i64, unit}` (the R706 shape; unit=minute registered). Mirrors the units/entity_kinds registries.
G3 (positive cost): `n > 0` (0 = free teleport, build-map.py's live G3) is a BOUNDARY check on the registry, not a scan — every edge_costs value's Quantity.n must be > 0.

DELETE rule = CASCADE-DROP (folded review Finding 4): when the adjacent fact is retracted, its `edge_costs[fid]` entry is dropped WITH it (ON DELETE CASCADE) — a subordinate side-table, so the cost goes with the edge (simpler + more correct than R707's block-and-retract-first, which fits a peer fact-ref, not subordinate metadata). This is a WRITE-PATH invariant in `retract_fact` (the R707 layer — NOT R698's continuity scan, which the design mis-cited), so the store can never hold an edge_costs entry whose fact is gone.

SINGLE COST PER EDGE is an explicit CHOICE, not a measurement (folded Finding 3): store the base `walk` cost; the `carry` mode (walk×1.5) is a READ-TIME multiplier, not stored. build-map.py's G3 already loops over per-mode costs, and map.json's `open` flags the mode-storage question undecided — so if per-mode stored costs are later needed, the key extends to `(fact_id, mode)` or the value to a small per-mode map. v1 keys single-cost.

Substrate: `add_edge_cost` primitive + CLI/MCP + a boundary detector (`unregistered`/orphan analog) + describe-schema surfacing, mirroring the `add_unit` (R706) build shape. code 0 THIS round — all of the above is the BUILD round's work.

Round 711 — map edge-cost adjacency sema.decision_summary: R711 BUILD (DEBT-J — the map edge-cost adjacency SEMANTIC, the R710 LOW-3 deferral): a validate-continuity check that an `edge_costs` side-table entry (R710, a map EDGE cost keyed by the adjacent fact id) is keyed by a fact that IS a map edge — a fact whose predicate is some transition rule's `adjacency` predicate. A cost keyed to a non-adjacency fact (a walk-cost on something that is not an edge) is flagged `EdgeCostNotAnEdge` and gates under `[continuity].severity`. This lives at the validate layer, NOT the store's `add_edge_cost` gate, for the same reason G1/G2 do: the store cannot know which predicate is the map's adjacency without the rules config (invariant 4 — core never hardcodes "place"/"adjacent"), so `add_edge_cost` only checks fact-exists + n>0 + unit-registered and ACCEPTS a cost on any existing fact. The two layers are proven end-to-end through the real binary: add-edge-cost on a non-edge SUCCEEDS, then validate-continuity — which holds the rules — catches it. The check keys off the transition rule's `adjacency` predicate (NOT its state `predicate`), is checked against the UNION of every transition rule's adjacency predicate so a second map's edge cost is not falsely flagged (unlike the per-rule MapInventedPlace / DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP scope), and is INERT when no transition rule is configured. LAYERING: `scan_continuity` calls `check_store_boundary` FIRST, which runs the R710 `edge_cost_violations` (orphan fact / unregistered unit) and returns Err, so the R711 loop only ever sees present, unit-valid facts — the missing-fact branch is belt-and-suspenders. FOLDED from the independent adversarial review (COMMIT-WITH-FIXES, no correctness defect, both load-bearing claims independently confirmed): the MED remediation gap — the old hint pointed at remedies that do not clear the finding (attach to another fact) or are BLOCKED by referrers (retract_fact refuses a referenced fact), leaving a stray cost on a legitimate/referenced fact with NO exit — is closed by a new symmetric primitive `remove_edge_cost` (drops a cost off a kept/referenced fact without retracting it, and cleans an out-of-band orphan cost; fail-loud when there is nothing to drop; acknowledged in the R630 every-remover tripwire as a leaf that strands no ref), and the hint reworded to name `remove-edge-cost`. A LOW inert-notice finding is NAMED-deferred (a general "map data but no map rule" surface, not an edge-cost-only one). SEPARATELY, this round establishes that CANDIDATE 1 (the derived stay-time READ, the R710-named DEBT-J consumer, minutes-within-tide = tide_budget - Sum(cost)) is BLOCKED, not deferred by preference: build-map.py only DESCRIBES stay-time in prose (no implementation), and map.json `open`[0] reserves the tide length (tide_budget) as owner-undecided with the edge costs marked provisional ratios — so the read cannot be computed without inventing an owner-reserved number, which CORRECTS the R710/RESUME claim that "the stored n:i64 + G3 is sufficient" (that is the Sum(cost) half only). Round 712 — hierarchical/temporal/guarde.decision_summary: R712 DESIGN (code 0) — the corrected formalization of the hierarchical / temporal / guarded SPATIAL MODEL, answering the owner's two questions (hierarchical spaces map-in-school-in-rooms; place access limited to certain times or conditions). Proposed: generalize the current flat single-map (adjacency graph R698-703, 2-level containment R703, a TIMELESS map scan, boolean guards living OUTSIDE the store in map.json) onto a hierarchical, guarded, time-scoped transition system. An INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER returned RESCOPE + one REFUTED load-bearing claim, and all findings are folded (not downplayed): (a) the "it is a Harel statechart / SCXML" framing is REFUTED as a CONSUMER CONFLATION — the game-map consumer is pinion (unbuilt, nowhere stated to be SCXML), while SCE is an SCXML engine but consumes Mnemosyne as a SPEC-compliance ledger, not the map; so the integrity checks are ordinary GRAPH properties and the statechart name is decorative (dropped); (b) the guard-integrity payoffs (dead-content-under-guards, static-contradiction) are KILLED — judging guard satisfiability either EVALUATES guards (crosses the layering line) or is vacuous, and a single opaque condition-ref's only checkable property is that it resolves to a real declared fact, which R707 Fact{id} already gives; (c) the four-piece "unification" is presentational — the pieces touch different code arms and are INDEPENDENT. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS DURABLE: the LAYERING LINE — Mnemosyne holds STATIC authored structure + its consistency, the consumer (pinion runtime) evaluates DYNAMIC playthrough state; the decision test is "does answering this require a playthrough state?" (no = Mnemosyne, yes = consumer). This line was validated across tide_budget (a domain formula input, consumer-side) and reused here. THREE INDEPENDENT PIECES, owner-confirmed PULLED by the upcoming authored world (nested + changing across authored chapters + guarded), so licensed by a real authored instance rather than speculation, but each built one per round on its own pull re-check, in order: (1) NESTING — contains as a place tree/DAG + adjacency scoped PER CONTAINER (the DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP generalization) + refinement-aware exclusivity (co-holding at-values conflict only if NOT comparable in the containment order, evaluated within the pair's frame-world at the co-hold canon point); (2) TIME-SCOPED MAP — the map scan reads adjacency via holds_at at each canon point (closing the asymmetry that the exclusive rule already uses holds_at while the map scan reads flat), so an edge authored to appear in ch5 is a canon-windowed adjacency fact; (3) VERIFIED GUARDS — an edge carries a typed condition-ref (R707 Fact{id}) that Mnemosyne integrity-checks resolves to a real declared fact (v1 = dangling-ref only) and NEVER evaluates (the consumer's job); tide_closes stays SCE's per the owner's prior decision and is not this piece's instance. INVARIANT-4 holds throughout (no domain concept hardcoded; kinds declared on predicates, R701). NEXT = R713, the NESTING piece design (the biggest pull + the structural foundation). Round 713 — nesting spatial piece design.decision_summary:
R713 DESIGN (code 0) -- piece 1 of R712's three independent spatial pieces: NESTING, the structural foundation the other two attach to. Answers R712's three open questions (tree-vs-DAG; the per-scope adjacency scope model + cross-depth ambiguity; frame-scoped refinement exclusivity) and hands a BUILD plan (R714). GROUNDED FIRST (R668, read continuity.rs not a memory of it): the transition arm builds ONE flat `edges` map + flat `nodes` set with G4/G2 over them; the load-bearing forcing fact is that the R703 2-level containment checks CANNOT represent 3 levels -- `contains(campus,school)` + `contains(school,hall)` forces `school` to be a node (MapContainedOffMap: a contained thing must be a node) AND not a node (MapContainerAsNode: a container must not be a node), a contradiction at continuity.rs:3001/3016 -- so nesting must GENERALIZE (and partly repeal) those checks, not add to them.

DECISIONS. (1) tree-vs-DAG = START TREE (v1): at most one direct container per place within one (frame,branch) query-world; a co-scoped second parent is a new ContainmentMultipleParents fail-loud; DAG deferred (its weaker "shares a common descendant means compatible" comparability defers with it). WHY: parent() must be a total, unambiguous function for scope derivation + ancestry, and the authored world is strictly hierarchical (map in school in rooms) -- multi-parent is speculation (YAGNI). (2) per-scope adjacency = SIBLINGS-ONLY, scope = the shared direct container, DERIVED from the tree (no stored scope field: one source, no drift with the tree). A cross-container edge (parents differ) is a new AdjacencyCrossScope violation. PORTALS (exit-the-building) are the CONTAINER participating as a node in its parent's scope (adjacent(school,quad), both children of campus), NOT a cross-depth edge -- so the container/node dichotomy DISSOLVES: a place is a NODE in its parent's scope and a CONTAINER in its own, roles that are scope-relative. WHY siblings-not-LCA: the least-common-container is ambiguous when the two endpoints sit at different depths (R712's open question); requiring siblings makes the scope trivially unambiguous (= the shared parent) and turns every cross-depth edge into a free integrity finding. (3) refinement-aware exclusivity: two co-holding at-values conflict ONLY if NOT comparable in the containment order (ancestor/descendant = a refinement, a finer + coarser statement of one location, compatible; siblings/disjoint = a real conflict), a containment twin of order.comparable (continuity.rs:499), read holds_at-scoped in the pair's frame-world at the co-hold point. The R703 checks GENERALIZE per-scope (G4 connectivity per named scope + root; G2 completeness per scope = the mechanism DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP needs) plus a new ContainmentCycle acyclicity. Invariant-4 throughout (the containment predicate is the rule's declared field, the place kind is derived from R701, nothing hardcoded). BACKWARD-COMPAT: zero `contains` facts means every node sits in the implicit single ROOT scope in a single world, so the result is IDENTICAL to today (the live tide island unaffected) -- this degeneration is the BUILD's falsification test.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES; the core thesis (the 2-level model cannot represent 3 levels and must generalize) CONFIRMED, not refuted; all 4 grounding claims re-verified against the code (no R668 misread); 3 findings folded, none downplayed. F1 (HIGH): MapContainedOffMap is kind-INDEPENDENT but MapInventedPlace is kind-GATED, so dissolving the former into the latter would SILENTLY ACCEPT an unkinded map's off-map contained place -- the R703 test map_g2_container_leak_and_contained_off_map Injection 2 (an unkinded ent-far) isolates exactly this. FOLD: MapContainedOffMap SURVIVES, generalized per-scope + kept kind-independent; only MapContainerAsNode is removed (its residue, a container adjacent to its own child, is caught kind-independently by AdjacencyCrossScope). F2 (HIGH): the Exclusive rule carries NO containment field, so the refinement check had no declared predicate source = an invariant-4 hole + a missing schema change. FOLD: extend Exclusive{per} to Exclusive{per, containment: Option<String>} in-place (exactly as R703 extended Transition), inert when absent; this also makes the "inert for per:object custody" claim true (the predicate is per-rule declared, so a location rule's containment never relates two custody holders). F3 (MED): reading `contains` frame/branch-BLIND would FALSE-REJECT a legal multi-frame store (base-frame contains(campus,school) + a belief-frame contains(district,school) are both true) on the new hard ContainmentMultipleParents. FOLD: the whole containment machinery (parent map, multiple-parents, cycle, the per-scope partition + G4/G2) is evaluated PER QUERY-WORLD (frame,branch) -- the per-world generalization the flat map scan always owed, degenerate for a single-world store = today; the TIME axis (holds_at per canon point in the map scan) stays deferred to piece 2. LOW build notes folded: the ancestry walk carries its OWN visited-set cycle guard (the per-point frame subset is not the flat set ContainmentCycle validated); le_contains is recomputed per co-hold point per frame (unlike the prebuilt order); e2e must add an unkinded-contains case (F1) and a multi-frame-contains case (F3), not just 0-contains. Design decisions that held up under attack: portal-via-container-as-node (internally consistent with per-scope G2/G4), MapContainerAsNode -> AdjacencyCrossScope (a complete, kind-independent migration), the root-scope disjoint-map honesty (does not overclaim DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP closure), tree/siblings as well-justified YAGNI.

Round 714 — refinement-aware exclusivity.decision_summary:
R714 BUILD (code) — the FIRST of two build rounds for the R713 NESTING design: REFINEMENT-AWARE EXCLUSIVITY (the exclusive-arm half). SCOPE SPLIT (measured, flagged): R713.10 numbered the nesting build 0-5 across `continuity.rs`'s most intricate arms; R714 delivers the pieces that live in the EXCLUSIVE arm (which ALREADY iterates per-(frame,world) via `for_each_world_pair`), leaving the transition-arm map-scan refactor (containment-tree integrity = multiple-parents/cycle, per-scope adjacency, `AdjacencyCrossScope`, remove `MapContainerAsNode` / keep+generalize `MapContainedOffMap`) to a later round. The seam between the two arms is clean and each half is its own commit + independent adversarial review (the commit-sized-round principle; the design bundled them because they share the containment tree, and the shared substrate `contains_comparable` built here is exactly what the map-scan round reuses).

WHAT: `NarrativeRuleSpec::Exclusive` gains an optional `containment` predicate (IN-PLACE, no vN — the R712/R713 Finding-2 fold, because the exclusive rule had no containment source and reading `contains` store-wide would be ambiguous / invariant-4-unclean). When declared, the exclusive gate becomes REFINEMENT-AWARE: two co-holding non-keyed values that are COMPARABLE in the containment order (one transitively contains the other, e.g. at(p,classroom) + at(p,school) with classroom in school) REFINE one location (a finer + a coarser statement of the same place) and are NOT flagged; siblings / disjoint places still conflict. New fn `contains_comparable` is a containment-order twin of `CanonOrder::comparable`, built holds_at-scoped in the pair's frame-world (R713.5/R713.7 frame/branch axis; the TIME axis of the MAP scan stays a later round); cycle-safe by its own visited-set (the containment-tree integrity gate is the later round's, so the walk must terminate on any store, R440 out-of-band). Invariant-4: the containment predicate is the rule's DECLARED field (`referenced_predicates` typo-guards it, fail-loud on a misspelled predicate), nothing hardcoded; inert without the field (backward-compatible) and inert for values the containment tree does not name (per:object custody holders). `forbid_transition_legs` still forbids adjacency/undirected/containment on INTERVAL; the exclusive arm now forbids only the EDGE legs (adjacency/undirected) and reads `containment`. describe-schema documents the new field. narrative-rules is FILE-authored (no add-rule primitive), so no mutate-API/CLI/MCP wiring; and no store schema bump (rules live in narrative-rules.json; violations are computed, not stored).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = REQUEST-CHANGES -> 2 PROVEN silent-accept modes folded (none downplayed), the other 5 verification claims independently confirmed holding against the code. F1 (MED, BUILD, folded): `key_of` used the coarse `typed_object_key` for the object leg (a Quantity's `unit`-only borrow) while the exclusive gate compares via `claim_leg`/`typed_object_display` (collision-free) — two distinct quantities {5,floor} and {3,floor} collapsed to "floor", hit the a==b short-circuit, and FALSELY REFINED a real conflict (the "one field, two read paths, different invariant" anti-pattern CLAUDE.md bans, R305). FOLD: the refinement now keys on `claim_leg` (the SAME identity as the gate) and `contains_comparable`'s node identity is `typed_object_display`; a Quantity regression test guards it. F2 (LOW-MED, DESIGN, folded): the scan dismissed the whole pair on the FIRST co-hold point being a refinement, so a later co-hold conflict where the containment has LAPSED was missed (not triggerable while containment is static, but R714 adopts holds_at scoping so the door is open). FOLD: the scan now finds the FIRST co-hold point that is NOT a refinement (a genuine conflict), preserving both the co-held-but-all-refine skip and the never-co-held unordered accounting; a time-scoped-lapse regression test guards it. VERIFIED HOLDING (the reviewer tried to break and could not): frame/world scoping (a.frame is the pair's frame; a different-frame containment cannot leak in, a legitimately-holding same-frame one is not excluded); the wire/parse split (exclusive rejects adjacency/undirected + accepts containment + blank-containment rejects; interval rejects all three; the typo-guard covers the exclusive containment); scope-split soundness (refinement over a non-tree store is PERMISSIVE-safe — first-container-per-contained only REDUCES reachability, never false-skips; every parent edge is a real fact; the cycle guard never returns a false true); backward-compat (serde-default None, `if let Some(cont)` guard fully inert without the field). per:object inertness is an AUTHORING ASSUMPTION (custody holders are not contains nodes), documented, not structurally guaranteed. 8 unit tests (ancestor/descendant skip, siblings conflict, inert-without-field, cycle-safe, quantity-not-collapsed, lapse-still-flags, transitive-multi-hop, wire accepts-containment/rejects-edge-legs) + a committed CLI e2e (`refinement_aware_exclusivity_end_to_end`: the SAME castle+hall store gates WITHOUT the field and passes WITH it, through the real binary). 1039 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0 violations. NEXT = the map-scan nesting build round (per-query-world containment tree + multiple-parents/cycle + per-scope adjacency + AdjacencyCrossScope + remove MapContainerAsNode / keep MapContainedOffMap kind-independent), its own commit + adversarial review. Round 715 — containment-tree integrity (.decision_summary:
R715 BUILD (code) — the SECOND of the R713 NESTING build rounds: containment-tree INTEGRITY (the tree foundation; the per-scope map partition — AdjacencyCrossScope, per-scope G4/G2, MapContainerAsNode removal — is the next and final nesting round). WHAT: a new post-pass `scan_containment_tree` in `scan_continuity` validates that EVERY declared containment predicate — a transition rule's map `containment` (Round 703) OR an exclusive rule's refinement `containment` (Round 714), deduped — forms a TREE within each (frame, branch) query-world: at most one direct container per place (`ContainmentMultipleParents`) and acyclic (`ContainmentCycle`). Two new `ContinuityViolation` variants (structural, ride `severity`) + verdict arms + a describe-schema note + a committed CLI e2e. Node identity = the collision-free `typed_object_display` (Round 714), so two distinct Quantity contained legs never collapse to a false shared child. FRAME-scoped (the R713 review's Finding 3: cross-frame containers naming one child are both-true — a belief-frame hierarchy differing from ground truth — not flagged; only a same-(frame, world) pair is) and BRANCH-scoped via `visibility`. This is the foundation the per-scope partition sits on and the invariant the Round 714 refinement walk assumes; it does NOT touch the flat Round 702/703 G4/G2 (that per-scope generalization is the next round). No store schema bump (rules are file-authored; violations are computed).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES -> 1 HIGH design defect folded (none downplayed) + 2 LOW notes; the cycle detector independently verified panic-free and terminating on every shape (self-loop, rho-tail, disjoint cycles, deep chains), dedup-by-minimum-member correct, and the flat G4/G2 verified untouched. F1 (HIGH, folded): the gate was TIME-BLIND (it filtered `contains` facts by `visibility` only, not `holds_at`), so it HARD-REJECTED legal time-varying containment — a place MOVED between containers across DISJOINT canon extents (vault [ch1-2] then museum [ch3+], never co-holding) false-flagged as multiple-parents, and an early-then-reversed containment (`a` contains `b`, later `b` contains `a`) false-flagged as a cycle; worse, it disagreed with Round 714's `contains_comparable`, which reads the SAME relation through `holds_at` (the two-readers-one-field split CLAUDE.md bans), and its remediation advised deleting a still-true fact. The design's TIME-axis deferral (R713.7) was sound for an under-reporting DETECTOR but UNSOUND for a hard-reject GATE that over-rejects. FOLD: `scan_containment_tree` now evaluates the containment as a per-canon-point SNAPSHOT via `holds_at` — only facts co-holding at a point form that point's tree — so a move / reorganization across disjoint extents is one container per point (never a conflict); the two variants gained an `at` field naming the co-hold point, and the remediation now says "these co-hold at <point> — end one before the other begins (a move is fine), do not delete a true fact." This reconciles R714<->R715 on the one relation. F2 (LOW): a cycle closing only through a NON-first container when the place also has multiple parents is under-reported — but the store is still gated by the multiple-parents finding, so it is NOT a silent accept; noted in code. F3 (LOW / informational): the Entity/Token same-string identity is the module's established convention (shared with R714 and the exclusive gate), not an R715 defect. 6 unit tests (multi-parent same-frame flagged, cross-frame not flagged, cycle flagged, clean tree silent, moved-place-not-flagged, reorg-not-cycle) + a committed CLI e2e (a place with two co-holding containers gates with `containment_multiple_parents` through the real binary). 1046 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. NEXT = the per-scope map partition round (the third/final nesting build). Design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R713 section; R713.10 = the build plan). SSOT = this entry.

Round 716 — per-scope spatial map (per-c.decision_summary:
R716 BUILD (code) — the THIRD and final nesting build round: the PER-SCOPE SPATIAL MAP. The flat single-graph map scan (R702 connectivity + R703 G2 containment checks) is generalized to a PER-SCOPE, per-(frame,world) projection: adjacency edges are PARTITIONED by the endpoints' shared direct container (from the R715 containment tree), an edge between non-siblings is a new AdjacencyCrossScope, connectivity (MapDisconnected) + completeness (MapInventedPlace) + off-map (MapContainedOffMap) run PER SCOPE, and MapContainerAsNode is REMOVED (its residue — a container adjacent to its own child — is a cross-scope edge, caught kind-independently). A "portal" (exit-the-building) is the container participating as a NODE in its parent's scope, so the container/node dichotomy dissolves. This changes `contains` semantics from R703's "grouping" (all nodes one graph) to "scope boundary" (siblings-only edges), the R713.2 design. New shared helpers `containment_snapshot` + `snapshot_parent` are the SINGLE tree reader for BOTH R715 (tree integrity) and R716 (partition) — SSOT, they cannot disagree.

OWNER-DIRECTED DESIGN FINDING (revises R712's "3 independent pieces"): the owner asked for "the most long-term-correct method, cost no object." The correct answer is a PER-CANON-POINT map — and that unifies the nesting-partition (piece 1) with the adjacency-time-scoping (piece 2), because a place's container and an edge's existence both vary over authored canon (holds_at), so sibling-ness is per-point and a flat partition is a lossy collapse that cannot represent a changing map. REFERENCES that make per-point correct: (1) the store's own model — holds_at/canon_from/canon_to is THE time primitive, and EVERY other continuity check (frame-conflict, exclusive, interval, the R715 tree gate) is per-canon-point; the flat map scan was the LONE anomaly. (2) R715's F1 fold already moved the tree gate flat->per-point for this soundness reason; leaving the map flat would be an R715<->R716 two-time-models split. (3) CQRS read-side: "the map at time T" is a projection over the timeline. (4) R712's LAYERING LINE puts authored-canon time INSIDE Mnemosyne (only playthrough state is the consumer's). So AdjacencyCrossScope is evaluated per-canon-point (a MOVED place makes an edge sibling early + cross-scope late); only piece 3 (VERIFIED GUARDS) stays a separate later round.

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = REQUEST-CHANGES, and it REFUTED the load-bearing backward-compat claim by building + running four probe stores; 2 HIGH folded (none downplayed), the node-identity / SSOT-with-R715 / self-loop-reverse-dup / frame-world scoping / per-scope-partition axes explicitly VERIFIED SOUND. F1 (HIGH, folded): MapInventedPlace + MapContainedOffMap were evaluated PER CANON POINT over TIMELESS entities (entities carry no canon_from), so a place whose only map edge appears in a LATER chapter was false-flagged "invented / off-map" at earlier points — normal incremental authoring rejected. F2 (HIGH, folded, REFUTED "degenerates to R702/R703"): MapDisconnected was per-point too, so a bridge authored to appear in ch5 false-flagged ch1 as disconnected — directly the tide-changing-the-map content this arc exists to support, and a violation of R713.9's own falsification test. FOLD for BOTH: connectivity + completeness + off-map are now UNION-OVER-POINTS within the (frame, world) — a place is an island / invented / off-map only if it is off the map at EVERY point (the ∀ "dead content" semantic), which RESTORES the exact R702/R703 flat behavior for a static container-less map (true backward-compat) while never false-rejecting a legally evolving map; the three variants dropped their per-point `at` field. AdjacencyCrossScope stays per-point (correct — the moved-place semantic). F3 (MED, DOCUMENTED not folded): two internally-connected but mutually-unreachable top-level containers produce no finding — the DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP / disjoint-top-level-map tail R713 explicitly declined to close; NAMED in code as a weaker-than-R702 limitation, not hidden under backward-compat. F4/F5/F6/F7 (LOW, notes): the scan is O(worlds x frames x points x facts) — acceptable for the static single-world corpus, noted; node identity is sound for Entity/Token/Fact (only a mis-declared Quantity-object map — garbage-in, already documented — diverges); a directed rule with a containment predicate partitions (a mis-config, symmetric with R703's direction-agnostic G2); dedup under-reports a second same-identity instance (R698 precedent, still gates). VERIFIED SOUND by the reviewer's probes: SSOT with R715 (shared containment_snapshot, R715 tests + e2e still pass), frame/world scoping, the portal model + the MapContainerAsNode->AdjacencyCrossScope migration, and the flat checks that stay flat (self-loop, reverse-dup, the allowed succession-step set). 336 validate lib tests (incl. 6 new: nested-siblings-portal-clean, cross-scope, per-scope-disconnected, per-canon-point-when-a-place-moves, later-appearing-place-not-invented, bridge-appearing-later-not-disconnected) + 15 CLI continuity smoke (the R703 G2 e2e migrated to the per-scope semantic); 1052 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. NEXT = R712 piece 3 (VERIFIED GUARDS), the last nesting-arc round. Design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md. SSOT = this entry.

Round 717 — verified guards piece design.decision_summary:
R717 DESIGN (code 0) — the VERIFIED GUARDS piece, the LAST of R712's spatial arc (nesting piece 1 + its time axis piece 2 were unified by R716 into the per-canon-point map; only guards was genuinely independent). Decides HOW an adjacency edge carries a place-access GUARD (a condition the edge requires, e.g. "requires low tide / a key"). THE LAYERING LINE (the R712 review's non-negotiable constraint): v1 = DANGLING-REF ONLY — Mnemosyne integrity-checks that a guard resolves to a real declared fact and NEVER evaluates whether it holds now (that is the consumer's playthrough-state job); no satisfiability, no dead-content-under-guards, no boolean composition, no reification. DECISION: model a guard as `AtomicStore.edge_guards: BTreeMap<edge_fact_id, condition_fact_id>` — a side-table MIRRORING R710/R711 edge_costs (a guard is edge METADATA like a cost; R709's reification-vs-side-table fork already adjudicated this shape decisively FOR the side-table), with a fact-ref VALUE (the condition fact, R707 TypedObject::Fact{id} shape) integrity-checked for existence (dangling-ref, R707 check). add_edge_guard gates both facts exist (invariant-4: NOT that the keyed fact is a map edge — the store can't know the adjacency predicate; deferred to validate-continuity EdgeGuardNotAnEdge, mirroring R711). remove_edge_guard = the symmetric peer (R711 remove_edge_cost). DELETE two sides: retract the EDGE fact -> cascade-drop the guard; retract the CONDITION fact -> REFUSE (the guard references it; symmetric with conflicts_with/pays_off/the R707 Fact-object; escape hatch = remove_edge_guard).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES. THE TWO AXES I asked it hardest to break HELD, affirmatively: (F5) the side-table shape is CORRECT on frame/branch — frame variance rides fact identity (a belief-frame passage is a separate adjacency fact; scan_spatial_map already scans per (frame,world)), so no frame slot is needed; only the LINK is metadata, the CONDITION is a full fact. (F6) the design is GENUINELY EVALUATION-FREE — every check reads only existence or the edge fact's predicate, never what the condition means or whether it holds; it deliberately does NOT check condition/edge window overlap (that would be the satisfiability creep the layering line forbids). THE REAL FLAW is methodological (F4): R709 MEASURED the cost (20 edges) before adopting the side-table; R717 has ZERO in-corpus guard instances (tide_closes is SCE's and does not even fit a condition-ref shape), so it substituted "a guard looks like a cost" for measurement — and on THREE axes a guard demonstrably differs from a cost, all now NAMED as deferred instance-dependent choices (R709's discipline of naming unmeasured extensions): (F1, TIME) a guard has a lifecycle independent of the edge window (a troll guards A-B ch1-4 then dies; geography unchanged) — a single timeless value can't express it; "timeless like the cost" is partially REFUTED (NOTE: pure time-ACCESS is already the R716 edge window, this is the finer guard-sub-window case). (F2, DIRECTION) guards are often directional (a one-way locked door) but the owner's map is undirected (one fact per edge, R709), so a guard keyed by it applies both ways — the undirected assumption was inherited silently. (F3, CARDINALITY) "single guard, the consumer ANDs them" is incoherent (nothing to AND if one is stored); a "low tide AND a key" edge forces a composite condition fact that loses per-condition dangling-ref tracking. FOLDED: the design now NAMES all three as measure-before-building choices (value shape = bare String vs BTreeSet vs +canon-window, pinned by the first real instance, not guessed); softens the R661 license to substrate-ahead-of-instance; corrects the F7 build note (the condition-side refuse is NEW machinery, not a pure inbound_fact_refs mirror — the guard ref lives in a side-table, not the facts map); adds the F8 note (a place-access guard IS an adjacency guard via R716's portal model, so it passes EdgeGuardNotAnEdge). Invariant-4 holds (F9): no domain concept hardcoded, opaque fact-refs throughout.

CONCLUSION + THE SCOPE FORK (review F4, surfaced not auto-derived): the BUILD is a genuine owner decision, because there is no measured instance to pin the three axes. DEFER (R709-discipline-honest, recommended): capture the design, hold the build until the authored world creates a concrete guard that measures time/direction/cardinality, meanwhile continue the secondary store-internal debt slate. BUILD-NOW-AS-SUBSTRATE: the owner verbally pulled guards (R712) and the primitives are cheap + proven evaluation-free (F6) + frame/branch-correct (F5); build the minimal edge_guards side-table (bare-String value, the three axes named-deferred), accepting the first instance may force an in-place shape edit (pre-release, no compat cost). Either way the DESIGN stands; the fork is only whether to write the code now. code 0; SSOT = this entry; design doc = claudedocs/hierarchical-spatial-statechart-design.md (R717 section, LIVE).

Round 718 — interval-rule unit safety (R.decision_summary:
R718 BUILD (code) — the SECONDARY-DEBT slate, item 1: the R706-DEFERRED INTERVAL UNIT-BLINDNESS (a real correctness gap). Owner mandate: "부채 전부 청산 / 비용 무시하고 가장 장기적으로 올바른 방향". The interval-rule evaluator (NarrativeRuleSpec::Interval, the relation value(left) − value(right) op bound, R489) read a Quantity{n,unit} operand's NUMBER and DROPPED THE UNIT, so it (a) subtracted across units as raw numbers (`15 day − 10 hour` computed 15−10=5) and (b) de-duped two DISTINCT holding values {10,day}/{10,minute} for one (subject,predicate) on `n` alone (collapsed as "the same value restated"). Both violate the R450/R485/R489 no-silent-skip discipline (an ambiguous or non-comparable operand is SURFACED as interval_unverifiable, never silently compared). R706 introduced Quantity+units and explicitly deferred this. FIX (both halves): (1) new `operand_unit(o) -> Option<&str>` — Some(unit) for a Quantity, None for a bare scalar Token/Entity/Fact number; (2) resolve_operand de-dups on the TYPED identity (num, unit) instead of `n` (so {10,day} ≠ {10,minute} = ambiguous → Unverifiable, while two numerically-equal bare scalars "10"/"10.0" both unit-None still collapse — the R489 all-scalar legacy preserved), carrying the unit up via a new Operand::Value.unit field; (3) interval_verdict rejects a compare when left_unit != right_unit (Unverifiable), and a PREDICATE bound whose unit differs from the difference's unit. UNIT-COMPATIBILITY rule: two operands are compatible iff Option<unit> is EQUAL (both None = both unitless/legacy = compatible; both Some(u) = same registered unit; Some vs None or two different units = mismatch → Unverifiable). A CONST bound is unit-agnostic (an author's bare number read in the difference's own unit — the R489 legacy, and the only alternative "const only vs a unitless diff" would regress every const rule over the now-Quantity timeline; documented in describe-schema).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES. THE CORE CLAIM VERIFIED SOUND: a raw cross-unit subtraction is now IMPOSSIBLE — the reviewer traced every path to op.holds (left bare + right Quantity, left Quantity + right bare, both-Quantity-diff-unit, a predicate bound's unit, all five operators ge/le/eq/gt/lt) and found the left_unit != right_unit guard sits unconditionally before every op.holds path; the const leg is a comparison against a single-unit diff, not cross-unit arithmetic; no bypass exists. Second-reader (report-timeline-gaps) unaffected (Operand is module-private, 2 destructure sites both updated; IntervalOutcome/IntervalVerdict unchanged; interval_unverifiable is an unchanged usize downstream); the mismatch counts once per (frame,world,subject). Backward-compat verified: both-bare (None==None) and same-unit Quantity compares gate exactly as before (the R489/R706 tests pass). F1 (LOW, folded): the de-dup FIRST used the display STRING, which over-discriminated numerically-equal bare scalars ("10" vs "10.0" → distinct → a spurious Unverifiable, a narrow R489-legacy regression) — FOLDED to de-dup on (num, unit), keeping display only as the reported value (a Quantity's n is exact i64 so its display is deterministic, nothing regresses the other way); guarded by interval_numerically_equal_bare_scalars_still_collapse. F2 (LOW, DESIGN-note accepted): the const-is-unit-agnostic decision is a latent bound-semantics convention (a const 6 over hour-facts silently means 6 hours) but is NOT a cross-unit subtraction and is the least-bad v1 (const has no unit slot; the alternative regresses every const rule) — documented in describe-schema; a future const-with-unit is the real fix, out of scope. 4 new unit tests (mismatched-units-surface-not-gate + a non-vacuity same-unit gate; distinct-units-same-number-ambiguous; predicate-bound-unit-mismatch; numerically-equal-bare-scalars-still-collapse) + the 6 existing interval tests green. 1056 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. No store schema bump (a validate-layer evaluator fix; violations are computed). The evaluator has no live mixed-unit consumer (the 6 corpus interval uses are integer days), so this is hardening licensed by the R706-named hole, not live pull — but a real correctness gap now closed. SLATE STATUS: item 1 (interval unit-blindness) DONE; item "R698 uniqueness → write path" is a NON-DEBT (invariant-4: the store cannot know which predicate is adjacency without rules config — atomic/lib.rs ~4855 — so the uniqueness check correctly lives at the validate layer; moving it to the write path would hardcode the adjacency predicate); items DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP disjoint-top-level (R716 F3) + the mis-declared-Quantity-map node-identity (R716 F5) remain, each its own round. Round 718 — interval-rule unit safety (R.publishable_decision_summary:
R718 BUILD (code) — the SECONDARY-DEBT slate, item 1: the R706-DEFERRED INTERVAL UNIT-BLINDNESS (a real correctness gap). Owner mandate: "부채 전부 청산 / 비용 무시하고 가장 장기적으로 올바른 방향". The interval-rule evaluator (NarrativeRuleSpec::Interval, the relation value(left) − value(right) op bound, R489) read a Quantity{n,unit} operand's NUMBER and DROPPED THE UNIT, so it (a) subtracted across units as raw numbers (`15 day − 10 hour` computed 15−10=5) and (b) de-duped two DISTINCT holding values {10,day}/{10,minute} for one (subject,predicate) on `n` alone (collapsed as "the same value restated"). Both violate the R450/R485/R489 no-silent-skip discipline (an ambiguous or non-comparable operand is SURFACED as interval_unverifiable, never silently compared). R706 introduced Quantity+units and explicitly deferred this. FIX (both halves): (1) new `operand_unit(o) -> Option<&str>` — Some(unit) for a Quantity, None for a bare scalar Token/Entity/Fact number; (2) resolve_operand de-dups on the TYPED identity (num, unit) instead of `n` (so {10,day} ≠ {10,minute} = ambiguous → Unverifiable, while two numerically-equal bare scalars "10"/"10.0" both unit-None still collapse — the R489 all-scalar legacy preserved), carrying the unit up via a new Operand::Value.unit field; (3) interval_verdict rejects a compare when left_unit != right_unit (Unverifiable), and a PREDICATE bound whose unit differs from the difference's unit. UNIT-COMPATIBILITY rule: two operands are compatible iff Option<unit> is EQUAL (both None = both unitless/legacy = compatible; both Some(u) = same registered unit; Some vs None or two different units = mismatch → Unverifiable). A CONST bound is unit-agnostic (an author's bare number read in the difference's own unit — the R489 legacy, and the only alternative "const only vs a unitless diff" would regress every const rule over the now-Quantity timeline; documented in describe-schema).

INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEWER (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-WITH-FIXES. THE CORE CLAIM VERIFIED SOUND: a raw cross-unit subtraction is now IMPOSSIBLE — the reviewer traced every path to op.holds (left bare + right Quantity, left Quantity + right bare, both-Quantity-diff-unit, a predicate bound's unit, all five operators ge/le/eq/gt/lt) and found the left_unit != right_unit guard sits unconditionally before every op.holds path; the const leg is a comparison against a single-unit diff, not cross-unit arithmetic; no bypass exists. Second-reader (report-timeline-gaps) unaffected (Operand is module-private, 2 destructure sites both updated; IntervalOutcome/IntervalVerdict unchanged; interval_unverifiable is an unchanged usize downstream); the mismatch counts once per (frame,world,subject). Backward-compat verified: both-bare (None==None) and same-unit Quantity compares gate exactly as before (the R489/R706 tests pass). F1 (LOW, folded): the de-dup FIRST used the display STRING, which over-discriminated numerically-equal bare scalars ("10" vs "10.0" → distinct → a spurious Unverifiable, a narrow R489-legacy regression) — FOLDED to de-dup on (num, unit), keeping display only as the reported value (a Quantity's n is exact i64 so its display is deterministic, nothing regresses the other way); guarded by interval_numerically_equal_bare_scalars_still_collapse. F2 (LOW, DESIGN-note accepted): the const-is-unit-agnostic decision is a latent bound-semantics convention (a const 6 over hour-facts silently means 6 hours) but is NOT a cross-unit subtraction and is the least-bad v1 (const has no unit slot; the alternative regresses every const rule) — documented in describe-schema; a future const-with-unit is the real fix, out of scope. 4 new unit tests (mismatched-units-surface-not-gate + a non-vacuity same-unit gate; distinct-units-same-number-ambiguous; predicate-bound-unit-mismatch; numerically-equal-bare-scalars-still-collapse) + the 6 existing interval tests green. 1056 workspace tests green; clippy/fmt clean; validate-workspace + validate-code-refs 0. No store schema bump (a validate-layer evaluator fix; violations are computed). The evaluator has no live mixed-unit consumer (the 6 corpus interval uses are integer days), so this is hardening licensed by the R706-named hole, not live pull — but a real correctness gap now closed. SLATE STATUS: item 1 (interval unit-blindness) DONE; item "R698 uniqueness → write path" is a NON-DEBT (invariant-4: the store cannot know which predicate is adjacency without rules config — atomic/lib.rs ~4855 — so the uniqueness check correctly lives at the validate layer; moving it to the write path would hardcode the adjacency predicate); items DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP disjoint-top-level (R716 F3) + the mis-declared-Quantity-map node-identity (R716 F5) remain, each its own round. Round 719 — secondary-debt slate closure.decision_summary:
R719 BUILD (code — comment/disposition only) — the SECONDARY-DEBT SLATE CLOSURE (owner: "부채 전부 청산 / 비용 무시하고 가장 장기적으로 올바른 방향"). After R718 paid the one REAL debt (the R706-deferred interval unit-blindness), the remaining three slate items were INVESTIGATED against the actual code + the measured live map (R668 measure-first discipline), and each is a NON-DEBT — a correctly-placed, structurally-prevented, or design-correct behavior that must NOT be mechanically "fixed" (closing them would introduce false positives or hot-path complexity for garbage-in). This round records the dispositions and makes two HONESTY comment fixes so a future session does not re-litigate them:

(1) "R698 uniqueness legs → write path" — NON-DEBT by INVARIANT-4. A self-loop `adjacent(a,a)` / reverse-duplicate cannot be rejected at the write path (add_fact) because the store layer cannot know WHICH predicate is the map's `adjacency` without the rules config (atomic/lib.rs ~4855 states this; it is the same reason G1/G2 and the edge-cost semantic all live at the validate layer). Moving the check to the write path would require the store to hardcode the adjacency predicate = an invariant-4 violation. The validate-layer placement (AdjacencySelfLoop / AdjacencyReverseDuplicate in scan_continuity) is CORRECT. No change.

(2) DEBT-MAP-G2-SINGLEMAP disjoint-top-level tail (R716 F3) — NON-DEBT, the CORRECT nested-model relaxation. R716 checks connectivity PER SCOPE, so two internally-connected but mutually-unreachable top-level containers produce no MapDisconnected. R702's whole-map connectivity was the SINGLE-scope special case; re-imposing it would FALSE-POSITIVE on a legitimately disjoint authored world (two islands; a dream vs the waking world). A nested model makes a container a first-class "separate sub-map" declaration; an author who wants two containers connected declares an adjacency between their parent-scope nodes (a portal — a container as a node in its parent's scope), and THAT scope's connectivity then checks it. So the guarantee is exactly "every scope you declared edges within is connected" — the right invariant for a model with explicit containment. MEASURED: the live tide map is flat / 0 containers = one root scope = the R702 whole-map check, so no live case is affected either way. FIX: the R716-F3 code comment was reframed from "NAMED LIMITATION … weaker than R702" to this correct-relaxation framing (it was mislabeling correct behavior as a debt).

(3) mis-declared Quantity-object map node-identity (R716 F5) — NON-DEBT, structurally prevented by R701. `typed_object_key` (a Quantity's unit-only borrow) vs the containment snapshot's `typed_object_display` diverge ONLY for a Quantity object. But R701 forbids a Quantity object on any predicate that declares `object_entity_kind` (the write path rejects a non-entity object there, atomic/lib.rs ~3835), and a KINDED spatial map declares it — so a Quantity endpoint is UNREACHABLE on a real map. The only residue is an UNKINDED Quantity-object adjacency, doubly garbage-in (a spatial edge to a NUMBER), which the mutate API does not produce and which is inert for the kind-gated G2 anyway. MEASURED: the live tide map's endpoints are all `ent-*` entities. FIX: a clarifying comment at the map-partition site records that R701 makes this unreachable on a real map (documented tolerance, not a live divergence).

Round 720 — verified guards build (edge_.decision_summary:
R720 BUILD (code) — the VERIFIED GUARDS piece (R717 design, piece 3 of 3, the LAST of the R712 spatial arc). Owner chose BUILD-NOW and reframed the design decisively: "소설을 쓰고 증명해" + "므시모시네가 소설에서 키가 있을 때와 없을 때 어떻게 나눠져야 하는지 전부 알고 있어야 하는 거 아니야? 게임에서는 키가 있냐 없냐만 알면 되고, 나는 게임이 복잡해지는 게 싫어." So the guard is not a thin opaque edge-ref alone — it CONNECTS the spatial map to Mnemosyne's BRANCH engine: MNEMOSYNE holds the FULL branching (the got-key world-line AND the no-key world-line, both fully authored as forked branches), and the GAME only evaluates the boolean ("has key?") and follows the branch Mnemosyne already authored. The branching complexity lives in Mnemosyne (static authored structure); the game stays thin (dynamic evaluation). This keeps the R712 layering line EXACTLY (Mnemosyne never evaluates whether the guard holds) while grounding the guard in a REAL authored instance — resolving the R717-review F4 measurement gap by AUTHORING one.

SUBSTRATE (mirrors R710/R711 edge_costs, a fact-ref value): `AtomicStore.edge_guards: BTreeMap<edge_fact_id, condition_fact_id>` (schema v30→v31, additive). `add_edge_guard` gates BOTH facts exist (the dangling-ref check, R707) + rejects a self-guard; `remove_edge_guard` = the peer (R711). DELETE, both sides: retract the EDGE fact → CASCADE-DROP the guard (metadata follows the edge); retract the CONDITION fact → REFUSE (a guard references it — NEW machinery vs edge_cost, because the ref lives in the side-table not the facts map, the R717-review F7 correction). `edge_guard_violations` (out-of-band: gone edge/condition fact) folds into store_registry_violations. validate-continuity `EdgeGuardNotAnEdge` (mirror R711 EdgeCostNotAnEdge): the keyed fact must be an adjacency fact of some transition rule (INERT with no rule, union across rules, invariant-4); reads ONLY the edge fact's predicate, NEVER the condition — no evaluation. CLI add-edge-guard/remove-edge-guard + MCP + describe-schema RegistrySpec. remove_edge_guard acknowledged in the R630 remover tripwire (a leaf: the entry is a referrer of its condition, referenced by nothing). Three axes stay NAMED-DEFERRED per R717 (time/direction/cardinality; value = bare String condition id, first-instance measured below did not pull any of them). NO reification, NO expression composition, NO evaluation — the anti-creep boundary held.

THE PROOF (the "novel"): a committed CLI e2e (edge_guard_smoke.rs) authors the key-guard story through the REAL binary — a hall adjacent to a vault (the door edge f-door), a got-key branch (the hero holds the iron key f-has-key → steps into the vault f-in-vault) and a no-key branch (stuck in the hall f-stuck), forked at the door; add-edge-guard f-door f-has-key. PROBED the LIVE binary (R668 measure-first) rather than assume: ITEMS work fully (entities kind:item + holds facts + canon windows + exclusive rules); NON-SPATIAL CHOICES work TODAY (a choice = a DIRECTED transition-rule edge, R449/R697 supports directed state machines as well as spatial maps, and R720's edge_guards guards it — EdgeGuardNotAnEdge accepts ANY transition rule's adjacency predicate, so a guarded directed choice edge validates clean, PROVEN); ITEM COMBINATION reduces to a guarded choice edge (the "craft" transition guarded by the INPUT SET {iron,wood} + the authored outcome branch holds(axe)) since supersedes_in_frame takes ONE predecessor (no multi-input succession) and there is no recipe rule. THE ONE GAP (PROVEN: a second add-edge-guard on one edge is refused DIVERGENT) = MULTI-CONDITION gating, exactly the R717.1a CARDINALITY axis named-deferred, now PULLED by this concrete instance.

THE MODEL (derived, the answers to the two open questions DERIVED not asked, per derive-don't-over-ask): the game is a guarded transition system (states/transitions/guards/branch-outcomes); MNEMOSYNE authors + validates the STRUCTURE + integrity, the GAME executes (evaluates guards, follows edges/branches) — the R712/R717 layering line unchanged. (1) AND = a guard's condition SET; the game evaluates each condition (dangling-ref resolves + does it hold in my playthrough) and ANDs — Mnemosyne stores the flat set + integrity-checks each member resolves, NEVER evaluates the AND. (2) OR = MULTIPLE guarded edges to the same target (graph-level), NOT a stored boolean expression tree (which R717 KILLED as the layering-line crossing) — a transition system expresses alternatives as multiple transitions with distinct guards. SUBSTRATE: AtomicStore.edge_guards value String -> BTreeSet<String> (schema v31->v32, the bump justified only by the monotone > CURRENT guard since the live store's edge_guards is {} and empty maps round-trip identically — no real migration code); add_edge_guard INSERTS into the set (idempotent on the element, no divergent-reject); NEW remove_edge_guard_condition drops ONE condition (deleting the map KEY when the set empties — no vacuous empty-set entry); DELETE both sides set-aware (retract EDGE cascade-drops the whole set; retract a CONDITION in ANY guard's set REFUSES); edge_guard_violations checks each member resolves; EdgeGuardNotAnEdge unchanged (reads only the edge predicate, no evaluation). This makes the owner's three structures ONE thing: a guarded transition to an authored outcome (evidence-gated choice = a directed choice edge guarded by the evidence set; combination = a craft edge guarded by the input set + the outcome branch; items = entities+holds).

The principled path IF a real consumer pulls it: an edge_costs-style parameter/delta side-table (R710/R711 precedent) holding declared per-choice deltas and per-gate thresholds, with the consumer accumulating and evaluating (the R712 layering line — the same tide_budget/stay-time split). Round 731.decision_summary: R731 (DEBT-L — multiset/quantity custody; the DISTINCT part after DEBT-K paid currency as a global meter). Singular `holds` custody (a per:object Exclusive rule, one holder per thing) had no shape for a COUNT tied to a custody edge (5 potions). MEASURED FIRST (R668/R726 falsification, scratch sidecar): the only shape available today — a SEPARATE, disconnected count fact (stack-size 5) — has a SILENT HOLE: retract the custody fact and the stray count fact SURVIVES, validating clean (registry 0, continuity 0) = a phantom stack with no holder (the DEBT-K boolean-proxy analog). FIX: a fact-keyed side-table AtomicStore.fact_counts BTreeMap<fact_id,i64> (a POSITIVE count keyed BY the fact), mirroring edge_costs/parameter_gates; because it is keyed by the fact, retract_fact CASCADE-DROPS it -> the orphaned-count silent hole is UNREPRESENTABLE (make-unrepresentable, the DEBT-K hole-1 approach). KEY DESIGN DECISION (owner: "비용 무시 가장 장기적으로 올바른"): the count RIDES ANY FACT, with NO custody-predicate check, because anchoring to the per:object Exclusive rule is SEMANTICALLY INVERTED — a multiset count is meaningful precisely for FUNGIBLE items, which are exactly the ones NOT under exclusivity (a unique token has one holder and count 1; a fungible stack is not under the Exclusive rule, which would false-flag two holders as double-custody). The only machine-knowable custody signal is the per:object Exclusive rule (invariant 4 — core has no `holds`), so anchoring would REJECT the count where it is meaningful and ACCEPT it only where it is redundant — inverted, not merely narrow; there is no coherent middle. So the count is a GENERAL per-fact cardinality (holds is the motivating case; killed(A,goblin) x5 / carries(A,arrow) x20 are equally legit) — the R728 review F2 lesson (a side-table over a broad predicate class must not be pinned to one rule-predicate); NAMED fact_counts, not custody_counts, for honesty (the parameter_gates naming discipline: name = the shape, doc = the motivating case). A bare i64 (no unit — the thing counted is the fact's object leg), unlike EdgeCost's number+unit. PARITY-COMPLETE: fail-loud at the write path (add_fact_count) AND re-checked at the scan boundary (fact_count_violations: fact-exists + count>0), the edge_guard/parameter_delta precedent, not the n>0-blind edge_cost one. A2 via stage_registry_entry (a flat i64, not parameter_delta's nested hand-roll). Singular-custody stays UNCHANGED (the per:object Exclusive rule's job; the count is a store-side DECLARATION, Mnemosyne NEVER sums counts across facts or evaluates the multiset — the R712 layering line). NO report primitive (YAGNI — a count is a single per-fact value, no DEBT-K accumulation-invisibility gap; visible via query). schema v35->v36 additive; RegistrySpec (describe-schema) + CLI add-fact-count/remove-fact-count + MCP tool fns + the store_registry_violations extend wire; the R630 every-remover tripwire acked (remove_fact_count = a leaf, the edge_cost class). INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-AS-IS, NO defect — all 7 load-bearing claims (layering line via full grep, write<->scan parity via a neuter-and-fail injection, cascade/orphan-unrepresentable via the sole-removal-site proof, the semantic-inversion decision, the schema bump, half-wired-green, test non-vacuity) held under attack; 1 LOW = the pre-existing R730 carry (no iter()-forced completeness meta-test over the now-FIVE side-table detectors edge_cost/edge_guard/parameter_delta/parameter_gate/fact_count), NOT regressed by R731, a named follow-on (the removers already have such a forced meta-test, which R731 correctly extends). Round 732.decision_summary: R732 (DEBT-M — entity-kind inheritance tree; owner pull "DEBT-M 즉시 상환해"). entity_kinds were FLAT tags, so the R701 predicate endpoint-kind gate was EXACT-match: a general thing-scoped rule and a specific weapon-scoped rule could not both apply to one entity (a sword tagged weapon is rejected by the thing-scoped rule, though a sword IS a thing). MEASURED FIRST (R668/R726 falsification, scratch sidecar): with flat kinds there is NO tagging that satisfies both a thing-scoped and a weapon-scoped predicate on one entity — the Inform "a weapon is a kind of thing" idiom is unrepresentable (a hard fail-closed gap; the two workaround horns each lose the guard or the distinction). FIX: EntityKind.parent: Option<String> (a registered entity_kinds ref = the direct super-kind) forms a single-parent inheritance TREE; the endpoint-kind gate now scopes over the SUBTREE (a weapon satisfies a thing-scoped rule because weapon.parent=thing). ONE resolver is_kind_or_subkind (a cycle-safe parent-chain walk) is shared by all 5 kind-gated sites — the 4 write-path/tighten legs (build_typed_claim subject+object, use_satisfies_declaration subject+object) AND the R703 MapInventedPlace completeness scan (continuity.rs) — because switching only the write gate would DIVERGE from the completeness scan (adjacency admits a subkind node the scan would then not police, the R699 half-enforced trap); the resolver lives in atomic, continuity calls it (one resolver, two crates). DIRECTIONAL (a parent is NOT accepted where a subkind is required, no inversion) + OPT-IN (0 parent links => subtree = singleton => exact-match, the backward-compat line: the tide island + every flat store unchanged). add_entity_kind gains parent (registered + non-self, fail-loud, parent-declared-first — the add_entity symmetry); a multi-node cycle is unreachable via the mutate API (no parent-mutation setter), so the write path's only cycle case is self-parent. PARITY-COMPLETE detector entity_kind_parent_violations (dangling parent OR cycle) wired into store_registry_violations — re-checks at the scan boundary what the write path forbids (the edge_guard/parameter_delta/fact_count precedent, not the n>0-blind edge_cost one); the walk is MEMOIZED (proven_acyclic) so a deep legit chain is O(n log n), not O(n^2) (the review LOW-1 fold). LAYERING LINE (R712): the parent walk is a STATIC registry read, Mnemosyne never evaluates whether a kind holds at runtime. NO report primitive (YAGNI — the tree is visible via query/describe-schema, no accumulation-invisibility). schema v36->v37 additive; EntityKindImport.parent (manifest, parent-first array order); CLI add-entity-kind --parent; MCP AddEntityKindArgs.parent; describe-schema KindWire. Round 734.decision_summary: R734 (the R733 confluence FOLLOW-ON, DISPOSED — PROVEN BY TEST per the owner's directive "test로 증명해", not by reading; NO defect; a committed regression test added, no substrate change). The R733 review flagged that a pre-fork path-independent trunk fact reads undecidable / holding-0 in a confluence world's report-playthrough-manuscript, seemingly contradicting describe-schema's "the path-independent trunk survives" a merge (and core's fork_off_a_confluence_inherits_the_pre_merge_trunk membership test). INVESTIGATED VIA THE REAL BINARY (three probes + a neuter-and-fail), the finding resolves to a NON-DEFECT: (1) the DEFAULT manuscript dump enumerates only the PLAYTHROUGHS — main + the two forks — because query_worlds (R533) excludes a confluence (a converges branch is NOT a standalone world; its shared suffix renders WITHIN each parent via forward visibility); (2) in BOTH real playthroughs (thief, knight) the pre-fork trunk fact HOLDS all the way through the shared confluence suffix (merge, end) — so describe-schema's "survives" is CORRECT on the axis it describes, the fact axis; (3) the reviewer's Unknown came from an EXPLICIT --world <confluence>, which the code (continuity.rs playthrough_manuscript, R533) DELIBERATELY renders as a prefix-less FRAGMENT for inspection, and that fragment marks the pre-merge trunk undecidable (B-1 honest) — it does NOT silently drop it and does NOT falsely show it holding. So the reviewer's observation was a fragment-inspection artifact read as a trunk-survival bug: the trunk survives every real playthrough, and the confluence fragment is honest, so there is nothing to fix. NON-VACUITY proven by neuter-and-fail: authoring the SAME fact PATH-DEPENDENTLY (on a fork, not the trunk) drops the sibling playthrough's suffix holding from 1 to 0 — so the regression test WOULD go red if the trunk stopped surviving. DELIVERABLE (the owner's test-not-read directive): a committed regression test pre_fork_trunk_survives_the_confluence_suffix_in_every_playthrough in report_playthrough_manuscript_smoke.rs asserting all three properties plus the path-dependent negative control. describe-schema's wording STANDS (it describes the fact axis / playthroughs, which are correct); NO substrate change because there is no defect. This closes the last R733 carry_forward item; no independent subagent review this round — the disposition is backed by an executable, non-vacuous test rather than a prose claim (the higher bar). SSOT = this entry.
