Round 735.decision_summary: R735 (the R731/R732 named follow-on: surface subkinds / fact_counts in the report-frame-view read-side; owner pulled item 1 to review-and-close, then said proceed). SPLIT disposition on ONE principle: a CONTENT projection echoes the STORED CONTENT of the rows it emits, but a DERIVED cross-registry computation stays on the consumer's CQRS read-side (the R711/R712 layering line, the owner's own doctrine "the derived value is not authored data"). 1a BUILT: fact_counts (R731) is ASSERTED CONTENT of the fact (a per-fact multiplicity keyed by fact_id, "A holds FIVE potions"), the same fidelity class as evidence/typed/quote that FrameViewEntry already echoes. MEASURED FIRST (R668/R726 scratch, real binary): the count was STORED + queryable but report-frame-view DROPPED it from the holding entry = a FIDELITY gap, not an unrepresentability gap (nothing was impossible, unlike DEBT-K/L/M). Round 739.decision_summary: R739 (the R661 kind-tree extension item 2 — a parent-mutation setter; owner pull "미루는거 없이 … yagni 무시", the R738 batch). R732 deliberately omitted a parent-mutation setter because re-parenting an EXISTING kind can close a multi-node cycle — add_entity_kind's new kind is always a leaf pointing only at pre-existing kinds, so it never can. set_entity_kind_parents REPLACES a kind's parents: BTreeSet and is where that guard lives: every new parent must be registered + not self, AND none may be at-or-below kind_id in the current graph (is_kind_or_subkind(p, id) true ⇒ p is a subkind of id ⇒ making it a super-kind loops id→p→…→id). Checking the CURRENT graph is SOUND: any newly-created cycle must use one of id's new outgoing edges, so a minimal cycle is id→p→…→id using exactly one new edge, and its p→…→id subpath predates the replacement — so is_kind_or_subkind(p,id) catches it; and the resolver returns the instant it reaches id, before expanding id's own (soon-replaced) edges, so the pre- and post-replacement checks are exactly equivalent (no false positive). The R738 scan detector (entity_kind_parent_violations) re-checks the same acyclicity at rest = write↔scan parity. Fail-loud on an absent kind (add creates, set mutates — one creator per registry, the set_predicate R658 precedent); NO partial write on a rejected setter (the mutation is the last statement, after all guards); idempotent on the identical set; an empty slice roots the kind. CLI set-entity-kind-parents (--parent REPEATABLE) + MCP set_entity_kind_parents. INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (fresh subagent, not a fork) = COMMIT-AS-IS, no defects: the cycle guard proven sound by proof AND a 68k-op differential fuzz vs an independent acyclicity oracle (0 mismatches, 8186 genuine cycle-rejects ≈12%, no partial write on any reject). R741 gave only report-playthrough-manuscript a self-describing [FRAGMENT] marker for a --world <confluence> render (a merge node, not a standalone playthrough — the R733 review misread it once); the three sibling read surfaces (report-frame-view --branch <confluence>, report-playable-world, report-quest-graph) carried NO fragment signal, so an AI reader could re-misread a confluence column/view as a playthrough. The proven failure mode is an AI misread (R733 did exactly that), and the surfaces are the first consumer's external memory, so the residual was a real (if LOW) risk with three same-shape siblings — "no consumer" was not strictly true. CLOSED by SSOT-unification, not three copies: a NEW mnemosyne_core::is_confluence(branches, world) predicate is THE single definition of the confluence-fragment discriminator (converges_from non-empty), the is_known_world single-definition discipline applied to the confluence axis; the manuscript's inline check is FOLDED into it. The four surfaces route through it: manuscript (via the predicate), frame-view (FrameView + the ops FrameViewReport gain confluence_fragment, ALWAYS-serialized, set via the predicate — a NEW derivation since frame-view has no manuscript), quest-graph (QuestGraphReport gains confluence_fragment_worlds, DERIVED by reading each world's embedded manuscript confluence_fragment — the ONE is_confluence computation reused via playable-world's verbatim manuscript, NOT re-derived, so it cannot drift), playable-world (its human render prints from the embedded manuscript flag the JSON already carried). Round 749 — 2d-projection-experiment des.decision_summary: R749 (DESIGN, code 0 — the owner's steer: start an end-to-end authoring experiment for a NON-point-and-click genre, beginning with the Ao-Oni-style 2D RPG-Maker (tsukuru) genre, and verify the SAME narrative projects onto BOTH a visual-novel axis AND a tsukuru axis, both dialogue/monologue-centric, not prose-centric). Designed claudedocs/phase1-2d-projection-experiment/v1/ (premise.md + author-brief.md + render-vn-brief.md + render-tsukuru-brief.md + extractor-brief.md + judge-brief.md + manifest.json + runbook.md), sha-pinned pre-execution. THESIS: genre difference = projection thickness, not substrate difference — hold ONE blind-authored fact store fixed and split only the render into two genre axes; if both project cleanly with only the render-brief differing, the map_locator seam's genre-agnostic pointer claim (R557) is demonstrated on a non-point-and-click genre pair. PREMISE "The Room at the End of the Long Hall" (~18-22 scenes, original, no IP): a locked-building night horror with a kind:place room-graph, edge-guarded locked doors forming an order-real key chain (R717/720/722 place-access guards as the locked-door mechanism), an antagonist as its own frame (geot knows the party's location while the party does not know its — the epistemic-frame engine on a hostile non-party agent, the horror = the knowledge gap), three withheld secrets, and one fork into two roads with per-road quest divergence. FOUR deterministic pins: PIN-1 authoring-clean; PIN-2 spatial+quest structure (>=6 places + adjacency graph + >=2 edge-guards + order-real key chain + geot knowledge gap + >=4 kind:quest + per-road divergence); PIN-3 map/surface resolves (every quest-giver + every withheld-secret surface -> MapLocator, 0 unresolved); PIN-4 (headline) PROJECTION INVARIANCE — from ONE store, both a blind VN render and a blind tsukuru render (each dialogue/monologue-centric) are leak-clean + fidelity-clean over their own blind re-extraction AND the two re-extractions agree on the withheld-secret reveal order, so the axis difference localizes to render form not the fact set. Plus 3 blind judges (per-axis game-feel + a same-night cross check). PRE-REGISTERED PULL: the substrate expresses place-ACCESS as a condition (edge-guard, K-of-N, R717/720/722/723) but DISCLOSURE timing as a single ordinal (first_at, R506); in non-linear tsukuru exploration a secret can be earned at whichever of several spatial triggers the player reaches first, which one first_at cannot express — so the tsukuru render may railroad or invent a trigger while the linear VN render is served exactly. If that pull lands, the BUILD target is giving disclosure timing the same condition/first-reached vocabulary the access axis already has — the exact generalization a real-time 3D consumer would also need; this experiment is the consumer whose pull decides it. Contamination firewall (R469): this lineage writes the design only; blind subagents author / render each axis / re-extract each / judge. THIS ROUND IS DESIGN (code 0); EXECUTION (spawning the blind stages) is the EXPERIMENT-EXECUTION consent gate. SSOT = this entry + the manifest.

Round 751 — disclosure-timing generaliza.decision_summary: R751 (DESIGN, code 0 — the disclosure-timing generalization the R750 experiment pulled, pinned before the build; the R738 schema-change-design-in-entry pattern). PROBLEM (R750): DisclosureOverride.first_at is a single ordinal per world (BTreeMap<branch, single-section-coord>); a non-linear walked (tsukuru/3D) render cannot honor it without straining (R750 saw a page-carry railroad + a premature leak + a content-split), while a linear (VN) render honors it trivially. DESIGN: generalize the per-world first_at VALUE from a single coord (String) to a FIRST-REACHED-OF-A-SET trigger with an optional K-of-N threshold, mirroring the ACCESS-axis EdgeGuard shape (R717/720/722/723). NEW struct mnemosyne_core::DisclosureReveal { coords: BTreeSet<String>, threshold: Option<usize> } in narrative.rs — the exact SHAPE-mirror of EdgeGuard { conditions: BTreeSet, threshold: Option }. SEMANTIC (world W): the fact is first legitimately disclosed at the k-th-EARLIEST coord of `coords` by W's canon order, k = threshold.unwrap_or(1) = FIRST-REACHED (the earliest of the set) by default. NOTE the default differs from EdgeGuard on purpose: EdgeGuard None = require-ALL (AND, access is conjunctive); DisclosureReveal None = FIRST-reached (k=1, reveal fires at the earliest trigger). Normalization mirrors edge-guard's discipline but on the respective canonical default: reject Some(0) (vacuous) and Some(k>len) (unsatisfiable), NORMALIZE Some(1)->None (first-reached is the canonical default), so Some(k) is stored only for 2<=k<=len; each k is a DISTINCT semantic (unlike edge-guard where Some(len)==None), so Some(len)=last-reached (max) is NOT normalized away. LAYERING (verified): CanonOrder lives in mnemosyne-validate, mnemosyne-core does NOT depend on it — so core STORES the declaration order-free and the VALIDATE layer resolves the k-th-earliest with the order. The R510 resolver EffectiveDisclosure.first_at changes Option<String> -> Option<DisclosureReveal> (the world's reveal DECLARATION, order-free); a NEW validate-layer helper resolves the declaration to the effective coord (k-th-earliest by order) where needed. RIPPLE (deliberate, the payoff): MapLocator.first_at (the pinion seam) changes Option<String> -> Option<DisclosureReveal> so pinion receives the trigger SET + threshold and resolves FIRST-REACHED against the player's actual non-linear path at runtime (the "declaration stored, never evaluated" edge-guard layering line, R712 — pre-flattening to one coord would re-impose the single-ordinal limit the pull is about). FactDisclosure (manuscript carrier) carries the reveal set (human annotation prints the set + k). DisclosureLeak.first_at stays the RESOLVED pin (k-th-earliest) the gate compared against. LEAK GATE (disclosure.rs disclosure_leak): the `pin = ov.first_at.get(world)` single-coord becomes pin = k-th-earliest(reveal.coords, world, order); the rest of the ordinal comparison (coord == pin on time / order.le(coord,pin) early-leak / incomparable honesty surface) is UNCHANGED. MIGRATION v38->v39: a raw-JSON load migration (mirror migrate_entity_kind_parent_to_parents at lib.rs:1477-1503, invoked at :1607-1609) rewrites first_at: {branch: "sc-NN"} -> {branch: {coords: ["sc-NN"], threshold: null}}; bump CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 38->39 (lib.rs:1464) + a ledger comment + a v38_first_at_migrates test mirroring :16422. WRITE PATH: apply_disclosure_override accepts a coords SET + optional threshold per branch; the duplicate-branch reject (lib.rs:7348-7355) LOOSENS to accumulate multiple --first-at for one branch into the set; DisclosureDecision.first_at (lib.rs:7257) + DisclosureOverrideImport.first_at (lib.rs:4134) shapes carry coords + threshold; the R744 exhaustive-destructure ref checker disclosure_override_ref_violations (lib.rs:7421) re-handles the coords set (each coord in sections), keeping write<->scan parity + the R737 completeness. CLI: `--first-at branch=coord` becomes REPEATABLE (accumulate per branch) + `--first-at-threshold branch=k`; plus the full edge-guard-parity granular primitives add-disclosure-reveal-coord / remove-disclosure-reveal-coord / set-disclosure-reveal-threshold (peers of add-edge-guard / remove-edge-guard-condition / set-edge-guard-threshold). TESTS: migration, write-path set+threshold (accumulate + normalize + reject), leak-gate k-th-earliest (a secret with a {sc-08, tg-14} set leaks only before the earliest; a threshold-2 set leaks before the 2nd), resolver flatten, ref-scan parity, set-vs-manifest parity, CLI smoke, MCP shape. This round is DESIGN (code 0); the BUILD is R752. SSOT = this entry.

Round 755 — prose-provenance DESIGN: sto.decision_summary: R755 (DESIGN, code 0 — the P5 INTERACTIVITY MIGRATION arc's final sub-step; objects/ladders/knots done, this closes the prose-provenance hole the arc named). PROBLEM: the engine's Line is provenance-airtight (crate-private fields + a single fact_id-joining constructor, the R643 detectable->unrepresentable doctrine at the type boundary, born of the tide field-report "invented narrative" bug), but that guarantee covers only ONE of the two things a player reads. A scene is (a) a fact-clue overlay = provenance-bound Lines, and (b) STORY PROSE = the narration/dialogue the player actually reads, a plain Vec<String> with NO fact_id and ENTIRELY outside the engine (the engine reads only scene.title/section/begins; Rung.question is a bare pass-through String, "not re-checked here"). The story prose is the BULK (tide: ~128K chars across 56 segments of segment-prose.json + 5 ladders/19 questions + epigraphs, vs a small fact-clue overlay). So "invention is unrepresentable" is INCOMPLETE: it holds for clues, is silent on the story, and a new engine consumer (a second game, pinion) could fabricate story prose freely. The prose is NOT unanchored, though: it is a fail-loud projection of the Markdown manuscripts via TEXT/positional anchors (prose-anchors.json 50-char verbatim prefixes, derive-prose.py); there is NO EPUB and 0 of 66 sections carry an epub_locator. So there are already TWO content-SSOTs (the atomic store for facts, the manuscript for prose) and two provenance chains, but the KERNEL owns only the fact chain. FORK: (1) collapse-to-store-fact = make every rendered sentence a fact — REJECT (a question/epigraph asserts no world-claim; distorts the fact model, overloads the store with non-facts, violates fact-store purity + the structured-fact doctrine "free narrative asserting no structured fact stays in prose, where AI judgment belongs"); (2) content-anchored prose = a rendered unit is provenance-bound to EITHER a store fact_id OR a resolvable content-anchor into the manuscript/content-SSOT — RECOMMEND; (3) two chains, engine owns only facts — REJECT AS TARGET (tide's chain IS closed but per-consumer; the kernel guarantee stays incomplete for any future consumer; a good interim, not the destination). DECISION = fork-2, realized as TWO provenance-bound SIBLING types, NOT a dual-provenance Line (keep Line's fact_id invariant pure): a NEW Passage (crate-private fields + a single constructor joining a resolvable ContentAnchor, no public ctor / no Deserialize = the Line forgery guard applied to prose) carries authored narration; a rendered narrative unit is a fact-Line OR a content-Passage, neither fabricable. ContentAnchor { source, locator: Prefix(String) today = tide's verbatim manuscript prefix | Cfi(String) later } is abstract over the substrate; a Passage carries (anchor, projected text) with fail-loud resolution (the text is what is AT the anchor) + a text-hash drift check = the normative_excerpt EPUB-projected-cache model (R393 epub_locator ingestion / R403 projected cache / R404 offline text-hash drift) generalized from spec sections to narrative prose. This respects the structured-fact SSOT principle (prose lives once in the content-SSOT; the kernel holds a pointer + a fidelity-checked projection, never a restatement) AND fact-store purity AND closes R643's fabrication hole — the three doctrines reconciled, not traded off. It is the SAME CQRS seam and migration shape as objects/ladders/knots (a tide mechanism lifted into the provenance-bound kernel, tide keeping runtime + presentation); the prose mechanism (prose-anchors.json + derive-prose.py) is the LAST one outside the kernel. PHASING: Phase 1 (the BUILD) = engine Passage + ContentAnchor + fail-loud resolution, consumer-SUPPLIED content-SSOT + anchors (no store schema change, defers the store question); Phase 2 = tide migration (segment-prose.json / ladders.json -> engine Passages); Phase 3 (future) = store-owned anchors (generalize epub_locator / normative_excerpt to narrative sections); Phase 4 (future) = Prefix->Cfi, Markdown->EPUB (a substrate swap). OPEN (named): anchor granularity (section vs sub-section; EPUB sub-section-CFI = the contract's open question), one passage stream vs interleaved in SceneView (Phase 2 render), Markdown vs EPUB SSOT (Phase 4). Round 756 — prose-provenance P3 DESIGN:.decision_summary: R756 (DESIGN, code 0 — P3 of the R755 prose-provenance arc; owner chose fork b + additive, 2026-07-23). PROBLEM: R755 closed the prose-invention hole on the CONSUMER side (tide's Passage-bound prose via prose-anchors.json + ManuscriptSource), but the anchor is PER-CONSUMER — the engine's ContentAnchor/Passage (R755) and the store's normative_excerpt/epub_locator (R393/R403/R404) are TWO parallel provenance families with NO bridge (mnemosyne-engine does not depend on mnemosyne-atomic), and the narrative anchor lives in a tide file, not the store, so a manuscript-less consumer (pinion, a generic renderer) cannot get provenance-bound prose and every consumer re-owns the anchor. VERIFIED (subagent mechanism map + a direct read of tide's store): tide's store has 66 Sections whose ids == the spine segments (d01-bam ...), 0 carrying any excerpt; the spec normative_excerpt/epub_locator mechanism is fully built but populated on 0 sections in every committed store (spec-mirror only, for external-standard ledgers like SCE). GOAL: move the prose anchor + projected-text cache + drift INTO the store's Section (generalize normative_excerpt to narrative), so ANY consumer gets provenance-bound prose from the store with no per-consumer anchor file. DECISIONS: (1) ContentAnchor + Locator move to mnemosyne-core (Layer 0, medium-neutral pointers beside SectionSkeleton) so both store (mnemosyne-atomic) and engine (mnemosyne-engine) share them; the engine RE-EXPORTS them (public API mnemosyne_engine::{ContentAnchor, Locator} unchanged); no atomic->engine dependency inversion. (2) ADD AtomicSection.content_excerpt: Option<ContentExcerpt { anchor: ContentAnchor, text, text_sha256 }> = the GENERALIZED anchor + projected-text + drift cache (the L0 ContentAnchor model, not the EPUB-specific epub_locator) — ADDITIVE (owner-chosen): normative_excerpt (the spec/EPUB-external-mirror mechanism, with its extra anchor_url/source_revision identity) is UNCHANGED; convergence (refactor normative_excerpt to hold a ContentExcerpt + its external extras, so spec and narrative share one substrate) is DEFERRED to P3c, narrative-first, not churning the built-but-unused spec mechanism now. (3) Ingestion = consumer-supplied import-content-excerpts: the consumer (which HAS the manuscript) resolves prose + supplies (section_id, anchor, text) triples; the store computes/checks text_sha256 + stores (the import_sections/build_normative_excerpt discipline — one validator/constructor, sha enforced when non-empty); the store never re-derives prose (it has no manuscript). (4) Bridge = engine builds a Passage from a store ContentExcerpt via mnemosyne-ops (the STORE-CACHE model, design section 4 Phase 3): the excerpt's (anchor, text) is provenance-bound at ingestion (manuscript-resolved, sha-pinned), so a Passage built from it is trusted the way a Line is (a store projection), WITHOUT the engine needing the manuscript — this is what lets a manuscript-less consumer get the prose; the forgery guard holds (the constructor takes a store excerpt, never a free string, and the excerpt only exists via ingestion). (5) Drift = generalize scan_content_drift to re-hash content_excerpt (same offline sha check as normative_excerpt, R404). OPEN sub-questions RESOLVED: granularity (Locator::Prefix addresses sub-section now, e.g. ladder rungs; EPUB sub-section CFI stays P4); CACHE THE TEXT in the store, not just the anchor (a manuscript-less consumer needs the prose from the store — the whole point; drift-guarded by sha); Markdown now (Prefix into tide's manuscript), EPUB (Cfi) is P4 the ContentAnchor absorbs; one-passage-stream-vs-interleaved is a P3b render decision. PHASING: P3a (mnemosyne, PUSH-gated: ContentAnchor/Locator to core + content_excerpt field + import-content-excerpts CLI + scan_content_drift coverage + SectionView/report-spec-map expose + schema bump/migration; substrate only, no consumer behaviour change) -> P3b (mnemosyne ops+engine bridge PUSH-gated; then tide LOCAL: tide ingests its prose-anchors.json + ManuscriptSource prose into its store ONCE, then Prose/manuscript.rs read the store excerpts instead of the manuscript + anchor file, and prose-anchors.json + the ManuscriptSource anchor-file dependency are DELETED = the last per-consumer anchor file) -> P3c (future, separate round: normative_excerpt converges onto ContentExcerpt + its spec extras = spec and narrative under ONE prose-anchor substrate; also closes the deferred EngineRung.question residual, since the engine can then resolve a store anchor so the rung question binds). Round 756 — prose-provenance P3 DESIGN:.publishable_decision_summary: R756 (DESIGN, code 0 — P3 of the R755 prose-provenance arc; owner chose fork b + additive, 2026-07-23). PROBLEM: R755 closed the prose-invention hole on the CONSUMER side (tide's Passage-bound prose via prose-anchors.json + ManuscriptSource), but the anchor is PER-CONSUMER — the engine's ContentAnchor/Passage (R755) and the store's normative_excerpt/epub_locator (R393/R403/R404) are TWO parallel provenance families with NO bridge (mnemosyne-engine does not depend on mnemosyne-atomic), and the narrative anchor lives in a tide file, not the store, so a manuscript-less consumer (pinion, a generic renderer) cannot get provenance-bound prose and every consumer re-owns the anchor. VERIFIED (subagent mechanism map + a direct read of tide's store): tide's store has 66 Sections whose ids == the spine segments (d01-bam ...), 0 carrying any excerpt; the spec normative_excerpt/epub_locator mechanism is fully built but populated on 0 sections in every committed store (spec-mirror only, for external-standard ledgers like SCE). GOAL: move the prose anchor + projected-text cache + drift INTO the store's Section (generalize normative_excerpt to narrative), so ANY consumer gets provenance-bound prose from the store with no per-consumer anchor file. DECISIONS: (1) ContentAnchor + Locator move to mnemosyne-core (Layer 0, medium-neutral pointers beside SectionSkeleton) so both store (mnemosyne-atomic) and engine (mnemosyne-engine) share them; the engine RE-EXPORTS them (public API mnemosyne_engine::{ContentAnchor, Locator} unchanged); no atomic->engine dependency inversion. (2) ADD AtomicSection.content_excerpt: Option<ContentExcerpt { anchor: ContentAnchor, text, text_sha256 }> = the GENERALIZED anchor + projected-text + drift cache (the L0 ContentAnchor model, not the EPUB-specific epub_locator) — ADDITIVE (owner-chosen): normative_excerpt (the spec/EPUB-external-mirror mechanism, with its extra anchor_url/source_revision identity) is UNCHANGED; convergence (refactor normative_excerpt to hold a ContentExcerpt + its external extras, so spec and narrative share one substrate) is DEFERRED to P3c, narrative-first, not churning the built-but-unused spec mechanism now. (3) Ingestion = consumer-supplied import-content-excerpts: the consumer (which HAS the manuscript) resolves prose + supplies (section_id, anchor, text) triples; the store computes/checks text_sha256 + stores (the import_sections/build_normative_excerpt discipline — one validator/constructor, sha enforced when non-empty); the store never re-derives prose (it has no manuscript). (4) Bridge = engine builds a Passage from a store ContentExcerpt via mnemosyne-ops (the STORE-CACHE model, design section 4 Phase 3): the excerpt's (anchor, text) is provenance-bound at ingestion (manuscript-resolved, sha-pinned), so a Passage built from it is trusted the way a Line is (a store projection), WITHOUT the engine needing the manuscript — this is what lets a manuscript-less consumer get the prose; the forgery guard holds (the constructor takes a store excerpt, never a free string, and the excerpt only exists via ingestion). OPEN sub-questions RESOLVED: granularity (Locator::Prefix addresses sub-section now, e.g. ladder rungs; EPUB sub-section CFI stays P4); CACHE THE TEXT in the store, not just the anchor (a manuscript-less consumer needs the prose from the store — the whole point; drift-guarded by sha); Markdown now (Prefix into tide's manuscript), EPUB (Cfi) is P4 the ContentAnchor absorbs; one-passage-stream-vs-interleaved is a P3b render decision. Round 757 — field-report §5 root: B-maxi.decision_summary: R757 (DESIGN, code 0 — the field-report §5 ROOT fix; owner-chosen B-maximal, 2026-07-23). The field-report bug (a consumer offered UNDISCLOSED entities as interaction choices via a parallel identity the kernel could not see — a first-night call naming people the player has never met) was fixed on the CONSUMER side in tide (§4, tide `eefa7c9`: the call/substitute cast axis migrated off a hardcoded `NameId`/`name_key`/`[JONGDEUK,BUNOK,PANSU]` array onto `cast.askable` gated by disclosure). That cured the instance but left the KERNEL BLIND-SPOT: the engine's store-projection gates watch only what flows through the store, so a consumer that builds its own identity/data space bypasses them, and a future consumer (pinion) re-introduces the class. DOCTRINE (the default-engine-into-Mnemosyne directive 2026-07-21, itself triggered by a tide field-report bug): the provenance invariant lives in the ENGINE layer so fabrication is inexpressible. PRINCIPLE (owner: ignore YAGNI/cost, most long-term-correct): CQRS to the limit — drive consumer-held world-data to ZERO. The boundary is AUTHORED world-truth (store write-SSOT + engine read-projection: entity identity/kind, disclosure order, prose, quest structure, AND PRESENCE) vs the LIVE play-session (the consumer's cursor/known/taken + presentation chrome/i18n/layout/input). PRESENCE — who is in a scene, who can answer — is authored world-truth (tide and pinion must agree 종득 is present at d08; disagreement is a bug), so it MOVES to store+engine, not the consumer; keeping it in tide (my first YAGNI answer) leaves another consumer world-data space of exactly the field-report class. KEY CONVERGENCE (found by reading a tide prose-cast batch): each `present` entry carries a verbatim manuscript `quote` = the R756 P3a `ContentAnchor`/`ContentExcerpt` shape, so presence-facts RIDE THE SAME PROVENANCE SUBSTRATE as prose — B0 (presence→store) and P3 (prose→store) are ONE model (an un-resolvable quote is an un-assertable presence, the Line/Passage invariant applied to cast). B0 (store): `AtomicSection.scene_cast: Vec<ScenePresence { entity, modality (observed|guessed|told|remembered), can_answer, excerpt: ContentExcerpt }>`, attached like content_excerpt; authored judgments (modality, can_answer) are world-truth so they are STORED, never engine-re-derived (re-deriving an authored judgment loses fidelity); ingestion = consumer-supplied `import-scene-cast` reusing the P3a sha validator (the consumer resolves manuscript forms → store ids and supplies the quote; the store sha-checks and stores, never re-derives); `scan_content_drift` generalizes to scene_cast excerpts (offline sha, R404 discipline). B1 (engine): `PlayableProjection::cast_at` (present + modality + can_answer projected from scene_cast) + `referenceable_entities` (union of disclosed `Line::entities` over the walk at-or-before a section = the §5 discourse-order invariant) + a `GateViolation::ChoiceReferencesUndisclosed`/`AbsentEntity` over consumer-DECLARED choice→entity refs (a new `EngineOverrides` field, the `journal_predicates`/`quest_precondition_predicates` pattern) so any hand-built parallel-identity choice is RED for ANY consumer. B2 (tide, LOCAL): `cast.rs` becomes a thin reader of the engine `cast_at`, the prose-cast batches migrate into the store via `import-scene-cast` ONCE and are DELETED (the last consumer world-data), and tide declares its choice refs so the gate covers the call. This round is DESIGN (code 0); the B0 substrate BUILD (mirroring the R756 P3a 9-file diff, schema v40→v41) is the next round. Scratch = claudedocs/referenceable-entity-set-design.md. SSOT = this entry.

TWO gaps remain after P3a/P3b/R758. GAP 1: NormativeExcerpt (spec, R393/R403/R404; mnemosyne-atomic/src/lib.rs:254) and ContentExcerpt (narrative, R756; lib.rs:320) DUPLICATE text + text_sha256 + recompute_text_sha256 + text_sha256_matches (byte-identical impls) and scan_content_drift re-hashes each family separately — the same provenance shape (a positioned, verbatim, drift-hashed projection) held as two types. GAP 2: the engine's Rung.question is still a bare pass-through String (types.rs:373 "novel-anchored upstream ... not re-checked here" -> projection.rs:260 copies it into Door::Ask), so a manuscript-less/generic consumer (pinion) can fabricate a ladder DOOR LABEL freely (the leak gate checks reveals, never the question prose) — R643's fabrication hole, open on the last authored-prose surface the P3 arc had not reached (R755 sec 7 closed it only CONSUMER-side in tide 5d48c9d). PART 1 DECISION: ContentExcerpt is the ONE substrate (provenance = content-SSOT anchor + verbatim text + drift hash; ContentAnchor is already medium-neutral, a new Locator variant being the substrate swap not a redesign). NormativeExcerpt becomes a spec-facing WRAPPER: { excerpt: ContentExcerpt, anchor_url, source_revision }. KEY distinction between two things that COINCIDE today and DIVERGE later: the content-SSOT anchor (excerpt.anchor, ultimately the EPUB per epub_ssot_architecture) vs the upstream origin (anchor_url + source_revision, which external standards doc + revision the baseline was captured from). Today there is no EPUB baseline so the URL looks like the content-SSOT; the moment one exists, excerpt.anchor becomes an EPUB CFI while anchor_url stays the W3C URL — independent facts, so BOTH are kept. REJECTED "drop anchor_url, make the URL the permanent anchor" (conflates current-location with origin, LOSES the upstream URL once the anchor becomes an EPUB CFI) and "share only a text+text_sha256 tuple" (leaves two anchor families forever, never converges onto ContentExcerpt). Migration v41->v42 is total and blocker-free: synthesize excerpt.anchor from epub_locator IF the section carries one, ELSE from anchor_url (source = anchor_url, locator = Prefix(text) — the passage IS its own verbatim text within the cited doc, the SAME Prefix model narrative uses, so NO new Locator variant); pure field-reshuffle, no field dropped, no data invented, never panics on a missing fragment / query string. Cost-no-object does NOT mean backfilling EPUB CFIs now (that is the SCE-PoC-gated epub_ssot arc); it means the TYPE is EPUB-forward-compatible while the DATA migrates when a baseline lands. VALIDATOR PARITY (CLAUDE.md multi-write-path rule / R305): text/sha invariants live in ONE place — the shared ContentExcerpt validator both import-content-excerpts (narrative) and build_normative_excerpt (spec) route through; the spec-only invariants (anchor_url absolute-http(s)-with-host, source_revision non-blank) layer at the NormativeExcerpt constructor; no field carries two conflicting invariants (anchor.source is legitimately polymorphic — URL for spec, manuscript id for narrative — the URL check being an ADDITIONAL spec-path invariant, not a loosened shared one); a field-invariant-parity test feeds the same edge inputs through both write paths. PART 2 DECISION: Rung MUST stay Deserialize (StaticOverrides::load reads ladders from JSON, overrides.rs:116), so the Passage forgery guard (no Deserialize, sole ctor = resolve) cannot apply directly — which is exactly why the residual could not be a standalone round before P3 (no store resolution path). Now there is one (P3b store_passages / Passage::from_excerpt). So Rung gains question_anchor: Option<ContentAnchor> (plainly constructible / Deserialize — an anchor is consumer INPUT, like Rung.reveals; the guarantee is resolution, not unconstructibility); at projection (Door::Ask assembly) when question_anchor is Some the engine RESOLVES the question text from the section's store content_excerpt and FAILS LOUD if it does not resolve, the resolved text being what the player sees (never the free question); question: String STAYS as the un-anchored fallback for pure interactive chrome (asserting no manuscript prose). The doctrine: a provenance-bound consumer supplies question_anchor and a fabricated door label becomes inexpressible for that consumer — R755 fork-2 ("a rendered unit is provenance-bound to a fact_id OR a content-anchor") extended to the ladder question, the last bare-String authored-prose surface in the engine (mnemosyne-atomic is already an engine dep since R757 B1b, so resolving a store excerpt inside projection is in-crate). PHASING: P3c-1 (store/atomic: converge NormativeExcerpt onto ContentExcerpt + extras + shared validator with the R305 parity test + scan_content_drift reads ne.excerpt + schema v41->v42 + total migration arm + fixture round-trip + repoint the SCE-facing consumers to ne.excerpt.text/ne.anchor_url) -> P3c-2 (engine: question_anchor + fail-loud projection resolve + injection-proven). CLOSES the arc's last open gap (R759 Gap 2): the engine's Rung.question was a bare pass-through String (types.rs:373 "novel-anchored upstream ... not re-checked here" -> projection.rs Door::Ask copied it straight through), so a manuscript-less / generic consumer (pinion) could fabricate a ladder DOOR LABEL freely — the leak gate checks reveals, never the question prose (R643's fabrication hole, the last bare-String authored-prose surface in the engine; R755 sec 7 had closed it only CONSUMER-side in tide 5d48c9d). BUILT: Rung gains question_anchor: Option<ContentAnchor> (Deserialize, #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none)] — a CONSUMER INPUT like reveals; Rung MUST stay Deserialize for StaticOverrides::load overrides.rs:116, so the guarantee is RESOLUTION not unconstructibility). At projection the engine RESOLVES an anchored question from the section's store content_excerpt via the P3b store_passages / Passage::from_excerpt bridge (R757) and FAILS LOUD if it does not resolve; the resolved store text is what renders (never the free question, which STAYS as the un-anchored fallback for pure interactive chrome). Resolution is a new free fn resolve_rung_question: None -> the free question verbatim; Some(anchor) -> the section's Passage MUST exist AND its anchor MUST equal the declared anchor, else EngineError::RungQuestionUnresolvable { section, anchor, reason: RungQuestionFault::{SectionHasNoExcerpt | AnchorMismatch} }. The anchor-equality check is the teeth: a rung cannot claim provenance the store does not back (a false anchor is REJECTED, not silently resolved to whatever the section happens to hold) — R755 fork-2 ("a rendered unit is provenance-bound to a fact_id OR a content-anchor") extended to the ladder question. ARCHITECTURE: resolution is EAGER at construction, not lazy in doors_at — the read path (doors_at / scene / gate) stays infallible and the provenance failure is localized to one build point. PlayableProjection gains a world-independent ask_doors: HashMap<section, Vec<Door>> built once (ladders + excerpts are both section-keyed), which doors_at appends regardless of world; rungs_at is unchanged (the gate still reads reveals / needs structurally). No parallel or versioned constructor was minted: from_report (pure core, empty passages) and from_workspace (loads store_passages) both delegate to ONE crate-internal core from_report_and_passages(report, overrides, passages); from_workspace now does the second store read (store_passages) the anchored question needs. Engine-only — NO store / atomic change (P3c-1 R760 already converged the excerpt substrate). Round 762.decision_summary: R762 (DESIGN, code 0 — P4a: promote the interaction fresh-effect RULE to the default engine, resolving the tide field-report 2026-07-24 §5 dead-"go"-door). Owner picked (b) "the rule belongs in the default engine" over (a) a tide-local patch, and pushed the architectural point: a bug in REACTING to a selection is a BASIC feature the default engine must cover, not something each consumer re-fixes locally. §5 root cause verified in code (tide engine/src/lib.rs): (1) choose_by_key("go:dest") (lib.rs:1909) sets world.at and discloses nothing, while the on-screen tableau is driven only by a `did` beat or a `known` delta — a bare `at` flip changes nothing, so "go" is a dead button; (2) the "no dead door" invariant is HALF-ENFORCED — objects_here (lib.rs:804) and cast_here (lib.rs:850) skip a door whose facts are all already known, but places_here (lib.rs:746) offers a go: for any place with >=1 line with NO known-check. Defect 2 IS the CLAUDE.md half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern (three door-builders, two apply the freshness invariant and one does not) — which is exactly why one kernel-owned rule, shared by all builders, is the correct fix: a second tide patch re-applies the check in a third place but cannot make the FOURTH omission impossible; kernel ownership does. DESIGN DECISION (v2, review-corrected): the kernel gains ONLY the disclose-freshness RULE, as a READ QUERY. A disclose-door is LIVE for a reader holding `known` iff door.discloses() \ known is non-empty; the fresh disclosure IS that set. Kernel surface: Door::discloses() -> &[String] (Examine->reveals, Ask->slice::from_ref(reveals), Fork->&[]); a free fn fresh_disclosure(reveals, known) -> Vec<&str>; PlayableProjection::live_doors_at(world, section, known) -> Vec<Door> filtering the kernel's OWN Examine/Ask doors by freshness and passing Fork through. CQRS-PURE (R643/R337): `known` is a QUERY COORDINATE like world/section — f(frozen_store, coords) -> view; NO reducer (the kernel never computes the next state), NO Standpoint type (v1's carried an `at` field no kernel rule reads), store untouched. §5 fixed with NO dual-write: tide's places_here filters candidates through fresh_disclosure (defect 2); tide's choose_by_key go-arm feeds fresh_disclosure into the EXISTING reveal_probe so the screen changes because known grows (defect 1, "go = move + reveal") — the kernel returns a QUERY, tide's reveal_probe stays the SOLE writer of known and prices the reveal into the summon/count economy (no second write path). Round 763.decision_summary: R763 (BUILD, P4b of the interaction-model promotion arc — R762 DESIGN; mnemosyne engine-only, no store schema change). Landed the disclose-freshness RULE in the default engine, the universal half of the tide field-report §5 fix (the dead-"go"-door). THREE additions to mnemosyne-engine, all pure/read-side: (1) Door::discloses() -> &[String] (types.rs) — Examine returns its reveals, Ask returns its single answer fact via std::slice::from_ref, Fork returns &[] (a nav door discloses no fact); the uniform surface the rule reads. (2) free fn fresh_disclosure(reveals: &[String], known: &HashSet<String>) -> Vec<&str> (projection.rs, re-exported at lib.rs) — the door's discloses() minus what the reader holds, order-preserving; empty = the door is DEAD. THE universal rule: the kernel applies it to its own doors, a consumer applies the SAME fn to a door IT builds (tide's go-door reachable facts the kernel never holds), so every disclose-door obeys one liveness definition and the half-enforced-invariant class cannot recur. (3) PlayableProjection::live_doors_at(world, section, known) -> Vec<Door> — doors_at filtered so an Examine/Ask door whose discloses() is fully known is dropped and a Fork passes through unchanged (navigational liveness = not-taken is the consumer's, never disclosure-relative). CQRS-PURE (R643/R337): known is a QUERY COORDINATE like world/section — f(frozen_store, coords) -> view; NO reducer (the kernel computes no successor state), NO Standpoint type, store untouched; a door filtered out is not mutated away and a different known yields a different answer from the same immutable projection. The kernel's Ask is reveal-priced (the gate G5 already models it as reveal-bearing), so live_doors_at filters it by reveal-freshness; tide's ACT-priced dialog rung liveness (next_rung / reveal_probe pricing) is a separate richer model that stays entirely in tide — a consumer that wants act-pricing keeps its own rung liveness and simply does not route act-rungs through live_doors_at (the design's "act-priced rungs stay tide"). The v1 kernel state machine the three adversarial reviews demolished is absent by construction: no apply/Standpoint/visible_lines/Door::Move/DeadDoor gate. VERIFICATION: 3 injection tests (projection.rs) — discloses reports each door kind's disclosure (Fork empty, Examine the set, Ask a one-element slice); fresh_disclosure is the not-known subset in door order (whole set at empty known, middle-dropped when one known, empty when all known); live_doors_at drops a fully-known Examine door but keeps the fresh Ask + the Fork, and at both-known only the Fork survives — the §5 dead-door made structurally unofferable through the kernel's own doors while navigation remains. 1182 workspace tests green (scripts/verify.sh, +3 from R761's 1179), clippy -D + fmt clean. Round 764 — build-time projection DESIGN.decision_summary:
R764 (DESIGN, code 0) — projection at BUILD time, and the sub-section coordinate that makes it need no consumer script. Origin: the tide lift request claudedocs/MNEMOSYNE-LIFT-REQUEST-projection-at-build-time.md (pinned at 08e71f0), which measured PlayableProjection::from_workspace re-projecting the whole store on every run and asked for ONE thing: Deserialize on PlayableWorldReport so the projection could be baked at build time and read back at runtime. The owner then gave the directive that reshapes the answer — remove runtime validation, make it all compile-time — and, when my first shape pushed derivation work into a consumer build script, the one-word correction: the store.

REJECTED, the request as written. Two independent reasons, either sufficient. (a) serde is structurally incapable of compile-time verification: unknown fields are ignored and a missing Option silently becomes None, so a baked JSON survives every engine type change without a word. For a build-time artifact JSON is the worst available medium precisely on the axis the directive cares about. (b) It would widen a provenance hole that mnemosyne-engine's own module doc claims is closed. That doc says invention is unrepresentable, a compile error and not a test to remember, and Line really is locked (non_exhaustive, pub(crate) fields, a sole crate-private from_disclosed ctor) — but its INPUT is not: PlayableProjection::from_report is pub and PlayableWorldReport with its twelve nested types are all pub-field with no non_exhaustive, so a downstream crate can hand the kernel a fabricated report and the kernel mints Lines from the forgery. The guarantee is one layer too shallow TODAY; the derive would have turned a Rust-only fabrication path into a file-shaped one. Recorded so the request is not re-proposed unchanged: ForkTreeBranch.converges carries skip_serializing_if Vec::is_empty with no serde default, so every fork or standalone world omits the key and the naive derive fails to deserialize the first real report — the repo pairs default with skip in all 31 of its Deserialize sites.

THE HONEST FORM OF THE DIRECTIVE. rustc cannot read the store, so "all compile-time" is two things, and conflating them would be an overclaim. Store-DATA checks (a dangling locator, an unresolvable anchor, grounding, the ladder prose gates) move to BUILD TIME, into the one place that holds the store, where they become a build failure instead of a runtime one. What rustc actually carries is the SHAPE contract between the generated artifact and the engine types: change an engine type and the build breaks — the thing JSON can never give. The slogan is therefore not "delete the checks" but "delete the input that needs checking": zero runtime validation because zero runtime input. Explicitly NOT claimed: GateViolation and the quest preconditions are game rules over player state rather than artifact validation, and they stay at runtime.

NO CONSUMER SCRIPT. cargo's only build-time hook is build.rs, so the hook stays; what must not stay is logic inside it. The consumer's build.rs is a one-line delegation into a mnemosyne crate, and everything else — reading the store, declaring cargo:rerun-if-changed, emitting the tables — lives here. My first shape failed this: it asked tide to move its Objects and Ladders loading into build time, which is to say it asked a consumer to CREATE a derivation script in its own repo, the exact artifact class the engine census pass condition is driving to zero. The owner's "why a script?" killed that shape, and the answer to "then where does Interactivity come from?" was: the store.

WHAT MAKES THAT POSSIBLE, read from the programs rather than the data (R668's sign). The objects axis is already store-derived: tide's Objects::ids() is the key set of its object-names.json, and tide's own G1/G2 test asserts that set EQUALS the store's kind:object entities in both directions via mnemosyne_engine::store_entity_kinds — so the emitter filters store entity kinds and needs no consumer input and no schema change, while object-names.json stays the consumer's because names are presentation. The ladder axis is store-owed structure plus a rule that belongs in the default engine: ladder-anchors.json declares nothing but store coordinates (a carrier entity, a prose-prefix anchor, needs and reveals fact ids, an object entity), and ladders.rs derive() is a program over store prose — it locates each declared anchor verbatim and uniquely inside the seat's content_excerpt, requires the anchors to appear in prose order, requires a non-empty frame, and cuts each span into question (the first line) and answer (the rest). A declaration plus the program enforcing it means the program is the spec, and this program reads the store and belongs in the kernel (the R762/R763 precedent that the RULE belongs to the default engine, and R758's precedent that the grounding CHECK moved into the engine rather than being re-implemented per consumer).

THE ROOT GAP THE TWO FINDINGS SHARE. The store's coordinates stop at the section: canon refs, content_excerpt anchors, and DisclosureReveal coords are all section-granular. The playable layer needs a SUB-SECTION coordinate — this fact opens at THIS LINE of that seat — and tide built one out of mnemosyne's own ContentAnchor, Locator::Prefix, and Passage types because the store cannot express it. The same gap is why R761's P3c-2 has no consumer: it requires the declared anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, so a rung question, which IS a slice of the seat's store excerpt, has no anchor it can declare. Correct the record: tide's ladder questions are store prose today, and the ladders.rs comment calling them un-anchored authored chrome is inaccurate — the None is an expressiveness gap on OUR side, not a provenance opt-out on theirs. And rung reveals is not a structure parallel to R752's DisclosureReveal but its sub-section refinement: the store says a fact is revealed at a section, the ladder says at which rung within it and gated on what.

DECIDED SEQUENCE, four commit-sized rounds, each PUSH-gated. R765 store: the sub-section coordinate plus the ladder declaration on the section, dangling-ref validation against facts/entities/sections, schema v42 to v43 with a total migration arm; coordinates only, no derived prose stored, since the content_excerpt already holds it. R766 engine: store_interactivity(root) — objects from store entity kinds, ladders derived from the declaration by the kernel running the locate/order/frame gates fail-loud — and question_anchor expressible at sub-section granularity, so R761's guarantee reaches its first real consumer. R767: a new crate mnemosyne-engine-build (mirroring the sce_build precedent tide's build.rs already uses) carrying StaticProjection (all &'static and const-constructible), an INFALLIBLE PlayableProjection::from_static, and emit_playable_projection writing OUT_DIR with its rerun-if-changed declarations, proven by a fixture-store equivalence test across every public query; the same round narrows from_report out of the public API so the module doc's claim finally becomes true. tide's half runs in a tide session per the cross-repo rule.

REVERSED ON PURPOSE, and not quietly. quest.rs states that the kernel reads the store at RUNTIME so that the compile-time snapshot a consumer would otherwise bake in cannot drift from the store. The anti-drift property comes from DERIVING FROM THE STORE, not from the timing: an artifact regenerated under cargo:rerun-if-changed and never committed cannot go stale, and the compile-time contract is strictly stronger, since an engine type change breaks the build where a JSON snapshot would pass. The honest residual is that a pre-built distributed binary is pinned to the store revision it was built from — the same class of trade tide already makes by pinning mnemosyne to a git rev. That sentence gets corrected in R767 rather than left contradicting the shipped design.

WEAK POINTS, recorded so they are not rediscovered as objections. StaticProjection must expose pub fields for generated code to construct a static, so the fabrication surface MOVES from a runtime file to a build script instead of vanishing; that is an improvement, not forgery-proofing, and a malicious consumer was never the threat model. A large generated file trades startup milliseconds for compile seconds. And most of the PERFORMANCE win is in the first half — removing the store read — while the infallible from_static buys verification LOCATION rather than speed; emitting the report as a Rust literal and calling from_report would have been roughly ninety percent of the speed with the runtime Result left intact, and the remaining tenth is bought for the provenance and the type contract, not the milliseconds.

R765 (BUILD, store-only, first of the R764 sequence) — the section ladder: the store learns the sub-section coordinate. AtomicSection gains `ladder: Option<SectionLadder>` = { carrier: Option<entity>, rungs: Vec<LadderRung> }, and LadderRung = { anchor: ContentAnchor, needs: Vec<fact>, reveals: Vec<fact>, object: Option<entity> }. Written by the new `import-ladders` verb (manifest `ladder-map/v1`: {ladders: [{section_id, carrier, rungs}]}), each section's ladder REPLACED by its entry, the `import_scene_cast` grouping rule. Schema v42 to v43.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO R764, stated here in prose because the ledger is frozen and append-only.

FIRST, R764 said this round would carry a TOTAL migration arm. It does not, and should not. The field is ADDITIVE with a serde default, which is the v39-to-v40 content_excerpt and v40-to-v41 scene_cast pattern the schema comment block already documents as deliberately arm-less: a pre-v43 section has no `ladder` key, serde fills `None`, serialization skips `None`, and an un-laddered store stays byte-identical to what a pre-v43 binary wrote. A migration arm exists for SHAPE changes to existing data (v38-to-v39 first_at, v41-to-v42 normative_excerpt); inventing one for an additive field would be ceremony that reads as data movement and is not. A test pins the byte-identity claim rather than leaving it asserted in a comment.

SECOND, and larger: R764 said this round would introduce the sub-section coordinate. It already existed. `mnemosyne_core::ContentAnchor { source, locator: Prefix | Cfi }` is a Layer-0 type the store has held since R756, `ContentExcerpt.anchor` is one, and `mnemosyne_engine::ContentAnchor` is a RE-EXPORT of it rather than a sibling — so there was never a coordinate to build, only a rule that refused to accept one. R761 requires a declared rung anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, which is what makes a hold part-way down a scene inexpressible and is why the first consumer passes `question_anchor: None`. That narrowing is a RESOLUTION rule and it is the engine's to relax (R766), not the store's. What this round adds is therefore not the coordinate but the DECLARATION that uses it.

WHAT THE STORE CHECKS, AND WHAT IT REFUSES TO. Every reference is checked present before the save, never a partial import: `needs` and `reveals` must be `narrative_facts` keys, `carrier` and a rung's `object` must be registered entities, the anchor must name a non-empty source and carry a non-empty `Locator::Prefix`, and two rungs of one ladder may not declare the SAME anchor. A ladder whose coordinates dangle is a gate that silently never opens, which is exactly the failure a store is for. A CFI locator is REJECTED rather than stored: a sub-section coordinate into authored narrative prose is a prefix today, and accepting a CFI would store a coordinate nothing in the pipeline can resolve.

What the store deliberately does NOT check is whether each prefix actually occurs in the section's `content_excerpt`, exactly once, in the declared order. That is the resolution rule, the engine owns it (it is the one that slices the excerpt at these anchors), and duplicating it here would make one invariant answer to two write paths — the half-enforced-invariant class CLAUDE.md names. The store stores coordinates; the engine judges whether they land. For the same reason the declared rung ORDER is stored verbatim rather than normalized: whether it must agree with the prose order is a question about resolution, so the store keeps what the author said and leaves exactly one place to judge it.

NO PROSE IS STORED. A rung carries no rendered word — its prose IS the excerpt's own text from its anchor line to the next rung's. So the declaration cannot smuggle in a sentence the store does not already hold, and the Line/Passage provenance invariant carries down one level of resolution for free rather than needing a second grounding check.

Round 766 — the kernel's prose slicer st.decision_summary:
R766 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — the kernel's prose slicer stops guessing. `PrefixSlices::new` is the engine's one implementation of "cut a document at its declared anchors", and R765 found it strictly WEAKER than the consumer slicer it is meant to replace: where the consumer rejects an ambiguous anchor, this took `text.find`, i.e. the FIRST occurrence, silently; and where the consumer rejects a duplicated anchor, the slice map's `insert` overwrote the twin silently. Two declared holds, one surviving slice, no error. Moving the ladder rule into a primitive with those holes would have been a regression wearing a promotion's clothes, so the debt is paid BEFORE the promotion rather than after it, and it is paid for every consumer at once. Two new fail-loud faults: `ProseError::PrefixAmbiguous { source, prefix, occurrences }` and `ProseError::DuplicateAnchor { source, prefix }`.

SCOPE CORRECTION TO R765's CARRY, stated in prose because the ledger is frozen. R765 said R766 would tighten the slicer AND land `store_interactivity`. It lands only the tightening. The tightening is complete, independently correct, and useful to every current caller with no consumer in sight; bundling it with the interactivity projection would have made a round whose two halves fail for unrelated reasons. `store_interactivity` moves to R767 and the emitter crate to R768.

WHAT I GOT WRONG FIRST, RECORDED BECAUSE THE TEST CAUGHT IT AND NOT ME. I initially tightened a THIRD invariant into the same place: that the declared anchor order must equal the prose order (the consumer's G3). The engine's own test suite rejected it immediately — `a_passage_projects_the_manuscript_slice_at_its_anchor` feeds deliberately unsorted anchors and the doc comment called the input order-independent, on purpose. That is right and my change was wrong: `PrefixSlices` is a GENERIC slicer, an anchor set may legitimately arrive from a map, and a generic slicer has no business demanding that a caller's iteration order match a document. Order is meaningful for a LADDER, whose nth rung must be the nth passage — it is a property of that caller's semantics, not of slicing. Pushing it down here would have made every unordered caller pay for one ordered caller's rule, which is the same category error as putting a markdown parser in the fact engine (the W-rejection). So the order check is NOT here.

But it must not be re-implemented upstairs either — a second `find` walk in the ladder layer would be a second locator, free to drift from this one. The primitive therefore EXPOSES the ordering it already computed: `PrefixSlices::in_prose_order() -> &[ContentAnchor]`, the anchors in the order their prefixes occur, built during the one locate pass. An ordered caller judges its declared order against that. One search, one truth, and the semantic question is answered by the layer that owns the semantics — the same split as R765's store-stores-coordinates / engine-judges-resolution line.

WHY AMBIGUITY AND DUPLICATION ARE DIFFERENT FROM ORDER, and belong here: neither depends on any caller's semantics. A prefix occurring twice names no single place for ANY caller, and picking an occurrence is picking a slice on the author's behalf; the remedy is to extend the prefix, which is an authoring fix, not a guess the kernel should make. A duplicated anchor is a caller declaring one coordinate twice and getting one slice, which is never what was meant. Round 767 — a rung takes hold part-way d.decision_summary:
R767 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — a rung may now take hold part-way down a scene. This is the round the whole arc exists for: R761 bound a ladder question to store prose but required the declared anchor to EQUAL the section's excerpt anchor, and a rung question is one LINE of a scene, not the whole scene. So the only expressible anchor was the useless one, the first provenance-bound consumer declared `question_anchor: None` for every rung, and the guarantee never reached a real ladder. `resolve_rung_question` is replaced by `resolve_ladder_questions`, which resolves a whole section's ladder at once against the section's `content_excerpt`.

THE NEW RULE: an anchor must name the SAME document as the section's excerpt and must LOCATE within its text. Locating goes through R766's tightened `PrefixSlices`, so a prefix naming two lines is refused rather than resolved to the first, and a hold declared twice is refused rather than silently collapsed. A hold's question is then the LINE it starts at, not its slice: the slice runs to the next hold and carries whatever follows the question, which is the scene's business and not the door's label.

WHY A WHOLE LADDER AT ONCE, and not a rung at a time. The order invariant needs the ladder. R766 deliberately kept "the declared order must be the prose order" OUT of the generic slicer — a slicer must not demand that a caller's iteration order match a document — and left `in_prose_order()` exposed so an ordered caller could judge for itself. This is that caller: the nth declared hold must be the nth passage, or the author's numbering does not describe the scene they wrote. Resolving per-rung would have had no place to ask that question, and re-deriving the offsets here would have been a second locator free to drift from the first. One search in the primitive, one judgment in the layer that owns the semantics.

TWO NEW FAULTS on `RungQuestionFault`: `Unlocatable(Box<ProseError>)` carrying the slicer's own cause (wrong document, absent prefix, ambiguous prefix, duplicated hold) and `OutOfProseOrder`. `AnchorMismatch` is GONE, not deprecated — it named the narrowing this round removes, and keeping it would leave a variant no code can produce (no-legacy-carry). The payload is boxed because carrying `ProseError` inside `EngineError` widened every `Result` on the read path past clippy's `result_large_err` threshold; the fault is rare and the return is not, so the box goes on the rare thing. That was clippy's catch, not mine, and it is fixed at the cause rather than allowed away.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LOOSEN. An un-anchored rung still keeps its free question — un-anchored interactive chrome is a legitimate thing for a consumer to author, and the store never claimed it. A section carrying NO anchored rung no longer needs an excerpt at all (previously any ladder forced the lookup); a section with even one anchored rung and no excerpt is still `SectionHasNoExcerpt`, fail-loud. The guarantee remains RESOLUTION rather than unconstructibility, because `Rung` must stay `Deserialize` for `StaticOverrides::load` — that only changes when the runtime override-loading path goes away, which is R769's business.

VERIFICATION: 3 injection tests, each non-vacuous in BOTH directions rather than merely asserting a reject. The capability test puts TWO holds at two different lines of one excerpt and asserts each door's label is ITS line — not the free string, not the whole excerpt, and not the first line for both, which is what a naive implementation would produce. The order test rejects the same two anchors declared backwards AND asserts the identical pair in prose order is accepted, so the reject is the order and not the anchors. The ambiguity test rejects a prefix naming two lines AND asserts the extended prefix resolves, so the reject is the ambiguity and not a refusal to anchor on a recurring name. 1191 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+3 on R766's 1188), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0.

With that, a consumer stops constructing its interactive layer from its own files, which is what makes the build script of R769 a delegation with no logic in it.

THE SPLIT THIS ROUND KEEPS. `store_interactivity` reads COORDINATES and never prose: a derived rung carries its hold's anchor and an EMPTY question, and the label is resolved later by R767's per-ladder resolver against the section's own excerpt. Round 769 — a projection re-enters the k.decision_summary:
R769 (BUILD, engine-only, no store change) — the runtime seam: a projection can leave and re-enter the kernel with NO check on the way back in. `PlayableProjection::to_parts` emits the whole indexed projection as plain data; `PlayableProjection::from_parts` takes it back, and takes NO `Result`. That signature is the round: it is the first place in this arc where the directive "런타임 검증 없애고 전부 컴파일 타임 검증으로" is visible as a type rather than as a plan.

SCOPE SPLIT FROM R768's CARRY, stated in prose because the ledger is frozen. R768 said R769 would be the emitter crate — the parts seam AND the code generation AND the `from_report` narrowing AND the quest.rs correction. That is two rounds' worth and its halves fail for unrelated reasons, so this round lands the SEAM (complete, verified, useful on its own) and R770 lands the emitter crate that writes parts as Rust source, narrows `from_report`, and corrects quest.rs.

WHY `from_parts` CAN BE INFALLIBLE, which is the only interesting question here. Not optimism: every check that `from_workspace` runs has already run by the time parts exist. The store read happened, the locator join happened, the ladder questions resolved against real prose (R767). What comes back in is the RESULT of those checks, not their input. So there is nothing to validate — and the deeper point is that this is not "we skipped the checks", it is "there is no untrusted input left to check". A consumer that bakes does no startup validation because it takes in nothing that could be wrong: the artifact is generated from the store by its own build and type-checked by its own compiler.

WHY PARTS AT ALL, rather than emitting the runtime types directly. `Line` and `CastMember` keep crate-private fields so that invention is unrepresentable — which also means generated code in ANOTHER crate cannot construct them. Hence `LinePart` / `CastPart`: pub-field mirrors the engine converts back inside the crate, where the private constructors are reachable. Everything else in the projection (`Door`, `Fork`, `Rung`, `ChoiceEntityRef`, `Interactivity`) already has public fields, so only those two needed a mirror. The guard this does NOT weaken is the one that matters: a RENDERER still cannot mint a sentence, because a renderer holds a `Line` and never a part. The guard it DOES move is the ingestion one — and that was already open at the report boundary (R764 weak point 1). A build-time forger and a report forger are the same forger, and neither is the threat model. R770 narrows the OTHER ingestion door (`from_report`) so there is one instead of two.

DETERMINISM IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, not a nicety: `to_parts` emits every map in sorted key order and the divergent-ending set sorted, so the same store produces byte-identical generated source and a rebuild that changed nothing changes nothing. Without that, `cargo:rerun-if-changed` would still fire correctly but every rebuild would churn the generated file and its downstream compile.

VERIFICATION: one equivalence test, and it is the whole claim of the arc stated as an assertion — a projection that goes out through `to_parts` and back through `from_parts` answers EVERY public query identically: `telling`, `spine`, and per world per section `walk`, `is_divergent_ending`, `lines`, `title`, `cursor_of`, `cast_at`, `forks_at`, `scene`, `referenceable_entities`, `live_doors_at`. It also asserts the ask doors survive with their RESOLVED labels, which is what lets a runtime with no store still show store prose, and that `to_parts` is idempotent across the round trip.

The test was made honest twice over. First, its fixture was THICKENED after the thin one proved little: a one-scene one-world report leaves `cast`, `forks`, and `divergent_endings` empty, so dropping any of those fields in `from_parts` would have passed. It now runs two worlds, a fork tree, and scene cast, and asserts up front that the fixture actually carries cast and a fork before comparing anything. Second, non-vacuity was PROVEN by injection rather than argued: dropping `cast` from `from_parts` fails the test, dropping `forks` fails it, and restoring each passes.

A NEAR-MISS worth recording, because it looked like a kernel defect and was not. The first thick fixture gave one world a scene WITH cast and its sibling the same scene WITHOUT, and `cast_at` came back empty — the projection lets the first world to carry a section fix its cast, and worlds iterate in sorted order, so the empty one won. That is not a bug: scene presence is authored on the SHARED section, so every world walking it sees one cast, and the fixture had built a state the store cannot produce. The fixture was corrected rather than the kernel. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it as a finding.

Round 771 — the ingestion door closes an.decision_summary:
R771 (BUILD, engine + render, no store change) — the ingestion door closes, and the crate's headline promise becomes true. `mnemosyne-engine`'s module doc has said since R643 that invention is unrepresentable: a downstream crate can READ a `Line` but never fabricate one, "a compile error here, not a test to remember". R764 found that claim was true of the RENDER side and false of the INGEST side — `PlayableProjection::from_report` was public and every type inside a `PlayableWorldReport` is a pub-field struct with no `non_exhaustive`, so a consumer could hand the kernel a fabricated world and receive real `Line`s minted from it. The guard sat one layer above the hole. This round takes `from_report` off the public API, leaving `ProjectionParts` as the single ingestion door.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT BUY, stated carefully because the temptation is to overclaim a win. It does not make forgery impossible: `ProjectionParts` is plain data BY NECESSITY, since generated code cannot construct a `#[non_exhaustive]` type, so an author who edits their own build script still forges their own game — which the threat model always allowed and R764 recorded as weak point 1. What it buys is that there is now ONE door instead of two, and the remaining one is filled by a build from the store rather than written by hand. The render-side guarantee — a renderer holds a `Line` and cannot mint a sentence — is untouched and was never the thing in doubt.

THE NARROWING IS PROVEN BY A PAIR OF DOCTESTS, not by one. A lone `compile_fail` passes when its snippet fails for ANY reason, so a typo'd path would "prove" the guard while proving nothing — the classic way this kind of test lies. So the positive half (`from_parts` resolves) must COMPILE and the negative half repeats the same path spelling before adding `from_report`. A wrong path now breaks the suite instead of faking a pass.

GATED, NOT MERELY NARROWED. Taking `from_report` off the public API left it with no caller outside tests, and the dead-code lint said so immediately. Rather than silence that with an allow, the function is marked `#[cfg(test)]`, which is what it now is: a test helper that builds a projection from a report with no passages. The alternative — deleting it and inlining `HashMap::new()` at some thirty in-crate call sites — is churn for no gain, and the name carries meaning the inline would lose.

THE ONE EXTERNAL CALLER WAS REHOMED, and usefully. `mnemosyne-render`'s test fixture built a `PlayableWorldReport` by hand and called `from_report`; it now builds a `ProjectionParts` and calls `from_parts`. That is not just a port: it makes render a SECOND downstream crate exercising the ingestion door, so if parts ever readmit a type a foreign crate cannot construct (the R769 defect R770 fixed), two crates stop compiling instead of one. The fixture also got smaller — a report is a manuscript shape that the projection immediately indexes away, while parts are what the projection actually holds.

ALSO CORRECTED: `quest.rs` said the kernel reads the quest graph "at runtime" so that "the compile-time snapshot a consumer would otherwise bake in cannot drift from the store". R764 decided to reverse that reasoning rather than quietly contradict it, and this is where the sentence gets rewritten: the anti-drift property comes from DERIVING FROM THE STORE, not from the timing. A projection baked under `cargo:rerun-if-changed` and never committed cannot go stale either, and it carries a check a runtime read cannot — change a kernel type and the generated source stops compiling. The honest residual is stated where the claim is: a pre-built binary is pinned to the store revision it was built from, the same trade a consumer already makes pinning this workspace by git rev. The quest axis has no baked path yet; nothing there argues against one now.

VERIFICATION: 1199 workspace tests green via scripts/verify.sh (+2 on R770's 1197 — the doctest pair), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace T1 orphan = 0 and T3 reject = 0, validate-code-refs 0. The dead-code finding was fixed at the cause (the function really is test-only) rather than allowed away, which is the same discipline R767 applied to `result_large_err` and R770 to `needless_doctest_main`: three lint findings across this arc, three fixed at the cause, no allows added.

THE MNEMOSYNE HALF OF THIS ARC IS DONE. Eight rounds from a lift request that asked for one `Deserialize`: R764 rejected it and reshaped the answer, R765 gave the store the ladder declaration, R766 stopped the prose slicer guessing, R767 let a rung take hold part-way down a scene, R768 derived the interactive layer from the store, R769 built the infallible seam, R770 built the emitter that compiles its own output, and R771 closed the door the review found open. What remains is the consumer's own session.

Round 771 — the ingestion door closes an.publishable_decision_summary:
R771 (BUILD, engine + render, no store change) — the ingestion door closes, and the crate's headline promise becomes true. `mnemosyne-engine`'s module doc has said since R643 that invention is unrepresentable: a downstream crate can READ a `Line` but never fabricate one, "a compile error here, not a test to remember". R764 found that claim was true of the RENDER side and false of the INGEST side — `PlayableProjection::from_report` was public and every type inside a `PlayableWorldReport` is a pub-field struct with no `non_exhaustive`, so a consumer could hand the kernel a fabricated world and receive real `Line`s minted from it. The guard sat one layer above the hole. This round takes `from_report` off the public API, leaving `ProjectionParts` as the single ingestion door.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT BUY, stated carefully because the temptation is to overclaim a win. It does not make forgery impossible: `ProjectionParts` is plain data BY NECESSITY, since generated code cannot construct a `#[non_exhaustive]` type, so an author who edits their own build script still forges their own game — which the threat model always allowed and R764 recorded as weak point 1. What it buys is that there is now ONE door instead of two, and the remaining one is filled by a build from the store rather than written by hand. The render-side guarantee — a renderer holds a `Line` and cannot mint a sentence — is untouched and was never the thing in doubt.

THE NARROWING IS PROVEN BY A PAIR OF DOCTESTS, not by one. A lone `compile_fail` passes when its snippet fails for ANY reason, so a typo'd path would "prove" the guard while proving nothing — the classic way this kind of test lies. So the positive half (`from_parts` resolves) must COMPILE and the negative half repeats the same path spelling before adding `from_report`. A wrong path now breaks the suite instead of faking a pass.

GATED, NOT MERELY NARROWED. Taking `from_report` off the public API left it with no caller outside tests, and the dead-code lint said so immediately. Rather than silence that with an allow, the function is marked `#[cfg(test)]`, which is what it now is: a test helper that builds a projection from a report with no passages. The alternative — deleting it and inlining `HashMap::new()` at some thirty in-crate call sites — is churn for no gain, and the name carries meaning the inline would lose.

THE ONE EXTERNAL CALLER WAS REHOMED, and usefully. `mnemosyne-render`'s test fixture built a `PlayableWorldReport` by hand and called `from_report`; it now builds a `ProjectionParts` and calls `from_parts`. That is not just a port: it makes render a SECOND downstream crate exercising the ingestion door, so if parts ever readmit a type a foreign crate cannot construct (the R769 defect R770 fixed), two crates stop compiling instead of one. The fixture also got smaller — a report is a manuscript shape that the projection immediately indexes away, while parts are what the projection actually holds.

ALSO CORRECTED: `quest.rs` said the kernel reads the quest graph "at runtime" so that "the compile-time snapshot a consumer would otherwise bake in cannot drift from the store". R764 decided to reverse that reasoning rather than quietly contradict it, and this is where the sentence gets rewritten: the anti-drift property comes from DERIVING FROM THE STORE, not from the timing. A projection baked under `cargo:rerun-if-changed` and never committed cannot go stale either, and it carries a check a runtime read cannot — change a kernel type and the generated source stops compiling. The honest residual is stated where the claim is: a pre-built binary is pinned to the store revision it was built from, the same trade a consumer already makes pinning this workspace by git rev. The quest axis has no baked path yet; nothing there argues against one now.

Round 772 — the bake watched a file the.decision_summary:
R772 (BUILD, ops + engine + engine-build, no store change) — a defect found in R770 while reading the consumer's second lift request, fixed before its actual ask is built on top of it. R770's emitter printed `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for three HAND-WRITTEN paths: `mnemosyne.toml`, `docs/.atomic/workspace.atomic.json`, `canon-order.json`. The first real consumer declares `[atomic] sidecar_path = ".atomic/tide.atomic.json"`. So the bake watched a store that does not exist in that workspace and never watched the one it read: rebuild the store, and the baked projection stays whatever it was, silently.

THE CLAIM THAT WAS FALSE. This crate's module doc carries a section titled "Why the artifact cannot go stale", and its argument is exactly the rerun declaration. The argument held for a workspace that happens to use every default and failed for the only consumer the crate was written for. A declared input that is not the file the loader OPENS is worse than making no claim: an undeclared dependency is visibly absent, while a wrong one reads as watched. Two of the three paths were wrong the same way — `canon-order.json` is `[continuity] canon_order_path`, configurable — and the third assumed `mnemosyne.toml` at the root, though `discover_config` also accepts `.mnemosyne/config.toml` and walks upward.

THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SECOND CORRECT LIST. `mnemosyne_ops::projection_inputs` resolves the config through `discover_config` and the sidecar through `resolve_sidecar` — the same two resolutions `playable_world_report` and `quest_graph_report` use to open those files — and returns the resolved config path, the declared canon-order file, and the sidecar. `mnemosyne_engine::projection_inputs` reads it through so a consumer talks to its kernel rather than past it into `ops` (the `store_entity_kinds` precedent), and `emit_playable_projection` calls that. `mnemosyne-engine-build` now holds no path knowledge at all. Writing a second, correct list would have fixed today's bug and left the same drift open for tomorrow's.

THE ORACLE IS THE RESOLVER, NOT A HAND-WRITTEN EXPECTATION. The test asserts the declared sidecar EQUALS what `resolve_sidecar` returns for that workspace, because a hand-written expected list is a copy of exactly the class of bug being killed and would have been just as wrong in R770. Non-vacuity was proven by injection rather than argued: putting `default_sidecar_path` back made the test fail with "the sidecar the loader opens (/tmp/.../.atomic/tide.atomic.json) is not declared", which is the consumer's real configuration.

WHAT WAS KEPT AND WHAT WAS DROPPED. R770's conservative-listing property — a path that does not exist is still declared, so creating it rebuilds — was right and is kept: a workspace with no config declares its would-be `mnemosyne.toml`, since creating one moves the sidecar. What is dropped is guessing the contents. The list stays exactly what the two projections open; `[continuity] rules_path` is not declared because neither reads it, and declaring an unread file buys spurious rebuilds. Inputs are now declared BEFORE the projection runs, so the dependency registers even when the projection then fails.
