Round 883.decision_summary: R883 BUILD (replaying every declared unit at its own revision — and the mechanism immediately caught two of our own errors, one of them mine from four rounds earlier): every one of the 23 declared revisions still BUILDS, 32 of the 35 replay-input manifests import cleanly at the revision that authored them, and every single successful replay is DETERMINISTIC across two separate processes. R880 measured one revision, deliberately the oldest; this measures all of them. Build times are 12-15 seconds each. So the pin-the-revision design is not feasible at a sample — it is feasible at the whole corpus, today. THE THREE FAILURES ARE THE ROUND. The first is OURS AND IT IS MINE: `2d-projection/v1/run/author/facts.json` failed at `14d7a1e0`, THE REVISION THAT PRODUCED IT, because R879 edited that manifest in place to make it readable by today's binary. R879 argued the edit was safe because the transcription provably preserved content — the (telling, fact, branch, coords) triples were compared before and after and were identical — and that argument was RIGHT and the conclusion was WRONG. Measured here: the original bytes import at `14d7a1e0` cleanly (20 sections, 59 facts, 7 disclosure overrides); the edited bytes do not. The edit bought readability by today's tool at the price of readability by its own, which is the whole property the record exists to have. The rule R879 wrote for itself — "provable transcription in place, model re-decision as a derived copy" — has no exception for transcriptions, and R873 had it right from the start: the record is never edited, and a shape today's tool needs lives in a derived copy. So the record is back to its authored bytes, the migrated version now lives at `tests/fixtures/projection-2d-author/` beside a README that says why, and the R879 smoke test reads its facts from there while still reading sections, order and rules straight out of the record. Both halves verified: the restored record replays at `14d7a1e0`, and the derived copy still passes the R879 gate. THE OTHER TWO ARE A FORMAT FINDING, not a data one: `disclosure-craft`'s A and B facts manifests fail with `frame 'ground' not present in the frames registry`, and reading them shows why — they declare only `entities`, `facts`, `predicates`, so the frames their facts reference were registered by an earlier step the kit's runbook performed and R882's declaration does not record. The pairing is not wrong, it is INSUFFICIENT: a replay unit is not always (sections, facts), and `kit-replay/v1` can express a pair but not a sequence. That is the next increment of the schema and it is named rather than hacked around. WHAT THIS ROUND ESTABLISHES: the expected-output leg of the triple is now buildable — 32 digests were computed and each was confirmed by running its revision twice — but they are NOT written into the declarations yet, deliberately, because writing digests for a corpus with two known-incomplete units would record a completeness the corpus does not have.

Round 884.decision_summary: The record could say which pair, not in what order, and its census recognised an input by filename
changes_bullets: Widened the evidence record from `kit-replay/v1` pairs to `kit-replay/v2`: an `inputs` list (path + role, one home per file) plus `replays`, each an ORDERED list of `{verb, input, expect}` steps. R883 measured why a pair is the wrong unit — `disclosure-craft` feeds six manifests through four verbs, and `continuity-stress` ends with three `propose-verdict` probes that must be REJECTED. All 23 manifests converted; 36 replays, 81 declared inputs (was 68).

Replaced the coverage oracle. R882 recognised an input by matching its basename against a `FACTS_NAMES` const — a hand-list, which is a copy of the class it was built to kill — and it passed green while 14 tracked inputs sat undeclared, among them a whole re-extraction arm (`unattended-loop/v1/run/extract/reextracted.manifest.json`, 54 facts, a second replay unit nobody had enumerated). The oracle now asks the bytes: sections by `section_id`, proposals by their schema string (hoisted to `TYPING_PROPOSALS_SCHEMA` / `EDGE_PROPOSALS_SCHEMA` so the gate cannot keep a second copy of the literal), facts by whether any `FactsManifest` array — the key set taken FROM the type, via an all-default parse re-serialized — is non-empty.

Shape and parseability are two questions, and the first cut of the new oracle asked only the second, which silently dropped 6 of the 14. Measured on identical state: parse-based finds 8, shape-based finds all 14. The gap is R878's population — 39 of the 81 inputs predate the R708 `{kind:value}` removal, so today's binary rejects the bytes with a migration work-list. A file the tool can no longer read is still an input; that is the entire premise of pinning the revision that CAN read it. An oracle whose reach shrinks as the tool moves forward reports full coverage while the corpus falls out from under it. The count is printed, never asserted on — it is a measurement of where the tool has moved, not a property of the record.

The pin derivation generalised from "the facts manifest's add-commit" to "the newest add-commit across ALL of a replay's inputs". A replay needs a tree holding every input it feeds, so the max is the earliest revision at which it could run; the pair rule was a special case. Measured: all 36 pins are unchanged under the new rule.

New gate `every_step_cites_only_what_an_earlier_step_created` — the declared order is now machine-checked without paying for a replay. 2427 citations resolved: facts cite sections an earlier step created, typing proposals and edge proposals cite facts an earlier step created, a `reject` step contributes no ids. This is the same reasoning that DERIVED the `disclosure-craft` order rather than reading it off the runbook prose: its one `-facts-add` fact is the target of a typing proposal and a succession edge, so it must land between the base facts and the proposals.

`disclosure-craft` A and B are declared BLOCKED, naming what is missing: the frame and branch registries were built by out-of-band `add-frame` / `add-branch` calls no tracked file records, so facts citing 4 frames and 4-5 non-main branches fail at `frame 'ground' not present`. Reconstructing them would be authoring a step, not replaying one. R883's discovery is now the record's own declaration.

J6 (a valid but different commit as the pin) reddened the derivation alone. J9 (relabel `raw-agent-output` as `replay-input`) reddened the role check alone.

J8 (rename `import-facts` to `import-fact`) reddened TWO: the verb check and the citation walk, whose match has no reference rule for an unknown verb. Same closed set asserted on two surfaces, reported as two.

J7 was MIS-AIMED and its green was correct: I moved `probe-exclusive` ahead of the facts it probes, and that probe carries no `supersedes_in_frame` — only `canon_from`, which the sections step already satisfied. Re-aimed at `probe-interval`, which supersedes `f-open-clock`, it reddened the citation walk alone. The first result measured my choice of probe, not the gate.

Measured absence, not assumed: flipping all three `expect: reject` values to `apply` leaves every test green. Nothing downstream cites a probe's fact id, so this file has no fixture separating the two values; the comment says so. Enforcing that outcome needs the runner, which actually runs the verb.

Round 885.decision_summary: The record now says what its evidence rebuilds to, and replaying it found the negative control was not controlling
changes_bullets: Built the replay runner and recorded the third of the triple. For each of the 23 declared revisions it extracts that tree (`git archive`, not a worktree — a worktree registers state in `.git` and leaks on panic), builds `mnemosyne-cli` into an isolated target dir, and feeds the untouched inputs through the declared steps in order. 34 of 36 replays reproduce; the 2 declared blocked fail exactly as declared. Every digest was taken twice in separate processes and adopted only on agreement, then re-verified on a third full run before being written and a fourth after.

Determinism is measured per replay, not inherited. R881 established it structurally (BTreeMap 17 / BTreeSet 1 / hash-order 0) and sampled it; a digest taken from a single run could pin a hash map's iteration order and start rejecting the same evidence tomorrow. Round 886.decision_summary: The replay had no clock; the two things that can break it run on different ones
changes_bullets: New workflow `.github/workflows/evidence-replay.yml` runs the R885 replay runner on GitHub. R885 left it `#[ignore]`d and unrun, which is the shape R873 named as the reason evidence rots — tracked, and nothing loads it. This closes the other half.

Two triggers, because the two failure modes run on different clocks. A digest can only change if an input, a step, or the runner changes, so `push` / `pull_request` are path-filtered to `claudedocs/phase1-*/**` plus the test file. The filter is tight BY CONSTRUCTION, not by guesswork: a digest is produced by the binary built at the kit's own pinned revision, so no change under `crates/` can move it. A pinned revision that stops BUILDING is the world moving instead — a yanked crate, a registry that stops serving an old lockfile — and no commit of ours triggers that, so it gets a weekly `schedule` plus `workflow_dispatch`.

Separate workflow rather than a job in `mnemosyne-validate`: that one runs on every push and all PRs, and paying 5 minutes there for a result our own code cannot change would be the wrong trade. Only the cargo registry is cached, not `target` — each replay builds into a throwaway target dir, so there is nothing there to reuse; what repays caching is the crate sources for 23 historical lockfiles.
verification_bullets: `fetch-depth: 0` is measured, not assumed. Cloned this repo at `--depth 1` and asked it for a pinned revision: `git archive 7d95e688` exits 128, `not a valid object name`. The runner extracts 23 historical commits, so checkout's default shallow clone would fail every one of them for a reason with nothing to do with the evidence.

Cost measured before recommending, not after: all 23 pinned revisions declare toolchain 1.94.1 — one toolchain, no per-revision download — and one cold isolated build is 12.8s, which is where the 272s full run comes from. `timeout-minutes: 45` leaves margin for a cold dependency cache, which this job pays more often than most.

Both workflow files parse, checked with a YAML parser rather than by eye: triggers and jobs enumerate as intended and the new checkout carries `fetch-depth: 0`. R583 is why this is checked at all — this repo has already shipped a malformed workflow that left CI silently non-running.
The declaration-gates step was run locally with `--locked` (6 passed) so the job cannot fail on a lockfile mismatch before it reaches the work.

NOT verified, and only a push can: that GitHub accepts the schedule, that the hosted runner's checkout behaves as the local shallow-clone experiment predicts, and that 23 historical lockfiles still resolve against crates.io from a hosted runner. That last one is the residual risk R880 recorded as UNOBSERVED — this workflow exists partly to observe it, and until it runs once the observation has not been made.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing prevents a malformed workflow YAML from landing. R583's failure was silent — the CI simply did not run — and the check above was a one-off run of a parser this repo does not carry: there is no YAML crate anywhere in the dependency tree, and pulling one in for a single test assertion was declined rather than done quietly. A future round that wants this gated should decide the dependency deliberately.

The weekly schedule is a guess at a cadence, not a measurement. A yanked dependency has no known arrival rate here; weekly was chosen because the job is 5 minutes and the failure it looks for is slow-moving.
GitHub disables scheduled workflows on repositories with no activity for 60 days. If this repo goes quiet, the cadence stops silently — the same class of silence R583 was.

Round 887.decision_summary: The carry was a cost judgement wearing a note, and the gate it deferred had a hollow job inside it
changes_bullets: Paid the carry R886 left instead of carrying it. The reason given there — that pulling in a YAML parser for one assertion was a dependency decision worth making separately — was deferring a real defect on a cost judgement, which this repo's round discipline does not allow. The owner asked why it was left; there was no good answer.

Three gates over this repo's own workflows, in the same file as the declarations because one of them is a cross-check between the record and the CI config. `every_shipped_workflow_parses_and_declares_work`: every tracked workflow parses and declares at least one trigger and one job — R583 lost an unknown stretch of CI to a workflow that did not parse, and GitHub says so nowhere the author looks. `the_replay_workflow_still_replays`: the checkout takes full history, some step passes `--ignored`, and every `--test` target named anywhere in the job exists. `the_path_filter_covers_every_file_the_replay_reads`: every input, config, and declaration a replay reads is matched by the push trigger's path filter.

The gate is a parser, not a text match, and that is not a preference: the R886 workflow names `fetch-depth: 0` and `--ignored` in its own comments, so a substring check passes on prose while the job is hollow. `yaml-rust2` with `default-features = false` — 4 transitive crates, dev-dependency only, never in a shipped binary. Not `serde_yaml`, which is deprecated upstream; adopting a dead crate is the legacy-carry pattern this repo forbids.

The `paths:` matcher supports exactly the two pattern shapes this workflow uses and PANICS on any other. A matcher that quietly mis-read a pattern it did not understand would report coverage it had never checked, which is the same failure the gate exists to catch.
verification_bullets: 1342 green (+3), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

Injections, self-reported. J2 (drop `-- --ignored`) reddened the replay gate alone — that is the vacuous-pass this round is really about: without it the job runs the cheap tests twice, goes green, and replays nothing. J3 (`fetch-depth: 1`) reddened it alone. J4 (narrow the filter to `claudedocs/phase1-2d-*/**`) reddened the coverage gate alone, naming the uncovered files.
J1 (a tab-indented broken block) reddened THREE — every test that loads this file. Correct and reported as three: an unparseable workflow is unreadable to all of its readers, not one.

J5 was MIS-AIMED and the green was mine, not the gate's: I renamed the test target in the first of the two steps that name it, and the assertion only read the step carrying `--ignored`. So the check was reading one of the two places a rename can land. Generalised it to every `--test` target in the job, with a non-vacuity count, and re-ran BOTH placements — each reddens now.
The path-filter check has no discriminating fixture in the tree as it stands: every declared input already lives under one prefix, so it can only be shown to discriminate by injection, which J4 does.
carry_forward_bullets: GitHub disables scheduled workflows on repositories with no activity for 60 days. If this repo goes quiet the weekly replay stops, and the stopping is silent — the same shape as R583, one level up. Nothing here can see that from inside the repo.

Round 888.decision_summary: CI was red for four commits, and the thing that noticed was me reading the runs by hand
changes_bullets: `mnemosyne-validate` CI has been failing on every push, at BUILD, before a single test ran, and the failure is one missing package: `mnemosyne-server`'s build script runs tonic-build, which shells out to `protoc`, and the hosted runner does not ship one. Both jobs install it now, from the runner's own apt source rather than a third-party action — one less thing to trust, and the version question belongs to prost-build, which takes what Ubuntu ships. The `msrv` job needed it too: `cargo check --workspace` builds the same script.

Found by looking at `gh run list` after the R884-R887 push, not by any gate. The four most recent runs on main were all red — R872, R874, R877, R883 — so this had been the state for at least eleven hours and four commits while local `cargo test --workspace` stayed green the whole time. The local pre-commit and pre-push hooks cannot see it: they run on a machine that HAS protoc.
verification_bullets: The diagnosis is the runner's own words, read from the job log rather than inferred: "Could not find `protoc` ... Error: Custom { kind: NotFound }" from `mnemosyne-server`'s build script. Locally `protoc` is 3.12.4 at /usr/bin/protoc, which is why the same command passes here and has for every round.
Not verified: that the fix works. Only a push settles it, exactly as R886 said of its own workflow, and this commit has not been pushed.

Verified in the same session, and this is the part worth keeping: the R886 workflow RAN on GitHub and was not a hollow green. 7m22s, exit 0, and the log says "36 replays across 23 revisions", "34 replays reproduced their declared digest, 2 blocked as declared". So three things that were open are now observed — GitHub accepts the workflow, `fetch-depth: 0` really does let it extract 23 historical commits, and 23 historical `Cargo.lock` files still resolve against crates.io from a hosted runner, which is the residual risk R880 recorded as UNOBSERVED.

It also closes an R885 carry that was honestly open: the 34 digests were measured on one machine, and nothing proved a path or environment value had not leaked into the store bytes. They reproduce byte-for-byte on GitHub's runner, on different hardware and a different OS image.
carry_forward_bullets: Nothing tells this repo its CI is red. That is the whole finding here and it is not fixed: the gate that catches a hollow workflow (R887) does not catch a workflow that runs and fails, because the result lives on GitHub and nobody here reads it. Four red runs went unnoticed across eleven hours. A local hook cannot answer it either — the hooks pass because this machine has what the runner lacks.

The two workflows install a toolchain the local machine happens to have. Any other build-time system dependency added later will fail the same way, at build, only on CI, and only where someone happens to look.
`actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/cache@v4` are annotated as targeting a deprecated Node.js 20 and are being forced onto Node 24. Both workflows use them. Not a failure yet.

Round 889.decision_summary: The gates needed history and the job that runs them had none; protoc had been hiding that
changes_bullets: `mnemosyne-validate`'s validate job now checks out full history. `cargo test --workspace` includes the R884-R887 declaration gates, and those resolve pinned historical commits — a shallow clone has none of them, so the gates could not run in that job at all. R886 measured this exact constraint and fixed it in the workflow it was writing; the job that runs ALL the tests kept the default depth. My own gate was the thing failing on the first CI run that got far enough to execute it.

Two defects were stacked and the outer one hid the inner one. R888's missing `protoc` killed the workspace build before a single test ran, so these gates had never once executed on CI. Fixing protoc uncovered mine — the msrv job went green in the same run and validate advanced from failing at BUILD to failing inside a test.

The failure now names its cause. A shallow clone made every declaration report `revision does not resolve`, which reads as a corrupt record and sent me hunting; the test asks `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` first and says what is actually wrong. It FAILS rather than skips: a gate that quietly stops asserting where the history is thin is worse than a red one.

New gate `every_job_that_could_run_these_gates_checks_out_full_history` — the check that would have caught this at commit time. It is R887's shape one axis over: R887 asserted the CI path filter covers what a replay reads, this asserts the requirement the gates place on their runner against the runner's own configuration, rather than leaving it remembered. The recogniser defaults to "this command could run these tests" and only backs off on an explicit `--test` or `-p` naming something else, because being wrong in the other direction is what produced a gate that could not run and said nothing.
verification_bullets: 10 green in the file (+1), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, validate-workspace clean.

The shallow predicate discriminates, measured on both sides: a `--depth 1` clone of this repo answers `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` with `true`, this tree with `false`, and in that clone the pinned revision is `fatal: Not a valid object name` — the confusing message the new assertion replaces.

Injections, self-reported. J1 (delete the `fetch-depth: 0` I just added — the R889 defect restored) reddened the new gate alone, naming the file, the job, and `fetch-depth: Some(None)`. J2 (blind the recogniser so no command matches) reddened it on the non-vacuity clause instead, which is the direction that matters: a recogniser that stops matching would otherwise leave the loop asserting nothing while looking thorough.

SELF-REPORTED PROCESS ERROR: I reverted J2 with `git checkout -- <test file>`, which restored the file to its last COMMITTED state and deleted this round's implementation. That is the exact hazard my own notes record from R817 — revert from a copy, never with git checkout, because the round's work is not committed yet. Round 891.decision_summary: R891 (BUILD — the map axis reaches the work-list). The authoring frontier (R589) describes itself as "every coverage gap an unattended generate-gate-repair loop pulls its next work from", JOINed from the scattered projections. THE MAP AXIS WAS NEVER IN THAT JOIN. It was built afterwards and in pieces — R697 made the edges store facts declared by a rule, R710 added costs, R722 added guards — and its read arrived only at R875, three hundred rounds after the frontier was written. None of those rounds reached back. R875 even listed the reads it had NOT reached (report-playable-world, report-quest-graph, the consumer's own bake) and the loop's work source was not on that list, because nobody was looking at it. THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE FAILURE CLASS THIS SUBSTRATE EXISTS TO REMOVE: a store can register places with no way between any of them, and the work-list reports its other gaps and stays SILENT on this one — an absence that reads as health. Measured on the deepest end-to-end authored narrative this repo holds, the R873 dnd-quest store: 136 facts, 25 entities, 4 world-lines, 56 order nodes, four authored quest-giver surfaces, and the frontier's answer says nothing about whether a player can walk anywhere. THE FIX IS A JOIN, NOT A NEW DERIVATION: map_frontier calls transition_map, so the frontier, the read and the gate share one answer to "what is an edge" — the SSOT shape R875 established in the other direction. What it adds is the subtraction nobody had written: the adjacency predicate declares its leg kinds (R701 subject_kind / object_entity_kind), those kinds admit a registered entity set under the R738 subkind resolver, and the places that set holds MINUS the map's nodes are the authoring work. Core never learns the word "place" — the rule names the predicate, the predicate names its kinds, and the consumer's vocabulary stays the consumer's (invariant 4). THE THIRD STATE IS THE POINT, NOT A DETAIL. Zero transition rules is not zero map work: with no rule there is no declared adjacency predicate and the store genuinely cannot know which facts are edges, so the render says that sentence rather than omitting the section (R864). The same discipline one level down: when the adjacency predicate declares no leg kind, the registered place set cannot be asked for, and place_kinds being empty carries that discriminator rather than a parallel bool free to drift from it. An empty list that means "unaskable" must never render like an empty list that means "complete" — omitting the axis is precisely how it stayed invisible for three hundred rounds. ALSO CORRECTED IN THIS ROUND, against my own first draft: costs and guards keyed to a non-edge do NOT belong here. They are already continuity violations the gate rejects and the R875 read echoes, and this report is the never-gated todo surface (R442) — counting a defect as authoring work conflates two categories and gives the datum a third home. Removing them also removed the only line of the derivation no test covered.

Per declared map it resolves the adjacency predicate's `subject_kind` / `object_entity_kind` (R701) and subtracts the map's node set from every registered entity those kinds admit under `is_kind_or_subkind` (the R738 one resolver). Round 892.decision_summary: R892 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 — the seam I suspected was under-built is not, and my own NEXT was the speculation). R891 closed the map axis's work-list gap and left a NEXT that leaned on R875's carry line: report-playable-world hands a consumer an unweighted graph, so measure whether making the consumer JOIN two reads is a hidden cost R875 named and walked past. MEASURED, THE ANSWER IS THAT R875 WAS RIGHT AND MY NEXT WAS WRONG. The playable world is a scene walk plus disclosure pointers; the map is a place graph; these are two axes, and the boundary between them is not a missing feature. The join key exists and is type-correct: MapLocator.object is a registered entity and every one in the corpus is place-kind, which is the same entity space the map's nodes live in. THE REAL NUMBER IS THAT THE KEY IS PRESENT ON 4.4 PERCENT OF LOCATORS — 16 of 361, being 4 authored surfaces across 4 world-lines — so for 345 pointers a runtime holds a scene and no place. THAT IS A DATA FACT, NOT A SUBSTRATE FACT, and the distinction is the whole round: a derived seat has no authored surface because the author never placed one, which is exactly what an authored surface MEANS. I THEN CHASED THE ONE HYPOTHESIS THAT WOULD HAVE MADE IT A SUBSTRATE FACT, AND THE MACHINE KILLED IT. If scene_cast (R757) bound a scene to a place, the join would be total rather than 4.4 percent, and the absence of a read composing them would be ours. It does not. Its closed modality vocabulary is observed / guessed / told / remembered — an EPISTEMIC axis, how a character KNOWS, carried with can_answer and a quote. A scene's PLACE is not a thing that vocabulary can say, and it is not a thing the store can know at all: deriving it would be core inventing domain semantics, which invariant 4 forbids. So the narrative half of the scene-place seam is NOT OURS TO BUILD, and the half that is ours R891 already built. THE PROBE FOUND A SECOND CAUSE I WAS NOT LOOKING FOR: scene_cast's anchor is a ContentAnchor pinning a quote by sha256 against the section's content, and this corpus has no prose — the continuity gate says so itself. So 0 of 56 sections carry a cast because the primitive needs a manuscript a fact-first store does not have, not because an author skipped it. Counting that emptiness as authorial neglect would have been the wrong reading, and it is the reading I would have written from a grep. THE ROUND'S VALUE IS THE BUILD THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. R891's NEXT proposed carrying edge references into report-playable-world; on this measurement that would have duplicated a join the consumer can already make, given the axis a second home to drift in, and asserted a scoping this substrate does not perform.
changes_bullets: No code. This round's output is numbers and a named cause, and its conclusion is that the build my own R891 `NEXT` proposed must NOT happen.
verification_bullets: `report-playable-world --telling delve` on the R873 dnd-quest store (rebuilt from tracked inputs): per world-line the payload is `manuscript` + `locators` and nothing else — zero edges, zero places, by construction.

The only possible join key to the map is `MapLocator.object`, and it is present on 16 of 361 locators (4.4 percent): 4 authored surfaces x 4 world-lines. All 4 objects ARE `place`-kind entities, so the join is type-correct exactly where it exists; for the other 345 the locator carries a scene and no place.

BOTH ACTIONS THIS REPO USES DECLARE THE DEPRECATED NODE 20 RUNTIME: checkout@v4 and cache@v4 carry `runs.using: node20`, GitHub deprecated it on 2025-09-19, and the runners now force them onto Node 24 regardless. THE BUMP IS THE SMALL HALF. The reason it sat is that R890 taught this repo to read a CI CONCLUSION, and a conclusion is one word: every run went green while its ANNOTATIONS said this, back to the oldest run GitHub still lists (2026-05-07), where the wording is still the earlier pre-forcing form — so the message itself escalated and nothing here noticed that either. That is R887's green-and-hollow class one axis over: not a workflow that passes without doing anything, but a workflow that does its work and tells you something no one collects. Bumped in the same change, because a half-cleanup leaves the defect alive precisely where this project ships it. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT is a tree-local gate asserting that an action's runtime is current: that fact does not live in this tree, it lives upstream and arrives only as an annotation, so the mechanism for this class IS making the annotation legible.

Round 894.decision_summary: R894 (MEASUREMENT, code 0 — I ran the verbs R892 had only read, and the first one refuted R892). R892 closed by naming an un-enumerated carry: a fact-first store holding no prose cannot use any primitive that pins a quote, `scene_cast` is one such primitive, and the rest were never counted. THIS ROUND COUNTED THEM, AND THE COUNT STARTS BY OVERTURNING THE EXAMPLE. Run against the very corpus R892 measured — R873's dnd-quest fixture, 56 sections, 0 with prose — `import-scene-cast` APPLIES. It never consults the section's `content_excerpt`; the quote it carries is a `ContentExcerpt` whose invariant (R759) is a non-blank source, non-blank text, and a hash the store computes for itself, with nothing resolving it against prose the store holds. So `scene_cast` is 0 of 56 in that corpus because THE AUTHOR DID NOT WRITE ONE, which is the reading R892 explicitly ruled out. R892 warned that a grep would have misread this and then made the mirror-image error: it read the TYPE, saw a content anchor, and concluded a block the machine does not enforce. THE CLASS IS REAL BUT IT HAS TWO MEMBERS, NOT ONE, AND NEITHER IS `scene_cast`. `import_ladders` (R765/R815) rejects a rung anchored into a section carrying no `content_excerpt`, and `import_evidence_reviews` (R806) rejects an affirmation against a section holding no prose — both fail loud, both name the cause, and both say in their own message that this is a reject and never a skip so the check cannot go vacuous. AND THE CLASS COLLAPSES FURTHER: one `import-content-excerpts` call putting 37 characters of prose on one section made BOTH rejected inputs apply unchanged. There is one prerequisite, one verb supplies it, and the verb requires nothing of the store. `import_epub_excerpts` is not a member at all — it refreshes a spec `normative_excerpt` and reports narrative sections as unmatched. So the correct statement is NOT that a prose-less store cannot use quote-pinning primitives; it is that two primitives are gated on prose being in the store, and nothing about a fact-first corpus prevents putting it there. WHAT THE ROUND FOUND WITHOUT LOOKING FOR IT is on the read side: `validate-content-drift` on this corpus prints `sections=56` and `drift: total=0`, where `sections` is the store's section count and not the number carrying an excerpt. Zero of the 56 hold prose. Every number is true and the line reads as coverage — the same zero-that-cannot-say-which-thing-it-means that R891 printed a sentence for and R864 named. That is a defect, it is not fixed here because this round is a measurement, and it is the next round of this session.
changes_bullets: No code. The output is an enumeration, a measurement of each member against the corpus R892 drew its conclusion from, and the RETRACTION of that conclusion.

One defect found and NOT fixed here (it is the next round's, this session): `validate-content-drift` cannot distinguish "no prose drifted" from "no prose exists". Naming it in a MEASUREMENT round rather than fixing it in passing keeps the two round types honest; deferring it past this session would not be acceptable.
verification_bullets: The corpus is R873's dnd-quest fixture rebuilt from tracked inputs exactly as `dnd_quest_map_seam_smoke.rs` rebuilds it (frozen `sections.json` / `order.json` / `narrative-rules.json` plus the fixture `facts.json`): 56 sections, 136 facts, and MEASURED 0 content_excerpt, 0 scene_cast, 0 ladder. The same store R891 and R892 measured.

`import-scene-cast` against that store: APPLIED, exit 0, one section's cast written. It does not consult `section.content_excerpt` at all — the quote it carries is validated by `validate_content_excerpt` (R759) for a non-blank source, non-blank text, and a hash the store itself computes, and nothing resolves it against the section's prose. R892's stated cause is REFUTED by its own corpus.

`import-ladders` against the same store: REJECTED, naming the cause — "anchors a rung into a section carrying no content_excerpt ... this is a reject, never a skip, so the check is never silently vacuous".
`import-evidence-reviews` against the same store: REJECTED, same shape — "carries no content_excerpt — nothing to affirm against".

THE DISCRIMINATING STEP: `import-content-excerpts` applied 37 characters of prose to one section (accepted; the store required nothing of itself to take it), and then the SAME two rejected inputs both applied. So the block is one prerequisite with one supplier, not a property of the store class.

`import-epub-excerpts` is a different axis, not a member: it refreshes a section's `normative_excerpt` (the spec corpus) and reports every narrative section as unmatched, erroring "no entry matched a refreshable excerpt" rather than silently no-opping.

READ SIDE, measured on a clean rebuild: `report-playthrough-manuscript --world claim` renders in full — 36 scenes, every fact one-liner, `unplaced=0` — so the north-star read does not want prose at all. `report-playthrough-manuscript --world delve` fails loud on an unregistered world rather than rendering empty, which is the behavior the third-state rule asks for.

`validate-content-drift` on the same store prints `sections=56 severity=reject unrevalidatable=0` and `drift: total=0`. Read in the source: `sections` is `store.sections.len()`, not the number carrying an excerpt, and the scan iterates sections and finds nothing to check. Every number is true and the reader is told 56 sections are clean when 0 of them hold prose.

NOT MEASURED: whether any primitive outside `mnemosyne-atomic`'s import surface pins a quote. The enumeration is of the atomic write layer plus its CLI verbs, which is where R892's claim was made; the engine's `Passage` resolution is a read path and was not swept.
carry_forward_bullets: `validate-content-drift` reports section COUNT where a reader hears coverage. The next round of this session fixes it; the general shape (a zero that cannot say which of two things it means) is the one R891 and R864 already named, now found in a third verb.

The two rejecting primitives are gated on prose being IN THE STORE, and `import-content-excerpts` will accept any text unless the caller passes `--grounding-source`. So the substrate does not stop an author from inventing prose into a frozen record — the R892 objection to authoring into the dnd fixture stands, but it is an EVIDENCE argument, not a substrate one, and this round is why the difference is now stated.

THE FIX IS THE SCAN REPORTING ITS OWN REACH, derived from the walk that already produces the violations. `scan_content_drift` now returns an `ExcerptCensus` alongside them — how many caches it examined, how many it skipped as unrevalidatable, and how many sections carry a cache at all — and when nothing was examined the CLI stops printing a bare zero and prints the sentence instead. A SECOND WALK WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WRONG SHAPE: two passes, one answering "what is wrong" and one answering "how much did you look at", are free to drift apart, which is the half-enforced class this project already refuses elsewhere. THE ROUND FOUND A SECOND, OLDER DRIFT WHILE WIRING IT. Round 896.decision_summary: R896 (BUILD — the audit R895 left, and the test that finds this class is only half a method). R895's carry asked whether other verbs share the defect it fixed: a zero that cannot say whether nothing is wrong or nothing was there. THE TEST IS MECHANICAL — run every verb on a rich store and on an empty one and compare byte for byte, because two different states rendering the same words IS the defect. All 31 `report-*` / `validate-*` verbs were run on R873's dnd-quest corpus and on this repository's own store: 16 differ, 6 need an argument, 9 came back byte-identical. AND SEVEN OF THOSE NINE ARE NOT DEFECTS. They read inputs NEITHER store holds — pre-v5 bindings, confirmation events, meters, unset config, transition rules — so identical output is identical state, correctly reported. The byte-identical test finds CANDIDATES; a candidate is only a defect once you have shown the two stores differ in the input that verb actually reads, and this round nearly recorded seven that do not. `report-transition-map` is the sharpest of them: it matches because R891 gave it the honest "the store cannot know which facts are edges" sentence, so byte-identical there is the signature of a verb that is already right. TWO SURVIVED AND ARE FIXED. `report-entity-kind-migration` said "0 unregistered kinds — every in-use kind is registered" in the same words on a store with 25 entities and a store with none; it now prints the store's entity count and, at zero, says nothing was checked. `report-excerpt-hash-backfill` — the R402 report R895 named while taking its number away — said "0 excerpt(s) lack a text_sha256" identically whether every excerpt is hashed or no excerpt exists; it now prints `N of M`, and the discriminator had to be CONSTRUCTED because neither real store carries a normative excerpt. AND MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG IN THE WAY THIS ROUND IS ABOUT. The entity-kind branch reached for the report's `total_entities`, a name that says store total and a value that counts entities naming an UNREGISTERED kind — zero by construction on exactly the branch that wanted a denominator. Re-running the comparison printed "over 0 entity(ies)" on the 25-entity store; the field is renamed `entities_naming_an_unregistered_kind` and a real count added. A misleading name produced a fix that looked like a fix and measured nothing, which is the same failure one layer up from the zeros this round went hunting.

Round 898.decision_summary: R898 (DESIGN — a corpus for the map axis, and the line between what it proves and what it merely contains). Round 891 gave the authoring frontier a map arm and Round 892 established the narrative half of the scene-place seam is not ours; what neither could do is show the map primitives carrying AUTHORED data. Every store in this tree declares zero transition rules, so every map verb answers from its empty branch — `report-transition-map` prints "no transition rule declares an adjacency predicate — the store cannot know which facts are edges" on both real stores, correctly, which is exactly why Round 896 found it byte-identical and honest. Seven primitives have no authored instance here: the transition rule itself (Round 697), containment and the G2 completeness checks it turns on (Round 703), edge costs (Round 710), edge guards (Round 722), place-kind subkind resolution (Round 738), the Round 875 map read, and the Round 891 frontier arm. Round 891's own J2 injection could not fail through the CLI for want of a place SUBKIND in the fixture. THE SHAPE IS AUTHOR-ONLY — NO RENDER, NO EXTRACTION, NO JUDGES. Round 892 measured the map reads working on a store with zero prose (36 scenes rendered), so a structure axis needs no prose arm, and adding one would double the protocol to test a different thing. The stated cost: this corpus does NOT unblock `validate-render-fidelity` / `validate-disclosure-leak`, which Round 897 showed need a re-extracted store this tree cannot load, whose revival is an authoring decision under the Round 469 bound. THE ORACLE IS OUR OWN VERB OUTPUT, SO THE CLAIM IS BOUNDED TO EXERCISE, NOT CORRECTNESS — a verb cannot be its own correctness oracle (Round 884: a hand-built oracle sharing the blind spot of what it grades is one measurement, not two). What it does establish: the non-empty branches run on data a person authored; a THIRD store for the Round 896 sweep that differs exactly where the current two agree, which is the only way that sweep gains discriminating power on this axis; and the authoring contract walked end to end by someone who did not build it. EVERYTHING THE BRIEF MANDATES IS DECORATION. The place count, the unreachable place, the one-way descent, the region — all demanded, so all they prove is that the author followed the brief. The evidence is what the brief does not mandate: E1, whether a blind author given only `describe-schema` reaches for the `transition` class at all (the contract does surface it — verified: it names adjacency, undirected and containment and says in as many words that this is how movement between places is gated, so a NO is a finding about reachability and a YES about sufficiency); E2, whether the FIRST submission imports, frozen with its full error text before anything is handed back, because an author holding the CLI iterates to green and "does the corpus load" would be the Round 854 vacuous pass; E3, the author's sealed self-report of how many places and ways and unreachable places they wrote, compared to the machine's counts, where a disagreement is a finding about the substrate or the contract and not an author error; E4, the byte difference as a third sweep arm. THE BRIEF SPEAKS FICTION, NEVER SCHEMA — "a chute you cannot climb back up", not `undirected: false`. The translation from world to schema is the author's, and a schema-worded brief would make the corpus a copy of our own expectations, which is the Round 469 bound in its quietest form. Two stages: Stage A blind with no map word anywhere in it, measuring E1; Stage B adding one fiction paragraph and guaranteeing the corpus exists either way. The corpus lands as a `kit-replay/v2` record registered in CI from day one, with `revision_provenance` EXACT rather than the derived upper bound Round 882 had to reconstruct for every existing kit — because a corpus nothing loads is precisely the rot Round 873 named and Round 897 found still open on the other half of the same experiment. AND THIS ROUND FOUND ITS OWN INSTANCE OF THAT ROT WHILE WRITING THE FIX: `/claudedocs/*` is ignored by default, so the runbook this round wrote was untracked until the exception landed — the same shape as the four quest-giver surfaces that lived only in gitignored files. Checked with `git check-ignore`, not by eye.

Round 900.decision_summary: R900 (DEBT — the carries, and one of them was not true). The owner asked why a round leaves carries at all, and the honest answer is that three of Round 899's four were work DECLINED, not limits of the world. Naming a gap in a carry reads as rigor, which is precisely how it substitutes for closing the gap — the mechanism by which the untested-hooks defect survived Round 890 naming it and Round 893 naming it again while adding logic to the same file. This round closes what was closable and, more usefully, finds that one of the four was FALSE. CLOSED: `.githooks/` is now inside the code-citation gate. Adding the path naively produced ELEVEN `section_missing` rejects, measured before deciding anything — the hooks cite `COMMIT_FORMAT.md §3` / `§4`, and the gate reads `§<digits>` as this store's own section namespace, the Round 867 whose-numbering question in miniature. The eleven were converted to the house `sec N` convention this repository already uses for design-doc references, the gate reports 0, and the `Round 899` citations the previous round wrote into three hooks are now checked like any other code citation instead of resting on my word. CLOSED for the request contract: the `gh` stub now CHECKS what it is asked rather than only answering — subcommand, the `--json` field list, the headSha filter, and both endpoint shapes, with violations written to a file the test asserts is empty. Dropping `conclusion` from the field list turns exactly one test red on that assertion while every canned answer still arrives, which is the shape of defect the old stub was structurally blind to. What stays genuinely uncoverable is jq SEMANTICS: a stub cannot evaluate the expression, only pin the request. ★CORRECTED, AND THE MACHINE DID IT: Round 899's carry claimed a hook calling the WRONG verb name "would still pass, since the stub answers to anything". That is false. Taking the new defense back out and misspelling the verb — the discipline of removing a defense to see what it was actually worth — still failed 2 of 10 tests, because the existing `mn_calls()` assertions check for the exact verb string. The carry was written from reasoning instead of from a run, and it overstated the hole in exactly the way this round is about. What the tightening buys, now measured rather than asserted: 2 of 10 becomes 7 of 10, and the failure names the cause at the point of the call ("no CLI verb is named 'validate-code-ref'") instead of surfacing as an argv-log mismatch three assertions later. STATED AS A LIMIT AND NO LONGER CARRIED: whether the hooks are INSTALLED cannot be checked from the tree at all. Git runs hooks from `.git/hooks` or `core.hooksPath`, both local configuration, and no tracked file can force or observe either — a property of the tool, not a choice, and it stops being pending work the moment it is named as a limit. The adjacent mode that IS checkable got closed: the helper now asserts the executable bit, because git SILENTLY SKIPS a hook without it and the gate disappears with no message at all. AND ONE ITEM WAS NEVER DEBT: `crates/*/tests/` staying outside the citation gate is a deliberate documented policy in `mnemosyne.toml` (Round 777 — single responsibility per asset class, review-time judgment carrying the residual). Round 899's carry restated it as though it were an open gap. Re-listing settled decisions as debt is its own noise, and it makes the list that matters harder to read.

Both exit 0. ADDING EITHER TO A WORKFLOW TODAY LANDS A GREEN STEP THAT ASSERTS NOTHING — the Round 887 green-and-hollow class three rounds of this session have been closing one verb at a time. So the answer is NO, and D3 closes as a decision rather than as deferred work. THIS IS NOT "THE VERBS DO NOT MATTER". Both were repaired this week — Round 895 for content drift, Round 901 for spec drift — precisely so that their zero is legible instead of passing for coverage. The repair is real; the INPUT is absent. A gate placed over an absent input measures the absence, and it would report success for it. THE TRIGGER THAT REOPENS THIS IS STATED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT: the moment this store starts carrying excerpt caches of any kind — any `import-content-excerpts` authoring landing here, including the map-corpus experiment if it ever writes prose — `validate-content-drift` becomes non-vacuous and the CI question is live again. `validate-spec-drift` reopens only if this workspace itself mirrors an external standard, which it does not and is not planned to: that is the consumer's shape (the SCE compliance ledger), not this tree's. AND ONE OPTION IS EXPLICITLY WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY UNCHOSEN: adding the step with a guard that fails when `examined == 0`. That inverts the contract Round 895 built — the zero was made LEGIBLE, not fatal — and would fail this repository on every push for a state that is correct. A gate that rejects a true state teaches everyone to bypass it.

ROUND 893'S CARRY CLOSES AS OBSERVED RATHER THAN REASONED. That round bumped `actions/checkout` to v7 and `actions/cache` to v6 and wrote that the bump itself was unobserved, because whether GitHub accepts the new majors and whether the Node 20 deprecation annotations disappear are visible only after a push. Both are measured now: every workflow is green on `1ee7e18`, and the annotation count runs 2, 2, 0, 0, 0 across `b138804`, `794ad8c`, `3bbdaf3`, `43cc1a6`, `1ee7e18`, with the vanished warning naming exactly `actions/cache@v4, actions/checkout@v4` as the actions forced off Node 20. BUT THE FIRST MEASUREMENT WAS NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A ROUND AND NOT A NOTE. I first took `43cc1a6` as the pre-bump baseline and read 0 there and 0 at `1ee7e18` — except the bump landed at `3bbdaf3`, THREE COMMITS EARLIER, so both arms were post-bump. Zero on both sides reads as "the bump changed nothing", which is the exact inversion of the truth, and the comparison was perfectly happy to say it. Round 904.decision_summary: R904 (EXPERIMENT — the map corpus, run on the owner's word against the protocol Round 898 froze). Two blind authors, fresh context each, firewalled to their own directory; no render, no re-extraction, no judges. THE ORACLE IS OUR OWN VERB OUTPUT, SO THE CLAIM IS EXERCISE AND DISCRIMINATION, NOT CORRECTNESS (Round 884). E1 CAME BACK YES AND IT IS NOT AN ARTIFACT OF ITERATION: given a fiction brief containing no map vocabulary and the 211-line contract, the Stage A author declared a rule of class `transition` with `adjacency`, `undirected: false` and `containment` — and `order.json` and `narrative-rules.json` are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the frozen first submission and the green store, so the map was right before any error message came back. Both authors independently chose directed edges and both explained it the same way unasked: a descent that cannot be climbed back is inexpressible if an edge admits both directions. E2 CAME BACK NO, TWICE, WITH THE SAME DEFECT: neither first submission imports, and both fail on `sections.json` being an object where the loader wants a bare array. Two authors who never saw each other's work produced the same wrong guess because THE CONTRACT GIVES NO WIRE SHAPE FOR THE SECTIONS FILE AT ALL, and each flagged it as a guess in the sealed self-report before running anything. The second error in each log is a cascade, and that was checked rather than believed: the fact manifests differ from their frozen originals by nothing that touches adjacency, and Stage B's imported with no content change whatever. THE EVIDENCE IS WHAT THE BRIEF DID NOT MANDATE, AND IT IS THREE CONTRACT GAPS, EACH REPRODUCED HERE ON AN ISOLATED STORE RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM AN AUTHOR'S REPORT. `parent_doc` is required on every section and appears ZERO times in the contract; both authors guessed a value and both were accepted, which as Stage B put it means "accepted is not correct" and the two commands they had could not tell them which. The contract under-declares the fact manifest by exactly one array, `units` — counted from the type, where `FactsManifest` has eight fields — and that single omission plus the contract's "Declared via add-unit" sentence led BOTH authors to conclude a Quantity is unauthorable from files and to author a workaround, a conclusion that sits in Stage A's SEALED report and is FALSE. And the manifest ignores unknown keys, so a typo of a real key returns exit 0 with zero created and no mention. THAT LENIENCY IS DELIBERATE AND LOAD-BEARING, NOT AN OVERSIGHT — `evidence_replay_smoke` states it and depends on it to tell a manifest that parses from one that BUILDS — SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THE PARSER BUT THAT THE CONTRACT HANDED TO AUTHORS NEVER MENTIONS IT, which is precisely what made the `units` gap undiscoverable: a correct guess and a typo are byte-identical. E3 DISAGREED IN OPPOSITE WAYS AND BOTH WAYS ARE FINDINGS. Stage A claimed thirteen locations against `12 node(s), 29 edge(s)`: edges exact, and the missing node is the unreachable place the brief demanded, authored with no adjacency at either end — the map READ cannot show an isolated place because a map's nodes are derived from its edges, and the GATE is where it surfaces, as `map_contained_off_map`. Stage B's counts agree exactly, and the disagreement moved to the question: its author reported a place UNREACHABLE while the frontier reports `unconnected places: none`, both true of different questions, with no read in this substrate answering the first. The two stages also split on the frontier itself — Stage B declared `subject_kind`/`object_entity_kind` on `adjacent` and Stage A did not, which is the whole difference between the Round 891 subtraction computing and printing `not derivable`; a blind author reproduced, from the contract alone, the exact shape Round 898 recorded as the reason Round 891's J2 could not fail through the CLI. C1: the previously empty branches ran, the Round 703 G2 checks fired on authored data, and `validate-continuity` REJECTS BOTH CORPORA — 27 violations in A and 12 in B, dominated in both by `adjacency_cross_scope`. THAT ONE REPLICATES ACROSS BOTH AUTHORS AND IS A FINDING, NOT AN AUTHOR ERROR: both authored quarters holding locations exactly as the brief asked and both wrote passages between locations in different quarters, which is what a town is, and the check treats a non-sibling edge as a violation while the contract mentions `cross_scope` zero times and describes G2 in three clauses that never say an edge must stay inside one container. Declaring `containment` silently tightens the gate in a direction the author cannot see. Whether the check is right or over-strict is a design question this round records and does not settle. C2: of the seven verbs Round 896 left byte-identical after its repairs, EXACTLY ONE now differs with this corpus as a third arm, and it is `report-transition-map`, the one Round 896 called the sharpest case of an honest byte-identical. The corpus discriminates on the axis it was built for and on no other, which is the honest result rather than a disappointing one. AND THE LANDING CORRECTED THE DESIGN: Round 898 specified `revision_provenance: "exact"`, a term the gate's closed vocabulary does not contain, so the pin lands as `declared-at-run`, the existing name for the same thing and the first kit in this tree to use it.

`v1/replay.json` registers both corpora as `kit-replay/v2` replays at `revision_provenance: "declared-at-run"`, so `evidence_replay_smoke` rebuilds them and CI's evidence-replay workflow triggers on this kit's own path filter.

verification_bullets: E1 IS NOT AN ITERATION ARTIFACT, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: `diff -q` reports `order.json` and `narrative-rules.json` byte-identical between `stage-a-first-submission/` and the green `stage-a/`, so the transition rule predates every error message. Stage A's `facts.json` differs by 13 lines, none of which touch adjacency.

E2's logs are frozen verbatim with both exit codes and no filtering, captured BEFORE anything was handed back, and the store was untouched by the failure (58 bytes, unchanged) so the rejection is clean rather than partial.

THE THREE CONTRACT GAPS WERE REPRODUCED HERE, NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE AUTHORS: on an isolated scratch store, a manifest carrying a key that does not exist returns exit 0 / 0 created / 0 bytes and names nothing, as does `"frame"` for `"frames"`; `{"units": [...]}` imports as `1 units created`, proving the array real; and `grep -c parent_doc contract.txt` is 0 against a field the loader requires. The manifest's true field count is 8, read off the `FactsManifest` type rather than counted from the tally string.

The `adjacency_cross_scope` intent was read from the source before being called a finding: the scan's own doc comment defines it as "a non-sibling edge", and the contract's G2 paragraph never states that constraint.

C2 is a byte comparison, not a reading: the seven verbs were run on this repository's store and on the Stage B corpus and compared with `cmp`. Six identical, `report-transition-map` differs. The same seven run on Stage A give the same one-verb answer.
Both replay hashes are deterministic, each reproduced from a fresh seeded workspace built exactly as `seed_workspace` builds it; Stage B's was computed three times across the round and never moved.

carry_forward_bullets: THE `adjacency_cross_scope` QUESTION IS OPEN AND IS THE ROUND'S LARGEST FINDING. Two independent authors hit it building the hierarchy the brief asked for, and 24 of the 39 violations across both corpora are that one kind. Either the check is right and a hierarchical map must also carry container-level edges (in which case the contract must say so), or it is over-strict for a shape a town naturally has. Deciding it needs the owner or a design round; this round recorded it rather than picking.
Neither corpus passes `validate-continuity`, so the registered replay covers the IMPORT only. A gate-clean map corpus waits on the question above.

The corpus still does not unblock `validate-render-fidelity` / `validate-disclosure-leak` (Round 897), does not compute reachability (Round 891 excluded it deliberately, and E3 now gives that exclusion an authored witness), does not settle per-world maps (Round 696 finding 6), and leaves the edge-cost and edge-guard side tables unexercised because they are argument lists rather than manifest arrays.

The E3 disagreements are recorded in the authors' terms and not resolved in the orchestrator's voice, per the protocol. Stage A's self-report carries a conclusion its own author later falsified; it stays sealed, because a report edited after the machine spoke is no longer evidence of what an author believed (the Round 469 bound, and the Round 883 rule that a record is never edited in place).

Round 904 left the largest finding open as a design question for the owner: `adjacency_cross_scope` rejected 24 of the 39 violations across two independently authored corpora, both of which built the container hierarchy the brief asked for. THAT QUESTION IS ANSWERED WITHOUT ASKING, BY READING THE MACHINE. `AdjacencyCrossScope` is not Round 703's check at all: Round 716 replaced the flat map with a PER-SCOPE projection, and its entry says so in as many words — "MapContainerAsNode is REMOVED", "this changes `contains` semantics from R703's grouping (all nodes one graph) to scope boundary (siblings-only edges)", "a portal is the container participating as a NODE in its parent's scope, so the container/node dichotomy dissolves". Under that model a quarter MAY be adjacent to a sibling quarter and movement between quarters goes through the quarters' own edges. THE CHECK IS CORRECT AND THE CORPUS IS WRONG — BUT THE AUTHORS ARE NOT. `describe-schema`'s containment field is still annotated "Round 703" and still tells an author that a region is "a container: a search-key, not a position" and that "a container must not be walked on". That is the exact semantic Round 716 deleted, and both blind authors paraphrased it back before being rejected for it: Stage A's sealed report says the quarters "are searchable places to be in rather than positions to move between", Stage B's says "containers, never adjacency endpoints". THE CONTRACT DID NOT MERELY OMIT THE MODEL, IT STATED THE SUPERSEDED ONE, AND TWO AUTHORS OBEYED IT. `describe-schema` never contains the words portal or cross-scope on this axis; its only two hits for sibling are about world-line roads. AND THE SECOND HALF IS WORSE, BECAUSE A GUARD EXISTS AND DID NOT FIRE. `manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key` asserts that every serde key is named in the wire prose — but its oracle is A HAND-WRITTEN EXAMPLE MANIFEST INSIDE THE TEST, and that example contains `"units"` zero times, so the guard never asked about the one array the prose omits. This is the Round 624 / Round 777 hand-list class in its purest form: the oracle is a second copy of the artifact it polices, so anything missing from BOTH copies is invisible. THE DERIVED FORM ALREADY EXISTS ONE CRATE AWAY — `evidence_replay_smoke::facts_manifest_keys` takes the key set FROM the `FactsManifest` type with the comment "a field added to the manifest joins this set on its own; a hand-copied list would not" — and this guard does not use it. The sections manifest has no wire prose at all: `parent_doc` appears zero times in `schema.rs` against a `SectionImport` field the loader requires, which is why two authors independently guessed the file's shape and both guessed wrong. Round 906.decision_summary: R906 BUILD (code) — the contract is derived from the types where it can be, and says the model the gate actually enforces where it cannot. R904 sent two blind authors at describe-schema with 211 lines of contract and a fiction brief; both submitted a sections manifest the loader rejects, both reported in sealed notes that a Quantity cannot be authored from a file, and 24 of their 39 gate findings were adjacency_cross_scope — three separate failures with one shape: the contract had drifted from the types and from the enforcement, under a guard that stayed green. This round closes all three at their source. (1) THE ORACLE WAS A HAND COPY. manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key walked a hand-written FactsManifest literal in the test body; when `units` was added to the type, the literal stopped compiling and the repair was `units: vec![]` — an empty array recurses into nothing, so the guard went quiet by being repaired, and the overview went on saying "seven arrays" for thirteen rounds. The R624/R777 hand-list class in pure form: the oracle was a second copy of the thing it watched. The roster is now DERIVED (set-equal to FactsManifest's serde keys), the overview is GENERATED from it so the count word cannot drift, and an empty array in the sample is now a test failure with a named reason. The derived form was already one crate away — evidence_replay_smoke::facts_manifest_keys, whose comment reads "a hand-copied list would not". (2) THE CONTRACT DESCRIBED THE SECTIONS MANIFEST NOWHERE: `parent_doc` appeared zero times in schema.rs, which is why two authors who could not see each other guessed the same wrong shape — a guess two isolated readers make identically is a contract gap, not two mistakes. New SchemaContract.sections_wire, reflection-pinned to SectionImport. (3) CONTAINMENT SAID THE SUPERSEDED MODEL. schema.rs still carried R703's "a container is a search-key, not a position" and "must not be walked on" while scan_spatial_map had, since R716, treated containment as a SCOPE BOUNDARY with the container participating as a node in its parent's scope — a portal. Both authors quoted the stale sentence back and were rejected by the live gate for obeying it. THE CHECK WAS RIGHT AND THE CONTRACT WAS THIRTEEN ROUNDS STALE; the corpora are not repaired here (R469: authoring on a blind record destroys the evidence). WHAT THIS ROUND LEARNED ABOUT ITS OWN FIX: my first draft of the sections prose offered coverage_expectation "normative"|"informative" — the two-state vocabulary R422 removed and R870 had already caught hand-retyped in five surfaces — and every key-level assertion passed on it, because a key-set walk checks that keys are NAMED and says nothing about what VALUES a closed-enum key accepts. So the closed vocabulary is pinned to serde_variants::<CoverageExpectation>() too. 5 new tests, 6 injections all firing exactly one test each, and every documented claim walked against the real loader in a throwaway store rather than asserted from reading: the bare array imports, the object-with-a-sections-key is rejected with "invalid type: map, expected a sequence", an omitted parent_doc is a parse error, and a Quantity is created from a file. NEXT = sweep describe-schema's remaining hand-authored tier-3 prose (canon_order, disclosure_encoding, invariant_enforcement, registry descriptions) for the same drift — this round found one because R904 walked into it; nothing swept the rest.
changes_bullets: describe-schema's manifest array ROSTER is now derived, not counted by hand: manifest_kinds() is the single ordered list (apply order, which serde cannot recover), the new manifest_kinds_cover_every_facts_manifest_array holds it set-equal to FactsManifest's real serde keys, and manifest_wire.overview is GENERATED from it (its type changed from &'static str to String) so the count word and the list cannot drift from each other or from the type.

The eighth array `units` is named, with the fact two blind authors got wrong stated outright: a Quantity IS authorable from a file — declare the unit here, then write {"kind":"quantity","n":…,"unit":<unit_id>} on the typed leg.

manifest_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key now REJECTS an empty array in its sample. That empty vec was the whole failure: `units` joined FactsManifest, the hand-written struct literal stopped compiling, and the repair `units: vec![]` recursed into nothing — a guard that went quiet by being repaired.

The manifest overview states that unknown keys are IGNORED DELIBERATELY, why that leniency is load-bearing (parse-vs-build are two questions, and evidence_replay_smoke::classify depends on separating them), and the consequence for the reader: a correct guess and a typo are byte-identical at the parse, so the roster is the only way to learn a kind exists. manifest_tolerates_unknown_keys_and_builds_nothing pins the behaviour with its discriminating pair.

NEW SchemaContract.sections_wire — the structure half of an authoring run, which this contract described NOWHERE (`parent_doc` appeared zero times). States the bare-array shape, every SectionImport key, the required-ness of parent_doc, the 3-way create/no-op/reject classification, and the asymmetry with the fact manifest. Guarded by sections_wire_prose_names_every_serde_key (reflection-pinned to SectionImport) and rendered by describe-schema.

The transition rule's `containment` prose is replaced with the R716 model the gate has enforced since R716: a per-(frame,world) containment tree PARTITIONS adjacency into SCOPES, an edge may only join SIBLINGS, a non-sibling edge is adjacency_cross_scope, and a container leaves its own scope by being a NODE in its parent's — a PORTAL. The same correction lands in narrative_rules_wire, and transition_containment_documents_the_scope_boundary_model asserts the R703 phrases are gone from both surfaces.
verification_bullets: 6 injections, each reverting one new guard's premise, each restored from a COPY: J1 drop the units KindWire / J2 leave a manifest array empty in the sample / J3 restore the R703 containment sentence / J4 drop parent_doc from the sections prose / J5 offer the R422-removed `informative` value / J6 hand-write the count word. 6 HIT, each failing EXACTLY ONE test — no silent branch, no over-firing.

The restore run reported 1 failure and it was NOT real: shutil.copy2 preserves mtime, so cargo saw no change and re-ran the J6 binary. This is the THIRD recurrence of the same harness defect (R891 hit it, R901 recorded it in memory, R906 repeated it) — `touch` then re-run gave 15/15.

The prose was held to the real loader in a throwaway store, not asserted from reading: sections.json as a BARE ARRAY imported 2 sections; the object-with-a-sections-key shape both R904 authors submitted was rejected with `invalid type: map, expected a sequence`; an omitted parent_doc failed with `missing field parent_doc` (a parse error, as the prose claims); and a manifest declaring a unit plus a quantity typed object created 1 units + 1 facts — the Quantity-from-a-file that both sealed reports called impossible.

My own first draft of the sections prose committed this round's exact defect: it offered coverage_expectation `"normative"|"informative"`, the two-state vocabulary R422 removed and R870 had already found hand-retyped in five surfaces. Every key-level assertion passed on it — a key-set walk checks that keys are NAMED, never what VALUES a closed-enum key accepts. The compiler caught it only because the test needed a variant; so the closed vocabulary is now pinned to serde_variants::<CoverageExpectation>() (J5 confirms it fires).
cargo test --workspace --locked = 131 test binaries, 0 failures; schema unit tests 15/15 (5 new). clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean.
validate-workspace clean at the same numbers as the pre-round baseline: T1 orphan 0, T3 reject 0 / warn 0 / T4 info 0, citation-gate 0 unscanned / 0 stale, decay surface 0.

Citation hygiene (R255): R422 / R595 / R600 / R703 / R706 / R708 / R716 / R870 / R904 / R905 each verified present via query --changelog-entry before the citation was written; R716's entry text is what supplied the scope-boundary/portal wording, and continuity.rs scan_spatial_map + verdict.rs supplied the violation names.
carry_forward_bullets: The derived roster catches a MISSING kind; it does not catch prose that names every key while describing the wrong MODEL. That is precisely how containment drifted for thirteen rounds under a green guard, and it is a limit of key-set oracles, not a deferred task — the containment repair here was possible only because R716's entry stated the model in prose a human could compare. Phrase-matching a semantic model would be theatre (R905's judgement, unchanged).

The APPLY ORDER of manifest_kinds() is still authored, not derived. Set-equality with the type makes the roster complete; nothing asserts that the documented order matches import_facts' loop order. They agree today (both are struct-declaration order, read directly). Deriving it would mean reading the apply function, which is not a serde fact.

Both R904 corpora remain REJECTED by the gate and this round does not change that. The corpora are correct evidence of what the stale contract produced; re-authoring them against the portal model would be authoring on top of a blind record, which R469 and R883 forbid. A gate-clean map corpus is a NEW authoring run, not a repair of this one — and it is now the first run that would read a contract describing the model it will be judged against.

The injection harness defect (copy2 preserving mtime, so a restored file does not trigger a rebuild) has now cost three rounds. It is not a limit of anything; the next harness must either copy without preserving mtime or touch the target after restoring.

Unmeasured here: whether describe-schema's OTHER hand-authored tier-3 prose surfaces (canon_order, disclosure_encoding, invariant_enforcement, the registry descriptions) have drifted the same way containment did. This round found one because R904 walked into it; nothing swept the rest, and the sweep is a real round, not a note.

Round 908.decision_summary: R908 BUILD (code) — the sweep I had priced at "several rounds" was ten thousand tokens, and paying it found one real defect. R907 ended by naming ~19 unswept prose surfaces as a COST for the owner to rule on. The owner asked why it was being left. The answer is that it should not have been: the estimate behind the carry was never measured. Measured, describe-schema's entire hand-authored prose is 99 fields totalling 40,476 chars across 14 surfaces — one read. THE ESTIMATE WAS OFF BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, AND IT WAS OFFERED AS A REASON TO DEFER, which is the R860 class (a countable thing asserted instead of counted) and the fourth time this project has recorded it. SWEPT AND CLEAN, mostly: the registries surface (21 fields, the largest) checks out claim by claim — edge_cost positivity, edge_guard threshold bounds and its refusal to drop below k, parameter_delta non-zero, fact_count positivity, and each one's scan-boundary re-check all exist where the prose says they do. ONE DEFECT IN THE WHOLE CONTRACT, in the interval rule's `bound` parameter: it read "a literal number, or a third scalar predicate id", and both halves are wrong. A bare number is a PARSE ERROR — verified by running it, not by reading types: `invalid type: integer 5, expected struct IntervalBoundWire`. And `scalar` is the object_kind R708 removed. So the contract's TWO descriptions of one field contradicted each other (narrative_rules_wire had the tagged object right all along), and the one an author meets first — the rule-class parameter list — was the wrong one, in dead vocabulary. TRACED TO ITS SOURCE: IntervalBound's own doc comment in continuity.rs said "a third scalar predicate", and describe-schema copied it. Core's PredicateObjectKind doc already records this token surviving in build_predicate's "expected one of" until R873; this was its third habitat, and the fix names NUMERIC-ness because that is the actual constraint. WHAT MAKES IT A TEST RATHER THAN A CORRECTION: no key-set or vocabulary-alternation oracle reaches this defect — `scalar` was an ADJECTIVE, not an enumerated value, and "a literal number" names no identifier at all. What is decidable is BEHAVIOUR, so the new test runs all three spellings through load_narrative_rules on a real file (the same call validate-continuity makes) and holds the prose to the outcome. That is the answer to R906's carry that a name-existence gate cannot reach model drift: some model claims are behavioural, and those can be pinned by running them. R907's ~19-surface carry is CLOSED, not deferred. NEXT = the map-corpus track: R904's two corpora are still gate-rejected, and the contract now describes the model they will be judged against.

Then it holds the prose to that outcome, and asserts neither surface offers a bare number or the word `scalar`.
verification_bullets: The sweep cost was MEASURED before it was paid, and the measurement refuted the estimate that had been offered as a reason to defer it: 40,476 chars across 99 prose fields is roughly ten thousand tokens — one read, not the "several rounds" R907 wrote down without counting.

The defect was verified by RUNNING both spellings against the real parser in a throwaway store, not by reading types: `"bound": 5` fails at load with `invalid type: integer 5, expected struct IntervalBoundWire`, while `"bound": {"const": 5}` gets past the parse and fails only on an unregistered predicate — a different and correct rejection.

2 injections, each firing the new test with a distinct named reason and each restored from a copy: J1 restores the stale prose (fails on "still offers a bare-number"), J2 breaks the const arm of interval_bound_from_wire (fails on "must parse"). The two cover the test's two halves — what the prose says, and what the parser does.

A third injection was DISCARDED because its anchor matched zero times and the harness asserted rather than proceeding. Recorded because a silently-unapplied injection reports as a clean pass, which is the failure this harness rule exists to prevent.

Two greps during the registry sweep returned zero and BOTH were bad greps, not gaps: `parameter_delta_violations` and the fact_count pair at lib.rs 7554/7624 are the scan-boundary re-checks the prose promises. Re-aimed rather than recorded as findings.

Round 911.decision_summary: R911 BUILD (code) — a person can walk into a quarter, the two ways an author reaches for first are both rejects, and my own prediction about the third was wrong until I ran it. R910's two blind authors each raised the same unprompted question — the contract never says how a subject gets INSIDE a container — and each invented the same answer alone. This round settles it by DEMONSTRATION, which is the discipline R909 established and R910 vindicated by catching R909 with it. THREE ENCODINGS, AUTHORED AND RUN. (A) Step across the boundary as a succession: `rule_transition_invalid`. (B) Add the edge that would license that step: `adjacency_cross_scope`. Both direct readings reject, and there is NO intermediate state to route through, because no edge may ever join a container to its own contents. (C) The refinement CO-HOLD passes: the coarse fact — `at` the container — holds across the whole visit as one fact with a spanning canon extent, while the fine facts inside succeed each other normally. AND IT PASSES ONLY THROUGH R714. Remove `containment` from the exclusive rule and the identical corpus becomes `rule_exclusive_overlap`, so the mechanism that makes entry expressible is the EXCLUSIVE rule, not the transition rule — a discriminating pair, not a single green assertion. I PREDICTED THE WRONG ANSWER AND THE RUN CORRECTED ME: I expected a boundary-crossing step to land in `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated. It is a reject. That bucket holds same-subject pairs which are NOT declared successions; once `supersedes_in_frame` names the step, an unreachable target is a violation. Reasoned rather than run, this round would have documented the opposite of the truth — which is exactly what R905/R906 did on the neighbouring question and what R910 caught. THE COST IS NAMED, NOT BURIED: with the co-hold, the crossing itself is not a CHECKED step. It lands in `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated, so the gate confirms walking inside a container and walking between containers and takes the crossing on trust. A corpus can claim a subject entered a container it was never adjacent to and pass. Closing that needs a hierarchical-entry notion in the transition rule — the statechart "entering a composite state enters its initial substate" — and that is a design round, not a fix. THE REJECT MESSAGE WAS ACTIVELY MISLEADING and is fixed: `rule_transition_invalid` offered only "author an intermediate succession through an allowed state", which for this case is unreachable, so an author obeying the hint searches forever for a state that cannot exist. It now names the container case and the co-hold. The contract carries all of it, guarded: an injection stripping the idiom fires, and so does one stripping the stated cost — those guards exist because R909 added guidance with no oracle and an injection removing it fired nothing. NEXT = a fresh blind run is the only test of whether the telling is enough (consent gate), or `evidence_unreachable`, still unmeasured at 43 findings across two independent authors.
