Round 912.decision_summary: R912 BUILD (code) — the check was right, the contract was silent, and the sharpest case is one nothing would have told an author. R910's second open question: are the 43 evidence_unreachable findings a real authoring trap or an over-strict gate? Demonstrated rather than argued, which is the discipline R909 established after R905/R906 got the neighbouring question backwards by reading the round that built the check. THE CHECK IS RIGHT. `evidence` is DEFINED as a backreference (R522) — reachable AND prior — so a forward reference is a real defect and all 43 were real. FIVE ENCODINGS, AUTHORED AND RUN. Evidence after `canon_from`: evidence_unreachable. At: clean. Prior: clean. And the one that matters — evidence mid-span, with `canon_to` reaching PAST the cited scene: STILL evidence_unreachable, because the comparison is against `canon_from` alone. A fact holding ch-1..ch-4 may not cite ch-3. THAT IS THE FINDING INSIDE THE FINDING: a reader who knows extents exist will assume the extent is the window, and nothing in the contract said otherwise. The fifth encoding is what the authors actually meant and it is CLEAN: `canon_from` where the claim becomes true, `evidence` at a prior establishing scene, and a disclosure `first_at` where the reader finds out. THE CONTRACT'S SILENCE WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: zero occurrences of at-or-before, prior, backreference or forward reference in the whole rendered contract. The rule appeared exactly once, as a clause inside the branches registry paragraph, framed as a fork-and-sibling concern that neither author's world had. Meanwhile the `evidence` field itself said only "Structure sections evidencing the claim ... a claim without provenance is unauditable", and the provenance invariant said "must name an existing section" — conflating EXISTENCE, which the write path checks, with ORDER, which the gate checks, so a manifest with a forward reference IMPORTS CLEANLY and fails later. That is precisely the sequence both authors experienced. AND THE FIELD THAT DOES CARRY THEIR INTENT WAS HIDING. `disclosure_encoding` opened with "Encoding a per-ROAD secret without leaking it" and described itself as a secrecy device only, so an ordinary unsecret fact discovered late read as out of its scope; an author with one would never look there. It now leads with the general axis and the three-way distinction the confusion is made of: `canon_from` is when the claim becomes TRUE, `evidence` is a prior establishing scene, and the reader's discovery is a THIRD thing that `first_at` carries. Both R910 questions are now answered and both answers had the same shape — the check was right and the contract was silent — so the two dominant failure kinds each have a documented idiom. NEXT = a fresh blind run is the only remaining test of whether the telling is enough (consent gate); R910's corpora stay untouched (R469/R883).

The failure was that the contract said this nowhere an author would look.

FIVE ENCODINGS MEASURED. Evidence after canon_from = evidence_unreachable. Evidence at canon_from = clean. Evidence prior = clean. Evidence mid-span with canon_to past it = STILL evidence_unreachable, because the comparison is against canon_from alone. And the encoding that expresses what the authors actually meant — canon_from where the claim becomes true, evidence at a prior scene, plus a disclosure `first_at` where the reader finds out — is CLEAN.

The `evidence` field description now carries the ordering rule, names `evidence_unreachable`, states that `canon_to` DOES NOT WIDEN the window, and redirects an author who wanted "true from here but discovered later" to `first_at`. Before this it said only "Structure sections evidencing the claim ... a claim without provenance is unauditable".

The evidence-provenance invariant now separates the two halves it was conflating: EXISTENCE is checked at the write path, ORDER at the continuity gate — so a manifest carrying a forward reference IMPORTS CLEANLY and fails later, which is exactly the sequence both authors experienced.

disclosure_encoding opened with "Encoding a per-ROAD secret without leaking it" and described itself as a secrecy device only, so a non-secret late reveal read as out of scope. Two new tests: the prose pins (ordering, the finding name, the canon_to caveat, the redirection, and the disclosure surface accepting that traffic) and a behavioural pin that a canon extent does not widen the evidence window.

E (mid-span, canon_to past the cited scene) = 1 violation, evidence_unreachable. D (canon_from early + evidence at + disclosure first_at late) = 0, and it says what the authors meant.

E IS THE FINDING INSIDE THE FINDING. A reader who knows about canon_to will assume the extent is the window; it is not, and nothing said so. That is the one part of the rule a careful author gets wrong on purpose.

Round 913.decision_summary: R913 DESIGN (code 0) — the crossing into a container is not merely unchecked, it is UNSAYABLE, and the measured cost was authors deleting half a town rather than a false claim slipping through. R911 closed its round by naming this design: entry and exit are not checked steps, and closing that needs a hierarchical-entry notion in the transition rule. THE MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST AND MOVED THE TARGET (R668 probe-first). Across FOUR independent blind authorings the boundary-crossing step was never declared once: R904's two corpora carry 14 + 10 = 24 `adjacency_cross_scope` and ZERO `rule_transition_invalid`; R910's two carry 27 + 16 = 43 `evidence_unreachable`, zero cross-scope and again ZERO `rule_transition_invalid`. The step R911 measured as a reject is a reject nobody ever wrote. What one author wrote instead is in R910's Stage B sealed report: 6 of 13 places "unreachable ... every place inside the quarter walls", and the author's own conclusion that this was "not an omission but the shape the map model forces". So the dominant consequence of the missing case is NOT the ungated false claim R911 named — it is LOST CONTENT: the substrate quietly taught two independent authors that the town had no insides, and they believed it and wrote none. THE CAUSE, ONE LINE: the step classifier admits exactly ONE relation — a sibling edge inside one scope — while the map declares TWO, `adjacency` and `containment`. A crossing between depths is therefore not wrong, it is unsayable, and both consequences fall out of that one missing case. THE DECISION: a declared step is checked AT THE DEEPEST COMPARABLE SCOPE. Four cases. `from == to` stays a violation (degenerate). `to` transitively contains `from` = ASCENT, allowed. `from` transitively contains `to` = DESCENT, allowed. Otherwise lift each endpoint to its ancestor that is a child of the deepest common container L, and require an edge between the two lifted nodes in L's scope. Today's behaviour is the L = root special case: with no `containment` every place sits in the root scope, both liftings are identities, and the required edge is exactly today's allowed-set membership, so a container-less map (the live flat one) is unchanged bit for bit. In one line: edges say which siblings you may walk between, containment says what is inside what, a step may use either, and it is judged where its endpoints are comparable. The sentence a blind author actually writes — "she walked from the gate into the market" — becomes legal AND checked: lift market to quarter, require edge(gate, quarter). The sentence a false corpus writes — gate to a throne-room inside a palace that no edge reaches — REJECTS, naming the lifted pair. THIS SUPERSEDES WHAT R911 TAUGHT IN THE CONTRACT. R911's prose tells an author that entry cannot be a step and that the co-hold is the encoding that passes; after this lands the first half is false and the repair hint that says "no such intermediate exists, do not model it as a step" is actively wrong. The co-hold stays legal (R714 untouched) — it becomes one encoding of two rather than the only one — and R911's two prose guards must be re-pointed in the same change, because a guard that goes on asserting a superseded idiom is worse than no guard. ALTERNATIVES REJECTED, WITH REASONS. (1) Gate the derived position timeline, declared or not: REJECTED, it kills narrative ellipsis — "later, at the palace" is legitimate untold travel and this would false-reject every authored jump; `supersedes_in_frame` IS the author's claim "this is one move", and gating what was never claimed is the wrong axis, turning `unchained_state_pairs` (never gated since R449) into rejects. (2) Allow cross-scope EDGES: REJECTED, that is R716's partition and R905 established the check is right while the CONTRACT was thirteen rounds stale. (3) Require a declared entry place per container, the literal statechart "enters its initial substate": DEFERRED, it needs new authored data and nothing pulls it — no blind corpus ever declared a crossing, so none needs to say which door; the pull test is an authored world where two doors into one container differ in consequence. (4) Require the coarse co-hold to cover every fine position: REJECTED, over-strict and contrary to R714, which made the co-hold legal rather than mandatory, and it leaves the author still unable to declare the crossing. (5) More contract prose, R911's move repeated: REJECTED as the whole answer — the telling is already there and the measured consequence was authors dropping content. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, NAMED RATHER THAN BURIED: no interior-path requirement (the container is ONE node in its parent's scope per R716, so leaving a quarter does not require walking to a boundary place first); ELLIPSIS STAYS UNGATED, so R911's false-claim hole SURVIVES — what changes is that it is no longer forced, the honest author gaining a declarable checked encoding and the dishonest one having to choose silence, and claiming closure of that half would be false; no new authored field, no schema version, no migration, gate-only; edges stay scope-partitioned. SCOPING AND IDENTITY, so no second reader appears: places resolve through the SAME containment snapshot `scan_spatial_map` partitions edges with, so a step and an edge can never disagree about which scope a place is in (R699 one-model discipline); the hierarchy is read per (frame, world, point) at the successor's frame and `canon_from`, so time-varying containment judges a step by the hierarchy in force AT the step, consistent with R715 and R716 both being per-point projections; the ancestor walk is cycle-safe on its own, because a gate must not depend on another gate having run (the R714 precedent). LAYERING RE-CHECKED (R712's non-negotiable line): answering "is this step allowed" needs no playthrough state — containment, edges and canon extents are all authored static structure. Invariant 4 holds: the classifier reads only the rule's declared `adjacency` and `containment`, so a non-spatial transition rule (`alive` to `dead`) is untouched. AND IT DOES NOT RESURRECT THE FRAMING R712's REVIEW REFUTED: the mechanism is stated as a graph with two relations and a lift to the deepest comparable scope, not as a statechart; R911's "enters its initial substate" was the analogy, and the literal feature is alternative 3, deferred. ONE DEFECT FOUND WHILE READING: `continuity.rs:824` still calls a container "a search-key not a position" — the retired R703 model in a FOURTH habitat. R906 replaced that model in the contract and added a negative assert, but it scans contract prose only and its needle carries a comma this doc comment does not, so it could not match this site even if it were scoped to code. Same class as R908 (a doc comment the contract copied) and R870 (one retired vocabulary hand-retyped five times). It is a code fix and lands in the BUILD round of this session, not as a carry. Round 914.decision_summary: R914 BUILD (code) — the crossing is now a declarable, checked step, and re-running the recorded blind corpora found a consequence the design had not predicted: a step could ride an edge the gate rejects. This lands R913's design. A declared succession is judged AT THE DEEPEST SCOPE WHERE ITS ENDPOINTS ARE COMPARABLE: same-scope siblings need an edge (the pre-R913 rule, unchanged), a pair where one transitively contains the other is a DESCENT or an ASCENT and is allowed outright, and anything else lifts both endpoints to the children of their deepest common container and requires an edge THERE. With no `containment` declared the parent map is empty, every lift is the identity in the root scope, and the verdicts are the pre-R913 ones — 1383 workspace tests pass with the container-less pin `rule_transition_catches_disallowed_step` untouched. THE UNPREDICTED CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. I re-imported all four recorded blind corpora and re-scanned them under the new gate rather than asserting the change was verdict-neutral. R910's two are byte-identical (27 and 16 `evidence_unreachable`, nothing added). R904's two GREW: 27 → 32 and 12 → 15, and every one of the 8 new findings is `rule_transition_invalid` on a step that had been RIDING A CROSS-SCOPE EDGE. Before this round the flat allowed-set held every edge including the ones `scan_spatial_map` rejects, so a succession along a rejected edge PASSED while the edge beside it was flagged — one relation with two verdicts, the half-enforced shape this project bans. The lift closes it as a side effect, which is strictly more correct and was NOT in the design; it is now pinned by its own test arm and its own injection, because an unpinned side effect is how a future "be lenient, fall back to the raw edge" fix would undo it silently. The replay kit is unaffected and that too was checked rather than assumed: the map replays pin the store digest after `import-sections` + `import-facts` only, with no continuity scan in their step list. WHAT THE INVERSION COSTS AND WHY IT IS RIGHT. R911's pin measured entry-as-succession as `rule_transition_invalid` and this round deliberately inverts that arm. Round 915.decision_summary: R915 REVIEW + DEBT (code) — three of R914's carries were not limits of the world, they were things I had not done, and the owner asked why twice in the project's history before asking again here. The trigger was the owner's "why don't you close it". Re-classified honestly, R914's carry list held six items: two need the owner's word (a blind run is the EXPERIMENT gate; an INDEPENDENT adversarial review needs an agent this session was not asked to spawn), one is a real substrate position (an author's silence is not a contradiction, so an UNDECLARED crossing cannot be gated), and THREE WERE MINE. All three are closed in this round, in the same session they surfaced. FINDING 1 — REDUNDANT BY CONSTRUCTION, not a measured hot spot. R914 read the containment snapshot once per STEP, while the snapshot is fully determined by (world, frame, canon point): every step judged at the same coordinates recomputed the identical map over every fact in the store. Now memoized on exactly those three keys. I make no wall-clock claim and did not measure one — the justification is that the work was provably duplicated, which is a correctness-of-design argument rather than an optimization. FINDING 2 — I DOCUMENTED A CODE PATH BY REASONING AND GOT IT WRONG TWICE. R914's step loop carries a fallback for "the successor is visible in NO world", and the comment explained it as "a fact on a pruned line". That was a guess. Trying to fire it found the guess wrong, and my SECOND guess — a store with no declared canon order — wrong too: with no order the fact stays `In` on main and it is the SNAPSHOT that comes back empty, which reaches the same flat verdict by a different route. The fallback appears to be UNREACHABLE, and the argument is now stated rather than invented: a fact is `In` in its own branch's world, because the departure bounds membership carries constrain INHERITED facts and not a fact on the branch itself, and a fact on an unregistered branch is rejected by the R440 boundary before the scan. It is kept so the loop has no silent hole, labelled as unreachable-so-far rather than given a mechanism it does not have, and the near-miss both attempts DO hit is now a test: an order that cannot place the `contains` fact yields an empty hierarchy, the lift degenerates to the identity, and the finding still names the world it was judged in. THE LESSON IS THE R905/R906 ONE AT ONE LEVEL DOWN: reasoning about behaviour instead of running it documents the opposite of the truth, and a comment is documentation. FINDING 3 — "AWAITING REVIEW" WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR A DEFINITIONAL QUESTION. R914 left "is an ASCENT sound with no edge at all?" open on the grounds that no corpus in this tree has ever declared an exit, so it could not be measured. But this is not a behavioural question, it is a question about what the model MEANS, and the answer is already in R714 and R716: being at a container and being at a place inside it are a COARSE and a FINE statement of one position, so moving between them changes the GRAIN of the claim and not the position. No parent-scope boundary is crossed, because the subject was already inside; no sibling edge within the container is crossed, because the coarse statement names no sibling. Requiring an edge would be requiring the crossing of something that is not crossed. What remains is not soundness but GRANULARITY — may a subject land at ANY interior place, or only at a declared entry — and that is the choice R716 already made when it put the container in its parent's scope as one node. Changing it needs authored data nothing pulls, which is the R913 alternative-3 deferral with its stated pull test. Recorded in the code at the classifier and in the design section, so the next reader gets the argument rather than the open question. AND ONE FINDING ABOUT ANOTHER ROUND'S CARRY, WHICH UNBLOCKS THE LARGEST REMAINING ONE: R891 deferred map REACHABILITY with the reason that the transition class also models one-way state machines where disconnection is the design, "and distinguishing the two needs a declaration the store does not have". THAT DECLARATION EXISTS AND THE GATE HAS BEEN USING IT SINCE R716/R719: `scan_spatial_map` runs per-scope connectivity ONLY for an `undirected` rule, precisely because a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`. So the blocker R891 named is not there, and the question "can this subject have got there" — which a blind author asked for in R904 and which R904 recorded as having no read in this substrate — is answerable for an undirected map. That is the next round, not this one, and it is named here so it cannot be re-deferred with a reason that has already lapsed.

The step loop's "successor visible in no world" fallback keeps the flat check so no step goes unchecked, but its comment no longer invents a mechanism: it now states the argument for why it appears unreachable (a fact is `In` in its own branch's world, and an unregistered branch is rejected by the R440 boundary) and says plainly that two attempts to fire it both failed.

Round 915.publishable_decision_summary: R915 REVIEW + DEBT (code) — three of R914's carries were not limits of the world, they were things I had not done, and the owner asked why twice in the project's history before asking again here. The trigger was the owner's "why don't you close it". Re-classified honestly, R914's carry list held six items: two need the owner's word (a blind run is the EXPERIMENT gate; an INDEPENDENT adversarial review needs an agent this session was not asked to spawn), one is a real substrate position (an author's silence is not a contradiction, so an UNDECLARED crossing cannot be gated), and THREE WERE MINE. All three are closed in this round, in the same session they surfaced. FINDING 1 — REDUNDANT BY CONSTRUCTION, not a measured hot spot. R914 read the containment snapshot once per STEP, while the snapshot is fully determined by (world, frame, canon point): every step judged at the same coordinates recomputed the identical map over every fact in the store. Now memoized on exactly those three keys. I make no wall-clock claim and did not measure one — the justification is that the work was provably duplicated, which is a correctness-of-design argument rather than an optimization. FINDING 2 — I DOCUMENTED A CODE PATH BY REASONING AND GOT IT WRONG TWICE. R914's step loop carries a fallback for "the successor is visible in NO world", and the comment explained it as "a fact on a pruned line". That was a guess. Trying to fire it found the guess wrong, and my SECOND guess — a store with no declared canon order — wrong too: with no order the fact stays `In` on main and it is the SNAPSHOT that comes back empty, which reaches the same flat verdict by a different route. The fallback appears to be UNREACHABLE, and the argument is now stated rather than invented: a fact is `In` in its own branch's world, because the departure bounds membership carries constrain INHERITED facts and not a fact on the branch itself, and a fact on an unregistered branch is rejected by the R440 boundary before the scan. It is kept so the loop has no silent hole, labelled as unreachable-so-far rather than given a mechanism it does not have, and the near-miss both attempts DO hit is now a test: an order that cannot place the `contains` fact yields an empty hierarchy, the lift degenerates to the identity, and the finding still names the world it was judged in. THE LESSON IS THE R905/R906 ONE AT ONE LEVEL DOWN: reasoning about behaviour instead of running it documents the opposite of the truth, and a comment is documentation. FINDING 3 — "AWAITING REVIEW" WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR A DEFINITIONAL QUESTION. R914 left "is an ASCENT sound with no edge at all?" open on the grounds that no corpus in this tree has ever declared an exit, so it could not be measured. But this is not a behavioural question, it is a question about what the model MEANS, and the answer is already in R714 and R716: being at a container and being at a place inside it are a COARSE and a FINE statement of one position, so moving between them changes the GRAIN of the claim and not the position. No parent-scope boundary is crossed, because the subject was already inside; no sibling edge within the container is crossed, because the coarse statement names no sibling. Requiring an edge would be requiring the crossing of something that is not crossed. What remains is not soundness but GRANULARITY — may a subject land at ANY interior place, or only at a declared entry — and that is the choice R716 already made when it put the container in its parent's scope as one node. Changing it needs authored data nothing pulls, which is the R913 alternative-3 deferral with its stated pull test. Recorded in the code at the classifier and in the design section, so the next reader gets the argument rather than the open question. AND ONE FINDING ABOUT ANOTHER ROUND'S CARRY, WHICH UNBLOCKS THE LARGEST REMAINING ONE: R891 deferred map REACHABILITY with the reason that the transition class also models one-way state machines where disconnection is the design, "and distinguishing the two needs a declaration the store does not have". THAT DECLARATION EXISTS AND THE GATE HAS BEEN USING IT SINCE R716/R719: `scan_spatial_map` runs per-scope connectivity ONLY for an `undirected` rule, precisely because a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`. So the blocker R891 named is not there, and the question "can this subject have got there" — which a blind author asked for in R904 and which R904 recorded as having no read in this substrate — is answerable for an undirected map. That is the next round, not this one, and it is named here so it cannot be re-deferred with a reason that has already lapsed.

Round 916.decision_summary: R916 BUILD (code) — the ellipsis no journey could have covered is now NAMED, which is the half of R911's hole that is closeable, and an injection that fired NOTHING caught one of my own assertions passing vacuously. R911 could only take the undeclared crossing on trust: "a corpus can claim a subject entered a container it was never adjacent to, and pass". It still passes, and that is correct — an author's silence is not a contradiction, so an undeclared crossing must never be gated. But there are two kinds of silence. An ellipsis between two positions a ROUTE joins is untold travel, which is legitimate storytelling. An ellipsis between two positions NO route joins is different in kind: there is no journey the telling could have omitted, and that is decidable from authored structure alone. So the second kind is counted separately as `unchained_unreachable_pairs`, a subset of `unchained_state_pairs`, surfaced and never gated. THE BLOCKER THAT UNBLOCKED IT HAD ALREADY LAPSED. R891 deferred map reachability because "the transition class also models one-way state machines where disconnection is the design, and distinguishing the two needs a declaration the store does not have". R915 found that declaration in the source: `scan_spatial_map` has gated its per-scope connectivity walk on `undirected` since R716/R719, precisely because a directed rule may be `alive -> dead`. This round reuses that field rather than inventing a second declaration, so a directed rule counts nothing. And the question it answers is one a blind author asked for: R904's Stage B reported places as unreachable, and R904 recorded that both the author and the verb were right and NO READ in this substrate answered the author's question. THE GRAPH IS THE HIERARCHY-AUGMENTED MAP: sibling adjacency edges PLUS a link between every container and what it holds, because entering and leaving a container are steps (R913) and a route may therefore use them. Union over canon points via world visibility — the same relaxation `scan_spatial_map`'s connectivity and completeness use, and for the same reason: an incrementally authored map (a bridge built in a later chapter) is legitimately disconnected at an earlier point, and a per-point answer would report the map's growth as a defect. Per (world, frame). R719 STAYS INTACT and this is not the check it rejected: two mutually-unreachable top-level containers remain a LEGAL map (two islands, a dream and the waking world), because what is counted here is not the map's shape but a SUBJECT asserted on both sides of it. The R712 layering line stays too — no guard is evaluated and no cost is spent, so a guarded edge counts as a route, because whether it OPENS is the consumer's question. A place the map does not hold at all is left to `map_invented_place` / `map_contained_off_map` rather than counted twice. MY OWN ASSERTION WAS VACUOUS AND THE INJECTION THAT FOUND IT FIRED NOTHING. The directed-rule test declared one `alive -> dead` edge, which read undirected is ONE component, so the count was 0 whether the `undirected` guard was present or not — the assertion could not have failed. Removing the guard reddened nothing, and that silence is what exposed it (R854's class: a true assertion with no discriminating input in the fixture). The fixture now declares two DISJOINT state pairs and the subject is asserted in each, so the guard is the only reason the count stays 0, and the injection fires. MEASURED LIVE, WITH THE HONEST BOUND STATED: all four recorded blind corpora were re-imported and re-scanned — 74 and 85 unchained pairs on the R910 arms, 1 and 0 on the R904 arms, and `unchained_unreachable_pairs` = 0 on every one of them. Those towns ARE route-connected once container links count, which is exactly what R913/R914 made true and is the structural resolution of the R910 author's "6 of 13 places unreachable, every place inside the quarter walls". A zero on real data is NOT evidence the check works, and I do not offer it as such: the discrimination is proven by the fixture that reports 1 and then reports 0 when a single road is added between the two districts.

Reported as what it is — those maps are route-connected once container links count — and NOT offered as evidence the check discriminates, which the fixture pair is.

Round 917.decision_summary: R917 REVIEW (code 0) — the independent adversarial review R913 asked for, and it refutes R913's stated reason for existing, R914's headline claim, R915's replacement comment and R916's whole measurement. The owner's word was "2": run the review R913's own carry named as never done ("The design was not adversarially reviewed ... the open-questions list is written FOR that review"). FOUR independent fresh subagents, non-overlapping lenses (model soundness / design-versus-implementation divergence / backward-compatibility and invariants / oracle vacuity by mutation), blind to each other and to this lineage's hypotheses, all held to RUN-DO-NOT-REASON. The orchestrator took a fifth lens no subagent had: R913's own cited measurements. THE DECISION SURVIVES AND FOUR OF ITS CLAIMS DO NOT. Making a hierarchy crossing declarable and checked is still right — R911's demonstration is independent and stands, the four R913.2 worked cases each behave exactly as tabled, deepest-not-shallowest is load-bearing (a shallower lift demands a self-loop edge and false-rejects everything), and container-less backward compatibility holds against 60 generated flat maps plus all four real corpora diffed against a binary built from the pre-R913 tree. WHAT IS REFUTED, none of it downplayed. (1) THE FOUR-CASE TABLE IS NOT CLOSED UNDER COMPOSITION. Ascent and descent are each unconditionally allowed, so inserting one coarse position between two fine ones launders any step the table rejects: the same map, plus a single `at(her, castle)` fact, takes `room-a -> room-b` from one `rule_transition_invalid` to ZERO violations with `unchained_state_pairs` and `unchained_unreachable_pairs` also zero, because every hop was declared. `at(s, C)` is not a position, it is an equivalence class over C's interior; an ascent discards which member and a descent picks a new one, so each hop crosses nothing and the pair crosses exactly what the gate says cannot be crossed. R913.5's "the honest claim is that every CLAIMED crossing is now checked" is therefore false, and that sentence was the design's own statement of its integrity. R915 answered "is one hop sound" and the model needed "is the relation sound". (2) `undirected: false` HAS NO EFFECT ON THE HIERARCHY ARM. `classify_step` contains zero references to the flag. R904's stage-a corpus declares `"undirected": false` together with `"containment": "contains"` and the author wrote why — the Cistern Slip "can be taken down and not climbed back" — and an ascent probe on that very map rejected before R913 and passes now. The author has no knob left. R916, the NEXT COMMIT, gates its own containment read on that same flag with that same reasoning, so R914's classifier walked into the hazard R916 protects against, on the same relation. (3) ONE RELATION, TWO READERS, and this is the read-path form of the half-enforced-invariant anti-pattern R914 itself closed one instance of. Containment is read per (world, frame, canon point); the edge set is a flat union over every frame, branch and point, because `transition_edges` filters on predicate alone — and its own doc comment states the obligation the caller then declined: "each edge carries its fact id and the caller reads that fact's frame/branch if it wants to scope". Confirmed consequences: a road existing only in a BELIEF frame licenses a ground-truth move; a road on a FORK licenses a main-line step; a RETIRED road licenses a later step; and a road the map gate rejects as `adjacency_cross_scope` at the only point it holds licenses a step at a point where it does not exist at all, which refutes R914's headline "a step may no longer be licensed by an edge the gate rejects". The mirror also bites: because the containment half IS frame-scoped, a step in a frame that does not restate the `contains` facts is judged flat and its author is handed the exact R911 dead-end advice R913 declared false. (4) R916's LIVE MEASUREMENT IS VACUOUS AND THE ROUND READ IT AS A RESULT. `unchained_unreachable_pairs` returns early for a directed rule; all four recorded blind corpora declare `undirected: false`; so the four zeros R916 reported were produced by that `return`, before `place_components` was ever built. Flipping only the flag on a copy takes a probe from 0 to 1. R916 then read the zeros as "those towns ARE route-connected ... the structural resolution of the R910 author's 6-of-13", which is a conclusion its evidence could not have contradicted.
